title: 導言
text: Open Music Theory（OMT）是一套開放教育資源，旨在作為大學部樂理課程的主要教材與練習冊。
en: Open Music Theory (OMT) is an open educational resource intended to serve as the primary text and workbook for undergraduate music theory courses.

title: 導言
text: 特色
en: Features

title: 導言
text: 多元主題
en: Diverse topics

title: 導言
text: 附有內嵌 MuseScore 播放器的譜例
en: Notated example with embedded MuseScore player

title: 導言
text: 互動內容
en: Interactive content

title: 導言
text: 各章附有作業
en: Assignments for each chapter

title: 導言
text: 免費使用
en: No cost

title: 導言
text: 大型出版社的教科書往往要價數百美元，OMT 則完全免費。
en: Unlike textbooks from big name publishers which cost hundreds of dollars, OMT is completely free to use.

title: 導言
text: 適合行動裝置
en: Mobile-friendly

title: 導言
text: 整套教材從一開始就以網路形式製作，版面能隨行動裝置調整，讓學生在智慧型手機上也能舒適閱讀。
en: The whole textbook is natively online and responsive to mobile devices, which means students can comfortably use the textbook on their smartphones.

title: 導言
text: 多元主題
en: Diverse topics

title: 導言
text: OMT 不只涵蓋完整的傳統大學部核心樂理課程，包括基礎樂理、自然音和聲、半音化和聲、曲式及二十世紀技法，也提供爵士、流行音樂、對位法與配器等單元，供採用多元課程的教師使用。這些內容來自多位專精不同領域的樂理學者共同合作。
en: OMT provides not only the material for a complete traditional core undergraduate music theory sequence (fundamentals, diatonic harmony, chromatic harmony, form, 20th-century techniques), but also several other units for instructors who have diversified their curriculum, such as jazz, popular music, counterpoint, and orchestration. This was made possible through collaboration between many different music theorists with expertise in these subfields.

title: 導言
text: 彈性的課程設計
en: Flexible curriculum design

title: 導言
text: 本書涵蓋傳統樂理課程序列中的所有主題，但 OMT 的各部分不必依特定順序教授。多數部分只要求學生熟悉基礎樂理，就能開始學習該方法或曲目，因此很適合採取模組式課程的學校。每個部分的導言都會清楚說明預設的先備知識。
en: This book covers all the topics in a traditionally-conceived theory sequence, but the sections in OMT need not be taught in a specific order. Most sections are written so that a student only needs familiarity with music fundamentals before studying a given approach or repertoire, which makes this book an excellent choice for schools with modular curricula. Each section’s introduction clearly states what prerequisite knowledge is assumed for that section.

title: 導言
text: 包容多元
en: Inclusive

title: 導言
text: OMT 的作者仔細挑選音樂範例，使不同種族與性別的創作者都能獲得呈現。
en: The authors of OMT carefully selected music examples to represent people of diverse races and genders.

title: 導言
text: 多媒體
en: Multimedia

title: 導言
text: OMT 充分運用線上網頁形式，在全書各處納入音訊與影片範例。傳統教材往往要求學生前往另一個網站，或自行演奏譜例，因而增加使用上的障礙；OMT 則把這些資源直接嵌在正文旁，方便取用。
en: OMT takes full advantage of the online and web-based format and includes audio and video examples throughout. Where traditional textbooks instead create a roadblock for students by requiring them to navigate to a separate website or perform the examples themselves, OMT has embedded these things directly alongside the text for easy access.

title: 導言
text: 互動學習
en: Interactive

title: 導言
text: 許多章節包含互動內容，讓學生輕鬆檢驗自己是否理解某個概念，並立即查得正確答案，有助於自學。
en: Many chapters include interactive content that allow students to easily test their knowledge on a concept and immediately find the correct answer, facilitating self-teaching.

title: 導言
text: 練習冊
en: Workbook

title: 導言
text: 除了少數例外，每章至少附有一份對應主題的練習單，可作為回家作業。練習單均提供 PDF 及可編輯格式（MuseScore 或 Word 文件），讓學生可以選擇在紙上或裝置上完成，也讓教師能修改作業，以配合自己的教學目標。許多章節另蒐集其他線上樂理學習資源的連結。
en: Each chapter (with a few exceptions) features at least one accompanying worksheet intended to serve as a homework assignment on the topic. Worksheets are always given as PDFs and as an editable format (MuseScore or Word document). This allows flexibility for students to complete the assignment on paper or on their devices, and for instructors to edit the assignments to better fit their own goals. Many chapters also collect links to other online resources for studying music theory.

title: 導言
text: 教師資源與社群
en: Instructor resources and community

title: 導言
text: 我們的 Humanities Commons 群組提供解答、考題、課程大綱範例、討論區等資源，讓使用 OMT 的教師能彼此分享教材。詳情見下文。
en: Answer keys, exams, sample course outlines, a discussion board, and more are available in our Humanities Commons group, so that any instructor using OMT can share material with others (more information below).

title: 導言
text: 第二版
en: Version 2

title: 導言
text: 本教材第二版由 Mark Gotham、Kyle Gullings、Chelsey Hamm、Bryn Hughes、Brian Jarvis、Megan Lavengood 與 John Peterson 共同撰寫。
en: Version 2 of this textbook is collaboratively authored by Mark Gotham, Kyle Gullings, Chelsey Hamm, Bryn Hughes, Brian Jarvis, Megan Lavengood, and John Peterson.

title: 導言
text: 各位作者分別主導教材的不同部分。Hamm 博士負責基礎樂理，並共同負責後調性音樂；Gotham 博士負責樂曲選集、十二音序列主義及配器；Gullings 博士負責全書各章的作業與練習冊；Hughes 博士共同負責流行音樂與後調性音樂；Jarvis 與 Peterson 兩位博士負責和聲與曲式；Lavengood 博士負責爵士、共同負責流行音樂，並編輯了許多章節。此外，每章也會個別列出實際撰寫該章的作者。
en: Each author led certain parts of the textbook. Dr. Hamm led fundamentals and co-led Post-tonal; Dr. Gotham led the Anthology, 12-tone Serialism, and Orchestration sections; Dr. Gullings led the assignments and workbook for all chapters; Dr. Hughes co-led Pop and Post-tonal; Drs. Jarvis and Peterson led Harmony and Form; Dr. Lavengood led Jazz and co-led Pop and edited many of the chapters of the book. Furthermore, each chapter individually lists the authors that wrote that chapter.

title: 導言
text: OMT 第二版的多數章節都是全新撰寫，但我們仍受惠於第一版的理念。第一版以 Kris Shaffer、Bryn Hughes 與 Brian Moseley 撰寫的資源為基礎，由 Kris Shaffer 與 Robin Wharton 編輯，並由 Hybrid Pedagogy Publishing 出版。第一版將持續保留在 http://openmusictheory.github.io。
en: While the majority of our chapters are entirely new to OMT v. 2, we are indebted to the vision of Version 1. Version 1 was built on resources authored by Kris Shaffer, Bryn Hughes, and Brian Moseley, edited by Kris Shaffer and Robin Wharton, and is published by Hybrid Pedagogy Publishing. Version 1 will continue to live at http://openmusictheory.github.io.

title: 導言
text: 無障礙使用
en: Accessibility

title: 導言
text: 我們致力遵循網頁無障礙的原則。
en: We are committed to the principles of accessibility on the web.

title: 導言
text: 為了協助使用螢幕閱讀器的讀者，我們採用某些較不常見的術語記法。尤其不會以大寫 M 與小寫 m 區分大、小性質，而改用「ma」與「mi」兩個縮寫。希望這套命名方式能逐漸普及。羅馬數字的大小寫雖然仍反映和弦性質，但性質也能由上下文推知，因此不必完全依靠螢幕閱讀器讀出大小寫。所有圖片均提供替代文字。許多譜例與作業使用 MuseScore；它是一套具有無障礙功能的樂譜閱讀器。
en: We use some less-standard terminology to help readers who use screen readers; in particular, we never use a capital/lowercase letter M to distinguish major and minor qualities, and instead use the abbreviations “ma” and “mi.” Hopefully this nomenclature will become more common over time. While capital and lowercase do reflect quality in Roman numerals, quality can also be inferred from context and is thus not essential information for screen readers. Alt text is provided for all images. Many examples and homework assignments use MuseScore, which is an accessible score reader.

title: 導言
text: 如果你發現有可以改善的地方，請透過〈建議與回饋〉告訴我們。
en: If you notice something that we can do better, please let us know through Suggestions and Feedback.

title: 導言
text: 更新
en: Updates

title: 導言
text: 為了避免干擾課堂教學，我們不會在學年期間（9 月至隔年 5 月）大幅更動本書內容或編排。不過，在各版本之間仍會持續修正小錯誤、改善視覺呈現；這正是開放取用形式的好處之一。如果遇到錯字、失效連結或其他需要修正的地方，或有新內容的構想，請透過〈建議與回饋〉提出。每逢重大更新，我們都會在〈修訂紀錄〉中列出。
en: We do not make major changes to the content or organization of the book during the school year (September–May) to avoid disrupting classroom instruction. We will, however, continue to fix small mistakes and improve aesthetics between versions, as this is one of the benefits of our open access format. Use Suggestions and Feedback to report any typos, broken links, or anything else you might come across that needs fixing, as well as ideas for new content. Any time we have a major update, we will list it in the changelog.

title: 致謝
text: OMT 的作者組成與一般教科書不太相同。這是一項集結許多人合作的計畫。封面列出的作者撰寫了大多數章節，另有其他貢獻者負責部分章節。因此，本書每一章都會署名給實際主導撰寫該章的人。
en: The authorship of OMT is not quite like other textbooks. This was a collaborative venture that brought together many people. The authors listed on our front cover wrote the majority of the chapters, but we have additional contributors that wrote some chapters as well. For this reason, each chapter of the book is attributed to the specific people who primarily authored that chapter.

title: 關於使用 Spotify 的說明
關於使用 Spotify 的說明
text: 為了讓本教材易於取得並維持低成本，我們選擇以 Spotify 連結提供部分音訊範例；若以其他方式使用這些曲目，OMT 將負擔相當高的著作權費用。使用者若有 Spotify Premium 帳號，閱讀本書的體驗會較完整。學生帳號的費用是一般 Premium 帳號的一半，我們希望這項費用不至於使太多使用者卻步。可在此申請 Spotify Premium 學生方案。
en: To keep this resource accessible and low-cost, we have opted to use Spotify links for audio examples for tracks which otherwise would cause OMT to incur considerable copyright costs. This book is best accessed if the user has a Spotify Premium account. Student accounts are half the cost of normal premium accounts, so we are hopeful that this does not dissuade many users. Sign up for Spotify Premium for Students here.

title: 關於使用 Spotify 的說明
text: 我們也必須指出，Spotify 的報酬制度向來受到不利於音樂人的批評。我們鼓勵讀者在能力許可時購買音樂，直接支持創作者。
en: We also state that Spotify is well-known to be bad for artists because of its pay scheme. We encourage readers to support artists directly by purchasing music when they can.

text: 基礎樂理練習單更新音程、三和弦與七和弦的練習單重新命名，原本的 1–5 改為 A–E。新增或更新音程練習單：D、E 新增兩種活動：音程轉位與分析。新增四份練習單，分別練習 ma／mi／P 與 d／A 音程，每一類各有兩個版本。大調與小調音階章節的練習單重新命名：Scales: Major → Major Scales（大調音階）。Key Signatures: Major → Major Key Signatures（大調調號）。其他項目依此類推。大調與小調音階練習單新增三項活動：依數字與名稱辨識大調、小調的音階級數。在指定調號下寫出音階。在與音階不相符的調號下寫出音階。每份大調、小調音階練習單均新增第二個版本。〈五線譜上的半音與全音〉：新增只用高音與低音譜號的版本；兩版都加入旋律分析，更新說明；可編輯檔改為 .mscz，取代 .docx。〈等音等價〉：新增只用高音與低音譜號的版本；可編輯檔改為 .mscz，取代 .docx。單拍子與複拍子練習單：〈單拍子／複拍子的符槓重組〉更名為〈單拍子／複拍子的節奏記譜〉；單拍子新增範例；複拍子調整頁面方向，使完整範例能排在同一行。自然音調式練習單：1、2 更名為 A、B；新增高音與低音譜號版本；所有版本都增加在同主音大調或小調調號下寫出調式的活動。各章新增「延伸閱讀」；增加大量互動範例；修正錯字、失效連結等問題，並作小幅編修。〈譜號的判讀〉：在高音譜號一節新增八度移位高音譜號的內容與範例；新增「其他 C 譜號」及「中性譜號」兩節，均附範例。〈其他記譜要素〉：在速度及結構要素兩節新增內容與範例，包括 a tempo、單小節／雙小節反覆記號，以及 d.c.／d.s. al fine／coda。〈其他節奏基礎〉：章首新增範例。〈大調音階〉：章首新增範例。〈小調音階〉：章首新增範例。〈自然音調式〉：新增附有範例的五聲音集合一節，並在半音階一節新增範例與文字。聽音訓練附錄導言：補入幾乎全部的正文。大幅重寫〈轉位〉，並使用新網址：https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/inversion。大幅重寫數字低音相關章節。調整〈七和弦〉之後部分基礎樂理章節的順序。自然音和聲：新增自然音模進章節。
en: Fundamentals Worksheets updates Intervals, Triads, and Seventh Chords worksheets renamed (1–5 became A–E) New intervals worksheets or updated worksheets: D & E have two new activities: intervallic inversion and analysis Four new worksheets, focusing on ma/mi/P and d/A intervals separately (two versions of each) Renamed worksheets in major/minor scales chapters: Scales: Major → Major Scales Key Signatures: Major → Major Key Signatures Etc. Three new activities on major/minor scales worksheets: Identifying major/minor scale degrees by number and name Writing scales within a key signature Writing scales against a mismatched key signature Second version of each major/minor scales worksheet Half and Whole Steps in Staff Notation: new treble/bass only version; both versions now have melodic analysis added; updated instructions; editable versions now in .mscz format instead of .docx Enharmonic Equivalence: new treble/bass only version; editable versions now in .mscz format instead of .docx Simple and Compound Meter worksheets: “Rebeaming in Simple/Compound Meter” retitled “Notating rhythm in simple/compound meter”; additional example added to simple meter; orientation changed on compound meter so entire examples are on one line. Diatonic modes worksheets: 1 and 2 renamed A and B; treble/bass versions added; all versions have a new activity to write modes within a parallel major/minor key signature. “Further Readings” section added to each chapter; numerous interactive examples added; typos/broken links etc. fixed, small edits made Reading Clefs: New content on octave treble clefs (Reading Treble Clefs section) with examples; Other C Clefs section added (with example); Neutral Clef section added (with examples) Other Aspects of Notation: New content in Tempo and Structural Features sections with examples (a tempo, one/two-measure repeat signs, and d.c./d.s. al fine/coda) Other Rhythmic Essentials: New examples added at beginning of chapter Major Scales: New example added at beginning of chapter Minor Scales: New example added a beginning of chapter Diatonic Modes: Pentatonic Collection section with examples added, new example and text in Chromatic Scales section Ear Training Appendix (Introduction): added almost all of the text Major Rewrite of Inversions chapter with new URL (https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/inversion) Major rewrite of Figured Bass Chapters New ordering of some music fundamentals chapters after Seventh Chords. title: 給德語使用者的說明
text: 跳至英文版說明
en: View in English

title: 給德語使用者的說明
text: 歡迎使用 Open Music Theory！（德文版說明）
en: Herzlich willkommen zu Open Music Theory!

title: 給德語使用者的說明
text: 本教材雖然以美式英語撰寫，卻有來自世界各地的讀者與使用者。很遺憾，我們沒有能力為本書製作涵蓋各種語言、專業上精確的完整翻譯；但如果國際讀者能從這裡的內容獲益，我們仍感到十分高興。
en: Obwohl dieses Lehrwerk in englischer Sprache (American English) verfasst ist, wird es dennoch auf der ganzen Welt gelesen und verwendet. Und auch wenn wir leider nicht die Möglichkeiten haben, fachgenaue Übersetzungen des Lehrwerks in allen möglichen Sprachen zu erstellen, freuen wir uns sehr darüber, wenn internationale Leser von den Inhalten profitieren können.

title: 給德語使用者的說明
text: 當然，只要熟悉西方記譜法，任何人都能同樣閱讀及理解音樂範例；此外，世界各地的人愈來愈熟悉英語，而自動翻譯程式的品質與精確度也持續提升。
en: Natürlich sind die Musikbeispiele für all diejenigen, die mit westlicher Musiknotation vertraut sind, gleichermaßen lesbar und zu verstehen; zudem sind Menschen auf der ganzen Welt zunehmend mit der englischen Sprache vertraut und automatische Übersetzungsprogramme gewinnen an Qualität und werden immer präziser.

title: 給德語使用者的說明
text: 然而，自動翻譯仍一再碰到限制，應審慎看待，尤其是涉及音樂專業術語的文章。即使由人翻譯，也會出現其他問題，因為這些問題根植於不同的教學慣例與學科傳統。
en: … Doch leider stoßen automatische Übersetzungen immer wieder an ihre Grenzen und sollten daher mit Vorsicht genossen werden, insbesondere bei fachsprachlichen Texten mit entsprechenden musikspezifischen Termini. Und selbst bei Übersetzungen durch den Menschen zeigen sich weiterführende Probleme, die in unterschiedlichen pädagogischen Konventionen und Traditionen des Faches begründet sind.

title: 給德語使用者的說明
text: 在這篇簡短導言中，我們這些以英語或德語為母語的人，將說明三個特別困難的面向：
en: In einer kurzen Einführung werden wir (als sowohl englische als auch deutsche Muttersprachler/-innen) drei besonders schwierige Aspekte beleuchten:

title: 給德語使用者的說明
text: 有些英語或德語專業術語，在另一種語言中沒有對應詞。遇到這種情形，就無法給出正確的對譯，只能希望英文說明已足夠清楚，讓讀者理解其意義。即使是非常基本的術語，直接翻譯也可能無法呈現所有層面的意義。幸好，德語與美式英語在這方面相當接近。例如，「quarter note」與「Viertelnote」可以直接對應，兩者都是四分音符；英式英語與法語卻沒有這種相同的命名對應。另外，有些詞乍看似乎相同，實際用法卻不同。最容易造成混淆、又經常出現的詞，也許就是「parallel」。現代德語樂理用它來描述大調與小調具有相同調號的關係，例如 C 大調與 a 小調，以及對應和弦之間的關係。在英語中，無論英式或美式，這種關係都稱為「relative」；「parallel」則指建立在同一根音上的大、小和弦，以及同主音的大、小調關係，例如 C 大調與 c 小調，德語稱為「Varianttonarten」。這雖然只是一個例子，卻可能是眾多差異中最令人困惑的一個。
en: Es gibt englische sowie deutsche Fachbegriffe, für die es keine Entsprechung in der jeweils anderen Sprache gibt. Also kann in solchen Fällen keine korrekte Übersetzung erstellt werden und wir müssen darauf hoffen, dass das Englische ausreichende Klarheit bringt und die Bedeutung verstanden wird. Selbst bei ganz grundlegenden Begriffen kann es sein, dass eine direkte Übersetzung womöglich nicht alle Bedeutungsebenen abbildet. Glücklicherweise sind sich das Deutsche und das amerikanische Englisch in dieser Hinsicht relativ nahe. Man denke dabei an die direkte Entsprechung der Begriffe „quarter note“ und „Viertelnote“ – eine Entsprechung, die es im britischen Englisch oder aber im Französischen nicht gibt. Hinzu kommen noch einige besondere Fälle, in denen Begriffe, die auf den ersten Blick scheinbar wie Entsprechungen aussehen, in Wahrheit unterschiedlich verwendet werden. Ein Begriff, der womöglich die größte Verwirrung mit sich bringt und zudem auch noch äußerst häufig verwendet wird, ist „parallel“. In der modernen deutschen Theoriesprache wird der Begriff verwendet, um die Beziehung von Dur- und Moll-Tonarten, die sich dieselben Vorzeichen teilen (z. B. C-Dur und a-Moll), sowie die Beziehung dieser Akkorde selbst zueinander zu beschreiben. Im (britischen wie auch amerikanischen) Englischen wird diese Beziehung als „relativ“ bezeichnet; der Begriff „parallel“ hingegen meint die Beziehung von Dur- und Moll-Akkorden auf demselben Grundton (z. B. die Varianttonarten C-Dur und c-Moll). Auch wenn es sich hierbei natürlich lediglich um ein einzelnes Beispiel handelt, so ist es doch neben weiteren vermutlich der verwirrendste Fall.

title: 給德語使用者的說明
text: 希望這些簡短提醒能對你有所幫助，讓你從 OMT 中獲益。
en: Wir hoffen, dass diese kurzen Hinweise hilfreich für Sie sind und Ihnen dabei helfen, von der OMT profitieren zu können.

title: 給德語使用者的說明
text: ——Mark Gotham 與 Andreas Feilen
en: —Mark Gotham und Andreas Feilen

title: 給德語使用者的說明
text: 歡迎使用 Open Music Theory！（英文版說明）
en: Welcome to Open Music Theory!

title: 給德語使用者的說明
text: 本教材以美式英語撰寫，但讀者與使用者遍布世界各地。雖然我們沒有資源進行多種語言的完整翻譯，若國際使用者能從這裡的內容獲益，我們仍感到十分高興。對熟悉西方記譜法的人而言，音樂範例同樣清楚可讀；世界上愈來愈多人具備更好的英語能力，自動翻譯的品質也不斷改善。
en: This textbook is written in American English, but we have readers and users all over the world. While we don’t have the resources to make thorough translation into multiple languages, we are very pleased if international users can benefit from what’s here—the musical examples are equally legible to anyone familiar with Western music notation, ever more of world’s inhabitants speak ever better English, and the quality of automatic translation is likewise improving all the time.

title: 給德語使用者的說明
text: 不過，使用自動翻譯時仍須留意，尤其是本書使用的音樂專業術語。無論是機器翻譯還是人工翻譯，不同語言的教學慣例之間，都存在超出單純翻譯層面的差異，容易令人困惑。本篇簡短導言將指出三個特別困難的面向。
en: But beware automatic translation, especially for specialist language like the music-specific terminology used here. And with machine or human translation, there are confusing differences between different languages pedagogical conventions that go beyond simple translation. In this brief introduction, we shine a light on three particularly difficult aspects.

title: 給德語使用者的說明
text: 有些德語術語在英語中沒有對應詞，反之亦然。這時沒有正確的對譯，只能希望英文說明已足夠清楚，讓讀者理解其意義。即使是基本術語，也可能因組成方式不同而無法直接翻譯。幸好，德語與美式英語在這方面相當接近。例如，「quarter note」與「Viertelnote」可以非常直接地對應；英式英語與法語則不是如此。最後，還有一些特別容易誤解的情形：看似相同的詞，實際用法卻不同。其中最常用、也最令人困惑的詞，也許是「parallel」。現代德語樂理教學以「Parallel」描述調號相同的兩個調，例如 C 大調與 a 小調，以及具有同樣關係的三和弦。英語樂理無論英式或美式，都稱這種關係為「relative」；「parallel」則用於同主音的調或同根音的三和弦，例如 C 大調與 c 小調，德語稱為「Varianttonarten」。這只是一個術語，卻格外容易混淆，也牽涉更廣泛的差異。
en: There are terms which exist in German for which there is no English equivalent and vice versa. In that case, there is no correct translation, and we have to hope that the meaning is clear enough from the English. Even basic terminology can be structured in a different way that defies direct translation. Fortunately, German and American English are relatively close to one another in this respect. Note, for example, the very direct translation between “quarter note” and “Viertelnote”. The same is not true of British English or French. Finally, there are some special pitfalls where what looks like the same terms is actually used differently. Perhaps the most confusing and commonly used term here is “parallel.” Modern German music theory pedagogy uses “Parallel” to describe the relationship between two keys with the same key signature (e.g., C major and a minor) and for the same relationship between triads. English (British and American) music theory use “relative” for this and “parallel” for keys and triads on the same root (e.g., C major and c minor, “Varianttonarten” in German). This is just one term, but a particularly confusing one that percolates through wider differences.

title: 給法語使用者的說明
text: 歡迎使用 Open Music Theory！（法文版說明）本教材以美式英語撰寫，但讀者與使用者遍布世界各地。雖然我們沒有資源進行多種語言的完整翻譯，若國際使用者能從這裡的內容獲益，我們仍十分高興。顯而易見的是：熟悉西方記譜法的人，都能理解音樂範例。世界上愈來愈多人具備更好的英語能力。自動翻譯的品質也持續改善。然而，使用自動翻譯仍須小心，尤其是本書使用的音樂專業術語。不同文化與語言有不同教學慣例，帶來的困難超出機器或人工翻譯本身。本篇簡短導言指出三個可能困難的面向。首先，有些法語術語在英語中沒有對應詞，反之亦然。這時沒有正確的對譯，只能希望英文說明已足夠清楚，讓人理解其意義。其次，即使是基本術語，也可能因組成方式不同而無法直接翻譯。例如，法語的「ronde」在美式英語稱為「whole」，指填滿一小節 4/4 拍的全音符；「blanche」與「noire」則分別稱為「half」與「quarter」，每一種時值都是前一種的一半。德語的命名方式很相近，法語卻不採這種方式。順帶一提，英式英語還要更複雜！最後，法語教學通常採取固定唱名法，英語稱為「fixed-do」。一個「ré」始終是「ré」，美國人則以「音高 D」表示。因此，韋瓦第的《榮耀頌》是「Ré majeur」，也就是「D major」（D 大調）。美式英語若使用「Do」或「Ré」這些音節，多半採首調唱名法「moveable-do」，柯大宜教學法也使用這套系統：「Do」指音階的主音，「Ré」指其上一個音階級數。所以，韋瓦第《榮耀頌》的第一個音，在法語中是「Ré」，用首調唱名卻要唱成「Do」！希望這些簡短提醒有所幫助，讓你從 OMT 中獲益。若遇到其他認為應列在此處的困難，請與我們聯絡。——Mark Gotham，並感謝 Zélie Jouenne 與 Mathieu Giraud。
en: Bienvenue dans l’Open Music Theory! Ce manuel est écrit en anglais américain, mais nous avons des lecteurs et des utilisateurs partout dans le monde. Bien que nous n’ayons pas les ressources nécessaires pour effectuer une traduction complète dans plusieurs langues, nous sommes très heureux si les utilisateurs internationaux peuvent bénéficier de ce qui se trouve ici. Il est clair que : les exemples musicaux sont compréhensibles pour quiconque est familier avec la notation musicale occidentale, de plus en plus d’habitants du monde parlent de mieux en mieux anglais, et la qualité de la traduction automatique s’améliore également tout le temps. … Mais méfiez-vous de la traduction automatique, en particulier pour le vocabulaire spécialisé comme la terminologie musicale utilisée ici. Les cultures et langues ont des conventions pédagogiques différentes qui vont au-delà de difficultés de traduction, qu’elle soit automatique ou humaine. Cette brève introduction met en lumière trois aspects potentiellement difficiles. Premièrement, il existe des termes qui existent en français mais pour lesquels il n’existe pas d’équivalent en anglais et vice versa. Dans ce cas, il n’y a pas de traduction correcte, et nous devons espérer que le sens soit suffisamment clair à partir de l’anglais. Deuxièmement, même la terminologie de base peut être structurée d’une manière différente qui défie la traduction directe. Par exemple, la « ronde » est appelée « whole » en anglais américain, remplissant une mesure 4/4, et les « blanches » et « noires » sont nommées « half » et « quarter », représentant à chaque fois la moitié de la durée précédente. L’allemand aborde cela d’une manière très similaire, mais le français ne le fait pas. (Soit dit en passant, l’anglais britannique est encore plus compliqué!) Enfin, la pédagogie française utilise généralement le système dit de « solfège fixe » (« fixed-do » en anglais). Un « ré » est toujours un « ré », ce qui se note « pitch D » pour les américains. Le Gloria de Vivaldi, en Ré majeur, est ainsi en « D major ». Lorsque l’anglais américain utilise les syllabes « Do » ou « Ré », c’est le plus souvent dans un système de « solfège mobile » (« moveable-do », utilisé aussi par la méthode Kodály) : « Do » fait référence à la tonique de la gamme, et « Ré » au degré au-dessus. La première note du Gloria de Vivaldi, un « Ré » en français, est ainsi solfiée… « Do » ! Nous espérons que ces brèves mises en garde vous seront utiles et que vous pourrez profiter de l’OMT. Merci de nous contacter si vous rencontrez d’autres difficultés qui, selon vous, devraient être énumérées ici. — Mark Gotham, avec remerciements à Zélie Jouenne et Mathieu Giraud.

title: 給法語使用者的說明
text: 歡迎使用 Open Music Theory！（英文版說明）
en: Welcome to Open Music Theory!

title: 給法語使用者的說明
text: 本教材以美式英語撰寫，但讀者與使用者遍布世界各地。雖然我們沒有資源進行多種語言的完整翻譯，若國際使用者能從這裡的內容獲益，我們仍十分高興。熟悉西方記譜法的人，都能同樣清楚地閱讀音樂範例；世界上愈來愈多人具備更好的英語能力，自動翻譯的品質也持續改善。
en: This textbook is written in American English, but we have readers and users all over the world. While we don’t have the resources to make thorough translation into multiple languages, we are very pleased if international users can benefit from what’s here. Clearly the musical examples are equally legible to anyone familiar with Western music notation, ever more of world’s inhabitants speak ever better English, and the quality of automatic translation is likewise improving all the time.

title: 給法語使用者的說明
text: 然而，使用自動翻譯仍須小心，尤其是本書使用的音樂專業術語。即使由機器或人工翻譯，不同語言的教學慣例之間仍存在超出單純翻譯層面的差異，容易令人困惑。本篇簡短導言指出三個可能困難的面向。
en: … But beware automatic translation, especially for specialist language like the music-specific terminology used here. And even with machine or human translation, there are confusing differences between different languages pedagogical conventions that go beyond simply translation. This brief introduction shines a light on three potentially difficult aspects.

title: 給法語使用者的說明
text: 首先，有些法語術語在英語中沒有對應詞，反之亦然。這時沒有正確的對譯，只能希望英文說明已足夠清楚，讓人理解其意義。其次，即使是基本術語，也可能因組成方式不同而無法直接翻譯。例如，美式英語的音符時值命名中，「whole」指填滿一小節 4/4 拍的時值，「half」是它的一半，其餘依此類推。德語的命名方式很相近，法語卻不是如此。順帶一提，英式英語也不採這種方式，而且還要更複雜！最後，法語教學通常使用固定唱名法「fixed-do」，其中「Do」永遠指音高 C，「Re」指音高 D，其餘依此類推。相對地，美式英語使用首調唱名法「moveable-do」（可參照柯大宜教學法）：不論在哪個調，「Do」都指主音級，「Re」指其上一個音階級數。你絕不會看到美式英語把一首樂曲描述為「Re Major」。
en: First, there are terms which exist in French for which there is no English equivalent and vice versa. In that case, there is no correct translation, and we must hope that the meaning is clear enough from the English. Second, even basic terminology can be structured in a different way that defies direct translation. For example, American English uses a system for note names with “whole” for the note value that fills a 4/4 measure, “half” for half of that duration, and so on. The German language approaches this in a very similar way, but French does not. (Incidentally, neither does British English which is even more complicated!) Finally, French pedagogy typically uses what’s called the “fixed-do” system of solfege, with “Do” always referring to the pitch “C”, “Re” to the pitch “D”, and so on. American English, by contrast, uses “moveable-do” (cf. the Kodály method), such that “Do” refers to the tonic scale degree of whatever key we’re in, and “Re” to the scale degree above that. You will never ever see American English describe a piece as being in “Re Major”.

title: I. 基礎樂理
text: 本部分介紹西方記譜法的基礎，包括節奏、音高及表情記號。學生也會學習建構與辨識基本的和聲組合，包括音程（兩個音的和聲組合）、三和弦（三個音的和弦），以及七和弦（四個音的和弦）。
en: This section introduces students to the basics of Western music notation, including rhythm, pitch, and expressive markings. Students also learn to construct and identify rudimentary harmonies, including intervals (two-note harmonies), triads (three-note chords), and seventh chords (four-note chords).

title: I. 基礎樂理
text: 先備知識
en: Prerequisites

title: I. 基礎樂理
text: 基礎樂理部分不要求讀者已熟悉西方記譜法。不過，本部分每章都預設讀者已理解前面各章，因此建議按順序學習。
en: The Fundamentals section assumes no previous familiarity with Western musical notation. However, each chapter in this section assumes familiarity with all preceding chapters; for that reason, it is recommended that chapters are studied in order.

title: I. 基礎樂理
text: 內容安排
en: Organization

title: I. 基礎樂理
text: 第一章〈西方記譜法入門〉鼓勵學生思考，如何把喜愛的歌曲或樂曲寫下來。接下來六章，從〈音符、譜號與加線的記寫〉到〈其他記譜要素〉，著重音高記譜，以及西方記譜法的表情與風格慣例。
en: In the section’s first chapter, Introduction to Western Musical Notation, students are encouraged to think about the ways in which they might write down their favorite song or composition. The next six chapters (Notation of Notes, Clefs, and Ledger Lines through Other Aspects of Notation) focus upon the notation of pitch and the expressive and stylistic conventions of Western musical notation.

title: I. 基礎樂理
text: 接著的四章，從〈節奏記譜〉到〈其他節奏基礎〉，介紹西方節奏記譜的慣例。之後再回到音高，從音階、調號、自然音調式與半音集合的記寫及辨識著手，相關內容見〈大調音階、音階級數與調號〉至〈自然音調式與半音「音階」入門〉。
en: Next, students are introduced to the conventions of Western rhythmic notation in the subsequent four chapters (Notating Rhythm through Other Rhythmic Essentials). Pitch is then revisited, beginning with the spelling and identification of scales, key signatures, the diatonic modes, and the chromatic collection (in Major Scales, Scale Degrees, and Key Signatures through Introduction to Diatonic Modes and the Chromatic “Scale”).

title: I. 基礎樂理
text: 其後的〈視唱與聽寫基礎〉預設讀者已理解前面各章的概念，可在聽音訓練課獨立使用，也可納入樂理或基礎樂理課。最後，教材探討和聲的建構，從兩個音構成的音程，一路到四個音構成的七和弦。
en: The following chapter, The Basics of Sight-singing and Dictation, presumes knowledge of the concepts in all previous chapters. It can be used as a stand-alone chapter in an aural skills class or within the context of a music theory or fundamentals course. Finally, the construction of harmonies is explored, from two-note Intervals through four-note Seventh Chords.

title: I. 基礎樂理
text: 〈三和弦〉與〈七和弦〉不討論轉位及數字低音，因為這些內容另於〈轉位與數字低音〉介紹。該章與〈羅馬數字〉、〈織度〉、〈SATB 四聲部風格的和弦〉，可作為聲部寫作、對位法、音樂欣賞或西洋音樂史的入門教材。
en: The Triads and Seventh Chords chapters do not include inversion or figured bass, as this is covered in a separate chapter (Inversion and Figured Bass). This chapter, along with Roman Numerals, Texture, and Chords in SATB Style can be used as introductions to part-writing, counterpoint, music appreciation, or Western music history.

title: I. 基礎樂理
text: 適用對象
en: Audience

title: I. 基礎樂理
text: 基礎樂理部分面向廣泛的學習者，包括高中生（也包含修讀 AP Music Theory 的學生）、大學非音樂主修學生及音樂劇主修學生，以及大學音樂主修學生。
en: The Fundamentals section is designed for a wide audience, including high school students (including those taking AP Music Theory), collegiate non-music majors (and musical theater majors), and collegiate music majors.

title: 西方記譜法入門
text: 重點整理「西方記譜法」指的是用來傳達音樂聲響的書寫符號。不同時代、地點與文化都有各種記譜系統；西方記譜法只是其中之一。把音樂寫下來的人，會依這些因素，也就是其社會脈絡或環境（milieu），選擇記譜系統。
en: Key Takeaways The term “Western musical notation” refers to written symbols that are used to communicate musical sounds. Western musical notation is one of many different systems of musical notation that appear across time spans, places, and cultures. Someone who writes down music chooses a musical notation system based on these factors, also known as their social context or milieu.

title: 西方記譜法入門
text: 音樂是一種聽覺的，也就是 aural 的藝術形式，可以透過記譜將它轉為視覺呈現。
en: Music is an auditory or aural art form that can be represented visually with notation.

title: 西方記譜法入門
text: 想一想，把一種語言翻成另一種語言是怎麼回事。這項工作可能很有挑戰性：逐字直譯不一定可行，也不一定有用，因此譯者必須思考如何把意思傳達給讀者。同樣地，把聲音寫下來，也必須決定要傳達什麼，以及如何傳達。沒有任何記譜系統能把聲音的每個面向都完整詳錄，同時還保持實用、可讀；因此，記譜只能呈現其中一部分音樂要素。
en: Think about what it’s like to translate one language to another. It can be a challenging task—a direct word-for-word translation isn’t always possible or useful, so a translator needs to think about how best to communicate to the reader. Similarly, writing down sounds involves making decisions about what needs to be communicated and how. No system of notation could capture every aspect of sound in full detail and still be useful or readable, so only some musical elements can be depicted.

title: 西方記譜法入門
text: 即使如此，書面記譜仍有許多好處。例如，把音樂作品寫下來，就不必完全依靠記憶，也能記錄原本可能遺忘的細節。此外，記譜能讓更多人接觸音樂作品：只要懂得那套記譜系統，就能自行學習已記下的作品，不必由教師協助。
en: Despite this, there are several advantages to written musical notation. For example, a written musical work does not need to be memorized, and details can be recorded that might otherwise be forgotten. Additionally, written notation makes musical works accessible to more people, since anyone who knows the notation system can learn a notated work on their own without the help of a teacher.

title: 西方記譜法入門
text: 試著想像，你要發明一種方法，把喜愛的歌曲或樂曲寫下來，讓音樂家即使從未聽過，也能演奏。在下方「發明一套記譜系統」的作業中，你將有機會選擇一首歌曲或樂曲來實際嘗試。聆聽並思考如何建立自己的記譜系統時，可以考慮以下問題：
en: Imagine inventing a way to write down a favorite song or musical work so that a musician could perform it without ever having heard it before. In the assignment below (“Inventing a Notation System”), you’ll have the opportunity to do this for a specific musical work or song of your choice. Here are some questions to consider as you listen to and think about creating your own musical notation system:

title: 西方記譜法入門
text: 作品中哪些音樂特徵比較重要？哪些比較不重要？你想記下哪些音樂特徵？有沒有打算省略的部分？如果改記另一首歌曲或作品，你對前兩個問題的回答會改變嗎？你會如何向別人解釋自己的記譜系統？
en: What are the more important musical features of the work? What are the less important musical features? What are the musical features that you would want to write down? Are there any that you would leave out? Would your answers to questions 1 and 2 change if you were writing down a different song or work? How would you explain your notation system to someone else?

title: 西方記譜法入門
text: 延伸閱讀

A Brief History.” (WQXR) “How did Music Notation Actually Begin?” (Classic FM) Assignments Inventing a Notation System (.pdf, .docx); Rubric (.pdf, .docx)

title: 音符、譜號與加線的記寫
text: 重點整理音符同時表示音高與節奏。音符寫在五線譜上。頻率較高、波長較短的音，記寫位置比頻率較低、波長較長的音更高；也就是高音在低音上方。符頭必須仔細寫在五線譜上。符頭呈橢圓形，不是圓形；大小要適中，並略向右上方傾斜。音符的符幹可以朝上，接在符頭右側；也可以朝下，接在符頭左側。第三線以上的音符，符幹朝下；第三線以下則朝上。第三線上的音符可以朝任一方向，依周圍音符而定。記寫二度音程時，總要把一個音移到符幹的左側或右側。不論符幹朝上或朝下，較低的音永遠在左側。譜號決定五線譜各線與各間所對應的音高。加線是額外的小短線，用來向上或向下延伸五線譜。
en: Key Takeaways A note indicates both pitch and rhythm. Notes are written on a staff. Notes with a higher frequency (shorter wavelength) are written higher on the staff than notes with a lower frequency (longer wavelength). That is, higher notes are placed above lower ones. A notehead must be written carefully on a staff. A notehead is oval (not round); additionally, it should be neither too large nor too small, and it is tilted slightly upward toward the right. The stems of notes can point either upward (on the right side of a note) or downward (on the left side of a note). For notes above the middle line, the stem points downward, and for notes below the middle line, stems point upward. Notes on the middle line can point in either direction, depending on the surrounding notes. Writing seconds always involves displacing one note to the left or right of a stem. The lower note always goes on the left, regardless of whether the stem points up or down. A clef indicates which pitches are assigned to the lines and spaces on a staff. Extra lines (that are small) called ledger lines extend a staff higher or lower.

title: 音符、譜號與加線的記寫
text: 西方記譜法特別著重兩種音樂特徵：音高與節奏。音高記在垂直方向，也就是 y 軸；節奏則記在水平方向，也就是 x 軸。閱讀西方樂譜的方向與英文書頁相同，由左至右、由上至下。
en: Western musical notation privileges two musical features: pitch and rhythm. Pitches are notated vertically (on the y-axis), while rhythms are notated horizontally (on the x-axis). Western musical notation is read left-to-right and top-to-bottom, like the page of a book in written English.

title: 音符、譜號與加線的記寫
text: 音符的記寫
en: Notation of Notes

title: 音符、譜號與加線的記寫
text: 音符同時表示音高與節奏。每個寫下來的音符都有符頭，可能空心，也可能實心；另外還可能有符幹，以及符槓或符尾，詳見〈節奏記譜〉。例 1示範符頭、符幹、符槓及符尾：
en: A note indicates both pitch and rhythm. Each written note consists of a notehead (either empty or filled in) and may also have a stem and a beam or flag (see Notating Rhythm). Example 1 shows an illustration of noteheads, stems, beams, and flags:

title: 音符、譜號與加線的記寫
text: 例 1。符頭、符幹、符槓與符尾。
en: Example 1. Noteheads, stems, beams, and flags.

title: 音符、譜號與加線的記寫
text: 五線譜記譜
en: Staff Notation

title: 音符、譜號與加線的記寫
text: 五線譜（英文單數 staff，複數 staves）是傳達音高的關鍵。它由五條等距的水平線構成，每個音符都放在與其音高對應的線或間上，詳見下方〈譜號〉。例 2是一個五線譜：
en: A staff (plural “staves”) is essential for conveying pitch. A staff consists of five horizontal lines, evenly spaced, and each note is placed on the line or space that corresponds to its pitch (see Clefs below). Example 2 depicts a staff:

title: 音符、譜號與加線的記寫
text: 例 2。五線譜。
en: Example 2. A staff.

title: 音符、譜號與加線的記寫
text: 將音符寫在五線譜上
en: Placing Notes on a Staff

title: 音符、譜號與加線的記寫
text: 寫在線上的符頭，應各占上、下相鄰間距的一半；寫在間內的符頭，則應剛好碰到上、下兩條線。例 3示範正確的符頭，包括線上與間內的空心、實心符頭：
en: Noteheads on a line should fill in half of each space above and below. Noteheads in a space should just touch the lines above and below. Example 3 shows examples of correct noteheads, both open and filled in, both on lines and in spaces:

title: 音符、譜號與加線的記寫
text: 例 3。正確的符頭：線上與間內的空心（白色）及實心（黑色）符頭。
en: Example 3. Correct noteheads, open (white) and filled in (black), both on lines and in spaces.

title: 音符、譜號與加線的記寫
text: 符頭應呈橢圓形，而非圓形，並略向右上方傾斜。例 4示範不正確的符頭。[1]如圖所示，符頭可能畫得太小、太大，或形狀不正確。
en: Noteheads should be oval (not round), and they are tilted slightly upward toward the right. Example 4 shows incorrect noteheads.[1] As you can see, noteheads can be drawn too small, too big, or the wrong shape.

title: 音符、譜號與加線的記寫
text: 例 4。不正確的符頭範例。
en: Example 4. Incorrect examples of noteheads.

title: 音符、譜號與加線的記寫
text: 符幹與符槓
en: Stems and Beams

title: 音符、譜號與加線的記寫
text: 音符的符幹可以朝上，接在符頭右側；也可以朝下，接在符頭左側。第三線以上的音符，符幹朝下；第三線以下的音符，符幹朝上。第三線上的音符則可朝任一方向，視周圍音符而定，如例 5所示：
en: The stems of notes can point either upward (on the right side of a note) or downward (on the left side of a note). For notes above the middle line, the stem points downward, and for notes below the middle line, stems point upward. Notes on the middle line can point in either direction, depending on the surrounding notes. This is shown in Example 5:

title: 音符、譜號與加線的記寫
text: 例 5。正確的符幹方向。
en: Example 5. Correct stemming directions.

title: 音符、譜號與加線的記寫
text: 〈單拍子與拍號〉及〈複拍子與拍號〉會進一步討論符幹方向與符槓分組慣例。手寫符幹時，其長度等於五線譜中四條線所跨的距離；符槓的粗細則約為符幹的四倍。
en: Stemming directions and beaming conventions are discussed more in Simple Meter and Time Signatures and Compound Meter and Time Signatures. When hand-drawing stems, their length is equal to four lines of the staff. Beams are about four times thicker than stems.

title: 音符、譜號與加線的記寫
text: 你可以透過下列拖曳配對練習，熟悉符幹方向：
en: You can practice stemming directions by dragging and dropping in the following exercise:

title: 音符、譜號與加線的記寫
text: 練習符幹方向配對
en: Practice Stem Direction Matching (requires internet)

title: 音符、譜號與加線的記寫
text: 二度音程的記寫
en: Drawing Seconds

title: 音符、譜號與加線的記寫
text: 相距二度的音若同時發聲，便位於五線譜相鄰的線與間，因此必須將其中一個符頭移到符幹的左側或右側。二度的概念可參閱〈鍵盤與大譜表〉中的〈音程度數〉。不論符幹朝上或朝下，較低的音永遠在左側。例 6示範正確的二度記法：
en: When notes at the interval of a second (see the Generic Intervals section of The Keyboard and the Grand Staff) occur harmonically, they are on an adjacent line and space of the staff, so one note needs to be displaced to the left or right of the stem. The lower note always goes on the left, regardless of whether the stem points up or down. Example 6 shows the correct way to draw seconds:

title: 音符、譜號與加線的記寫
text: 例 6。三個正確記寫的二度音程。
en: Example 6. Three correct seconds.

title: 音符、譜號與加線的記寫
text: 二度音程的兩個符頭不應直接上下堆疊，也不應把較低的音放在右側；例 7示範這些錯誤：
en: Seconds should not be stacked on top of one another, nor should the lower note be on the right, as seen in Example 7:

title: 音符、譜號與加線的記寫
text: 例 7。三個不正確的二度記法。
en: Example 7. Three incorrect seconds.

title: 音符、譜號與加線的記寫
text: 七和弦中出現二度時的記寫方式，將於〈七和弦〉討論。
en: Drawing seconds in seventh chords is discussed in Seventh Chords.

title: 音符、譜號與加線的記寫
text: 譜號
en: Clefs

title: 音符、譜號與加線的記寫
text: 五線譜各線與各間上的音符表示音高。音樂家以空間比喻描述譜上的音符：靠近上方的音稱為「較高」，靠近下方則稱為「較低」。較高的音由波長較短、因而頻率較高的聲波產生；波長較長、頻率較低的聲波，則產生較低的音。
en: The notes drawn on the lines and spaces of a staff represent pitches. Musicians use spatial metaphors to describe notes placed on a staff: notes appearing toward the top of the staff are said to be “higher” than those toward the bottom, which are said to be “lower.” Higher pitches are produced by sound waves with a shorter wavelength (and consequently a higher frequency); sound waves with a longer wavelength (lower frequency) produce lower pitches.

title: 音符、譜號與加線的記寫
text: 若要讓音符提供超出「較高」與「較低」的具體音高資訊，五線譜就必須包含譜號。譜號決定各線與各間所對應的音高，另見〈譜號的判讀〉。今日最常用的兩種譜號是高音譜號與低音譜號；另外也可能遇到中音譜號與次中音譜號。例 8把同一音高分別寫在高音、低音、中音及次中音譜號之後：
en: For notes to convey pitch information beyond “higher” and “lower,” the staff on which they appear must include a clef. A clef indicates which pitches are assigned to the lines and spaces on a staff (see also Reading Clefs). The two most commonly used clefs today are the treble clef and bass clef. Two other clefs that you may encounter are the alto clef and the tenor clef. Example 8 shows the same pitch placed after the treble, bass, alto, and tenor clefs:

title: 音符、譜號與加線的記寫
text: 例 8。同一音高，分別寫在高音、低音、中音及次中音譜號之後。
en: Example 8. The same pitch placed after a treble, bass, alto, and tenor clef.

title: 音符、譜號與加線的記寫
text: 較高的音，例如長笛演奏或女高音演唱的音，通常以高音譜號記寫；較低的音，例如長號演奏或男低音演唱的音，通常以低音譜號記寫。與這兩種譜號相比，中音與次中音譜號較少見；但某些情況會以中音譜號記寫中高音，以次中音譜號記寫中低音。
en: Higher notes, such as those played by a flute or sung by a soprano, are usually written in treble clef, and lower notes, such as those played by a trombone or sung by a bass, are usually written in bass clef. Alto and tenor clefs are relatively rare compared to treble and bass. But in some cases, alto clef is used for medium-high notes, and tenor clef is used for medium-low notes.

title: 音符、譜號與加線的記寫
text: 譜號的畫法
en: Drawing Clefs

title: 音符、譜號與加線的記寫
text: 高音譜號可以分成三個簡單步驟來畫，如例 9：[2]
en: One can draw a treble clef in three simple steps, as demonstrated in Example 9:[2]

title: 音符、譜號與加線的記寫
text: 例 9。分三步畫高音譜號。
en: Example 9. Drawing a treble clef in three steps.

title: 音符、譜號與加線的記寫
text: 畫一條略微傾斜的直線，上、下都稍微超出五線譜。畫一個半圓，在由上往下第二條線的位置與斜直線相交。繞著由下往上第二條線畫圈，盡量讓圈保持在最下方兩個間的範圍內。
en: Draw a slanted vertical line that extends slightly above and below the staff. Draw a half circle that intersects with your slanted line at the second staff line from the top. Circle around the second staff line from the bottom. Try to keep your circle within the bottom two spaces.

title: 音符、譜號與加線的記寫
text: 同樣地，低音譜號也可以分成三個步驟來畫，如例 10：
en: Likewise, one can also draw a bass clef in three steps, as shown in Example 10:

title: 音符、譜號與加線的記寫
text: 例 10。分三步畫低音譜號。
en: Example 10. Drawing a bass clef in three steps.

title: 音符、譜號與加線的記寫
text: 在由上往下第二條線上畫一個點。畫一個反向的 C，末端停在最下方的間內；注意 C 的上方不要超出五線譜。在反向 C 的右側畫兩個點，分別置於最上方兩個間的中央。
en: Draw a dot on the second staff line from the top. Draw a backward C that ends in the bottom space of the staff, making sure that the top part of the C does not extend above the staff. Place two dots to the right of the backward C, centered respectively in the top two spaces of the staff.

title: 音符、譜號與加線的記寫
text: 中音譜號可以分成四個步驟來畫，如例 11：
en: One can draw an alto clef in four steps, as Example 11 shows:

title: 音符、譜號與加線的記寫
text: 例 11。分四步畫中音譜號。
en: Example 11. Drawing an alto clef in four steps.

title: 音符、譜號與加線的記寫
text: 畫一條跨越五線譜高度的粗直線。在旁邊再畫一條較細的直線。畫兩個反向的 C：第一個占略少於五線譜上半部的範圍，第二個占略少於下半部的範圍。以一個落在第三線上的尖角，連接兩個反向的 C。
en: Draw a thick vertical line that spans the staff. Draw a thinner vertical line next to it. Draw two backward Cs, the first taking up slightly less than the top half of the staff and the second taking up slightly less than the bottom half of the staff. Connect these backward Cs with a point that rests on the middle line of the staff.

title: 音符、譜號與加線的記寫
text: 如例 12所示，次中音譜號的畫法與中音譜號相同，只是整體上移一條線。步驟 1、2 的直線從由下往上第二條線開始，向上稍微超出五線譜。第一個反向的 C 稍微超出五線譜的上半部；第二個占略少於中間兩個間的範圍。連接兩者的尖角，落在由上往下第二條線上。
en: As seen in Example 12, the tenor clef is drawn the same way as the alto clef, just shifted up one line of the staff higher. The vertical lines in steps 1 and 2 begin on the second staff line from the bottom and extend slightly above the staff. The first backward C extends slightly above the top half of the staff, and the second takes up slightly less than the middle two spaces of the staff. The point connecting them rests on the second staff line from the top.

title: 音符、譜號與加線的記寫
text: 例 12。分四步畫次中音譜號。
en: Example 12. Drawing a tenor clef in four steps.

title: 音符、譜號與加線的記寫
text: 音樂家手寫中音或次中音譜號時，有時會以字母「K」作為簡寫，如例 13：
en: Sometimes when musicians draw the alto or tenor clef, they do so by writing the letter “K” as a form of shorthand. Example 13 shows this:

title: 音符、譜號與加線的記寫
text: 例 13。用字母「K」簡寫中音與次中音譜號。
en: Example 13. Using the letter “K” to draw the alto and tenor clefs.

title: 音符、譜號與加線的記寫
text: 加線的記寫
en: Writing Ledger Lines

title: 音符、譜號與加線的記寫
text: 音太高或太低，無法寫在五線譜內時，就畫上稱為加線的小短線，延伸五線譜。例 14呈現五線譜上方與下方的加線：
en: When notes are too high or low to be written on a staff, small lines called ledger lines are drawn to extend the staff. Example 14 shows ledger lines written above and below a staff:

title: 音符、譜號與加線的記寫
text: 例 14。低音譜號五線譜上、下方的加線。
en: Example 14. Ledger lines, both above and below a staff with a bass clef.

title: 音符、譜號與加線的記寫
text: 例 15呈現寫在五線譜上、下方加線上的音符，包含符幹及符槓。
en: Example 15 shows notes (with stems and beams) drawn on ledger lines, above and below a staff.

title: 音符、譜號與加線的記寫
text: 例 15。高音譜號五線譜上、下方加線上的音符，包含符幹與符槓。
en: Example 15. Notes (with stems and beams) on ledger lines, above and below a staff with a treble clef.

title: 音符、譜號與加線的記寫
text: 寫加線時，注意不要在所寫音符更上方或更下方，多畫一條不需要的加線。例 16先示範正確記法，再示範音符上、下方多畫加線的錯誤記法：[3]
en: When writing ledger lines, be sure not to put in an extra ledger line above or below the note you are writing. Example 16 first shows the correct way of writing notes on ledger lines, followed by the incorrect way, with extra ledger lines above and below the notes:[3]

title: 音符、譜號與加線的記寫
text: 例 16。正確與錯誤的加線記法。
en: Example 16. Correct and incorrect notation of ledger lines.

title: 音符、譜號與加線的記寫
text: 依 Joseph Straus，《音樂要素》（Elements of Music，紐約：Oxford University Press，2022），第 2 頁製作。↵關於譜號畫法的另一種說明，見 Mark McGrain，《記譜法》（Music Notation，波士頓：Berklee Press，1986），第 13–15 頁。↵依 Straus，《音樂要素》（Elements），第 3 頁製作。↵

title: 譜號的判讀
text: 重點整理西方記譜法以 A、B、C、D、E、F、G 這七個字母標示音高，並循環重複使用。不同譜號能讓不同音域的樂譜更容易閱讀。每種譜號都決定五線譜各線與各間如何對應音高。
en: Key Takeaways Pitch in Western musical notation is designated by the letters A, B, C, D, E, F, and G, which repeat in a loop. Different clefs make reading different ranges easier. Each clef indicates how the lines and spaces of the staff correspond to pitch.

title: 譜號的判讀
text: 西方記譜法用拉丁字母表的前七個字母 A、B、C、D、E、F、G 標示音高。到了 G 之後，字母音名便循環重複：A、B、C、D、E、F、G、A、B、C、D、E、F、G、A、B、C……。這種循環來自當今音樂家與樂理學者接受的八度等價概念，也就是認為相隔一個八度的音應使用相同字母音名。下一章〈鍵盤與大譜表〉將進一步說明。
en: In Western musical notation, pitches are designated by the first seven letters of the Latin alphabet: A, B, C, D, E, F, and G. After G these letter names repeat in a loop: A, B, C, D, E, F, G, A, B, C, D, E, F, G, A, B, C, etc. This loop of letter names exists because musicians and music theorists today accept what is called octave equivalence, or the assumption that pitches separated by an octave should have the same letter name. More information about this concept can be found in the next chapter, The Keyboard and the Grand Staff.

title: 譜號的判讀
text: 這項假定會隨所處環境而異。例如，有些古希臘樂理學者不接受八度等價，而以超過七個希臘字母為音高命名。[1]
en: This assumption varies with milieu. For example, some ancient Greek music theorists did not accept octave equivalence. These theorists used more than seven letters of the Greek alphabet to name pitches.[1]

title: 譜號的判讀
text: 譜號與音域
en: Clefs and Ranges

title: 譜號的判讀
text: 〈音符、譜號與加線的記寫〉介紹了高音、低音、中音與次中音四種譜號。譜號決定五線譜各線與各間所對應的音高。下一章〈鍵盤與大譜表〉將說明，多種譜號如何讓不同音域的樂譜更容易閱讀。高音譜號通常用於較高的聲音與樂器，例如長笛、小提琴、小號或女高音；低音譜號通常用於較低的聲音與樂器，例如低音管、大提琴、長號或男低音。中音譜號主要用於音域居中的中提琴。次中音譜號則有時用在大提琴、低音管與長號樂譜中，雖然這些樂器主要使用的仍是低音譜號。
en: The Notation of Notes, Clefs, and Ledger Lines chapter introduced four clefs: treble, bass, alto, and tenor. A clef indicates which pitches are assigned to the lines and spaces on a staff. In the next chapter, The Keyboard and the Grand Staff, we will see that having multiple clefs makes reading different ranges easier. The treble clef is typically used for higher voices and instruments, such as a flute, violin, trumpet, or soprano voice. The bass clef is usually utilized for lower voices and instruments, such as a bassoon, cello, trombone, or bass voice. The alto clef is primarily used for the viola, a mid-ranged instrument, while the tenor clef is sometimes employed in cello, bassoon, and trombone music (although the principal clef used for these instruments is the bass clef).

title: 譜號的判讀
text: 每種譜號都決定各線與各間如何對應音高。記熟各譜號的音名排列，有助於閱讀不同聲種與樂器的樂譜。
en: Each clef indicates how the lines and spaces of the staff correspond to pitch. Memorizing the patterns for each clef will help you read music written for different voices and instruments.

title: 譜號的判讀
text: 高音譜號的判讀
en: Reading Treble Clef

title: 譜號的判讀
text: 高音譜號是目前最常用的譜號之一。例 1顯示使用高音譜號時，五條線的字母音名。一個可用的記憶口訣是「Every Good Bird Does Fly」（每隻好鳥都會飛），各字首依序為 E、G、B、D、F。如例 1所示，高音譜號環繞著 G 所在的線，也就是由下往上第二條線，因此有時也稱為「G 譜號」。
en: The treble clef is one of the most commonly used clefs today. Example 1 shows the letter names used for the lines of a staff when a treble clef is employed. One mnemonic device that may help you remember this order of letter names is “Every Good Bird Does Fly” (E, G, B, D, F). As seen in Example 1, the treble clef wraps around the G line (the second line from the bottom). For this reason, it is sometimes called the “G clef.”

title: 譜號的判讀
text: 例 1。高音譜號各線的字母音名。
en: Example 1. The letter names for the lines with a treble clef.

title: 譜號的判讀
text: 例 2顯示高音譜號各間的字母音名。記住它們依序拼成英文單字「face」（臉），就更容易辨識這四個間。
en: Example 2 shows the letter names used for the spaces of a staff with a treble clef. Remembering that these letter names spell the word “face” may make identifying these spaces easier.

title: 譜號的判讀
text: 例 2。高音譜號各間的字母音名。
en: Example 2. The letter names for the spaces with a treble clef.

title: 譜號的判讀
text: 例 3是一個八度移位高音譜號。請注意譜號下方的小「8」：
en: Example 3 shows an octave treble clef. Notice the small “8” at the bottom of the clef:

title: 譜號的判讀
text: 例 3。下方標有「8」的八度移位高音譜號。
en: Example 3. An octave treble clef with an “8” at the bottom of the clef.

title: 譜號的判讀
text: 高音譜號下方標「8」，表示實際演唱或演奏的音應比記譜低一個八度。男高音、吉他與貝斯的樂譜經常使用這種八度移位高音譜號。雙高音譜號也表示實際音比記譜低一個八度，但較少見。例 4就是雙高音譜號：
en: An octave treble clef with an “8” at the bottom of the clef indicates that notes should be sung or played an octave lower than written. Music for tenor vocalists, guitarists, and bassists often uses the octave treble clef. A double treble clef also indicates that notes should be sung or played an octave lower than written, but it is much less common. Example 4 shows a double treble clef:

title: 譜號的判讀
text: 例 4。雙高音譜號。
en: Example 4. A double treble clef.

title: 譜號的判讀
text: 短笛或長笛樂譜有時會使用上方標「8」的八度移位高音譜號，表示實際演奏的音比記譜高一個八度。例 5顯示這種譜號：
en: Sometimes music for piccolo or flute will use an octave treble clef with an “8” at the top of the clef. This indicates that notes should be played an octave higher than written. Example 5 shows this clef:

title: 譜號的判讀
text: 例 5。上方標有「8」的八度移位高音譜號。
en: Example 5. An octave treble clef with an “8” at the top of the clef.

title: 譜號的判讀
text: 不過，短笛樂譜無論採一般高音譜號，還是八度移位高音譜號，都一律按比記譜高一個八度的實際音理解。
en: However, piccolo music is always assumed to sound an octave higher than written, regardless of which clef is used–a regular treble clef or an octave treble clef.

title: 譜號的判讀
text: 低音譜號的判讀
en: Reading Bass Clef

title: 譜號的判讀
text: 另一種今日最常用的譜號是低音譜號。例 6顯示使用低音譜號時，五條線的字母音名。可以用「Good Bikes Don’t Fall Apart」（好腳踏車不會散架）作為口訣，各字首依序為 G、B、D、F、A。低音譜號有時也稱為「F 譜號」；如例 6所示，它的起始圓點位在 F 所在的線，也就是由上往下第二條線。
en: The other most commonly used clef today is the bass clef. Example 6 shows the letter names used for the lines of a staff when a bass clef is employed. A mnemonic device for this order of letter names is “Good Bikes Don’t Fall Apart” (G, B, D, F, A). The bass clef is sometimes called the “F clef”; as seen in Example 6, the dot of the bass clef begins on the F line (the second line from the top).

title: 譜號的判讀
text: 例 6。低音譜號各線的字母音名。
en: Example 6. The letter names for the lines with a bass clef.

title: 譜號的判讀
text: 例 7顯示低音譜號各間的字母音名。「All Cows Eat Grass」（所有牛都吃草）這句口訣的字首依序為 A、C、E、G，可幫助你辨識這四個間。
en: Example 7 shows the letter names used for the spaces of a staff with a bass clef. The mnemonic device “All Cows Eat Grass” (A, C, E, G) may make identifying these spaces easier.

title: 譜號的判讀
text: 例 7。低音譜號各間的字母音名。
en: Example 7. The letter names for the spaces with a bass clef.

title: 譜號的判讀
text: 中音譜號的判讀
en: Reading Alto Clef

title: 譜號的判讀
text: 例 8顯示較少使用的中音譜號各線的字母音名。可用「Fat Alley Cats Eat Garbage」（巷子裡的胖貓吃垃圾）記憶，各字首依序是 F、A、C、E、G。如例 8所示，中音譜號中央的凹入處對準 C 所在的第三線，因此有時也稱為「C 譜號」。
en: Example 8 shows the letter names used for the lines of the staff with the alto clef, which is less commonly used today. The mnemonic device “Fat Alley Cats Eat Garbage” (F, A, C, E, G) may help you remember this order of letter names. As seen in Example 8, the center of the alto clef is indented around the C line (the middle line). For this reason it is sometimes called a “C clef.”

title: 譜號的判讀
text: 例 8。中音譜號各線的字母音名。
en: Example 8. The letter names for the lines with an alto clef.

title: 譜號的判讀
text: 例 9顯示中音譜號各間的字母音名。可用「Grand Boats Drift Flamboyantly」（大船華麗地漂流）記憶，各字首依序是 G、B、D、F。
en: Example 9 shows the letter names used for the spaces of a staff with an alto clef, which can be remembered with the mnemonic device “Grand Boats Drift Flamboyantly” (G, B, D, F).

title: 譜號的判讀
text: 例 9。中音譜號各間的字母音名。
en: Example 9. The letter names for the spaces with an alto clef.

title: 譜號的判讀
text: 次中音譜號的判讀
en: Reading Tenor Clef

title: 譜號的判讀
text: 次中音譜號也是較少使用的譜號，有時同樣稱為「C 譜號」，但其中央凹入處對準由上往下第二條線。例 10顯示次中音譜號各線的字母音名，可用「Dodges, Fords, and Chevrolets Everywhere」（到處都是 Dodge、Ford 與 Chevrolet 汽車）記憶，各字首依序為 D、F、A、C、E：
en: The tenor clef, another less commonly used clef, is also sometimes called a “C clef,” but the center of the clef is indented around the second line from the top. Example 10 shows the letter names used for the lines of a staff when a tenor clef is employed, which can be remembered with the mnemonic device “Dodges, Fords, and Chevrolets Everywhere” (D, F, A, C, E):

title: 譜號的判讀
text: 例 10。次中音譜號各線的字母音名。
en: Example 10. The letter names for the lines with a tenor clef.

title: 譜號的判讀
text: 例 11顯示次中音譜號各間的字母音名。可用「Elvis’s Guitar Broke Down」（Elvis 的吉他壞了）記憶，各字首依序為 E、G、B、D。
en: Example 11 shows the letter names used for the spaces of a staff with a tenor clef. The mnemonic device “Elvis’s Guitar Broke Down” (E, G, B, D) may make identifying these spaces easier.

title: 譜號的判讀
text: 例 11。次中音譜號各間的字母音名。
en: Example 11. The letter names for the spaces with a tenor clef.

title: 譜號的判讀
text: 你可以利用下列練習辨識各種譜號：
en: You can practice identifying clefs in the following exercise:

title: 譜號的判讀
text: 練習辨識譜號
en: Practice Identifying Clefs (requires internet)

title: 譜號的判讀
text: 其他 C 譜號
en: Other C Clefs

title: 譜號的判讀
text: 女高音譜號、女中音譜號與男中音譜號也都屬於 C 譜號。它們現在很少使用，但在文藝復興時期（1400–1600）相當常見；關於風格時期，另見〈其他記譜要素〉。各譜號中央的凹入處都對準 C 所在的線。例 12顯示這幾種譜號各線的字母音名：
en: The soprano clef, mezzo-soprano clef, and baritone clef are also C clefs. These clefs are much less frequently used today, but they were common in the Renaissance period (1400–1600) (see Other Aspects of Notation for more information on stylistic periods). The center of each of these clefs is indented around the C line. Example 12 shows the letter names used for the lines of a staff with each of these clefs:

title: 譜號的判讀
text: 例 12。女高音、女中音與男中音譜號各線的字母音名。
en: Example 12. The letter names for the lines with a soprano, mezzo-soprano, and baritone clef.

title: 譜號的判讀
text: 加線
en: Ledger Lines

title: 譜號的判讀
text: 音太高或太低，無法寫在五線譜內時，會用小短線延伸五線譜。你也許還記得，上一章稱這些額外的線為加線。任何譜號的五線譜都能使用加線。例 13顯示高音譜號五線譜上方的加線：
en: When notes are too high or low to be written on a staff, small lines are drawn to extend the staff. You may recall from the previous chapter that these extra lines are called ledger lines. Ledger lines can be used to extend a staff with any clef. Example 13 shows ledger lines above a staff with a treble clef:

title: 譜號的判讀
text: 例 13。加線使高音譜號的五線譜向上延伸。
en: Example 13. Ledger lines extend a staff upwards with a treble clef.

title: 譜號的判讀
text: 請注意，五線譜上方的每一條加線與每一個間，都依序對應字母音名，就像五線譜不斷向上延伸。五線譜下方的加線也一樣，如例 14所示：
en: Notice that each space and line above the staff gets a letter name with ledger lines, as if the staff were simply continuing upwards. The same is true for ledger lines below a staff, as shown in Example 14:

title: 譜號的判讀
text: 例 14。加線使低音譜號的五線譜向下延伸。
en: Example 14. Ledger lines extend a staff downwards with a bass clef.

title: 譜號的判讀
text: 請注意，五線譜下方的每一條加線與每一個間，都依序對應字母音名，就像五線譜不斷向下延伸。
en: Notice that each space and line below the staff gets a letter name with ledger lines, as if the staff were simply continuing downwards.

title: 譜號的判讀
text: 中性譜號
en: Neutral Clef

title: 譜號的判讀
text: 中性譜號有時稱為「打擊樂譜號」，因為它經常用於沒有確定音高的打擊樂器。例 15顯示五線譜上的中性譜號：
en: A neutral clef is sometimes called a “percussion clef” because it is often used for percussion instruments with indefinite pitch. Example 15 shows a neutral clef on a staff:

title: 譜號的判讀
text: 例 15。五線譜上的中性譜號。
en: Example 15. A neutral clef on the staff.

title: 譜號的判讀
text: 使用打擊樂譜號時，各線與各間不表示字母音名，而可能表示不同樂器。中性譜號有時也用在單線譜上，如例 16：
en: In percussion clef, the lines and spaces of the staff do not represent letter names, but instead may represent different instruments. Neutral clefs are sometimes used on a single-line staff, as seen in Example 16:

title: 譜號的判讀
text: 例 16。單線譜上的中性譜號。
en: Example 16. A neutral clef on a single-line staff.

title: 譜號的判讀
text: Thomas Mathiesen 博士於 2025 年 6 月 17 日寄給作者的電子郵件中寫道：「沒有任何希臘音樂思想家……會把任何八度視為等價。」↵
en: Dr. Thomas Mathiesen in an email to the author (June 17, 2025) wrote: "no Greek musical thinker...would have considered any octaves to be equivalent." ↵

title: 鍵盤與大譜表
text: 重點整理彈鋼琴能讓你透過身體動作與感覺接觸音樂，幫助學習樂理。鋼琴鍵盤上，黑鍵以兩個一組、三個一組的方式排列，這個模式在七個八度間反覆出現。兩個一組的黑鍵緊鄰左側白鍵是 C；三個一組的黑鍵緊鄰左側白鍵是 F。鋼琴演奏者，也就是鋼琴家，使用大譜表讀譜。中央 C位於大譜表兩行五線譜之間的加線上。在鋼琴鍵盤上計算音程時，第一個音一律從「一」開始算。
en: Key Takeaways Playing the piano will help you in your music theoretical studies by allowing you to engage kinesthetically with music. A pattern of black keys grouped into twos and threes repeats on the piano keyboard for seven octaves. The white note C is to the immediate left of the two-note black key pattern, while the white note F is to the immediate left of the three-note black key pattern. Piano players, also called pianists, read music on the grand staff. Middle C is the note that appears on the line between the two staves in a grand staff. When counting intervals on a piano keyboard, always count the first note as “one.”

title: 鍵盤與大譜表
text: 許多學生發現，透過身體動作與感覺參與音樂，樂理就更容易學習。換句話說，親自演奏鋼琴等樂器、實際發出聲音，有助於你在心中更清楚地看見並內在聽想正在記寫或研究的音樂。這能讓學生更快理解並「感覺到」不同音高之間的關係。
en: Many students find studying music theory easier when they engage with music kinesthetically. In other words, physically creating sounds by playing a musical instrument (such as the piano) helps you to better visualize and audiate the music you are writing down or studying. This allows students to understand and “feel” the relationship between different pitches more quickly.

title: 鍵盤與大譜表
text: 鋼琴鍵盤
en: The Piano Keyboard

title: 鍵盤與大譜表
text: 學著在鋼琴上彈奏音符，是透過身體動作參與音樂的一種簡單方法。學校也許有可使用的傳統鋼琴或電子鍵盤；如果願意，你也可以購買價格不高的電子鍵盤。另一種選擇是下載能在手機上彈奏的免費鋼琴應用程式，例如 Tiny Piano。
en: Learning to play notes on the piano is one easy way to engage with music kinesthetically. You may find access to a piano keyboard (acoustic or electronic) at your school. You may also purchase an inexpensive electronic keyboard if you like. Another option is to download a free piano app that you can play on your phone, such as Tiny Piano.

title: 鍵盤與大譜表

en: In Example 1, notice that the keyboard has both white keys and black keys. The black keys are grouped into sets of either three or two. In Example 2, notice that the sets of three and two black keys alternate throughout the entire length of a piano keyboard, repeating the pattern for each octave.

title: 鍵盤與大譜表
text: 坐在鋼琴前時，應坐直，頭部保持在肩膀上方，肩膀自然放低。手肘與身體之間留出舒適距離，手指維持拱形，就像要從書架上抽出一本書。膝蓋與手腕保持靈活，不要僵硬；除非使用踏板，雙腳應平放地面。
en: When you sit at the piano, it is important to sit up straight, keeping your head over your shoulders, which should be kept down. Your elbows should be a comfortable distance from your body, and your fingers should remain arched (as if you were pulling a library book off of a shelf). Keep your knees and wrists flexible (not stiff), and keep your feet flat on the ground unless you are using the pedals.

text: 八度等價與鋼琴白鍵的字母音名
en: Octave Equivalence and White Key Letter Names on the Piano Keyboard

title: 鍵盤與大譜表
text: 例 4在鋼琴鍵盤上標出白鍵的字母音名。同樣的音名會出現在不同琴鍵上。如上一章所述，西方記譜法以 A、B、C、D、E、F、G 七個字母標示音高，並循環重複。由於西方體系採用八度等價原則，相隔一個八度的音具有相同字母音名。
en: Example 4 shows a piano keyboard with the letter names of the white key pitches labeled. The same letter names appear on different keys of the keyboard. As discussed in the previous chapter, pitches in Western musical notation are designated by the letters A, B, C, D, E, F, and G, repeating in a loop. Because of the principle of octave equivalence in the Western system, pitches separated by an octave have the same letter name.

title: 鍵盤與大譜表
text: 例 4。標有字母音名的白鍵。
en: Example 4. The letter names of the white key pitches are labeled.

en: On the piano keyboard, when the black keys appear as a set of two, the note to their immediate left is C. With a set of three black keys, the note to their immediate left is F.

title: 鍵盤與大譜表
text: 大譜表
en: The Grand Staff

title: 鍵盤與大譜表
text: 鋼琴譜通常以大譜表同時使用高音與低音譜號，如例 5。大譜表的上方是高音譜號五線譜，下方是低音譜號五線譜，左側用一條直線與花括號連接。通常，鋼琴演奏者用左手彈較低的音，也就是低音譜號部分；右手彈較高的音，也就是高音譜號部分。
en: Music for the piano is typically written in both the treble and bass clefs on a grand staff, as shown in Example 5. To make a grand staff, a staff with a treble clef is placed above a staff with a bass clef. The two staves are connected on the left side with a line and a brace. Typically, the pianist plays the lower notes (in the bass clef) with their left hand and the higher notes (in the treble clef) with their right hand.

title: 鍵盤與大譜表
text: 例 5。以直線及花括號連接的大譜表。
en: Example 5. A grand staff is connected with a line and a brace.

title: 鍵盤與大譜表
text: 例 6標出大譜表各線與各間的字母音名。可以看到，高音與低音譜號的線間音名，與上一章〈譜號的判讀〉所述相同。
en: Example 6 shows the lines and spaces on the grand staff labeled with letter names. As you can see, the letter names of the lines and spaces of the treble and bass clefs match what was discussed in the prior chapter (Reading Clefs).

title: 鍵盤與大譜表
text: 例 6。以音名標示各線與各間的大譜表。
en: Example 6. A grand staff with the lines and spaces labeled with pitch names.

title: 鍵盤與大譜表
text: 接著仔細看看，高音譜號五線譜下方，以及低音譜號五線譜上方，可能出現哪些加線音符。例 7標出其中幾個音的字母音名。每一組上下相對的音符雖然寫在不同譜號中，實際音高卻相同。符幹朝上的音符屬於高音譜號五線譜，符幹朝下的則屬於低音譜號五線譜。
en: Let’s take a closer look at the ledger-line notes that might appear below the treble staff and above the bass clef staff. Example 7 shows some of these notes, labeled with letter names. Each vertical pair of notes is the same pitch, even though the notes are notated in two different clefs. (The notes with upward-pointing stems belong to the treble clef staff, while the notes with downward-pointing stems belong to the bass clef staff.)

title: 鍵盤與大譜表
text: 例 7。高音譜號五線譜下方與低音譜號五線譜上方的音高，並附字母音名。
en: Example 7. Pitches below the treble clef staff and above the bass clef staff, labeled with letter names.

title: 鍵盤與大譜表
text: 例 8將例 7的兩行五線譜在垂直方向拉近，呈現大譜表上下兩行之間若沒有那麼大間距，這些音符會如何排列。例 8的字母音名與例 7相同。
en: Example 8 shows the staves of Example 7 vertically condensed—how these notes would appear if there were not so much space in between the treble clef and bass clef staves of a grand staff. The letter names are the same in Example 8 as they were in Example 7.

title: 鍵盤與大譜表
text: 例 8。將例 7的兩行五線譜在垂直方向拉近，並把每對音符合為一個符頭，保留兩支符幹。
en: Example 8. The staves of Example 7 have been vertically condensed and the two notes combined into one (with two stems).

title: 鍵盤與大譜表
text: 例 9是兩行距離拉近的大譜表，C 音以方框圈出。框內的 C 稱為中央 C，因為在例 9這種上下靠近的大譜表中，它位於高音與低音譜號兩行之間的中央。此外，中央 C 在鋼琴鍵盤上也大約位於中間，通常在品牌名稱下方。
en: Example 9 shows a vertically condensed grand staff with a box around the note C. This boxed C is called middle C, so named because in the vertically condensed grand staff shown in Example 9, it appears in the middle of the treble and bass clef staves. Additionally, middle C is the note that appears to be around the middle of a piano keyboard, usually underneath the brand name.

title: 鍵盤與大譜表
text: 例 9。兩行距離拉近的大譜表，以方框圈出 C 音。
en: Example 9. The note C is boxed in a vertically condensed grand staff.

title: 鍵盤與大譜表
text: 例 10把例 9的上下間距恢復成一般大小，中央 C 仍以方框圈出。雖然這個音現在分別出現在高音與低音譜號的五線譜上，聽起來仍是同一音高。
en: Example 10 shows Example 9 vertically expanded to its regular spacing, with middle C still boxed. Though it now appears in both the treble clef and bass clef staves, this note would still sound as the same pitch.

title: 鍵盤與大譜表
text: 例 10。將例 9的上下間距拉開。
en: Example 10. A vertically expanded Example 9.

title: 鍵盤與大譜表
text: 音程度數（音程大小）
en: Generic Intervals (Interval Size)

title: 鍵盤與大譜表
text: 學習樂理時，經常需要測量或描述鋼琴鍵盤或五線譜上兩音之間的距離。在鍵盤或譜上數出的這個「音數」，稱為音程度數（generic interval）。計算時，第一個音必須算作一，而不是零。例 11在高音譜號五線譜上標出 F 與 C 兩個音。若逐一數過例 11中兩音之間的線與間，你可能會想這樣算：F 到 G 是一、G 到 A 是二、A 到 B 是三、B 到 C 是四；但這樣不正確。正確做法是先把 F 算作一，接著到 G 是二、到 A 是三、到 B 是四、到 C 是五。因此，F 到 C 包含五個音，而不是四個。音樂家與樂理學者會稱這兩音的距離為「五度」，此處只計度數，尚不區分音程性質。
en: Often in music theory, you will want to measure or describe the distance between notes—either on a piano keyboard or on a staff. This “count” of notes on a piano keyboard or staff is called a generic interval. When counting generic intervals, it is important to know that when you count the first note, it should be counted as one and not zero. Example 11 shows two notes, an F and a C, on a staff with a treble clef. If you count the notes F to C in Example 11 (by counting each line and space between the two notes), you may be tempted to do this: F to G is one, G to A is two, A to B is three, and B to C is four. However, this would be incorrect. Instead, you need to count F as one, F to G as two, G to A as three, A to B as four, and B to C as five. Therefore, we would say that F and C are five notes apart, not four. Music theorists and musicians would call the distance between these two notes a “generic fifth.”

title: 半音、全音與變音記號
text: 重點整理在鋼琴上，比某鍵高一個半音的，是緊鄰其右側的琴鍵；低一個半音的，則是緊鄰左側的琴鍵。一個全音等於兩個半音。向上全音是在右側移動兩個相鄰琴鍵的位置；向下全音則往左移動兩個相鄰琴鍵的位置。變音記號會改變音高。升記號使音升高半音，降記號使音降低半音；還原記號取消先前變音記號的作用。重升記號使音升高全音，重降記號使音降低全音。變音記號寫在音符左側，並對準音符所在的線或間。音名拼寫不同、聽起來卻相同的音，具有等音等價關係。
en: Key Takeaways A half step above a key on the piano is the key to its immediate right, while a half step below a key on the piano is the key to its immediate left. A whole step is two half steps. A whole step above is two keys to its right, while a whole step below is two keys to its left. An accidental changes the pitch of a note. A sharp raises a note by a half step, while a flat lowers a note by a half step. A natural cancels a previous accidental. A double sharp raises a note by a whole step, while a double flat lowers a note by a whole step. Be sure to write accidentals to the left of a note, directly across the line or space on which a note appears. Notes have enharmonic equivalence when they are spelled differently but sound the same.

title: 半音、全音與變音記號
text: 上一章〈鍵盤與大譜表〉討論了鋼琴白鍵的字母音名，並指出黑鍵以兩個一組、三個一組的方式交替排列。不過，在介紹黑鍵音名之前，必須先認識半音與全音。
en: In the last chapter, The Keyboard and the Grand Staff, we discussed the letter names of the white keys on the piano keyboard and noted that the black keys are grouped into alternating sets of two or three. Before we discuss the names of the black keys, however, we must first learn about half steps and whole steps.

title: 半音、全音與變音記號
text: 半音與全音
en: Half Steps and Whole Steps

title: 半音、全音與變音記號
text: 在西方記譜法中，半音被視為最小的音程，也就是兩音間最小的距離。例 1在鋼琴鍵盤上標出白鍵音名及幾組半音。對多數白鍵而言，如例 1所示，高半音是右上方的黑鍵，低半音則是左上方的黑鍵。例如，G 右上方的黑鍵位於 G 與 A「之間」，它比 G 高半音，又比 A 低半音。有兩對白鍵——E／F 及 B／C——中間沒有黑鍵，見例 1，因為 E–F 與 B–C 本身就相距半音。黑鍵分成兩個或三個一組，使演奏者更容易快速看出並摸到它們的位置。
en: A half step is considered to be the smallest interval, or distance between two notes, in Western musical notation. Example 1 shows a piano keyboard with the letter names of the white-key pitches and some half steps labeled. On the piano keyboard (see Example 1), for most of the white-key notes, a half step above that note will be the black key to its upper right, while a half step below it will be the black key to its upper left. For example, the black key to the upper right of G is “in between” the notes G and A; one would say that this black key is a half step above G and a half step below A. Two pairs of white keys—E/F and B/C—do not have black keys in between them (see Example 1). This is because E–F and B–C are both half steps. Having the black keys grouped into sets of either two or three makes it easier for a keyboardist to see and feel them more quickly.

title: 半音、全音與變音記號

en: Example 1. A piano keyboard with letter names onthe white keys; some half steps are labeled.

title: 半音、全音與變音記號
text: 一個全音等於兩個半音。例 2標出白鍵音名，並以括線標示幾組全音。中間隔著一個黑鍵的兩個白鍵——A 與 B、C 與 D、D 與 E、F 與 G、G 與 A——都相距全音。要找 E 或 B 上方的全音，只要向右逐鍵移動兩次：E 上方全音是 F 右側的黑鍵，B 上方全音是 C 右側的黑鍵。同樣地，要找 C 或 F 下方的全音，就向左逐鍵移動兩次，分別得到 B 左側及 E 左側的黑鍵。從黑鍵出發找全音，也是一樣向右或向左移動兩個相鄰琴鍵的位置。例如，C 右側黑鍵上方的全音，是 D 右側的黑鍵；B 左側黑鍵下方的全音，則是 A 左側的黑鍵。
en: A whole step is the equivalent of two half steps. Example 2 shows a piano keyboard with the letter names of the white key pitches labeled, and some whole steps bracketed. Pairs of white keys with a black key in between them (A and B, C and D, D and E, F and G, and G and A) are a whole step apart. To find a whole step above the notes E or B, simply count two keys to the right: a whole step above E is the black key to the right of the note F, while a whole step above B is the black key to the right of the note C. Likewise, count two keys to the left to find a whole step below the notes C or F: the black keys to the left of the notes B and E, respectively. To find a whole step from a black key you will want to count two keys to the right or left. For example, a whole step above the black key to the right of C is the black key to the right of the note D. A whole step below the black key to the left of B is the black key to the left of the note A.

text: 升記號、降記號與還原記號
en: Sharps, Flats, and Naturals

title: 半音、全音與變音記號
text: 變音記號會改變音高。升記號（♯）看起來像傾斜的井字號，使音升高半音。降記號（♭）像略傾斜的小寫 b，使音降低半音。還原記號（♮）像傾斜的方框，左上角與右下角各伸出一條線；它會取消先前的升記號或降記號等變音記號。升、降、還原是最常見的三種變音記號。
en: An accidental changes the pitch of a note. A sharp (♯) looks like a tilted hashtag, and it raises a note by a half step. A flat (♭) looks like a slanted lowercase “b,” and it lowers a note by a half step. A natural (♮) looks like a tilted box with a line sticking out of the top left and bottom right corners, and it cancels a previous accidental such as a sharp or flat. Sharps, flats, and naturals are the three most common accidentals.

title: 半音、全音與變音記號
text: 重升記號通常寫作 𝄪，較少寫成 ♯♯，使音升高兩個半音，也就是一個全音。重降記號（𝄫）則使音降低兩個半音，也就是一個全音。不論符幹朝哪個方向，變音記號一律寫在音符左側，並正對音符所在的線或間。
en: A double sharp (usually notated as 𝄪 or less commonly as ♯♯) raises a note by two half steps (i.e., a whole step). A double flat (𝄫) lowers a note by two half steps (i.e., a whole step). Accidentals are always written to the left of a note, regardless of stem direction. An accidental should be written directly across the line or space on which a note appears.

title: 半音、全音與變音記號
text: 例 6標出鋼琴黑鍵的字母音名。比某白鍵高半音的黑鍵，沿用該白鍵的音名並加上「sharp」（升）。例如，C 右側的黑鍵稱為 C-sharp，記作 C♯。比某白鍵低半音的黑鍵，沿用該白鍵的音名並加上「flat」（降）。例如，D 左側的黑鍵稱為 D-flat，記作 D♭。
en: Example 6 shows a piano keyboard with the letter names of the black keys labeled. Black keys that are a half step above a white key take the name of the white key and add the word “sharp.” For example, the black key to the right of the note C is called “C-sharp” and is written as C♯. Black keys that are a half step below a white key take the name of the white key and add the word “flat.” For example, the black key to the left of the note D is called “D-flat” and is written as D♭.

title: 半音、全音與變音記號
text: 例 6。標有黑鍵音名的鋼琴鍵盤。
en: Example 6. A piano keyboard with the letter names of theblack keys labeled.

title: 半音、全音與變音記號
text: F 也可稱為 E♯，E 也可稱為 F♭；C 也可稱為 B♯，B 也可稱為 C♭。例 7另顯示部分重升與重降記號。重升使音高上移兩個半音，例如 D𝄪 就是 E，E𝄪 就是 F♯，也就是 G♭。重降使音高下移兩個半音，例如 A𝄫 就是 G，C𝄫 就是 B♭，也就是 A♯。
en: F is also known as E♯, and E is also known as F♭. C is also known as B♯, and B is also known as C♭. Example 7 also shows some of the double-sharp and double-flat accidentals. A double sharp is two half steps above a note. For example, D𝄪 is also E; E𝄪 is also F♯ (or G♭). A double flat is two half steps below a note. For example, A𝄫 is also G; C𝄫 is also B♭ or A♯.

text: 等音等價
en: Enharmonic equivalence

title: 半音、全音與變音記號
text: 你應該已經注意到，鋼琴每個琴鍵都不只有一個音名。音名拼寫不同、聽起來卻相同的音，具有等音等價關係。例如，例 6與例 7顯示 C♯ 與 D♭ 是等音。例 7也顯示 D 與 C𝄪、E𝄫 等音。換句話說，彈奏 D、C𝄪 或 E𝄫，都會得到相同音高。
en: You will have noticed by now that each key on the piano keyboard has more than one name. Notes have enharmonic equivalence when they are spelled differently but sound the same. For example, you can see that C♯ and D♭ are enharmonically equivalent, as seen in Examples 6 and 7. Example 7 also shows that the note D is enharmonically equivalent with the notes C𝄪 and E𝄫. In other words, playing a D, C𝄪, or E𝄫 will result in the same pitch.

title: 美國標準音高記法（ASPN）
text: 重點整理美國標準音高記法（ASPN）把音名（例如 C）與下標的八度編號（例如 4）結合，用來標示特定頻率的樂音。音高指具有特定頻率的個別樂音（例如 C4）；音級則不限定到這麼具體的程度（例如泛指 C）。ASPN 將 C 到 B 劃為一個八度，各八度由低至高編號，從 0 開始，再依序為 1、2 等。鋼琴鍵盤主要涵蓋 ASPN 編號 1 至 7 的八度，也包含第 0 與第 8 八度的一小部分。中央 C在 ASPN 中記為 C4。記住這個音的標記，可作為判讀其他音高的起點。
en: Key Takeaways American Standard Pitch Notation (ASPN) provides labels for specific musical frequencies by combining a note name (such as C) with a subscript octave designation (such as 4). A pitch is a discrete tone with an individual frequency (e.g. C4), while a pitch class is less specific (e.g., C in general). ASPN differentiates between octaves, from C to B. The octaves are labeled from lowest to highest, beginning with 0 and continuing in ascending numerical order (1, 2, etc.). A piano keyboard primarily uses the ASPN octave designations 1 through 7, although small portions of octaves 0 and 8 are included. Middle C is C4 in ASPN. It is helpful to memorize the ASPN label of this note as a starting point.

title: 美國標準音高記法（ASPN）
text: 美國標準音高記法，以及音高與音級的區別
en: American Standard Pitch Notation and Pitch versus Pitch Class

title: 美國標準音高記法（ASPN）
text: 為了討論特定的音，亦即特定音高，我們將使用美國標準音高記法，簡稱 ASPN。ASPN 將音名（例如 C）與下標的八度編號（例如 4）結合，形成由兩部分組成的標記，例如 C4。這套標記十分實用，因為人類聽覺範圍內所有可能的樂音，從最低音到最高音，都能藉此辨識。
en: In order to discuss specific notes, or pitches, we will use American Standard Pitch Notation, abbreviated ASPN. ASPN designates specific musical pitches by combining a note name (such as C) with a subscript octave designation (such as 4), creating a bipartite label (for example, C4). ASPN labels are very useful, since they can identify every possible musical note within human hearing range, from the lowest pitches to the highest.

title: 美國標準音高記法（ASPN）
text: 〈譜號的判讀〉介紹過八度等價：這個概念說明了為什麼相隔一個或多個八度的音會使用相同的字母音名。樂理學家會區分「音高」與「音級」：前者是具有特定頻率的個別樂音（用 ASPN 表示，例如 C4），後者則不限定到這麼具體的程度（例如泛指 C）。一個音級涵蓋所有八度中具有相同字母音名的音，以及它們的等音。例如，所有的 C 都屬於同一音級，而與 C 等音的 D𝄫 和 B♯ 也屬於 C 音級；詳見〈音高與音級〉。本章將以 ASPN 為特定音高命名。
en: The Reading Clefs chapter introduced octave equivalence, the concept that explains why notes one or more octaves apart have the same letter name. Music theorists distinguish between a pitch, a discrete tone with an individual frequency (e.g. C4 using ASPN), versus a pitch class, which is less specific (e.g., C in general). A pitch class includes all the pitches with the same letter name, in any octave, along with their enharmonic equivalents. For example, all Cs are the same pitch class, and the enharmonically equivalent notes D𝄫 and B♯ are also part of the C pitch class; see Pitch and Pitch Class for more information. In this chapter we are naming specific pitches with ASPN.

title: 美國標準音高記法（ASPN）
text: ASPN 與八度編號
en: ASPN and Octave Designations

title: 美國標準音高記法（ASPN）
text: ASPN 以 C 為起點、B 為終點，區分各個八度。[1]也就是說，每一個新的八度編號都從 C 開始，如例 1所示。編號由低至高，從 0 起依數字順序排列（1、2、3 等）。中央 C的音高記為 C4；記住這一點很有幫助。
en: ASPN differentiates between octaves, beginning with the pitch C and ending with the pitch B.[1] This means that each new octave designation begins on the note C, as seen inExample 1. The octaves are labeled from lowest to highest, beginning with 0 and continuing in numerical order (1, 2, 3, etc.). The pitch middle C is C4, which is useful to memorize.

title: 美國標準音高記法（ASPN）
text: 例 1。ASPN 的八度編號；每個八度都從 C 開始。
en: Example 1. ASPN octave designations; each octave begins with the pitch C.

title: 美國標準音高記法（ASPN）
text: 同一八度內、尚未到達下一個 C 的所有字母音名，都使用相同的八度編號。例如，例 2中的所有音都屬於第 4 八度，因為它們位於 C4至 C5以下的範圍。加在音符上的變音記號不會改變其 ASPN 編號。例如，B♯3與 C4雖然是等音，八度編號卻不同，因為 B♯ 仍算在較低的那個八度之內。
en: All letter names within an octave (below the C of the next octave) receive the same octave designation. For example, all of the notes in Example 2 would be designated in the 4 octave, because they are above C4 but below C5. Accidentals applied to a note do not have an effect on its ASPN number. For example, B♯3 and C4 have different octave numbers despite being enharmonically equivalent, because the B♯ is still considered part of the lower octave.
