title: 七和弦
text: 譜例 7。小調中的七和弦性質。
en: Example 7. Qualities of seventh chords in minor keys.

title: 七和弦
text: 寫出七和弦的音
en: Spelling Seventh Chords

title: 七和弦
text: 依和弦符號建立七和弦時，要先知道根音與性質；轉位會在下一章〈轉位〉討論。七和弦的記寫步驟與三和弦相似，先從大大七和弦開始：
en: To build a seventh chord from a chord symbol, you need to be aware of its root and quality—inversion is discussed in the next chapter, titled Inversion. The steps for spelling a seventh chord are similar to the steps for drawing a triad. Let's start with spelling a major-major seventh chord:

title: 七和弦
text: 在五線譜上寫出根音。在根音上方三度、五度、七度寫出音符，也就是畫出「加長的雪人」。想出或寫出以根音為主音的大調調號。將調號中適用於和弦音的變音記號加上去，形成大三和弦與大七度。
en: Draw the root on the staff. Draw notes a third, fifth, and seventh above the root (i.e., draw an "extra-long" snowperson). Think of (or write down) the major key signature of the triad's root. Write any accidentals from the key signature that apply to the notes in the chord, creating a major triad and a major seventh.

title: 七和弦
text: 若要寫其他性質的七和弦，再依需要加上其他變音記號，改變三音、五音或七音。
en: For any other quality of seventh chord, add additional accidentals to alter the chord's third, fifth, and/or seventh when appropriate.

title: 七和弦
text: 譜例 8以 D 大大七和弦（Dma7）示範：
en: Example 8 shows this process for a D major-major seventh chord (Dma7):

title: 七和弦
text: 譜例 8。四個步驟寫出 D 大大七和弦。
en: Example 8. Spelling a D major-major seventh chord in four steps.

title: 七和弦
text: 在五線譜上寫出根音 D。畫出加長的雪人，加入 F、A、C，分別位於 D 上方三度、五度與七度。回想 D 大調的調號：F♯、C♯ 兩個升記號。在 F、C 左側加上升記號（♯），因為 D 大調使用 F♯ 與 C♯。
en: The note D, the chord's root, is drawn on the staff. An extra-long snowperson is drawn—an F, A, and C, the notes a generic third, fifth, and seventh above the D. The key signature of D major has been recalled. D major has two sharps, F♯ and C♯. Sharps (♯) have been added to the left of the F and the C, because F♯ and C♯ are in the key signature of D major.

title: 七和弦
text: 下一個和弦的性質需要額外的變音記號，因此步驟會多一些。譜例 9示範 A♭ 全減七和弦（A♭o7）的記寫過程：
en: The quality of the next chord will require us to write additional accidentals, so the process has a couple more steps. Example 9 shows the process for an A♭ fully diminished seventh chord (A♭o7):

title: 七和弦
text: 譜例 9。六個步驟寫出 A♭ 全減七和弦。點擊可放大。
en: Example 9. Spelling an A♭ fully diminished seventh chord in six steps. Click to enlarge.

title: 七和弦
text: 先寫 A♭，因為它是和弦根音。畫出加長的雪人，加入 C、E、G，分別位於 A♭ 上方三度、五度與七度。回想 A♭ 大調的調號：B♭、E♭、A♭、D♭ 四個降記號。將 E 改為 E♭，因為它在 A♭ 大調的調號中。此時已寫出大大七和弦，但目標是全減七和弦，因此還要加入 A♭ 大調調號以外的變音記號：將 C 與 E♭ 各降低半音，成為 C♭ 與 E𝄫，把大三和弦改為減三和弦。要將七度從大七度改為減七度，必須降低兩個半音，因此將 G 改為 G𝄫。
en: The note A♭ is written because it is the root of the triad. An extra-long snowperson is drawn: C, E, and G are added because they are a generic third, fifth, and seventh, respectively, above A♭. The key signature of A♭ major is recalled. A♭ major has four flats: B♭, E♭, A♭, and D♭. E♭ is added, because it is in the key signature of A♭ major. We have now followed the process to spell a major-major seventh chord, but we want a fully diminished seventh chord, which means adding accidentals that are not in the key signature of A♭ major: C and E♭ are lowered by a half step to C♭ and E𝄫 to change the triad from major to diminished. To change the chord's seventh from major to diminished, it needs to be lowered by two half steps, from G to G𝄫.

title: 七和弦
text: 對初學者而言，這些步驟是可靠的七和弦記寫方法，但需要花些時間。若能在樂器上練熟各種性質的七和弦，就能逐漸直接掌握和弦音，不必每次都按步驟推算。
en: Following these steps is a reliable way for beginners to spell seventh chords, but it’s a time-consuming process. If you practice playing all of the qualities of seventh chords on an instrument until you are fluent in them, your knowledge of these notes will become more automatic without using this process.

title: 七和弦
text: 七和弦的辨識、重複音與排列
en: Identifying Seventh Chords, Doubling, and Spacing

title: 七和弦
text: 和三和弦一樣，辨識七和弦也要指出根音、性質與轉位。〈轉位〉會討論最後一項，因此本節先以原位和弦為例。
en: Like triads, seventh chords are also identified according to their root, quality, and inversion; inversion is discussed in the Inversion chapter, so the examples here will be in root position.

title: 七和弦
text: 找出並寫下根音。想像以根音為主音的大調調號。判斷並寫下三和弦部分的性質。判斷並寫下七度音程的性質。
en: Identify and write its root. Imagine the major key signature of its root. Identify and write its quality of its triad. Identify and write its quality of its seventh.

title: 七和弦
text: 譜例 10列出一個原位七和弦，供辨識練習。
en: Example 10 shows a seventh chord in root position for the process of identification.

title: 七和弦
text: 譜例 10。供辨識練習的原位七和弦。
en: Example 10. A seventh chord in root position for identification.

title: 七和弦
text: 辨識這個七和弦：
en: To identify this seventh chord:

title: 七和弦
text: 和弦是原位，因此最低音 C♯ 就是根音。C♯ 大調有七個升記號，也就是每個音都升高。E、G 在 C♯ 大調中本應帶升記號，但此處都是自然音，相當於各降低半音，因此三和弦部分是減三和弦。七音 B 在 C♯ 大調中也應帶升記號，但此處是自然音。大七度縮小半音，就變成小七度。減三和弦加小七度，形成半減七和弦，因此這是 C♯ 半減七和弦（C♯∅7）。
en: Because the chord is in root position, the root is the lowest note, C♯. The key of C♯ major has seven sharps (every note is sharp). E and G would be sharp in the key of C♯ major, but we see that both of those notes are natural instead—lowered by a half step—making the triad diminished. The chord's seventh, B, would also be sharp in C♯ major, but it is natural here. When a major seventh is made a half step smaller, it becomes a minor seventh. A diminished triad and a minor seventh form a half-diminished seventh chord; therefore, this is a C♯ half-diminished seventh chord (C♯∅7).

title: 七和弦
text: 七和弦的低音若因重升或重降記號而對應假想調號，可以依〈音程〉章最後一節的方法，用等音關係重新拼寫七和弦。
en: If the bottom note of a seventh chord has an imaginary key signature (because there is a double accidental that applies to it), use enharmonic equivalence to respell the seventh chord, following the process outlined in the last section of the Intervals chapter.

title: 七和弦
text: 和三和弦一樣，七和弦的辨識不受重複音或開放排列影響，即使跨越不同譜號也一樣。譜例 11列出兩個採開放排列、含有重複音的七和弦。和之前一樣，可先在心中或紙上移除重複音，整理成密集排列，再辨識和弦。
en: Like with triads, a seventh chord’s identification is not affected by the doubling of notes or open spacing of notes (even across multiple clefs). Example 11 shows two different seventh chords in open spacing with doublings. Simply imagine or write the notes of seventh chords in closed spacing without any doublings to identify these chords, as we did previously.

text: 這些是《Open Music Theory》使用的和弦符號，但學習時也可能遇到其他寫法。更多說明請參閱〈和弦符號〉。↵
en: These chord symbols reflect those used in Open Music Theory, but you may come across others in your studies. See Chord Symbols for a more thorough explanation of these variations. ↵

title: 轉位
text: 重點整理以三和弦為基礎的和聲，由低音聲部（常簡稱低音）決定轉位。轉位和弦的根音不在低音。三音在低音時是第一轉位，五音在低音時是第二轉位，七音在低音時是第三轉位。本章只使用和弦符號記法。辨識三和弦與七和弦時，要指出根音、性質與轉位。
en: Key Takeaways The bass voice of triadic harmonies, often simply called the "bass," determines inversion. Inverted harmonies do not have the root in the bass. When the third is in the bass, we say the chord is in first inversion, when the fifth is in the bass we say the chord is in second inversion, and when the seventh is in the bass we say the chord is in third inversion. In this chapter, only chord symbols will be used. Triads and seventh chords are identified according to their root, quality, and inversion.

title: 轉位

title: 轉位
text: 音樂家常特別留意三和弦和聲中的低音聲部，簡稱「低音」。它是作品中最低的聲部，不論實際由哪一種樂器或人聲演出。譜例 1將 A 大三和弦的三個不同和弦音分別放在低音，並在五線譜上方標出和弦符號：
en: Musicians often prioritize the note that is in the bass voice of triadic harmonies, simply called the "bass," which is the lowest part (or voice) of a composition, regardless of what instrument or voice type is singing or playing that lowest note. Example 1 shows an A major triad with three different notes in the bass and chord symbols (above the staff):

title: 轉位
text: 譜例 1。A 大三和弦的原位、第一轉位與第二轉位。
en: Example 1. An A major triad in root position, first inversion, and second inversion.

title: 轉位
text: A 大三和弦包含根音 A、三音 C♯ 與五音 E。依三度疊置成「雪人形狀」時，是原位，低音就是根音。根音不在低音的和弦，稱為轉位和弦。如譜例 1所示，三音在低音時是第一轉位，五音在低音時是第二轉位。和弦符號後方的斜線與音名，表示目前的低音。
en: An A major triad consists of three notes, the root (A), the third (C♯), and the fifth (E). When a triad is stacked in thirds (i.e. "snowperson form"), we say the triad is in root position. The bass note in root position is the root. Chords that do not have the root in the bass are said to be inverted. As you can see in Example 1, when the third is in the bass the chord is in first inversion and when the fifth is in the bass we say the chord is in second inversion. Chord symbols followed by a slash and a letter name indicate the pitch which is in the bass.

title: 轉位
text: 務必注意：和弦的低音與根音不是同一回事。A 大三和弦的根音永遠是 A，不論它是原位、第一轉位或第二轉位。但在這幾種位置中，低音依序是 A、C♯、E，如譜例 1所示。
en: It is important to note that the bass voice of the chord is NOT the same thing as the chord's root. The root of an A major triad is always A, regardless of whether the triad is in root position, first inversion, or second inversion. However, the bass voice changes between these inversions, from A to C♯ to E, as seen in Example 1.

title: 轉位
text: 依和弦符號建立轉位三和弦時，要在〈三和弦〉介紹的步驟後，再多加一步。先複習原本的步驟：
en: To build an inverted triad from a chord symbol, you need to add one more step to those shown in the Triads chapter. As a reminder, these steps were:

title: 轉位
text: 在五線譜上寫出根音。在根音上方三度與五度寫出音符，也就是畫出雪人形狀。想出或寫出以根音為主音的大調調號。若要寫大三和弦，就將調號中適用於和弦音的變音記號加上去。若要寫小、減或增三和弦，再依需要加上其他變音記號，改變三音或五音。
en: Draw the root on the staff. Draw notes a third and fifth above the root (i.e., draw a snowperson). Think of (or write down) the major key signature of the triad’s root. To spell a major triad, write any accidentals from the key signature that apply to the notes of the triad. For a minor, diminished, or augmented triad, add additional accidentals to alter the chord’s third and/or fifth when appropriate.

title: 轉位
text: 現在加入第六步：
en: Now we will add a sixth step:

title: 轉位
text: 將適當的和弦音移到低音，完成三和弦。
en: Move the appropriate note to the bass to complete the triad.

title: 轉位
text: 接著依這些步驟，寫出第一轉位的 A♭ 小三和弦（原文符號為 A♭mi/C），如譜例 3所示：
en: Let’s complete this process for an A♭ minor triad in first inversion (A♭mi/C), as seen in Example 3:

title: 轉位
text: 譜例 3。六個步驟寫出第一轉位的 A♭ 小三和弦。
en: Example 3. Drawing an A♭ minor triad in first inversion in six steps.

title: 轉位
text: 先寫 A♭，因為它是三和弦根音。畫出雪人形狀，加入 C、E，分別位於 A♭ 上方三度與五度。回想 A♭ 大調的調號：B♭、E♭、A♭、D♭ 四個降記號。將 E 改為 E♭，因為它在 A♭ 大調調號中。和弦沒有 B、D，因此不需要 B♭、D♭。此時已寫出 A♭ 大三和弦：A♭、C、E♭。小三和弦的三度是小三度，比大三度少半音。因此將三音 C 降半音至 C♭，得到 A♭ 小三和弦：A♭、C♭、E♭。由於和弦是第一轉位，將 C♭ 移到低音；原文在此仍將符號寫為 A♭mi/C。
en: The note A♭ is written because it is the root of the triad. A snowperson is drawn; in other words, the notes C and E are added because they are a generic third and fifth, respectively, above A♭. The key signature of A♭ major is recalled. A♭ major has four flats: B♭, E♭, A♭, and D♭. E♭ is added, because it is in the key signature of A♭ major. B♭ and D♭ are not needed, because those notes aren’t in an A♭ triad. Now we have successfully spelled an A♭ major triad (A♭, C, and E♭). Minor triads contain a minor third, which is one half step smaller than a major third. Therefore, our final step is to lower the chord’s third (the C) by a half step (to a C♭). Now we have an A♭ minor triad (A♭, C♭, and E♭). C♭ is moved to the bass because the triad is in first inversion (A♭mi/C).

title: 轉位
text: 這些步驟對初學者而言可靠，但需要花些時間。若能在樂器上練熟各種性質的三和弦，以及下文的七和弦，就能逐漸直接掌握，不必每次都按步驟推算。
en: Again, following these steps is a reliable way for beginners to spell inverted triads, but it’s a time-consuming process. If you practice playing all of the qualities of triads (and seventh chords below) on an instrument until you are fluent in them, your knowledge will become more automatic without using this process.

text: 如譜例 6所示，七和弦比三和弦多一個音，因此也多一種轉位。當和弦七音位於低音時，就是第三轉位。別忘了，低音與根音不是同義詞。譜例 6不論轉位與低音如何改變，根音始終是 A。

When the chordal seventh of a seventh chord is in the bass, the chord is in third inversion. Don't forget that the bass and the root of the chord are NOT synonymous. In Example 6 the root of the chord is always A, regardless of its inversion and bass note.

en: Draw the root on the staff. Draw notes a third, fifth, and seventh above the root (i.e., draw an “extra-long” snowperson). Think of (or write down) the major key signature of the triad’s root. Write any accidentals from the key signature that apply to the remaining notes in the chord.

text: 譜例 8。五個步驟寫出 D 大大七和弦的轉位。

title: 轉位
text: 在五線譜上寫出根音 D。畫出加長的雪人，加入 F、A、C，分別位於 D 上方三度、五度與七度。回想 D 大調的調號：F♯、C♯ 兩個升記號。在 F、C 左側加上升記號（♯），因為 D 大調使用 F♯ 與 C♯。由於和弦是第二轉位，將五音 A 放到低音。
en: The note D, the chord’s root, is drawn on the staff. An extra-long snowperson is drawn—an F, A, and C, the notes a generic third, fifth, and seventh above the D. The key signature of D major has been recalled. D major has two sharps, F♯ and C♯. Sharps (♯) have been added to the left of the F and the C, because F♯ and C♯ are in the key signature of D major. A is moved to the bass because the seventh chord is in second inversion.

en: Identify and write its root. Identify and write its quality of triad. Identify and write its quality of seventh. Identify its inversion. Write the appropriate slash and letter name.

title: 羅馬數字
text: 重點整理羅馬數字分析是一套和弦標記系統，表示和弦與作品整體調性之間的關係。羅馬數字的數值，對應和弦根音所在的音階級數。和弦若包含七音，就在羅馬數字旁加上標 7（7）。羅馬數字也標示和弦性質：根音上方為大三度的和弦，例如大和弦與增和弦，使用大寫羅馬數字。根音上方為小三度的和弦，例如小和弦、減和弦與半減和弦，使用小寫羅馬數字。增和弦加 +，減和弦加 o，半減和弦加 ø。
en: Key Takeaways Roman numeral analysis is a system of chord labels that contextualize a chord in relation to the overall key of a piece. The number represented in the Roman numeral corresponds to the scale degree of the chord's root. If the chord has a seventh, a superscript seven (7) is added to the Roman numeral. The quality of a chord is also indicated in Roman numeral analysis: Chords with a major third above the root (major, augmented) uses a capital Roman numeral. Chords with a minor third above the root (minor, diminished, half-diminished) use a lowercase Roman numeral. Special symbols are added for augmented (+), diminished (o), and half-diminished (ø) chords.

title: 羅馬數字
text: 音樂家以羅馬數字標示調性脈絡中的和弦。羅馬數字指出和弦根音的音階級數（譜例 1）。它依據的是級數，而非特定音名，因此能幫助我們理解不同調的和聲如何發揮相似作用。
en: Musicians use Roman numerals to identify chords within the context of key signatures. Roman numerals identify the scale degree of the chord's root (Example 1). Because Roman numerals are based on scale degrees rather than specific pitch names, they are useful for understanding how harmonies function similarly in different keys.

title: 羅馬數字
text: 音階級數大寫羅馬數字小寫羅馬數字1Ii2IIii3IIIiii4IViv5Vv6VIvi7VIIvii
en: Scale degree Uppercase Roman Numeral Lowercase Roman Numeral 1 I i 2 II ii 3 III iii 4 IV iv 5 V v 6 VI vi 7 VII vii

title: 羅馬數字
text: 譜例 1。音階級數與羅馬數字。
en: Example 1. Scale degrees and Roman numerals.

title: 羅馬數字
text: 圖例 2。手寫與打字的羅馬數字之差異。
en: Example 2. The difference between handwritten and typed Roman numerals.

title: 羅馬數字
text: 輸入大寫羅馬數字時，使用大寫拉丁字母「I」與「V」；小寫則使用「i」與「v」。[1]手寫大寫羅馬數字時，上下會加橫線，以更清楚區分大小寫（圖例 2）。小寫羅馬數字則沒有這種手寫與打字的差別。
en: To type uppercase Roman numerals, use the uppercase Latin alphabet letters “I” and “V”; likewise, for lowercase Roman numerals, type the lowercase “i” and “v.”[1] Handwritten uppercase Roman numerals have horizontal bars across the top and bottom of the numeral, in order to further distinguish between uppercase and lowercase (Example 2). There is no such difference with lowercase Roman numerals.

title: 羅馬數字
text: 羅馬數字與和弦性質
en: Roman Numerals and Quality

title: 羅馬數字
text: 羅馬數字除了表示根音，也能標示和弦性質（譜例 3）。[2]大寫表示大三和弦，小寫表示小三和弦。例如，在大調中，以第一級 [latex]\hat1[/latex]（do）為根音的和弦寫作「I」；以第二級 [latex]\hat2[/latex]（re）為根音的和弦，則寫作小寫「ii」，依此類推。小寫羅馬數字後加上標「o」，例如 viio，表示減三和弦；大寫後加「+」，例如 V+，表示增三和弦。
en: In addition to showing the chord root, Roman numerals may indicate quality of the chord (Example 3).[2] Uppercase Roman numerals denote major triads, and lowercase Roman numerals denote minor triads. For example, in a major key, a chord built on the first scale degree, [latex]\hat1[/latex] or do, is identified as “I,” a chord built on the second scale degree, [latex]\hat2[/latex] or re, is identified by the lowercase Roman numeral “ii,” and so on. Lowercase Roman numerals followed by a superscript "o" (such as viio) represent diminished triads. Uppercase Roman numerals followed by a + sign (such as V+) represent augmented triads.

title: 羅馬數字
text: 三和弦性質羅馬數字寫法範例大大寫V小小寫ii增大寫加 +V+減小寫加 oviio
en: Triad quality Roman numeral characteristics Example major uppercase V minor lowercase ii augmented uppercase with + V+ diminished lowercase with o viio

title: 羅馬數字
text: 譜例 3。以羅馬數字表示三和弦性質。
en: Example 3. Showing triad quality with Roman numerals.

title: 羅馬數字
text: 和音階級數、唱名一樣，羅馬數字也能跨調使用。譜例 4以 G 大調與 G 小調的調內三和弦為例；不論哪個音是主音，都會使用相同的羅馬數字。圖中也標出各根音的唱名與音階級數，請注意它們與羅馬數字的對應。
en: Just as scale degrees and solfège are the same across keys, so are Roman numerals. Example 4 shows the Roman numerals for the diatonic triads of G major and G minor as an example, but the same Roman numerals would be used regardless of which pitch is the tonic. The solfège and scale degree of the roots are also labeled—note the correspondence between these and the Roman numerals.

title: 羅馬數字
text: 譜例 4。G 大調與 G 小調三和弦的羅馬數字。

title: 羅馬數字
text: 〈三和弦〉已介紹：小調若升高第七級，形成導音，和弦性質與羅馬數字也會改變。小三和弦 v 變成大三和弦 V，下主音上的 VII 變成減三和弦 viio。因此，小調的羅馬數字有時隱含升高第七級；看到 V 或 viio 時，記得使用升高後的導音。
en: As discussed in Triads, if the leading tone is raised in minor, the chord quality changes, and thus the Roman numeral changes: the minor v chord becomes a major V chord, and the subtonic VII chord becomes a diminished viio chord. This means that a Roman numeral in minor sometimes implies a raised leading tone, so remember that when you see a V or a viio in a minor key, you will be using the raised leading tone.

title: 羅馬數字
text: 七和弦的羅馬數字
en: Roman Numerals for Seventh Chords

title: 羅馬數字
text: 七和弦的羅馬數字加上標 7，例如 V7、ii7、viio7。大小寫依性質決定：大七和弦與屬七和弦用大寫，小七、減七與半減七和弦用小寫。還要加上特殊符號區分半減與全減：∅ 表示半減七和弦，o 表示全減七和弦。譜例 5整理了這些寫法。
en: Roman numeral labels for seventh chords add a superscript 7 (for example, V7, ii7, and viio7). Whether or not the Roman numeral is capitalized depends on the quality: major and dominant seventh chords are capital; minor, diminished, and half-diminished seventh chords are lowercase. You will need to add special symbols to indicate half and fully diminished chord qualities: ∅ indicates a half-diminished seventh chord and o indicates a fully diminished seventh chord. This is summarized in Example 5.

title: 羅馬數字
text: 七和弦性質羅馬數字寫法範例大大七和弦（大七和弦）大寫IV7大小七和弦（屬七和弦）大寫V7小小七和弦（小七和弦）小寫ii7半減七和弦小寫加 ∅ii∅7全減七和弦（減七和弦）小寫加 oviio7
en: Seventh chord quality Roman numeral characteristics Example Major-major seventh chord (Major seventh chord) uppercase IV7 Major-minor seventh chord (Dominant seventh chord) uppercase V7 Minor-minor seventh chord (Minor seventh chord) lowercase ii7 Half-diminished seventh chord lowercase with ∅ ii∅7 Fully diminished seventh chord (Diminished seventh chord) lowercase with o viio7

title: 羅馬數字
text: 譜例 5。以羅馬數字表示七和弦性質。
en: Example 5. Showing seventh chord quality with Roman numerals.

title: 羅馬數字
text: 請注意，大七和弦與屬七和弦的羅馬數字寫法相同，都是大寫加上標 7，必須依調性脈絡判斷是哪一種。原文指出，屬七和弦只出現在 V7，或小調的 VII7；除此之外，大寫加 7 就視為大七和弦。
en: Note that major seventh and dominant seventh chords Roman numerals have the same features: a capital Roman numeral followed by a superscript 7. One should infer whether the chord is major or dominant through the key context. Dominant seventh chords are only found on V7 chords (or VII7 in minor); otherwise, assume that a capital Roman numeral with a 7 is a major seventh chord.

title: 羅馬數字
text: 譜例 6列出 G 大調與 G 小調的七和弦，並標示和弦符號與藍色羅馬數字。把這些調移調後，羅馬數字仍然相同。
en: Example 6 shows the seventh chords of the G major and G minor scales, labeled with chord symbols and Roman numerals (in blue). Again, the Roman numerals would be the same for any transposition of these keys.

title: 羅馬數字
text: 羅馬數字分析
en: Roman Numeral Analysis

title: 羅馬數字
text: 進行羅馬數字分析，首先要辨識作品的調性，並在作品或片段開頭標明。和和弦符號一樣，單獨的大寫音名表示大調，後加「mi」表示小調，例如 B♭mi 表示 B♭ 小調。另一種常見寫法是用小寫音名表示小調，例如 b♭ 表示 B♭ 小調。
en: To complete a Roman numeral analysis, you must first identify the work’s key. A Roman numeral analysis should indicate the key at the beginning of the work or excerpt. As with chord symbols, a capital note name alone indicates major keys, and "mi" would follow to indicate a minor key (e.g., "B♭mi" for B♭ minor). Another common practice is to use lowercase letters for minor keys (e.g., "b♭" for B♭ minor).

title: 羅馬數字
text: 羅馬數字依和弦根音的音階級數決定，因此下一步是找出根音。和弦可能已轉位，根音不一定在低音；若譜上不是原位，可以重新疊成原位，最好在心中完成。
en: Roman numerals are assigned according to the scale degree of each chord's root, so next, the root must be identified. A chord may be inverted, so the root is not necessarily in the bass. You can re-stack the chord in root position (preferably mentally) if it does not appear that way in the music.

title: 羅馬數字
text: 羅馬數字的大小寫依和弦性質決定。由於調內各和弦的性質模式固定，可以記住大小調中的和弦性質，據此決定大小寫及是否需要特殊符號。
en: The Roman numeral will be capital or lowercase depending on the chord quality. Because each chord in a key will always have the same quality, you can memorize the qualities of chords within major and minor keys to determine whether the Roman numeral should be capital or lowercase, and whether it needs added special symbols.

title: 羅馬數字
text: 辨識和聲羅馬數字的步驟如下：
en: To summarize, these are the steps for identifying the Roman numeral of a harmony:

title: 羅馬數字
text: 辨識調性，別忘了名稱中需要的升、降記號。找出和弦根音及其音階級數，決定羅馬數字。依和弦性質使用大寫或小寫，必要時加特殊符號。
en: Identify the key (don't forget any sharp or flat signs if applicable!). Find the root of the chord and note its scale degree. This corresponds to the Roman numeral of the chord. Write the Roman numeral, using upper- or lowercase letters and special symbols (if applicable) to show the chord quality.

title: 羅馬數字
text: 譜例 7分析路易絲・賴夏特（Louise Reichardt，1779–1826）的〈Die Wiese〉（草地，1811）。德文歌詞意譯如下：
en: Example 7 shows a Roman numeral analysis of "Die Wiese" (1811) by Louise Reichardt (1779–1826). The German text translates as follows:

title: 羅馬數字
text: 「春日的一天，一切都美麗而歡快，我曾來到一間僻靜的夏日小屋，一位甜美的女孩從屋裡走出，哭泣著。」
en: "One spring day, when everything was beautiful and cheerful, I once came to a lonely summer house where a sweet girl came out and cried."

title: 羅馬數字
text: 請留意這份分析的幾個特點：
en: Note several features of this analysis:

title: 羅馬數字
text: 分析開頭標明調性，羅馬數字寫在五線譜下方。和弦沒有改變時，不必重複寫羅馬數字。這首曲子是小調，有時會升高第七級作為導音，即 A 小調中的 G♯，形成大三和弦 V 與屬七和弦 V7。未升高的下主音 G♮，則在原來的 [latex]\hat7[/latex] 上形成屬七和弦性質的和弦。[3]第四小節聲樂中的 A 是裝飾性和弦外音，不屬於 VII7 和聲，因此不影響羅馬數字。即使省略五音，該和弦仍然是 V7。轉位不改變和弦的羅馬數字本身；老師會說明是否需要加上數字標示轉位，詳見〈數字低音〉。
en: The key is labeled at the start of the analysis. Roman numerals are written underneath the staff. Roman numerals do not need to be repeated if the chord is not changing. Because this piece is in minor, it sometimes uses a raised leading tone (G♯ in A minor), producing major V and dominant V7 chords. The unraised G♮ subtonic scale degree produces a dominant seventh chord built on the unraised [latex]\hat7[/latex].[3] The A in the vocal part of m. 4 is an embellishing tone—not part of the VII7 harmony and does not affect the Roman numeral. This is still a V7 even though the fifth of the chord is missing. Inversion does not change the Roman numeral of a chord. Your instructor will tell you if they want you to indicate inversions with figures. See Figured Bass for more information on this topic.

text: 和弦配置：包含各音的八度位置、重複音，甚至省略某些音，尤其是五音。轉位／低音：可以依〈數字低音〉的方法，用數字標示轉位，但羅馬數字本身不變。裝飾性和弦外音：曲中並非每個音都屬於當下和聲，有些音更適合視為裝飾性和弦外音，詳見〈和弦外音〉。它們偶爾也會以數字標示，但不影響羅馬數字。
en: Chord voicing, which includes the octave of the notes, doubling of notes, or even the omission of certain notes (especially the chordal fifth). Inversion/bass note. Inversion can be shown with figures, as described in the Figured Bass chapter, but the Roman numeral does not change. Embellishing tones. Not every note in a piece is necessarily considered part of the harmony—sometimes notes are better understood as embellishing tones (which you can learn more about in the Embellishing Tones chapter). Embellishing tones may occasionally be indicated with figures, but they do not affect a Roman numeral.

title: 羅馬數字
text: 音高以外的節奏、音色、發音方式、力度等，通常很少影響和弦的羅馬數字標記。因此，完整的音樂分析不能只看羅馬數字呈現的和聲。羅馬數字能描述某些音樂現象，卻無法說明音樂的全部。
en: Aspects of music outside of pitch—rhythm, timbre, articulation, dynamic, and so on—rarely impact the Roman numeral label of a chord. Because of this, a complete analysis of a piece of music ought to consider more than just the harmonies as understood with Roman numerals. Roman numerals are a helpful tool for describing certain musical phenomena, but they do not tell the whole story.

title: 羅馬數字
text: IV（4）與 VI（6）經常混淆。可以把 IV 想成 V 減 I，即 5 − 1 = 4；VI 則是 V 加 I，即 5 + 1 = 6。↵有些樂理學者，尤其在北美以外，偏好全部使用大寫羅馬數字，並假定和弦性質可由脈絡推知。↵VII 和弦，尤其 VII7，也可以分析為朝向 III 調的副和弦（V/III）。更多主音化與副和弦的說明，請參閱〈主音化〉。↵
en: The Roman numerals IV (4) and VI (6) are often confused. To remember the difference, think of IV (4) as V minus I (5 − 1 = 4), and VI (6) as V plus I (5 + 1 = 6). ↵Some music theorists (especially outside North America) prefer to use only uppercase Roman numerals, a system which assumes chord quality is intuited. ↵Another analysis for the VII chord, especially VII7, is as an applied chord in the key of III (V/III). Read more about tonicization and applied chords in Tonicization. ↵

title: 數字低音與附數字的羅馬數字
text: 重點整理十七、十八世紀的音樂家與作曲家，使用數字低音暗示合奏作品的和聲：在低音聲部下方加數字與符號，表示需要的和聲。數字低音通常不直接加在和弦符號上，但會加在三和弦簡記法中。依數字低音寫出或演奏和弦，稱為實現數字低音。三和弦與七和弦的原位、轉位各有對應數字；完整數字常會簡寫。要標示半音變化，可在相應數字前加變音記號（♭、♯、♮）；也可在數字上加斜線，或在前方加加號，表示升高半音。單獨出現、未附數字的變音記號，作用於低音上方三度的音。橫線可表示同一低音上方音的變動，或和聲變化。數字有時會與羅馬數字並用，提供更多分析資訊。
en: Key Takeaways Historically (in the 17th and 18th centuries) musicians and composers use figured bass to imply harmonies in ensemble works. Figured bass refers to the bass voice, under which figures and other symbols indicate implied harmonies. Figured bass is not usually added to chord symbols; however, it is added to triadic shorthand notation. It is called realizing figured bass when musicians turn figured bass into chords, either on paper or in performance. Triads and seventh chords have figures which correspond to root position and inverted harmonies when realized. Full figures are often abbreviated. In order to denote chromatic alterations to notes, musicians put accidentals (♭, ♯, ♮) before the figure that is altered. Musicians also use slashes through a figure or a plus sign before a figure, in order to indicate raising the note by a half step. Orphaned accidentals apply to the third above the bass. Horizontal lines indicate a change of note above a given bass, or a change in harmony. Figures are sometimes paired with Roman numerals to provide more information to music analysts.

title: 數字低音與附數字的羅馬數字
text: 十七、十八世紀的紙與墨水相對昂貴。為節省費用與時間，作曲家和音樂家有時不完整寫出合奏作品的和聲，而以簡記暗示。數字低音指的是低音聲部及其下方的數字、符號，演奏者藉此理解所需的和聲。[1]
en: In the 17th and 18th centuries, paper and ink were somewhat expensive materials. To save money--and also time--composers and musicians sometimes implied harmonies in ensemble works, without writing them out fully. Figured bass refers to the the bass voice or part, under which figures and other symbols indicate to musicians the implied harmony.[1]

text: 如譜例 1所示，原位三和弦在低音上方有三度與五度，以 [latex]\begin{smallmatrix}5\\3\end{smallmatrix}[/latex] 表示。第一轉位在低音上方有三度與六度，以 [latex]\begin{smallmatrix}6\\3\end{smallmatrix}[/latex] 表示；第二轉位則有四度與六度，以 [latex]\begin{smallmatrix}6\\4\end{smallmatrix}[/latex] 表示。數字低音中，較大的數字一定放在較小的數字上方。

A first inversion triad has a third and a sixth above the bass (indicated by "[latex]\begin{smallmatrix}6\\3\end{smallmatrix}[/latex]"), and a second inversion triad has a fourth and a sixth above the bass (indicated by "[latex]\begin{smallmatrix}6\\4\end{smallmatrix}[/latex]"). In figured bass, larger numbers always appear above smaller ones.

title: 數字低音與附數字的羅馬數字
text: 譜例 3第一小節的 E♭ 旁沒有數字，因此本例要實現的是原位 E♭ 大三和弦；下一小節將和弦音完整寫出。第三小節低音 G 下方標 6，表示在 G 上方加入六度與三度；下一小節寫出結果，即第一轉位的 E♭ 大三和弦。第五小節低音 B♭ 下方標 [latex]\begin{smallmatrix}6\\4\end{smallmatrix}[/latex]，表示在 B♭ 上方加入六度與四度；下一小節的結果是第二轉位的 E♭ 大三和弦。
en: As seen in the first measure of Example 3, an E♭ appears with no figured bass next to it. Therefore, we can assume that we are realizing an E♭ major triad in root position. This chord is realized (written out with notes) in the next measure. In measure 3, we see the figure "6" below the bass note G. We can understand that notation to mean that we are realizing a sixth and a third above the bass note G. This chord is realized in the next measure (an E♭ major triad in first inversion). In measure 5, we see the figures "[latex]\begin{smallmatrix}6\\4\end{smallmatrix}[/latex]" below the bass note B♭. This notation means that we are realizing a sixth and a fourth above the bass note B♭. This chord is realized in the next measure (an E♭ major triad in second inversion).

text: 譜例 6第一小節低音 A 下方標 7，因此本例要實現的是原位 A 屬七和弦；下一小節將和弦音完整寫出。第三小節低音 C♯ 下方標 [latex]^6_5[/latex]，表示在 C♯ 上方加入六度、五度與三度；下一小節的結果是第一轉位 A 屬七和弦。第五小節低音 E 下方標 [latex]^4_3[/latex]，表示在 E 上方加入六度、四度與三度；下一小節的結果是第二轉位 A 屬七和弦。第七小節低音 G 下方標 [latex]^4_2[/latex]，表示在 G 上方加入六度、四度與二度；下一小節的結果是第三轉位 A 屬七和弦。
en: As seen in the first measure of Example 6, an A appears with the superscript figure "7" under it. Therefore, we can assume that we are realizing an A dominant seventh chord in root position. This chord is realized (written out with notes) in the next measure. In measure 3, we see the figures "[latex]^6_5[/latex]" below the bass note C♯. We can understand that notation to mean that we are realizing a sixth, fifth, and third above the bass note C♯. This chord is realized in the next measure (resulting in an A dominant seventh chord in first inversion). In measure 5, we see the figures "[latex]^4_3[/latex]" below the bass note E. This notation means that we are realizing a sixth, fourth, and third above the bass note E. This chord is realized in the next measure (resulting in an A dominant seventh chord in second inversion). In measure 7, we see the figures "[latex]^4_2[/latex]" below the bass note G. This means that we are realizing a sixth, fourth, and second above the bass note G. This chord is realized in the next measure (resulting in an A dominant seventh chord in third inversion).

title: 數字低音與附數字的羅馬數字
text: 譜例 10第一小節的橫線表示低音上方音的變動，可讀成「低音上方五度的音移到六度」，第二小節寫出實現。有時這表示掛留音，詳見〈和弦外音〉；第三、第四小節就是一例，可讀成「低音上方四度的音移到三度」。橫線也可以標示終止四六和弦，詳見〈以終止四六和弦加強結尾〉。第五、第六小節的終止 [latex]^6_4[/latex] 可讀成「低音上方六度的音移到五度」，以及「低音上方四度的音移到三度」。譜例 10第五、第六小節也顯示，數字低音可以同時出現不只一條橫線。橫線還可以表示和聲變化，如第七、第八小節，可讀成「低音上方含六度的和弦，接到低音上方含五度的和弦」，因為此時移動的是低音本身。
en: In the first measure of Example 10, the horizontal line indicates a change of note above the given bass. We could read this as "a fifth above the bass moves to a sixth above the bass," as realized in measure 2. Sometimes this indicates a suspension, which you can read more about in Embellishing Tones. You can see an example of a suspension in measures 3 and 4 above; this could be read as "a fourth above the bass moves to a third above the bass." Horizontal lines can also indicate a cadential 6/4 chord, which you can read more about in Strengthening Endings with Cadential 6/4. You can see an example of a cadential [latex]^6_4[/latex] in measures 5 and 6 above; this could be read as "a sixth above the bass moves to a fifth above the bass," and "a fourth above the bass moves to a third above the bass." As you can see in measures 5 and 6 of Example 10, more than one horizontal line can appear at the same time in figured bass. Horizontal lines can also indicate a change in harmony, as seen in measures 7 and 8 above; this could be read as "a chord with a sixth above the bass moves to a chord with a fifth above the bass," since it is the bass itself which is moving.

en: Key Takeaways When constructing a chord in SATB style, there are six rules to keep in mind: Stem direction Chord construction Range Spacing Voice crossing Doubling

title: SATB 四部和聲中的和弦
text: 為了讓和聲內容更容易辨讀，樂理學者有時會將作品簡化為四個聲部。這種做法稱為SATB 四部和聲，名稱來自合唱中四種常見聲部的縮寫：女高音 soprano（S）、女低音 alto（A）、男高音 tenor（T）與男低音 bass（B）。
en: Music theorists sometimes simplify compositions into four parts (or voices) in order to make their harmonic content more readily accessible. This practice is called SATB style, abbreviated after the four common voice parts of a choir––soprano (S), alto (A), tenor (T), and bass (B).

title: SATB 四部和聲中的和弦
text: 以嚴格的 SATB 四部和聲配置和弦時，通常遵循六項規則：

text: 這六項原則是對位法與聲部寫作的基礎；〈對位法與嘉蘭特圖式〉及〈自然音和聲、主音化與轉調〉會進一步探討。

text: 符幹方向

text: 譜例 1。符幹方向錯誤。
en: Example 1. A stemming error.

title: SATB 四部和聲中的和弦
text: SATB 使用大譜表時，女高音與女低音寫在上方的高音譜號譜表，男高音與男低音寫在下方的低音譜號譜表。女高音、男高音的符幹朝上；女低音、男低音的符幹朝下。若方向顛倒，就是記譜錯誤。譜例 1先顯示符幹方向錯誤的和弦，再列出修正版本。
en: On a grand staff in SATB style, the soprano and alto are written in the treble clef (upper staff), while the tenor and bass are written in the bass clef (lower staff). The soprano and tenor voices receive up-stems, while the alto and bass parts receive down-stems. If the stem direction is crossed, this is an error. Example 1 shows a chord with incorrect stemming, followed by the corrected version.

title: SATB 四部和聲中的和弦
text: 和弦構成
en: Chord Construction

title: SATB 四部和聲中的和弦
text: 譜例 2。和弦構成錯誤。
en: Example 2. A chord construction error.

title: SATB 四部和聲中的和弦
text: 檢查每個和弦的音與變音記號是否正確，也要確認沒有遺漏和弦音。譜例 2的第一個和弦在兩個音上誤加變音記號；第二個和弦移除它們，成為正確的第一轉位 B 減三和弦。
en: Be sure to check each chord for correct notes and accidentals, and make sure that your chords are not missing any notes. In Example 2, the first chord has accidentals erroneously added to two of the pitches, which are removed in the second chord to create a correct B diminished triad in first inversion.

title: SATB 四部和聲中的和弦
text: 低音必須符合羅馬數字旁的數字所指示的轉位；上方各音則可以有許多排列方式。也就是說，同一和弦不一定只有一種正確配置。
en: The bass voice must always correspond with the inversion that the Roman numeral’s figures indicate. However, the order of the upper notes can be arranged in many ways. In other words, there is not necessarily just one correct way to voice a chord.

title: SATB 四部和聲中的和弦
text: 各聲部一般採用下列音域（譜例 3）：
en: There is a generally accepted range for each voice (Example 3):

title: SATB 四部和聲中的和弦
text: 女高音：C4 至 G5女低音：G3 至 D5男高音：C3 至 G4男低音：F2 至 D4
en: Soprano – C4 to G5 Alto – G3 to D5 Tenor – C3 to G4 Bass – F2 to D4

title: SATB 四部和聲中的和弦
text: 譜例 4。超出音域的錯誤。
en: Example 4. A range error.

title: SATB 四部和聲中的和弦
text: 譜例 4的女高音與男低音超出音域；將女高音降一個八度、男低音升一個八度，即可修正。
en: In Example 4, the soprano and bass notes are out of range; this is corrected by moving the soprano note down by an octave and the bass note up by an octave.

title: SATB 四部和聲中的和弦
text: 聲部間距
en: Spacing

title: SATB 四部和聲中的和弦
text: 譜例 15。聲部間距錯誤。
en: Example 15. A spacing error.

title: SATB 四部和聲中的和弦
text: 上方相鄰聲部，也就是女高音與女低音、女低音與男高音之間，不應超過八度；男高音與男低音之間則不應超過十二度。最常見的間距錯誤發生在女低音與男高音之間，因為兩者使用不同譜號。譜例 15先列出間距錯誤的和弦：女高音與女低音相隔超過八度，女低音與男高音也一樣；接著列出修正版本。
en: There should be no more than an octave between adjacent upper voices (soprano and alto, alto and tenor) and no more than a twelfth between the tenor and bass. The most common spacing error occurs between the alto and tenor because the notes appear in different clefs. Example 15 first shows a chord with incorrect spacing—the soprano and alto are more than an octave apart, as are the alto and tenor—followed by a corrected version:

title: SATB 四部和聲中的和弦
text: 聲部交叉
en: Voice Crossing

title: SATB 四部和聲中的和弦
text: 譜例 6。聲部交叉錯誤。
en: Example 6. A voice crossing error.

title: SATB 四部和聲中的和弦
text: 各聲部的高低位置不應交叉。換言之，女高音應高於女低音，女低音高於男高音，男高音高於男低音。譜例 6的女低音與男高音發生交叉；這也是最常出現交叉錯誤的一對聲部。
en: The ranges of voices should not cross. In other words, the soprano must always be higher than the alto, the alto must always be higher than the tenor, and the tenor must always be higher than the bass. In Example 6, the alto and tenor voices are crossed. This error is also the most common between the alto and tenor voices.

title: SATB 四部和聲中的和弦
text: 重複音
en: Doubling

title: SATB 四部和聲中的和弦
text: 譜例 7。重複音錯誤。
en: Example 7. A doubling error.

title: SATB 四部和聲中的和弦
text: 三和弦通常會在上方聲部重複低音。不過，導音是例外，不可重複；其他具有解決傾向的音，例如和弦七音，也不可重複。七和弦有四個音，正好每個聲部各分配一個，因此不需重複音。譜例 7第一小節錯誤地重複了導音，第二小節則是修正後的配置。
en: In a triad, the note in the bass is usually doubled in an upper voice. However, there is an exception to this: the leading tone is never doubled. Other tendency tones, such as chordal sevenths, are also never doubled. Seventh chords don’t have any notes doubled because they contain four notes, one for each voice part. Incorrect doubling is seen in the first measure of Example 7, where the leading tone is doubled, followed by a corrected voicing in the second measure.

title: II. 對位法與嘉蘭特圖式
text: Punctum contra punctum……點對點……音對音。
en: Punctum contra punctum… point against point… note against note.

title: II. 對位法與嘉蘭特圖式
text: 本部分以廣義的音符組合理解「對位法」。有時，人們將對位法視為「水平」或「旋律」層面，與和聲的「垂直」層面互補；但在實際音樂中，兩者並不容易分開。我們不在此作僵硬的區分，只把重點放在線條的組織。
en: This section on “counterpoint” takes that term to concern the combination of notes in general. Although “counterpoint” is sometimes used as the “horizontal” or “melodic” complement to harmony’s “vertical” aspect, the two are clearly not so easily separated in practice and we do not attempt to make any such hard-and-fast distinction here, beyond simply emphasising linear elements.

title: II. 對位法與嘉蘭特圖式
text: 本部分也特別重視「自己動手」：練習類種對位法，以及模仿十六、十八世紀風格的作曲，並提供 Fux 第一部分所有練習的數位版本。
en: This section also places a prominent emphasis on “try it yourself” exercises in species counterpoint and pastiche composition in 16th- and 18th-century styles, including digital versions of all the Fux Part I exercises.

title: II. 對位法與嘉蘭特圖式
text: 先備知識
en: Prerequisites

title: II. 對位法與嘉蘭特圖式

en: This second part of Open Music Theory assumes knowledge of Fundamentals, but nothing from the later parts.

title: II. 對位法與嘉蘭特圖式
text: 內容安排
en: Organization

title: II. 對位法與嘉蘭特圖式
text: 本部分介紹歷來對位教學中幾種主要的曲目與技法：
en: This section covers some of the main kinds of repertoires and techniques historically used in the teaching of counterpoint:

title: II. 對位法與嘉蘭特圖式
text: 先從可能最知名、沿用 Fux 教學方式的類種對位法開始。類種對位法有時會與十六世紀的模仿複調風格混為一談，因此在類種對位各章之後，我們會更仔細研究那一時期的曲目。十六世紀複調可以視為另一種模仿風格——賦格——的前身。這裡特別探討十八世紀初賦格的開頭段落。最後，仍停留在十八世紀，但離開嚴格模仿，轉向其他與對位思考有關的方法，尤其是嘉蘭特圖式：既有的短小聲部組合範型，可加以發展，成為實際的作曲或即興音樂。
en: We begin with probably the best-known, so-called species counterpoint approach (after Fux). Species counterpoint is sometimes conflated with the imitative polyphonic style of the 16th century, so after our chapters on species, we move on to a closer look at that repertoire in particular. 16th-century polyphony can be viewed as a precursor to another imitative style: the fugue. Here, we take a look at the opening section of fugues in the early 18th century specifically. Finally, staying in the 18th century, we take a step away from strict imitation to look at some other kinds of approaches relevant to the contrapuntal thinking, particularly the practice of Galant schemas: short pre-existing templates for combining voices that can be elaborated into “real” music (compositions or improvisation).

title: 類種對位法入門
text: 重點整理類種對位法是循序漸進學習旋律寫作與旋律組合的方法。其中的「規則」與十六世紀音樂略有關聯，但主要目的是訓練基本能力，而非限定某套曲目或風格。本章複習〈基礎樂理〉的重要概念，並介紹後續各章共用的基本規則與術語：協和與不協和：完全協和音程：完全同度、完全五度與完全八度。不完全協和音程：大、小三度與大、小六度。不協和音程：所有二度、七度，以及增、減音程。兩聲部進行的類型：反向進行：兩聲部往相反方向移動，一個上行、一個下行。同向進行：兩聲部往同一方向移動，同時上行或同時下行。平行進行：兩聲部往同一方向移動相同度數，起點與終點形成同類音程，例如平行三度。斜向進行：一個聲部移動，另一個維持同音。
en: Key Takeaways Species counterpoint is a step-by-step method for learning to write melodies and to combine them. While the "rules" involved are somewhat linked to music in the 16th century, the idea really is to train basic skills, independent of a specific repertoire or style. This chapter recaps some key concepts we met in the Fundamentals section and introduces some basic "rules" that will be relevant for each of the following chapters, including some terms for: Consonance and dissonance: Perfect consonances: perfect unisons, fifths, and octaves Imperfect consonances: major and minor thirds and sixths Dissonances: all seconds, sevenths, and diminished and augmented intervals Types of two-part motion: Contrary: the two parts move in opposite directions (one up, the other down) Similar: the two parts move in the same direction (both up or both down) Parallel: the two parts move in the same direction (both up or both down) by the same distance, such that the starting and ending intervals are of the same type (e.g., parallel thirds) Oblique: one part moves, the other stays on the same pitch

title: 類種對位法入門
text: 我們先從類種對位法這個特定方法開始。「Species」最熟悉的意思可能是動物的「物種」，但也能廣義指將相似事物分類的系統。這裡的類種是依特定順序進行的練習類型，每個階段引入一、兩個新的音樂問題。所以，很抱歉，這裡不會有大象或猴子一起唱複調！
en: We begin with a specific method called species counterpoint. The term "species" is probably most familiar as a way of categorizing animals, but it is also used in a wider sense to refer to any system of grouping similar elements. Here, the species are types of exercises that are done in a particular order, introducing one or two new musical “problems” at each stage. (So no, we won't have any elephants or monkeys singing polyphony, sorry!)

title: 類種對位法入門
text: 這套方法有許多變體，本書各章主要依據 Johann Joseph Fux 的〈Gradus ad Parnassum（通往帕納索斯山的階梯，1725）〉。十八至二十一世紀的許多作曲家，都使用過這套方法或其變體。Fux 在書的第一部分，依五種類種練習兩聲部組合，這也是接下來五章的重點。〈《Gradus ad Parnassum》練習〉提供書中所有練習的可編輯版本，讓你親自嘗試。
en: While there are many variants on this approach, the chapters here are closely based on Johann Joseph Fux's Gradus ad Parnassum (Steps to Parnassus, 1725). Many composers from the 18th to the 21st centuries have used this method, or some variation on it. In the first part of Gradus ad Parnassum, Fux works through five species for combining two voices, which will be the focus of our next five chapters. The “Gradus ad Parnassum” Exercises chapter provides all of the exercises from Gradus ad Parnassum in an editable format so you can try this yourself.

title: 類種對位法入門
text: 進入五種類種之前，本章先介紹各類旋律寫作都適用的原則。這些原則建立在〈基礎樂理〉的概念上，例如音程與音階級數。
en: Before getting into the five species, we begin in this chapter by introducing principles that apply to writing lines in any species. These principles build on concepts from the Fundamentals section, such as intervals and scale degrees.

title: 類種對位法入門
text: 協和與不協和
en: Consonance and dissonance

title: 類種對位法入門
text: 前面的章節已介紹協和與不協和，對位法還會進一步區分：
en: Consonance and dissonance was introduced in a previous chapter, but in counterpoint, we further distinguish between:

title: 類種對位法入門
text: 完全協和音程：完全同度、完全五度與完全八度。不完全協和音程：大、小三度與大、小六度。不協和音程：所有二度、七度，以及增、減音程。
en: Perfect consonances (perfect unisons, fifths, and octaves) Imperfect consonances (major and minor thirds and sixths) Dissonances (all seconds, sevenths, and diminished and augmented intervals)

title: 類種對位法入門
text: 下方譜例 1整理了這些分類。
en: These categories are summarized in Example 1 below.

title: 類種對位法入門
text: 譜例 1。完全協和、不完全協和與不協和音程。
en: Example 1. Perfect consonances, imperfect consonances, and dissonances.

title: 類種對位法入門
text: 不易一概而論的完全四度
en: The elusive perfect fourth

title: 類種對位法入門
text: 和許多調性音樂理論一樣，完全四度在類種對位法中有特殊地位，取決於它出現在哪些聲部之間。基本上，只要完全四度涉及最低聲部，就是不協和；若出現在兩個上方聲部之間，則是協和。
en: As in many theories of tonal music, the perfect fourth has a special status in species counterpoint that depends on where it appears in the texture. Basically, the interval of a perfect fourth is dissonant when it involves the lowest voice in the texture, but it is consonant when it occurs between two upper voices.

title: 類種對位法入門
text: 本系列的類種對位法只討論兩聲部，因此所有四度都會涉及最低聲部，一律歸為不協和。後續各章會說明如何解決；〈自然音和聲〉部分的〈以終止 [latex]^6_4[/latex] 加強結尾〉與〈作為延長手法的 [latex]^6_4[/latex] 和弦〉也會進一步討論。
en: As this survey of species counterpoint will only cover two-voice textures, all fourths will involve the lowest part and therefore be classed as dissonant. Later chapters in this section will address the resolution of this dissonance, and the Strengthening Endings with Cadential [latex]^6_4[/latex] and [latex]^6_4[/latex] Chords as Forms of Prolongation chapters in the Diatonic Harmony section discuss this topic further.

text: 類種對位法也關注旋律線條之間的相對進行方式，如譜例 2所示：

en: Contrary: the two parts move in opposite directions (one up, the other down) Similar: the two parts move in the same direction (both up or both down) Parallel: the two parts move in the same direction (both up or both down) by the same distance, such that the starting and ending intervals are of the same type (e.g., parallel thirds) Oblique: one part moves, the other stays on the same pitch

title: 類種對位法入門
text: 嚴格聲部進行或類種對位法的練習，從一條組織完整的旋律開始，稱為定旋律（cantus firmus），意思是「固定的聲部」或「固定的旋律」，複數為 cantus firmi。創作定旋律，可以練習下列基本音樂特質：
en: Exercises in strict voice leading, or species counterpoint, begin with a single well-formed musical line called the cantus firmus ("fixed voice" or "fixed melody"; plural "cantus firmi"). Cantus firmus composition gives us the opportunity to engage the following fundamental musical traits:

title: 類種對位法入門
text: 流暢性旋律線條的獨立性與完整性多樣性朝向目標的進行
en: smoothness independence and integrity of melodic lines variety motion (toward a goal)

title: 類種對位法入門
text: 譜例 3包含 Fux 在《Gradus ad Parnassum》中使用的全部定旋律，每種調式各一條，並分別放在兩聲部的上方與下方。除了複習 Fux 的定旋律類型，也可以用它練習任何類種、任何調式，並分別在上方與下方聲部作曲。
en: Example 3 contains all the cantus firmi that Fux uses throughout Gradus at Parnassum: one for each mode, presented here in the upper and lower of two parts. Apart from using this to review the type of cantus firmi Fux composed, you can use this to practice any of the species, on any of the modes, and in both the upper and lower parts.

title: 類種對位法入門
text: 譜例 3。《Gradus ad Parnassum》中的定旋律。
en: Example 3. Cantus firmi from Gradus ad Parnassum.

title: 類種對位法入門
text: 請觀察，流暢性、旋律完整性、多樣性與目標導向，如何在各個例子中化為具體特徵。組織良好的定旋律通常有以下特點：
en: Notice how in each case, the general musical characteristics of smoothness, melodic integrity, variety, and motion toward a goal are worked out in specific characteristics. The following characteristics are typical of all well-formed cantus firmi:

title: 類種對位法入門
text: 約 8–16 個音。不作節奏長短變化，全部使用全音符。從 do [latex](\hat1)[/latex] 開始，也在 do 結束。以級進接到最後主音，通常是 re–do [latex](\hat2-\hat1)[/latex]，有時是 ti–do [latex](\hat7-\hat1)[/latex]。每一對相鄰音都形成旋律上的協和音程。音域，即最低音至最高音的距離，不超過十度，通常小於八度。只有一個高潮，即最高點，而且通常在旋律中只出現一次。從開頭到高潮，再到結尾，有清楚的邏輯連接與流暢輪廓。以級進為主，搭配少量跳進，且多為小跳進。不反覆使用「動機」或慣用短句。任何四度以上的大跳之後，都接反方向級進。連續跳進不超過兩次，也不連續向同一方向跳進；F 調式定旋律是例外，其中相連的下行跳進勾勒出協和的三和弦。導音進到主音。各種情況都使用導音；具有小調性質的調式，須升高第七級以形成導音。
en: length of about 8–16 notes arhythmic (all whole notes; no long or short notes) begin and end on do [latex](\hat1)[/latex] approach final tonic by step: usually re–do [latex](\hat2-\hat1)[/latex], sometimes ti–do [latex](\hat7-\hat1)[/latex] all note-to-note progressions are melodic consonances range (interval between lowest and highest notes) of no more than a tenth, usually less than an octave a single climax (high point) that usually appears only once in the melody clear logical connection and smooth shape from beginning to climax to ending mostly stepwise motion, but with some leaps (mostly small leaps) no repetition of “motives” or “licks” any large leaps (fourth or larger) are followed by step in opposite direction no more than two leaps in a row and no consecutive leaps in the same direction (except in the F-mode cantus firmus, where the back-to-back descending leaps outline a consonant triad) the leading tone progresses to the tonic leading notes in all cases, including in "minor"-type modes for which that seventh degree needs to be raised

title: 類種對位法入門
text: 旋律的傾向
en: Melodic tendencies

title: 類種對位法入門
text: 上列部分特徵屬於嚴格類種對位法的規範；但整體而言，它們也反映許多不同風格中常見的旋律傾向。
en: Some of the characteristics listed above are specific to strict species counterpoint; however, taken together, they express some general tendencies of melodies found in a variety of styles.

title: 類種對位法入門
text: David Huron（2006）提出西方音樂旋律的五種一般特性，與前述知覺及認知原則有關，但在不同音樂風格中會呈現略有差異的形式：
en: David Huron (2006) identifies five general properties of melodies in Western music that connect to the basic principles of perception and cognition listed above, but play out in slightly different ways in specific musical styles. They are:

title: 類種對位法入門
text: 音高鄰近性（pitch proximity）：旋律傾向於多級進、少跳進，多小跳、少大跳，呈現流暢性與旋律完整性。級進下行傾向（step declination）：旋律的下行級進往往多於上行級進。這可能與目標導向有關，因為我們常把向下移動感受為能量減少，也就是趨向休止。級進慣性（step inertia）：旋律持續同一方向的次數，往往多於改變方向；也就是多數音與音之間的進行，延續前一步的方向。這呈現流暢性，有時也呈現目標導向。旋律回歸（melodic regression）：位於極高或極低音域的音，傾向回到中間音域。若將較不極端的音視為休止，這便是向休止位置移動的表現。它也反映音高分布的統計現象：音越高，下方可供作曲家選擇的音越多，上方則越少。拱形旋律（melodic arch）：旋律傾向在樂句前半上行，達到高潮，再於後半下行。這呈現目標導向與「休止—運動—休止」的模式，也是前述原則在樂句中的綜合結果。
en: Pitch proximity: The tendency for melodies to progress by steps more than leaps and by small leaps more than large leaps. An expression of smoothness and melodic integrity. Step declination: The tendency for melodies to move by descending step more than ascending. Possibly an expression of goal-oriented motion, as we tend to perceive a move down as a decrease in energy (movement toward a state of rest). Step inertia: The tendency for melodies to change direction less frequently than they continue in the same direction. (That is, the majority of melodic progressions are in the same direction as the previous one.) An expression of smoothness and, at times, goal-oriented motion. Melodic regression: The tendency for melodic notes in extreme registers to progress back toward the middle. An expression of motion toward a position of rest (with non-extreme notes representing “rest”). Also an expression simply of the statistical distribution of notes in a melody: the higher a note is, the more notes there are below it for a composer to choose from, and the fewer notes there are above it. Melodic arch: The tendency for melodies to ascend in the first half of a phrase, reach a climax, and descend in the second half. An expression of goal orientation and the rest–motion–rest pattern. Also a combination of the above rules in the context of a musical phrase.

title: 類種對位法入門
text: 旋律與和聲寫作規則
en: Rules for melodic and harmonic writing

title: 類種對位法入門
text: 類種對位法既要寫出旋律線，也要將它們結合。下列各類種共用的規則，先整理前面討論的旋律事項，再列出後續各章要著重的和聲考量。
en: In species counterpoint, we both write and combine such melodic lines. The following set of rules invoked in all the species begins with the melodic matters discussed already, then presents some harmonic considerations that we will focus on in the following chapters.

title: 類種對位法入門
text: 旋律寫作：水平音程
en: Melodic writing (horizontal intervals)

title: 類種對位法入門
text: 每個練習都以級進接到最後的八度或同度，形成 clausula vera 終止式。限制下列情況的數量：連續同音：同一音高接連出現。非連續的同音重複：同一音高在整個練習中出現多次。連續跳進：接連出現三度以上音程；應以級進分隔。非連續跳進：短時間內跳進的總數，即使它們並不相連。連續重複同一音程度數：即使性質不同，也要注意，例如接連使用二度，而非一定都是小二度。控制旋律高潮，也就是最高音：每個旋律聲部力求只有一個獨特的高潮。避免在高潮音上結束。最好以跳進到達高潮。避免兩聲部同時到達各自的最高音。避免以下旋律跳進：增音程。減音程。任何七度。任何六度，但上行小六度或可例外。任何超過八度的音程。也要避免連續旋律勾勒出下列音程（譜例 4）：增音程。減音程。任何七度。
en: Approach the final octave/unison of each exercise by step (this creates the clausula vera). Limit the number of: consecutive, repeated notes: the same pitch more than once in a row non-consecutive repeated notes: the same pitch more than once across the whole exercise consecutive leaps: multiple intervals of a third or greater in a row (separate them with stepwise motion) non-consecutive leaps: the total number of leaps within a short span, even if they're not successive consecutive repeated generic intervals: the same interval size (e.g., second) even if not the same specific interval (minor second) Control the melodic climax (highest note): Aim for exactly one unique climax in each melodic part Avoid ending on that climax Preferably leap to that climax Avoid the two parts reaching their respective climax pitches at the same time Avoid melodic leaps of: an augmented interval a diminished interval any seventh any sixth, except perhaps the ascending minor sixth any interval larger than an octave Also avoid outlining (Example 4): an augmented interval a diminished interval any seventh

title: 類種對位法入門
text: 譜例 4。旋律勾勒出的音程。
en: Example 4. Melodic outlinings.

title: 類種對位法入門
text: 和聲寫作：垂直音程與聲部組合
en: Harmonic writing (vertical intervals and the combination of parts)

title: 類種對位法入門
text: 第一個音程應為完全同度、完全五度或完全八度；最後一個則應為完全同度或完全八度，不能是五度。兩聲部間距最多為十二度，也就是複五度；大部分時間應維持在八度內。避免聲部「重疊」，也就是名義上的上方聲部跑到下方聲部之下。務必避免：平行八度：兩聲部原本相隔八度，再同向移動相同度數，最後仍相隔八度。平行五度：兩聲部原本相隔完全五度，再同向移動相同度數，最後仍相隔完全五度。也應盡量避免：直接五度與直接八度：兩聲部由任何音程出發，同向進入完全五度或完全八度。除開頭與結尾之外，在練習中使用同度。
en: The first interval should be a perfect unison, fifth, or octave, and the last interval should be a perfect unison or octave (not fifth). Restrict the gap between parts to a twelfth (compound fifth) maximum, and to an octave for the most part. Avoid "overlapping" parts (where the nominally "upper" part goes below the "lower" one). Make sure to avoid: parallel octaves: when two parts start an octave apart and both move in the same direction by the same interval to also end an octave apart parallel fifths: when two parts start an perfect fifth apart and both move in the same direction by the same interval to also end a perfect fifth apart Also try to avoid: direct fifths and octaves: when two parts begin any interval apart and move in the same direction to a perfect fifth or octave unisons at any point in the exercise other than the first and last intervals

title: 類種對位法入門
text: 對位法的心理學
en: The Psychology of Counterpoint

title: 類種對位法入門
text: 類種對位法各章不以某個特定風格為目標，例如古典、巴洛克、浪漫、流行或搖滾。練習會暫時擱置配器、旋律動機、曲式，甚至許多和聲與節奏要素，專注於少數基本音樂問題。這些問題與聽覺知覺及認知原則密切相關，也就是大腦如何感知並理解聲音，以及這些原則如何呈現在西方音樂結構中。
en: The chapters on species counterpoint will not involve a specific style (classical, baroque, romantic, pop/rock, etc.). Instead, these exercises will set aside important musical elements like orchestration, melodic motives, formal structure, and even many elements of harmony and rhythm, in order to focus very specifically on a small set of fundamental musical problems. These fundamental problems are closely related to how some basic principles of auditory perception and cognition (i.e., how the brain perceives and conceptualizes sound) play out in Western musical structure.

title: 類種對位法入門
text: 例如，大腦傾向將音高或音色相似的聲音，視為出自同一來源。我們也會聆聽規律；新聲音若延續或完成先前聽到的模式，通常會被歸為同一組。這與人類經驗中根深蒂固的部分，乃至演化經驗有關。規律的聲音通常意味著環境可預測且安全；變化則可能暗示危險，使我們更加注意聲音來源。這套將注意力與腎上腺素反應導向最可能需要之處的機制，對人類生存至關重要。二十一世紀聆聽音樂，通常不必提防掠食動物，但作者認為，這些演化經驗仍有部分深植於聽覺心理，參與音樂情緒效果的形成，即使身處安全環境也如此。
en: For example, our brains tend to assume that sounds similar in pitch or timbre come from the same source. Our brains also listen for patterns, and when a new sound continues or completes a previously heard pattern, we typically assume that the new sound belongs together with those others. This is related to some of the most deep-seated, fundamental parts of our human experience, and even evolution. Hearing a regular pattern typically indicates a predictable (and safe) environment, while any change can signal danger and will tend to heighten our attention to the source. This system for directing attention (and adrenaline) where it is most likely to be needed has been essential to the survival of the human species. While listening to music in the 21st century does not (usually!) require us to listen out for animal predators, some part of that evolutionary experience is "hard-wired" into the psychology of human listening, and it has a role in what gives music its emotional effect—even in a safe environment.

title: 類種對位法入門
text: 對西方聽者而言，若音樂只讓大腦輕易分辨與處理聲音，就可能顯得無聊：不需要特別注意，也不會讓心跳加快、後頸汗毛豎起，或帶來一點多巴胺刺激。另一方面，持續觸發本能危險感的音樂，對多數聽者也很難稱得上愉快。因此，張力與放鬆、運動與休止之間的平衡，是本書所研究的大多數音樂的重要基礎。
en: For Western listeners, music that simply makes it easy for the brain to parse and process sound is boring—it calls for no heightened attention; it doesn’t increase our heart rate, make the hair on the back of our neck stand up, or give us a little jolt of dopamine. On the other hand, music that constantly activates our innate sense of danger is hardly pleasant for most listeners. That being the case, a balance between tension and relaxation, motion and rest, is fundamental to most of the music we will study.

title: 類種對位法入門
text: 對位法學習讓我們在嚴格限制的情境中處理幾個重要音樂問題，逐步培養能廣泛運用的作曲與分析能力。這些問題來自我們希望同時兼顧以下特質：
en: The study of counterpoint helps us to engage several important musical “problems” in a strictly limited context, so that we can develop composition and analytical skills that can then be applied widely. Those problems arise as we seek to bring the following traits together:

title: 類種對位法入門
text: 流暢而獨立的旋律線條。聲音融合：希望同時發聲的音形成協和的整體。多樣性。朝向目標的進行。
en: smooth, independent melodic lines tonal fusion (the preference for simultaneous notes to form a consonant unity) variety motion (towards a goal)

title: 類種對位法入門
text: 這些特質根植於人類知覺與認知，但在具體音樂時刻往往彼此衝突，需要放到較長段落或完整作品中取得平衡。對位法能幫助我們開始練習這種取捨。
en: These traits are based in human perception and cognition, but they are often in conflict in specific musical moments and need to be balanced over the course of larger passages and complete works. Counterpoint will help us begin to practice working with that balance.

title: 類種對位法入門
text: 最後，雖然練習經過抽象化，仍最好把它們視為小型作品並實際演出：用人聲或樂器，能與夥伴合奏更好。如此，耳朵、手指、喉嚨，乃至心智，才能內化旋律線條如何運作與結合的聲音、譜面與身體感受。
en: Finally, despite abstractions, it's still best to treat counterpoint exercises as miniature compositions and to perform them—vocally and instrumentally, and with a partner where possible—so that the ear, the fingers, the throat, and ultimately the mind can internalize the sound, sight, and feel of how musical lines work and combine.

title: 第一類對位法
text: 重點整理第一類對位法是一種傳統的作曲練習，讓初學者學習如何安排旋律的起始與結束，更重要的是，如何保持各條旋律的獨立性。寫作第一類對位法時，請遵守下列規則：以完全一度、完全五度或完全八度開始。兩個聲部以完全相同的速率進行，沒有節奏變化，例如全部使用全音符。在和聲方面，兩聲部之間的音程全部為協和音程。在旋律方面，以級進為主，偶爾才用跳進。禁止使用三全音或七度的旋律跳進。禁止平行的完全協和音程。以完全一度或完全八度結束。本章還會介紹其他原則，幫助你寫好第一類對位法。
en: Key Takeaways First-species counterpoint is a traditional compositional exercise that teaches beginning musicians to consider how to start and end melodic lines, and most importantly, how to keep them independent of each other. When writing in first species, follow these rules: Begin on a perfect unison, fifth, or octave. Both voices move at exactly the same rate and have no rhythmic variety (for example, all notes are whole notes). Harmonically, the intervals between the two voices are all consonances. Melodically, prefer stepwise motion and leap only occasionally. Melodic leaps of a tritone or seventh are forbidden. Parallel perfect consonances are forbidden. End with a perfect unison or octave. This chapter presents additional guidelines that will help in writing a successful first-species counterpoint.

title: 第一類對位法
text: 對位法將兩條以上的旋律協調成有意義且悅耳的整體。在第一類對位法中，我們要寫出流暢的旋律，使它本身具有完整的形狀、變化，以及朝向目標的進行；另一條旋律也要具備這些特質。更重要的是，兩條旋律結合後，整體織度也必須流暢、有變化、有方向感，而且各自保持獨立，同時又在每個同時發聲的位置融合成協和的音響。「同時發聲」（simultaneity）是兩個以上音符同時響起的通稱。寫作第一類對位法時，先有一條定旋律，可以自行新作，也可以採用既有旋律，再在它的上方或下方寫出一條新旋律，稱為對位聲部。定旋律的每個音都對應新聲部的一個音；兩個聲部一律使用全音符。因此，第一類對位法也稱為「一音對一音」或 1:1 對位法。
en: Counterpoint is the mediation of two or more musical lines into a meaningful and pleasing whole. In first-species counterpoint, we not only write a smooth melody that has its own integrity of shape, variety, and goal-directed motion, but we also write a second melody that contains these traits. Further, and most importantly, we combine these melodies to create a whole texture that is smooth, that exhibits variety and goal-oriented motion, and in which these melodies both maintain their independence and fuse together into consonant simultaneities (the general term for two or more notes sounding at the same time). In first-species counterpoint, we begin with a cantus firmus (new or existing) and compose a single new line—called the counterpoint—above or below it. That new line contains one note for every note in the cantus: both the cantus firmus and the counterpoint will be all whole notes. Thus, first species is sometimes called "one-against-one" or 1:1 counterpoint.

title: 第一類對位法
text: 對位聲部的旋律
en: The Counterpoint Line

title: 第一類對位法
text: 大致而言，對位聲部應遵循前一章〈類種對位法入門〉所述的良好定旋律寫作原則。下文會說明幾個細微的差異，但總的來說，第一類對位法的兩條旋律都應達到良好定旋律的標準。
en: In general, the counterpoint should follow the principles of writing a good cantus firmus discussed in the previous chapter, Introduction to Species Counterpoint. There are some minor differences, to be discussed below, but generally a first-species counterpoint should consist of two cantus-firmus-quality lines.

title: 第一類對位法
text: 範例 1 收錄《Gradus ad Parnassum》第一部分的全部第一類對位法練習。每個範例都採用前面介紹過的一條定旋律，並在上方或下方加上一條新的對位聲部。我們在各例中標出了對位聲部與定旋律之間的音程。《Gradus ad Parnassum》完整的練習、解答與註解，請見〈《Gradus ad Parnassum》練習〉。
en: Example 1 shows the complete exercises of first-species counterpoint from Part I of Gradus ad Parnassum. Each example sees one of the cantus firmi we've already met combined with a new counterpoint line either above or below. We've annotated each one with the interval that the counterpoint line makes with the cantus firmus. For the complete examples from Gradus ad Parnassum as exercises, solutions, and annotations, see Gradus ad Parnassum Exercises.

title: 第一類對位法
text: 起始與結束
en: Beginning and Ending

title: 第一類對位法
text: 第一類對位法的起始
en: Beginning a first-species counterpoint

title: 第一類對位法
text: 請注意，範例 1 中的每道練習都以完全協和音程開始，讓旋律一開始就有安定感。
en: Note that each exercise in Example 1 begins with a perfect consonance. This creates a sense of stability at the opening of the line.

title: 第一類對位法
text: 若對位聲部寫在定旋律的上方，第一個音應為 do [latex](\hat1)[/latex] 或 sol [latex](\hat5)[/latex]，也就是與定旋律構成完全一度（P1），或在其上方的完全五度（P5）、完全八度（P8）。
en: When writing a counterpoint above a cantus firmus, the first note of the counterpoint should be do [latex](\hat1)[/latex] or sol [latex](\hat5)[/latex] (a P1, P5, or P8 above the cantus).

title: 第一類對位法
text: 若對位聲部寫在定旋律的下方，第一個音必須是調式終音 do [latex](\hat1)[/latex]，也就是與定旋律同音，或低一個完全八度。如果從 sol [latex](\hat5)[/latex] 開始，會構成不協和的四度；從 fa [latex](\hat4)[/latex] 開始雖能構成完全五度，卻會讓聽者混淆調性，因為樂曲開頭的 fa–do [latex](\hat4-\hat1)[/latex] 很容易被誤聽成 do–sol [latex](\hat1-\hat5)[/latex]。
en: When writing a counterpoint below a cantus firmus, the first note of the counterpoint must always be on the modal final, do [latex](\hat1)[/latex] (P1 or P8 below the cantus firmus). Beginning on sol [latex](\hat5)[/latex] would create a dissonant fourth; beginning on fa [latex](\hat4)[/latex] would create a P5 but confuse listeners about the tonal context, since fa–do [latex](\hat4-\hat1)[/latex] at the beginning of a piece is easily misheard as do–sol [latex](\hat1-\hat5)[/latex].

title: 第一類對位法
text: 第一類對位法的結束
en: Ending a first-species counterpoint

title: 第一類對位法
text: 對位聲部的最後一個音必須是 do [latex](\hat1)[/latex]，也就是與定旋律同音，或高、低一個完全八度。
en: The final note of the counterpoint must always be do [latex](\hat1)[/latex] (P1 or P8 above/below the cantus).

title: 第一類對位法
text: 為了流暢地進入結尾，同時具有變化與明確的方向感，最後的音程一律以反向級進到達，方式如下：
en: To approach this ending smoothly, with variety, and with strong goal orientation, always approach the final interval by contrary stepwise motion, as follows:

title: 第一類對位法
text: 若定旋律以 re–do [latex](\hat2-\hat1)[/latex] 結束，對位聲部的最後兩個音應為 ti–do [latex](\hat7-\hat1)[/latex]。若定旋律以 ti–do [latex](\hat7-\hat1)[/latex] 結束，對位聲部的最後兩個音應為 re–do [latex](\hat2-\hat1)[/latex]。
en: If the cantus ends re–do [latex](\hat2-\hat1)[/latex], the counterpoint’s final two pitches should be ti–do [latex](\hat7-\hat1)[/latex]. If the cantus ends ti–do [latex](\hat7-\hat1)[/latex], the counterpoint’s final two pitches should be re–do [latex](\hat2-\hat1)[/latex].

title: 第一類對位法
text: 因此，倒數第二小節中，兩條旋律之間會構成三度或六度（範例 2）。這種結尾公式稱為 clausula vera 終止式。範例 1 中的每道練習都以這種終止式結束。
en: Thus, the penultimate bar will either be a third or a sixth between the two lines (Example 2). This ending formula is known as the clausula vera. The exercises in Example 1 each end with a clausula vera.
