title: 十六世紀的對位風格
text: 重點整理十六世紀的對位風格與類種對位法的原則有關，但兩者並不完全相同。本章介紹幾項重要原則與寫作練習，尤其著重模仿。
en: Key Takeaways The 16th-century contrapuntal style is related—but not identical—to the principles outlined in species counterpoint. This chapter sets out some key principles and practice exercises especially for imitation.

title: 十六世紀的對位風格
text: 十六世紀的對位風格，長久以來在樂理教學中占有重要地位。以十六世紀模仿式合唱複調為對象的「仿作」或「假想創作」（pastiche、counterfactual composition），尤其是仿寫 Palestrina 的風格，經常出現在課程中；有時也被混同於較晚、十八世紀形成的類種對位法觀念，也就是前幾章介紹的內容。本章提供一些實用原則，幫助你依據這類作品的風格，完成只給出部分樂譜的續寫練習。章末有幾道這種形式的範例練習。
en: The 16th-century contrapuntal style has historically enjoyed a prominent position in the teaching of music theory. "Pastiche" or "counterfactual" composition of 16th-century imitative choral polyphony (especially in the style of Palestrina) has frequently appeared in curricula and is sometimes conflated with the later, 18th-century notion of species counterpoint which we met in the previous chapters. This chapter sets out some rules of thumb to bear in mind when completing style-composition exercises based on this repertoire where you are given a partial score to complete. At the end, you'll find a couple of example exercises in this format.

title: 十六世紀的對位風格
text: 模仿
en: Imitation

title: 十六世紀的對位風格
text: 模仿是指兩個以上的聲部先後進入，唱出相同旋律或其變體。這是十六世紀對位音樂的常見手法，尤其常用於整個樂章的開頭，以及樂章內較大段落的起始，例如開始唱新的一行歌詞時。可以把它看成後來賦格的前身；我們會在〈巴洛克盛期賦格的呈示部〉一章再談這個主題。以下範例出自 Vicente Lusitano 的〈Ave spes nostra〉，收錄於《Liber primus epigramatum》（點此前往 IMSLP 查看來源）。[1]Lusitano〈Ave spes nostra〉開頭譜例靜態樂譜尚待補齊；原始資源含有本章必要的音樂範例。〈Ave Spes Nostra〉，由 openmusictheory 提供。在這段開頭，五個聲部都先後唱出一個配上「Ave spes nostra」歌詞的模仿樂思（point of imitation）。除了一些小改動，模仿大致精確。第一個進入的聲部從 F 開始，下行到 C；接著再唱一次同樣的歌詞，這次從 C 開始，以相似的旋律下行到 F，並在結尾多加一個音。其他聲部模仿的可能是這個次序——先 F–C，再 C–F——也可能把這一對次序反過來，先 C–F，再 F–C。範例結尾開始出現第二個模仿樂思，配上下一行歌詞「Dei genitrix…」。這個新音型形似迴音：原音、上方音、下方音、原音，即 C–D–B♭–C。接下來的段落便以第二個樂思為基礎。兩個樂句彼此重疊，也就是新樂句在前一樂句結束前就開始，這在此風格中很常見；第二個樂思的模仿也比第一個更自由。在範例顯示的最後一小節、兩個樂句重疊之處，甚至可以看到第一個樂思有幾個細微的節奏變化。完成涉及模仿的練習時，應以題目已提供的材料為依據，並考量以下原則：
en: Imitation involves two or more parts entering separately with the same melody, or versions of the same melody. This is a common practice in 16th-century contrapuntal music, particularly for beginning whole movements and large sections in those movements (with the introduction of a new line of text, for instance). You might think of it as a precursor to the later fugue (which we'll return to in the High Baroque Fugal Exposition chapter). Here is an example from Vicente Lusitano’s “Ave spes nostra” from the Liber primus epigramatum (click here for the source on IMSLP).[1] Musical example (requires internet)Static score pending; the original resource contains a musical example. Ave Spes Nostra by openmusictheory In this opening passage, a “point of imitation” setting the text “Ave spes nostra” appears in all five voices. The imitation is exact, give or take small changes. The first voice to enter starts on F and descends to C, then it repeats the text a second time, now starting on C and descending to F with a similar melody, adding one more note at the end. Other parts imitate either this pattern (F–C then C–F) or this pair the other way round (C–F, then F–C). The end of this example sees the start of a second imitative point setting the next line “Dei genitrix ... ”. This new figure has a “turn”-like shape: original note, note above, note below, original note (C-D-Bb-C). What follows is a sectnmio based on that second point. As is common in this style, the two phrase overlap (i.e., the new phrase begins before the end of the previous one) and the imitation for this second point is treated more freely than the first. You can even see a couple of subtle rhythmic changes to the first point in this last bar shown where this overlap takes place. When completing an exercise involving imitation, let the existing material be your guide and consider the following guidelines:

title: 十六世紀的對位風格
text: 辨識可能的模仿樂思：在每個聲部中，留意歌詞改變的位置，通常前面有逗號或休止符；尤其注意同樣歌詞搭配同樣音樂的重複。音高間隔：在一個段落或樂章開頭，模仿聲部之間通常相隔完全協和音程。不過，其他音程也完全可能，尤其在樂章較後面的部分。這裡談的是兩聲部主要材料的對應音程，不一定是最初兩個音之間的音程。有時會看到後來巴洛克盛期賦格典型的調性答題，詳見下一章。拍節：在拍節上相對應的位置模仿，強拍對應強拍，弱拍對應弱拍。判斷哪些模仿關係可行時，兩個方向的所有選項都試一試。以某個模仿樂思為主的段落常會和下一段重疊，因此交界處進入的聲部，可能使用另一個樂思。先後進入的模仿聲部之間，應有實質的重疊。若模仿樂思較短，各聲部進入的時間間隔也可能需要相應縮短。考慮要模仿多少內容。較長的旋律最終會從精確模仿樂思，轉為自由對位；本例在何處發生這項轉變？考慮模仿要多精確。至少盡量保留樂思開頭的節奏，以及具有辨識度的音程、輪廓或形狀。記住，即使在強烈的終止處，樂句與段落仍可能彼此重疊。
en: Identify (potential) points of imitation: In any given part, look for changes of text (often preceded by a comma or rest), and particularly any repetition of text with the same music. Pitch interval: The interval between imitative parts at the start of a section or movement is usually a perfect consonance. That said, others are eminently possible, especially later in the movement. Note that we are talking about the primary corresponding interval between the parts and not necessarily the very first pitch. We sometimes see examples of the tonal answer typical of the later high Baroque fugue, discussed in the next chapter. Meter: Imitate at metrically comparable positions (strong beat → strong beat; weak beat → weak beat). When working out what imitative relationships will work, try out all options in both directions. As the section governed by one imitative point often overlaps with the next, imitative entries around that section change may come from other point. Make sure there is meaningful overlap between consecutively entering imitative parts. To achieve that, shorter points of imitation may require correspondingly shorter intervals between entering parts. Consider how much of the point to imitate. Longer melodies eventually go from being a point to imitate exactly, to free counterpoint. Where does that change occur in this case? Consider how closely to imitate the point. Try to preserve at least the rhythm and the distinctive intervals/contour/shape of the point’s opening. Remember that phrases and sections can overlap, even at strong cadences.

title: 十六世紀的對位風格
text: 旋律
en: Melody

title: 十六世紀的對位風格
text: 聲部之間以反向進行為主，部分原因是要維持旋律的獨立性。即使音程本身容許使用，也應避免過多平行進行；但「fauxbourdon」是例外，它是較長一段平行 [latex]^6_3[/latex] 三和弦的寫法。聲部內以級進為主。大多數聲部以級進到達終音。在多數調式中，從下方到達終音時，須升高導音；弗里吉安調式則不適用。旋律音程：二度、三度、四度、五度與八度都可以使用。六度的情況較複雜。上行小六度使用得相當自由，在 Palestrina 的彌撒曲中出現 814 次；上行大六度較少，54 次；下行六度極為罕見，下行小六度僅 7 次，下行大六度只有 1 次。避免七度與三全音。即使不是直接跳進，也不要以連續跳進或旋律音型的最高、最低點勾勒出這些音程。通常避免同方向連續跳進。若確實使用，應讓較大的跳進位於較低的音域：上行時先作較大的跳進，下行時則後作較大的跳進。大跳之後應反方向進行，之前也常如此。這與填補跳進留下的音域空間（gap-fill），以及回到常用音域中間的傾向有關。避免像分解和弦那樣勾勒三和弦。輪廓：旋律常呈弧形，上行之後會再下行。各聲部的音域：常見建議是限制在八度內，對應樂曲調式的正格或變格音域。不過，實際作品中的聲部較常跨越稍寬的 14 個半音。極少聲部超過十二度，即八度加五度，因此可把十二度視為上限。常見旋律手法：掛留：保留的音先在弱拍位置作為協和音「預備」，再用延音線連到強拍的不協和音，最後讓持續該不協和音的聲部向下級進解決。7–6 與 4–3 掛留的不協和音位於上聲部；2–3 掛留則位於下聲部，是 7–6 的轉位。〈第四類對位法〉有進一步說明。五度到六度的斜向進行也很常見，但它不屬於不協和掛留。樂句結尾比開頭更常出現裝飾。
en: Contrary motion predominates between parts (partly to maintain independence of lines). Avoid too much parallel writing even of permitted intervals (but note the exceptional case of the "fauxbourdon," which is an extended passage of parallel [latex]^6_3[/latex] triads). Conjunct motion predominates within parts. Approach the final by step (in most parts). Raise the leading note when approaching the final from below (in most modal contexts, though not Phrygian). Melodic intervals: Seconds, thirds, fourths, fifths, and octaves are all permitted; The status of sixths is more complex. Rising minor sixths are used fairly freely (814 times in the Palestrina masses), rising major sixths are rarer (54 times), and descending sixths are extremely rare (7 descending minor, 1 single case of descending major). Sevenths and tritones are avoided. Do not even outline these intervals with successive leaps or by the boundaries (high and low points) of a melodic gesture. Successive leaps in the same direction are generally avoided. If you do have such successive leaps, then position the larger leap lower (first when rising, second when descending). Large leaps are to be followed (and often preceded) by motion in the opposite direction. This is connected to both the idea of gap-fill and regression to the middle of the tessitura. Avoid outlining triads as if you were arpeggiating chords. Contour: The arch shape is common for melodies (what goes up must come down!). Range per part: A common recommendation is to place each voice within an octave, corresponding to either the authentic or plagal ranges of the piece's mode. But in practice, parts more often span a slightly wider range of 14 semitones. Extremely few parts exceed the twelfth (octave plus fifth), so take that as a maximum. Common melodic devices: Suspensions: Suspended notes are to be "prepared" as a consonance on a weak metrical tied to a dissonance (on a strong position) and resolved by moving the suspended dissonant part down a step. For 7–6 and 4–3 suspensions, this involves dissonance in the upper voice; for 2–3 suspension, the dissonance is in the lower voice (as an inversion of 7–6). This is explained further in the chapter on fourth-species counterpoint. While not a suspension, the oblique motion from fifth to sixth is also common. Decorations at the end of a phrase are more common than at the beginning.

title: 十六世紀的對位風格
text: 節奏與拍節
en: Rhythm and Meter

title: 十六世紀的對位風格
text: 這類曲目的原始記譜沒有小節線，但拍節思維非常清楚。現代版本通常會加上小節線，請記住這是編輯所加，並非原貌。編輯也可能縮短基本拍動（tactus）所對應的記譜時值，例如從二分音符改為四分音符。理解這些前提後，編輯處理仍很有幫助：小節線方便排練與指揮，有些演出者也較習慣閱讀較短時值的音符。編輯選擇還可能帶來更細緻的提示，例如採用拍單位較長的拍號，以 [latex]\mathbf{^2_2}[/latex] 取代 [latex]\mathbf{^4_4}[/latex]，暗示可用較長的拍子思考，因此也可能容許持續較久的不協和音。旋律常以較慢的節奏進行開始，也經常如此結束。半個基本拍動的進行，此處指四分音符，應從較弱的拍節位置開始：非重音拍位（第二或第四拍），或拍與拍之間，例如附點節奏的一部分。延音線由較長的音符連到較短的音符，反向則不採用。較少出現的三拍子通常採 2+1 的節奏分組，而非 1+2；許多其他風格也如此。
en: The original notation for this repertoire lacks bar lines, but metrical thinking is abundantly clear. While modern editions will usually put bar lines in explicitly, remember that these are editorial interventions, not original. Editors may also change the tactus-level note values to be shorter than what was originally notated (from half to quarter notes, for instance). With those caveats borne in mind, the editorial intervention can be helpful—barlines are helpful for rehearsal and for conducting, and some performers may feel more comfortable reading in shorter note values. Editorial choices may also offer subtler hints, such as the use of "longer" meters ([latex]\mathbf{^2_2}[/latex] in place of [latex]\mathbf{^4_4}[/latex]) to hint at the possibility of thinking in terms of longer beat, and thus the possibility of longer dissonances, for instance. Melodic lines frequently start (and often end) with slower rhythmic movement. Half-tactus (quarter-note) movement should begin on weak metrical positions—on an unaccented beat (2 or 4), or between beats (as part of a dotted rhythm). Ties connect long notes to shorter ones (not vice versa). In the (relatively rare) cases of triple meter, rhythms generally divide into 2+1 rather than 1+2 (as in many styles).

title: 十六世紀的對位風格
text: 歌詞配置
en: Text Setting

title: 十六世紀的對位風格
text: 當時許多作曲家都非常重視音樂與歌詞的清晰。[2]拍節：雖然有上述記譜與編輯上的前提，仍應把重讀音節放在「強拍」，使語言與音樂的韻律相配。規律性的例外依循上文慣例，包括切分音、掛留，以及「拍節不一致」：某一聲部持續採用的拍節，與其他聲部主導的拍節相牴觸；後者通常也是現代版本記出的拍節。樂句依歌詞形成。每個音節通常至少使用一拍，此處為二分音符。附點節奏是例外：較短的四分音符經常有自己的音節。可以把它看成均勻節奏的變形，而原本均勻的節奏符合「每拍一個音節」的原則。比基本拍動更短的四分音符進行之後，立即更換音節的情況很少見。
en: Clarity of music and text was held in high regard by many composers of this time.[2] Meter: The above caveats notwithstanding, match textual and musical meters by placing strong syllables on "strong beats." Systematic exceptions follow the conventions outlined above including syncopations, suspensions, and "metrical dissonance" (use of a consistent meter in one part that is contrary to that prevailing in other parts (usually the one notated in modern editions). Musical phrases follow the text. Typically use at least one beat (half note) for each syllable. Exceptions include dotted rhythms, where the shorter (quarter) note frequently receives its own syllable. This may be thought of as a modification of a "straight" rhythm, which meets the "one per beat" guideline. Syllable changes immediately after sub-tactus (quarter-note) motion are rare.

title: 十六世紀的對位風格
text: 織度
en: Texture

title: 十六世紀的對位風格
text: 在這類練習中，題目已給出的聲部通常會清楚呈現適合的織度。粗略而言，彌撒曲各部分的織度大致有以下慣例。I 表示通常採模仿織度；H 表示可能較偏向主調織度：Kyrie〈垂憐經〉：I。Gloria〈光榮頌〉：H。「qui tollis」經常另成一段。Credo〈信經〉：H。重要時刻尤其常用主調織度。「Crucifixus」可以獨立成段。Sanctus〈歡呼歌〉：I；Hosanna〈賀三納〉：H。Benedictus〈讚美歌〉：I，常使用較少聲部。第二次 Hosanna 通常重複第一次的音樂。Agnus Dei〈羔羊頌〉：I。可能有第二、第三次 Agnus Dei，常增加聲部並使用卡農。Magnificat〈尊主頌〉通常是較自由的體裁，模仿樂思的處理也更有彈性。
en: The appropriate texture is usually clear from the given parts in these exercises. To generalize rather crudely, broad conventions for textures in Mass settings are as follows (where I = usually imitative; H = may be [more] homophonic): Kyrie (I). Gloria (H). The "qui tollis" frequently exists as a separate section. Credo (H). Especially often homophonic at important moments. "Crucifixus" separable. Sanctus (I). Hosanna (H). Benedictus (I). Often for fewer voices. (Second Hosanna usually a repeat of the first.) Agnus Dei (I). There may be a second or third Agnus, often with more parts and canons. The Magnificat tends to be a freer genre that is more flexible with the points of imitations.

title: 十六世紀的對位風格
text: 和聲
en: Harmony

title: 十六世紀的對位風格
text: 這個時期的作曲家，並不像今日常見的方式，以和弦、羅馬數字、轉位等概念思考；他們主要關注各聲部之間的音程關係。掌握這一點後，以下是此風格中聲部垂直結合的幾項原則。
en: Composers of this era did not think in terms of chords, Roman numerals, inversions, and so on the way that we typically do today. Instead, they were principally concerned with intervallic relationships among parts. With this in mind, following are some guidelines for the vertical combination of parts in this style.

title: 十六世紀的對位風格
text: 平行五度與平行八度：和後來的風格一樣，應予避免。不過，與後來的風格不同，涉及減五度的平行進行也必須避免。直接五度或八度：原則上應避免。有些人的解釋是，如果補入中間的經過音，就會顯露出其中暗含的平行。它們較常出現在終止處，或在其他一個以上聲部有明顯反向進行、足以緩和效果的情況。減三和弦：在 Palestrina 的作品中並不少見，多為第一轉位。例如多聲部音樂的終止處，低音以 [latex]\hat2-\hat1[/latex] 進行時，這是一種特別有用的處理方式。依一般聲部進行原則解決：re–do、ti–do、fa–mi [latex](\hat2-\hat1,\ \hat7-\hat8,\ \hat4-\hat3)[/latex]。不協和音的類型與處理：掛留：預備（弱拍）—掛留（強拍）—解決（弱拍）。「非主要」的不協和音：位於基本拍動之下、四分音符層次的經過音與鄰音。Nota cambiata，轉換音：通常為 do–ti–sol–la [latex](\hat8-\hat7-\hat5-\hat6)[/latex]。這是從不協和音跳進離開的唯一情況。最後的和弦：空五度或大三和弦（皮卡第三度）。升高的「皮卡」三度，大約起源於 1500 年：當時首次開始讓三音出現在樂曲最後的和弦中；到了十六世紀後半，這種做法已相當普遍（Apel 1969，677）。到了 Palestrina，大三和弦已是最常見的結尾和弦，在他的彌撒曲中約占 85%。
en: Parallel fifths and parallel octaves: Avoid, as in later idioms. However, unlike in later idioms, those involving diminished fifths must also be avoided. Direct fifths or octaves: Avoid in principle (some rationalize this on the basis that they imply parallels that would present if the intervening passing notes were added). More common at cadences and/or when mitigated by strong contrary motion in one or more other parts. Diminished triad: Used not infrequently in Palestrina’s music, mostly in first inversion. Useful especially as a solution for cadences in multi-part music with [latex]\hat2-\hat1[/latex] motion in the bass, for instance. Resolve according to standard voice-leading: re–do, ti–do, fa–mi [latex](\hat2-\hat1,\ \hat7-\hat8,\ \hat4-\hat3)[/latex]. Dissonance: types and treatment: Suspensions: preparation (weak beat) – suspension (strong) – resolution (weak). "Inessential" dissonances: passing tones, neighbor tones at the sub-tactus (quarter-note) level. Nota cambiata, "changed note": generally do–ti–sol–la [latex](\hat8-\hat7-\hat5-\hat6)[/latex]. The only case of a dissonance left by leap. Final chord: Bare fifth or major triad (picardy third). The raised ("Picardy") third "originated c. 1500 when for the first time, the third was admitted in the final chord of a piece … in the second half of the sixteenth century this practice became fairly common" (Apel 1969, 677). By Palestrina, major triads are the most common kind of final chord (accounting for around 85% of cases in the Palestrina masses).

title: 十六世紀的對位風格
text: 延伸閱讀Apel, Willi. 1969.〈Picardy Third〉。《Harvard Dictionary of Music》，第 2 版。麻薩諸塞州劍橋：Harvard University Press。
en: Further Reading Apel, Willi. "Picardy Third." 1969. Harvard Dictionary of Music. 2nd ed. Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press.

title: 十六世紀的對位風格
text: 線上資源
en: Online Resources

title: 十六世紀的對位風格
text: 除了 IMSLP 等知名樂譜圖書館，也有一些專門研究文藝復興音樂的有趣計畫。
en: In addition to well-known libraries like IMSLP, there are some interesting projects dedicated specifically to Renaissance music.

title: 十六世紀的對位風格
text: 其中值得注意且與本章密切相關的是 Citations: The Renaissance Imitation Mass Project（CRIM，文藝復興模仿彌撒曲計畫）。你可以在那裡瀏覽廣泛的相關曲目、精美的現代版本與相關資訊。若想以類似的整理方式探索稍早的曲目，可以瀏覽 Josquin Research Project（JRP，Josquin 研究計畫）。
en: Perhaps most notable and relevant is Citations: The Renaissance Imitation Mass Project (CRIM), where you can explore a wide range of relevant repertoire in attractive, modern editions, along with related information. For a similar curatorial approach to a slightly earlier repertoire, you may wish to explore the Josquin Research Project (JRP)

title: 十六世紀的對位風格
text: 作業
en: Assignments

title: 十六世紀的對位風格
text: 十六世紀對位風格的模仿寫作（PDF、MuseScore 檔 .mscz）。題目至少提供一個完整聲部供參考，另有一個聲部缺少部分樂段，須依適當風格補完。練習保留原始音符時值，配上對應時值的現代拍號 [latex]\mathbf{^4_2}[/latex]，並加入少數編輯補定的變音（ficta），只使用 G 譜號與 F 譜號。
en: Imitative writing in the 16th-century contrapuntal style (.pdf, .mscz). These exercises provide at least one complete part for reference, and one part with missing passages to complete in a suitable style. Original note values are used, with modern time signatures for those values ([latex]\mathbf{^4_2}[/latex]), some editorial accidentals (ficta), and only G and F clefs.

title: 十六世紀的對位風格
text: IMSLP 只把這首編為第「10」首。查閱原始分譜時，須注意依書中次序，各聲部的編號如下：Supranus 為 24（「XXIIII」，名稱與編號均照原文）；Altus 為 26（「XXVI」）；Tenor 為 25（「XXV」）；Bassus 為 23（「XXIII」，照原譜，儘管原始目錄頁寫的是 22）；Quinta Pars 為 25（「XXV」）。其餘聲部不適用。本轉寫採用現代記譜，但保留原始音高與音符時值。↵據說 Palestrina 尤其重視這一點；也有說法認為，他因此平息了特倫托大公會議審視當時音樂新發展時的疑慮。↵
en: IMSLP has this numbered simply as No. “10”, but if consulting the source, note that the parts are numbered as follows in book order: Supranus 24 (“XXIIII”, name and numbering sic), Altus 26 (“XXVI”), Tenor 25 (XXV”), Bassus 23 (XXIII, sic even though the source index page says 22), and Quinta Pars 25 (XXV), remaining parts not applicable. The transcription is in modern notation, but preserves original pitch and note values. ↵This is said to be especially true of Palestrina, and further said to have appeased the Council of Trent in its review of recent developments in music. ↵

title: 巴洛克盛期賦格的呈示部
text: 重點整理賦格是一種對位音樂體裁，至少從十八世紀起便相當盛行。本章介紹開頭呈示部的幾項重要原則。新術語包括以下幾個；點選術語可前往術語表：主題答題對題呈示部也會介紹一些熟悉術語在賦格中的特定用法，尤其是：聲部SATB
en: Key Takeaways The fugue is a contrapuntal genre popular since at least the 18th century. This chapter sets out some key principles of the opening exposition section. We introduce new terms including these (click on the term for the glossary entry): Subject Answer Countersubject Exposition We also meet some fugue-specific variants of familiars terms, notably: Voices SATB

title: 巴洛克盛期賦格的呈示部
text: 接著，我們從十六世紀常見的模仿手法轉向賦格。可以把賦格看成十八世紀對應這項傳統、並承繼它的形式。不同賦格之間的差異很大，因此「賦格」其實很難有令人完全滿意的定義。一般而言，賦格是嚴格維持一定數目獨立聲部的對位作品，各聲部逐一進入，陳述賦格的主要旋律，也就是主題。本章將賦格視為一種寫作過程，從基本原理出發，示範如何建構賦格的第一部分。我們會依 Bach、Handel 及其同時代作曲家的「巴洛克盛期」技法，介紹根據既定主題寫作賦格呈示部的基礎。
en: We now move on from imitative practices common in the 16th century to the fugue, which may be thought of as the 18th-century equivalent and successor to this tradition. Fugues can vary quite a bit, and thus "fugue" is a surprisingly difficult term to define satisfactorily. Fugues in general are contrapuntal compositions that are defined by the strict use of a certain number of independent voices; each voice enters one by one, stating the main theme (subject) of the fugue. In this chapter, we will treat fugue as a process and show how to construct (the first part of) a fugue from first principles. This chapter deals with the basics of writing a fugal exposition from a given subject according to the "high Baroque" technique of Bach, Handel, and their contemporaries.

title: 巴洛克盛期賦格的呈示部
text: 基本定義
en: Basic Definitions

title: 巴洛克盛期賦格的呈示部
text: 先定義本章會用到的幾個術語。
en: First, let's define some of the terms we'll need.

title: 巴洛克盛期賦格的呈示部
text: 主題：構成賦格旋律基礎的一小段旋律，會在全曲中反覆出現。答題：主題的移調版本，有時也略作修改，下文會進一步說明。對題：與主題或答題同時發聲、並與之相配的旋律線。呈示部：賦格的第一部分，各聲部在此先後以主題或答題進入。請注意，這與奏鳴曲式的「呈示部」不同；兩者都是最初陳述主要材料的段落，但其他方面並不相同。聲部：獨立的對位旋律線，可以由樂器演奏，也可以由人聲演唱。對位聲部數不一定等於樂器分譜或演出者的人數：由一人演奏的鍵盤賦格，可以有三、四、五、六個聲部；甚至還有小提琴獨奏賦格，這在作曲上相當不容易！SATB：即使賦格沒有歌者參與，四聲部織度仍慣用 S（女高音）、A（女低音）、T（男高音）、B（男低音）依高至低稱呼各條旋律。它們的音域不必與人聲聲部完全一致。
en: Subject: A short tune that forms the melodic basis of a fugue, recurring throughout. Answer: A transposition of the subject that is also sometimes slightly altered, as discussed below. Countersubject: A melodic line that is sounded with (and complements) the subject/answer. Exposition: The first part of a fugue, during which each of the voices enters with the subject or answer. Note that this is distinct from the use of the term “exposition” in sonata form; they both refer to a first section setting out the main material, but they otherwise differ. Voices: The separate contrapuntal lines, which may be either instrumental or vocal. The number of voices does not necessarily correspond to the number of parts or musicians involved—a keyboard fugue for one player may have three, four, five, or six voices, and there are even some fugues for solo violin (which is quite a compositional feat!). SATB: Although a fugue may not involve any singers, it is customary to refer to the lines in a four-voice texture with S (soprano), A (alto), T (tenor), and B (bass) from highest to lowest. The ranges do not need to match those of the vocal parts exactly.

title: 巴洛克盛期賦格的呈示部
text: 結構與聲部進入
en: Structure / Voice Entries

title: 巴洛克盛期賦格的呈示部
text: 賦格呈示部的基本運作如範例 1：一個聲部先奏出主題，下一個聲部再以答題進入，同時第一個聲部繼續奏出對題，依此類推。
en: Basically, the fugal exposition works as shown in Example 1: one voice begins with the subject, then the next voices enters with the answer while the first continues with a countersubject, and so on.

title: 巴洛克盛期賦格的呈示部
text: 聲部 1主題對題自由對位聲部 2答題對題聲部 3主題
en: Voice 1 Subject Countersubject Free counterpoint Voice 2 Answer Countersubject Voice 3 Subject

title: 巴洛克盛期賦格的呈示部
text: 範例 1。賦格開頭各聲部進入次序的假設示意。
en: Example 1. Hypothetical structure of voice entries at the beginning of a fugue.

title: 巴洛克盛期賦格的呈示部
text: 請注意，這裡的聲部依進入次序編號。從最高聲部到最低聲部、或從最低到最高依序進入，都很常見，但不是硬性要求。不過，新聲部進入時，應成為當下的最高或最低聲部，因此中間聲部——女低音或男高音——最後才進入的情況並不常見。這仍留下許多選擇。例如，四聲部賦格可以採用：
en: Note that the voices are numbered according to the order in which they enter. While it is perfectly common for the voices to enter in order from highest to lowest or lowest to highest, this is not strictly necessary. However, when a new part enters, it should be the highest or lowest voice at that stage, so it is uncommon for an inner part (alto or tenor) to enter last. That leaves us plenty of options. For instance, the order of voice entries in a four-voice fugue could be:

title: 巴洛克盛期賦格的呈示部
text: 依音域由高至低：SATB；或由低至高：BTAS。從中間的女低音開始：ASTB、ATSB、ATBS。從中間的男高音開始：TBAS、TABS、TASB。
en: In register order from highest to lowest (SATB), or vice versa (BTAS) Starting in the middle with the alto: ASTB, ATSB, ATBS Starting in the middle with the tenor: TBAS, TABS, TASB

title: 巴洛克盛期賦格的呈示部
text: 若主題或答題的進入次數超過全曲聲部總數，額外的陳述稱為「附加進入」（redundant entries）。
en: Any further subjects/answers entering (beyond the total number of voices) are described as "redundant" entries.

title: 巴洛克盛期賦格的呈示部
text: 主題
en: Subject

title: 巴洛克盛期賦格的呈示部
text: 決定如何處理主題時，先觀察它的結構與性格。
en: When considering how to handle a subject, look at its structure and character.

title: 巴洛克盛期賦格的呈示部
text: 主題的結構常可分為三部分。和許多調性樂句一樣，它從具有辨識度的開頭，逐漸走向較通用的終止：
en: The structure of a subject can often be thought of in three parts. Like many tonal phrases, the subject charts a course from a distinctive opening to a generic cadence:

title: 巴洛克盛期賦格的呈示部
text: Kopfmotiv：字面意思是「頭部動機」，指開頭的動機或音型。Fortspinnung：延展，可能以模進或持續推進的動力節奏（motor rhythm），延續前面的材料，形成延長。終止。
en: Kopfmotiv (literally "head motive"): an opening gesture Fortspinnung: prolongation that may include sequence and/or motor rhythm Cadence

title: 巴洛克盛期賦格的呈示部
text: 主題的性格可包括：
en: Types of character include:

title: 巴洛克盛期賦格的呈示部
text: 觸技曲風格：有動力節奏的持續推進感，常帶有半音化特徵，節奏落點也可能不規則。利切爾卡（ricercar）風格：源於素歌與經文歌傳統，進行緩慢，帶有古雅感，並大量使用掛留。
en: Toccata style: this has a motor-rhythm feel, is often chromatic, and may have irregular rhythmic placement. Ricercar: deriving from the plainsong/motet tradition, this is slow moving, has an antiquated feel, and makes extensive use of suspensions.

title: 巴洛克盛期賦格的呈示部
text: 答題
en: Answer

title: 巴洛克盛期賦格的呈示部
text: 答題分為兩種：真實答題（real answer）是主題的精確移調；調性答題（tonal answer）則在移調之外另作修改。
en: We distinguish between two types of answer: real for an exact transposition, and tonal for one that has been altered further.

title: 巴洛克盛期賦格的呈示部
text: 真實答題直接將原主題移高完全五度或移低完全四度，音符之間的所有音程度數關係都保持不變。
en: A real answer simply transposes the original subject by perfect fifth/fourth. All generic intervallic relationships remain the same between the notes.

title: 巴洛克盛期賦格的呈示部
text: 主題若有以下情況，就需要調性答題：
en: We need a tonal answer if the subject:

title: 巴洛克盛期賦格的呈示部
text: 以 sol [latex](\hat5)[/latex] 開始，或在開頭其他位置突出使用它。這時須調整移調版本，使 sol [latex](\hat5)[/latex] 不往上移到 re [latex](\hat2)[/latex]，而改為 do [latex](\hat1)[/latex]。開頭以其他方式暗示 V–I。主題中突出的屬音，在答題中成為主音，因此主到屬的 T → D 進行，常會變成屬到主的 D → T，反之亦然。主題有轉調。這時將它分為各屬一個調的兩個樂句，分別作適當調整。若主題結尾轉到屬調，答題就必須轉回主調。
en: starts on sol [latex](\hat5)[/latex] or otherwise uses it prominently at the outset. In this case, we must adjust the transposed version such that sol [latex](\hat5)[/latex] is not transposed up to re [latex](\hat2)[/latex], but instead to do [latex](\hat1)[/latex]. includes any other V–I suggestion at start. Prominent dominant note in subject becomes tonic note in answer, so T → D progressions often become D → T and vice versa. modulates. In this case, split the subject into two phrases, one in each key, and adapt accordingly. If the subject modulates at its end to the dominant, the answer must modulate back to the tonic.

title: 巴洛克盛期賦格的呈示部
text: 無論哪種情況，都應只作最少的必要修改，讓主題與答題盡可能相似，而且兩者在旋律上都合理。
en: In all cases, we seek to make minimal adjustment such that the subject and answer are still as alike as possible, and both make melodic sense.

title: 巴洛克盛期賦格的呈示部
text: 對題
en: Countersubject

title: 巴洛克盛期賦格的呈示部
text: 先試著寫出對題的骨架，再補齊細節。一下子寫出漂亮的旋律，後來卻發現它無法搭配主題，會很令人挫折。此外，搭配主題與搭配答題的兩個版本，要同時構思；對題與主題配合得很好，遇到答題卻在和聲上不通，也同樣令人沮喪。
en: Try working up a skeletal version of your countersubject first before fully fleshing it out. It's frustrating to dash off a lovely tune and then realize that it doesn't fit. Additionally, sketch the version that will go with the answer at the same time as the version that goes with the subject. It's just as frustrating to write a countersubject that works beautifully with the subject but which the answer makes harmonically nonsensical.

title: 巴洛克盛期賦格的呈示部
text: 對題固然是一條旋律，但只有在和聲上也合理時才成立。請記住，對題第一次出現時只有兩個聲部，因此應考慮如何只用兩條旋律，仍清楚勾勒出更完整的和聲，例如三和弦與七和弦。
en: Indeed, countersubjects are melodies, but they only work if they make sense harmonically as well. To that effect, remember that your countersubject will first appear in a two-voice passage, so consider how best to outline clear larger harmonies (triads and sevenths) with only two voices.

title: 巴洛克盛期賦格的呈示部
text: 你也可以為自己增加一項限制：讓對題能作八度轉位，也就是放在主題上方或下方都能成立。若如此，寫作時也要同時檢查兩個版本，尤其注意：
en: You may wish to set yourself the additional constraint of a countersubject which is invertible at the octave—basically, one that can appear above or below the subject and still work. In this case, again work on both versions as you go, and specifically make sure to:

title: 巴洛克盛期賦格的呈示部
text: 避免五度，因為五度轉位後成為四度，而兩聲部寫作對四度有特別限制。主要使用同度與其轉位八度、三度與其轉位六度；涉及七和弦時，也可使用二度與七度。自由聲部中的五音不造成這個問題，因此可把補齊和弦所需的五音留給自由聲部。同樣地，避免 4–3 掛留，因為轉位後成為 5–6，第一個音程不再不協和。改用可以互相轉位的 7–6 與 2–3 掛留。
en: Avoid fifths, because fifths invert to fourths, which have special rules in two-voice writing. Stick to unisons (/ octaves), thirds (/ sixths), and in the case of seventh chords, also seconds (/ sevenths). The fifth is not a problem in the free part, so "reserve" that note as the completion of the chord and use it there. Similarly, avoid 4–3 suspensions, because the first note is not dissonant when inverted (5–6). Instead, use 7–6 and 2–3 suspensions (which invert to each other).

title: 巴洛克盛期賦格的呈示部
text: 要寫出對題骨架，先找出主題本身的骨架型態。將主題簡化成未加裝飾的形式，把它視為一種調性定旋律，再據此寫出對位，也就是對題骨架；之後再加以裝飾，形成更有趣的旋律。
en: To create your skeletal countersubject, first look for skeletal patterns in the subject. Find the simple, unembellished form of the subject and treat it as a kind of tonal cantus firmus against which to write your counterpoint (skeletal countersubject), which you can then embellish into a more interesting musical line.

title: 巴洛克盛期賦格的呈示部
text: 加上裝飾時，試著做到：
en: When it comes to embellishing, try to:

title: 巴洛克盛期賦格的呈示部
text: 對題的寫法應符合主題的性格。建立互補的節奏進行，讓一個聲部停留時，另一個聲部移動。對題從搭配主題改為搭配答題時，只在主題與答題確實不同的位置，作相應的必要修改。
en: be true to the character of the subject when composing the countersubject establish complementary rhythmic motion such that one voices moves while the other is stationary make changes to the countersubject when moving between subjects and answers only and exactly where those changes appear in the subject/answer

title: 巴洛克盛期賦格的呈示部
text: 自由對位
en: Free Counterpoint

title: 巴洛克盛期賦格的呈示部
text: 坦白說，「自由」對位這個名稱有些名不副實。尤其當對題還要能轉位時，主題與對題會把可選的寫法限制得很窄。這個聲部的「自由」，是指它之後不一定反覆出現；相較於更不自由的主題與對題，不妨把它理解成比較自由的聲部！你也可以選擇更嚴整的安排，用之後會再出現的第二個固定對題，取代自由對位。
en: Frankly, the idea of "free" counterpoint is a bit of a misnomer, especially if you're writing an invertible countersubject, because the subject and countersubject will leave your options highly constrained. This part is "free" in the sense that it doesn't necessarily recur later on, so you might like to think of it as a freer part, relative to the even less free subject and countersubject! Alternatively, you can embrace the extreme order and replace the free counterpoint with a second regular countersubject that does recur later.

title: 巴洛克盛期賦格的呈示部
text: 連接段
en: Links

title: 巴洛克盛期賦格的呈示部
text: 在賦格呈示部中，主題與答題的各次進入之間，可以插入短小的音樂段落，稱為連接段。連接段經常使用主題中的動機，例如讓短片段以模進方式反覆。它可以出現在任意幾次、甚至所有聲部進入之間，長度也可以不同。
en: Your fugal exposition may include short interpolations between the subject/answer entries. We call these links. Links frequently make use of a motive from the subject, for instance with sequential repetition of a short fragment. They may appear between any or all voice entries and may be of varying lengths.

title: 巴洛克盛期賦格的呈示部
text: 加入一個或多個連接段，可以有許多音樂上的理由。它能讓你：
en: There are many musical motivations for including one or more links. Links provide an opportunity to:

title: 巴洛克盛期賦格的呈示部
text: 改變和聲：前一次主題或答題的結尾，可能無法在和聲上直接銜接下一次的開頭；這時可以用連接段走到所需的和聲位置。改變音域：例如旋律持續下行時，可以用連接段重新調整音域，避免超出樂器的範圍。改變樂句長度：若主題正好兩小節，各聲部只是連續依序進入，可以加上連接段，使超小節拍節與樂句分組更有變化。不過，各聲部仍應在拍節相對應的位置進入；例如主題若以弱起開始，至少在呈示部中，所有主題與答題也應如此。銜接聲部進入：除了改變樂句長度，也可以改變聲部進入時的旋律環境。例如連接段以模進發展頭部動機，而下一次主題或答題正好以同一動機開始，就能順暢地接入。
en: Change harmony: The end of one subject/answer and the beginning of the next may not match up harmonically. In that case, you can use the link to get where you need to be. Change register: If you have a continually descending line, for instance, links can be a useful way of resetting the register so you don’t go outside the instrument’s range. Vary the phrase lengths: If you have a subject of exactly two measures and just proceed through several voices entering successively, then you may well want to use a link to make the hypermetrical and phrase groupings a little more interesting. That said, the voices should always enter on metrically comparable positions: for example, if your subject comes in on a pickup, all the subject/answer entries should do the same, at least in the exposition. Dovetail entries: Apart from varying the phrase lengths, we can also vary the melodic context in which a voice enters. For instance, if a link develops the Kopfmotiv sequentially, then you can bring in the next subject/answer in seamlessly, as it begins with that motive.

title: 巴洛克盛期賦格的呈示部
text: 一般寫作考量
en: General Matters

title: 巴洛克盛期賦格的呈示部
text: 除了賦格特有的考量，許多一般調性音樂的寫作原則也適用。尤其記得：
en: Apart from the specific considerations of the fugue, naturally much of the general practice of writing (tonal) music applies here. Remember in particular to:

title: 巴洛克盛期賦格的呈示部
text: 控制節奏流動：當某個時值層次的連續進行已建立起來，例如四分、八分或十六分音符，須仔細考慮是否適合中斷，以及何時中斷。安排終止的相對強弱，例如藉由控制最高、最低聲部的音階級數。寫法應符合演奏樂器的特性，並顧及手指可跨的距離、樂器音域等實際限制。
en: Control rhythmic flow: If and when continuous use of a given metrical level has built up (e.g., quarter/eighth/sixteenth notes), consider carefully whether and when it is appropriate to discontinue that motion. Graduate the relative strength of cadences, for instance by controlling the scale degrees in the top and bottom voices. Write idiomatically for the instrument/s. Remember to observe practical limitations of hand span, instrument range, and the like.

title: 巴洛克盛期賦格的呈示部
text: 作品範例
en: Example

title: 巴洛克盛期賦格的呈示部
text: 以下用範例 2 觀察上述手法的實際運用：Bach《平均律鍵盤曲集》第一冊的 C 小調賦格，BWV 847。
en: For an example of all of this in action, let's consider Example 2: the C minor fugue from Book I of Bach's Well-Tempered Clavier (BWV 847).

title: 巴洛克盛期賦格的呈示部
text: Bach：C 小調賦格 BWV 847 呈示部譜例靜態樂譜尚待補齊；原始資源含有本章必要的音樂範例。
en: Musical example (requires internet)Static score pending; the original resource contains a musical example.

title: 巴洛克盛期賦格的呈示部
text: 範例 2。Johann Sebastian Bach：C 小調賦格 BWV 847 的呈示部。
en: Example 2. Exposition of the Fugue in C minor (BWV 847) by Johann Sebastian Bach.

title: 巴洛克盛期賦格的呈示部
text: 請注意：
en: Note that:

title: 巴洛克盛期賦格的呈示部
text: 呈示部涵蓋第 1–8 小節；此處節錄也包含後續「插部」（episode）的開頭。所有主題與答題的進入，都用藍色符頭標示。共有兩個固定的對題，標為 CS1 與 CS2。答題是調性答題。第二與第三次進入之間的連接段，即第 5–6 小節，以及最後一個聲部進入後、從第 9 小節開始的插部，都以主題中的動機作模進發展，圖中以括線標出。
en: The exposition runs from from measures 1–8 (the extract here includes the start of the following "episode"). All the subject and answer entries are highlighted with blue noteheads. There are two regular countersubjects (annotated as CS1 and CS2). The answer is tonal. The link between entries 2 and 3 (mm. 5–6) and the episode following the last voice to enter (starting in m. 9) are built on sequential handling of a motive from the subject, as indicated with brackets.

title: 巴洛克盛期賦格的呈示部
text: 線上資源
en: Online Resources

title: 巴洛克盛期賦格的呈示部
text: 前往 dezrann.net 可以瀏覽這首 Bach 賦格的完整版，附有譜面註記，以及與譜面對齊的實際演出錄音。你可以選擇方便閱讀的現代記譜版本，各賦格聲部分列於不同譜表，也可以跟著 Bach 的手稿閱讀。
en: Head to dezrann.net for a full version of this Bach fugue, complete with on-score annotations and an aligned audio recording of a real performance. You can even choose between using this friendly version in modern notation with the fugal voices on separate staves, or following along with Bach's manuscript.

title: 巴洛克盛期賦格的呈示部
text: 作業
en: Assignments

title: 巴洛克盛期賦格的呈示部
text: 上面的 Bach C 小調賦格使用調性答題。根據本章對調性答題的說明，試著解釋主題與答題有何不同，以及為何要這樣改。選另一首賦格，辨識它有幾個聲部，找出每個聲部的進入位置，以及呈示部的結束位置。試著自行寫作答題與對題。下方範本收錄《平均律鍵盤曲集》兩冊全部 48 首賦格的主題，並附一行空白的第二譜表，供你練習。請注意，許多主題的最後一個音只有符頭、沒有符幹，表示只指定音高，不限定節奏時值。若其中有你很熟悉的賦格，可以改選較不熟悉的曲目練習。對答題與對題的寫作較有把握後，再試著寫出完整呈示部。同樣可以選擇較不熟悉的賦格主題。
en: In the Bach C minor fugue shown above, the answer is "tonal." Given what has been said about tonal answers in this chapter, try explaining how the subject and answer differ, and why. Pick another fugue, identify how many "voices" there are, and locate each voice's entry and the end of the exposition. Try writing your own answers and countersubjects. The template file below provides the subjects for all 48 fugues in both books of the Well-Tempered Clavier. An empty second staff is provided for your practice. (Note that the last note in many of the fugue subjects is given without a stem to indicate the pitch without specifying the duration rhythm.) If you know some of these fugues well, you may want to work on ones you're less familiar with. Once you are feeling confident with writing answers and countersubjects, try writing up a full exposition. Again, you may wish to work on fugues you're less familiar with.

title: 巴洛克盛期賦格的呈示部
text: 第 3、4 題可以把自己的答案與 Bach 的寫法比較。但 Bach 的解法並不是唯一可能，因此不必期待自己寫出完全相同的音樂。也請注意，並非每首賦格都有固定、可轉位的對題。可直接下載 MuseScore 檔 .mscz 或 PDF 格式。
en: For 3 and 4, you may wish to compare your solutions to Bach's. Note that Bach's solutions are not the only possible ones, so don't expect to come up with exactly the same music. Note too that not every fugue has a regular invertible countersubject. Here are direct downloads in .mscz and .pdf formats.

title: 固定低音
text: 重點整理固定低音作品有一條在全曲中持續反覆的低音旋律。本章著重巴洛克音樂中的固定低音，例如三重奏鳴曲；作曲家透過低音上方各聲部的織度與和聲改變，創造變化，尤其包括：為低音重新配和聲，常藉此暗示其他調的局部主音化。讓上方聲部活潑地模仿、互相應答。
en: Key Takeaways Ground bass compositions have a bass line that repeats continually throughout. This chapter focussed on the use of grounds in baroque context (like trio sonatas) where variety is created through textural and harmonic change in parts above the bass line, notably with: re-harmonisation of the bass, often to suggest local tonicizations of other keys; lively imitation and interplay between the upper parts.

title: 固定低音
text: 固定低音作品以一條貫穿全曲、反覆出現的低音旋律為基礎，通常每次完全相同，或幾乎相同。許多音樂家都喜歡這種寫作限制，讓自己再怎麼發揮，腳下仍有一塊穩固的基礎！
en: Ground bass compositions are based on a bass line that repeats throughout the piece, usually exactly, or nearly so. Many musicians have found this a compelling compositional constraint for keeping themselves ... well ... grounded!

title: 固定低音
text: 究竟有多少音樂家採用這種手法？它在巴洛克時期非常盛行，Purcell 尤其熱衷且精於此道；近年的流行歌曲中更常見，參見〈流行音樂的和聲圖式〉，兩個時期之間的例子也不少。這是一種流行程度高、而且歷久不衰的形式。
en: How many musicians are we talking about? Well, this practice was highly popular in the Baroque (Purcell was a particularly keen and expert protagonist), it is even more common in popular songs of recent years (see Harmonic Schemas in Pop Music), and there are more than a few examples from in between. In short, it is an extremely and enduringly popular form.

title: 固定低音
text: 「固定低音」容易與其他術語混淆。從最廣泛到較特定的概念，應區分：
en: It's easy to confuse "ground bass" with some other terms; going from broad to specific, the key terms to distinguish are:

title: 固定低音
text: 頑固音型（ostinato）：任何在一個聲部中，貫穿長段落或全曲反覆出現的型態，例如 Ravel《波麗露》中作為標誌的小鼓節奏。固定低音（ground bass）：頑固音型的一種，低音旋律在整首作品或一個段落中反覆。整首作品也可以稱為固定低音曲。夏康舞曲（chaconne）與帕薩卡利亞（passacaglia），以及「Chacony」等各國不同拼法：巴洛克固定低音曲的子類型。除了其他特徵，兩者都是三拍子。每首夏康或帕薩卡利亞都是固定低音曲，而每個固定低音也是頑固音型；但反過來並不成立：不是每個頑固音型都是固定低音，也不是每首固定低音曲都是夏康或帕薩卡利亞。
en: Ostinato: any pattern that repeats throughout a long section or whole work in one voice, like the motto side drum rhythm of Ravel’s Boléro. Ground bass: a specific type of ostinato in which a bass line repeats throughout a work or section. The work itself can also be called a ground bass. Chaconne and Passacaglia (and international variant spellings such as "Chacony"): sub-genres of the Baroque ground bass. Among their other characteristics, both of these two are in triple meter. Every Chaconne or Passacaglia is also a ground bass, and every ground bass is also an ostinato, but the reverse is not true: not every ostinato is a ground bass, and not every ground bass is a Chaconne or Passacaglia.

title: 固定低音
text: 本章提供檔案與寫作指引，幫助你探索如何寫出有效果的固定低音作品。我們以巴洛克模式為主，透過多種方式為同一條低音重新配和聲，並改變織度，創造變化。
en: This chapter provides some files and instructions to help you explore some of the ways to create effective ground bass compositions. We focus on the Baroque model, and on creating variety through re-harmonizing the same bass in different ways and varying the texture.

title: 固定低音
text: 同一條低音的多種和聲配置
en: Multiple Harmonizations of a Given Bass

title: 固定低音
text: 全曲不停反覆同一條低音旋律，可能變得乏味，尤其容易讓和聲停滯。因此，有創意的作曲家會為同一條低音重新配和聲，藉此轉往其他調，或至少暗示這種轉向。這常取決於如何從不同角度重新理解低音中的同一個音程。
en: Continually using the same repeating bass line throughout could get tedious, and is especially liable to make the harmony extremely static. To that effect, inventive composers find ways to re-harmonize the same bass line to move to other keys, or at least hint at such a move. This often relies on seeing the different ways in which a single interval in the bass could be reinterpreted.

title: 固定低音
text: 雖然可用材料看似不多，這份低音和聲配置速查表（PDF）卻顯示，低音音程有許多重新配和聲的方式。它依低音音程編排，從小二度到三全音，每個音程都列出上行與下行形式。請注意，速查表是幫你找出選項，絕對不需要全用！下文將看到 Purcell 如何只用其中幾種，在一首很長、幾乎始終維持 G 小調的作品中創造和聲變化。我們特別關注他如何避開固定低音每輪首尾原本主要的正格終止，讓兩輪之間銜接得較不明顯，從而同時改變和聲與樂句節奏。
en: While this might not seem like much to work with, this bass harmonization "cheat sheet" (PDF) shows that there are many ways to re-harmonize bass intervals. It is organized by bass interval: both ascending and descending forms of each interval from minor seconds to tritones. Note that this is supposed to help you work out your options—you definitely don't need to use all of these! We'll see below how Purcell uses just a few of these to create harmonic variety in a very long work that's almost entirely in G minor. We'll be especially interested in moments where Purcell avoids the main perfect cadence at the start/end of each iteration of the ground, joining two grounds together with a subtler seam and thereby varying not only the harmony but also the phrase rhythm of the piece.

title: 固定低音
text: 分析：Purcell《G 小調奏鳴曲》，Z 807
en: Analysis: Purcell's Sonata in G Minor (Z 807)

title: 固定低音
text: 為了探索這些選擇，我們來看 Purcell 的《G 小調奏鳴曲》（Z 807），觀察他如何大量使用模仿，並偶爾採用主音化。這些分析也以文字標註在樂譜相應位置（範例 1）。
en: To explore some of the options here, let's take a look at Purcell's Sonata in G Minor (Z 807). We'll look at how Purcell uses (extensive) imitation and (occasional) tonicization. All of these matters are also included on the score as text annotations at the relevant moment (Example 1).

title: 固定低音
text: Purcell《G 小調奏鳴曲》Z 807 分析譜靜態樂譜尚待補齊；原始資源含有本章必要的音樂範例。

title: 固定低音
text: 和聲
en: Harmony

title: 固定低音
text: 和聲方面，全曲幾乎始終明確維持 G 小調，但 Purcell 在過程中將幾個其他調的主音暫時突出。若採這種分析，可以把主音化位置列為以下各項；個別判定仍有討論空間：
en: Harmonically, the piece is resolutely in G minor almost throughout, though Purcell tonicizes several keys along the way. The full list of tonicizations is (arguably):

title: 固定低音
text: 第 17 小節：D 小調。第 27 小節：F 大調。第 28 小節：B♭ 大調。第 33 小節：C 小調。第 78 小節：E♭ 大調。第 87 小節：F 大調。第 88 小節：E♭ 大調。第 93 小節：C 小調。第 107 小節：D 小調。第 117 小節：F 大調。第 131 小節第三拍，以及第 133 小節：C 小調。第 158 小節：E♭ 大調。第 163 小節：E♭ 大調。
en: Dmi in measure 17 F in measure 27 B♭ in measure 28 Cmi in measure 33 E♭ in measure 78 F in measure 87 E♭ in measure 88 Cmi in measure 93 Dmi in measure 107 F in measure 117 Cmi in measure 131 (beat 3) and in measure 133 E♭ in measure 158 E♭ in measure 163

title: 固定低音
text: 特別注意，Purcell 如何避開再一次 G 小調正格終止，巧妙處理固定低音每輪首尾的交界。例如，第 16、106 小節使用原文所稱的 G 大和弦，作為 V[latex]^4_2[/latex]/v–v6 的一部分，大致對調主與屬的功能；第 26、86 小節則使用原文所稱的 G 減和弦，形成 F 大調的 viio6–I。這些特殊情況都已在譜上標示。
en: Notice especially how Purcell finesses that boundary between the start and end of a ground iteration by avoiding yet another perfect cadence in G minor. For instance, see m. 16 and m. 106 for uses of G major as part of V[latex]^4_2[/latex]/v–v6, broadly reversing tonic and dominant function, and likewise m. 26 and m. 86 for G diminished as viio6–I in F major. These special cases are marked on the score.

title: 固定低音
text: 再從較大的範圍觀察：Purcell 在旋律聲部中廣泛使用 5–6 級進，並藉此使和聲產生歧義，例如第 1、12 小節。5 或 6，究竟哪個屬於和弦？還是兩者都屬於和弦？判斷是否始終相同，或會隨情境改變？這些都讓和聲的身分與更換位置不易完全確定，也為樂譜增加更多層次的趣味；同時有助於建立如第 71 小節起的一連串 7–6 掛留。
en: As a wider matter, notice how extensively Purcell uses 5–6 steps in the melodic parts and how this creates ambiguity in the harmony, as in m. 1 and m. 12. Is the 5 or the 6 harmonic, or perhaps both? Is this consistent, or does it change? This all makes it harder to pin down exactly what the harmony is and where it changes, adding ever further layers of interest to the score. It also helps set up the sequences of 7–6 suspensions such as from m. 71.

title: 固定低音
text: 模仿
en: Imitation

title: 固定低音
text: 模仿貫穿全曲。譜上的「D」與「C」標示旋律模仿，分別是 dux（先行者）與 comes（跟隨者）的縮寫。例如，第一小提琴在第 1 小節第一拍開始一條旋律，第二小提琴於第 3 小節第一拍進入，模仿它。
en: Imitation is prevalent throughout. The melodic imitations are labeled "D" and "C" on the score. This is short for dux (leader) and comes (follower). For instance, the violin 1 parts starts a melodic line in measure 1 (beat 1), which is imitated by the violin 2 entering in measure 3 (beat 1).

title: 固定低音
text: 請注意，這些模仿經常在小節內相同的拍位開始，與我們在十六世紀和十八世紀模仿傳統中討論的做法一致。在相對應拍位進入，會讓各次進入的時間間隔成為三拍或六拍，即表中的進入間隔拍數（beat gaps）。不過，Purcell 偶爾也會使用更緊密的模仿，見第 36、41、56、63、71、133、171、178、181、182 小節。
en: Notice how often these imitations start in the same part of the bar. This is consistent with what we discussed in the context of 16th-century and 18th-century imitative traditions. Entering on equivalent beats leads to temporal gaps between entries of three or six beats (beat gaps on the table). Then again, note how Purcell occasionally uses closer imitation in measures 36, 41, 56, 63, 71, 133, 171, 178, 181, and 182.

title: 固定低音
text: 如譜所示，本曲有大量模仿；幾乎每一輪固定低音，都伴隨上方聲部新的模仿關係，例外列在下方第二張表。最特別、最有意思的兩處或許是：
en: As the score shows, there is a great deal of imitation in this piece; almost every iteration of the ground is accompanied by a new imitative relationship in the upper parts (the exceptions are given in the second table below). Perhaps the two most special and interesting cases are:

en: the double imitation starting in m. 196 and imitated with parts swapped in m. 201 the imitation of the ground itself in the violin 2 part at m. 99/102

title: 固定低音
text: 節奏與拍節
en: Rhythm and Meter

title: 固定低音
text: 最後，請注意 Purcell 如何持續變換節奏時值與拍節層次，使用廣泛的選擇：第 36 小節開始連續八分音符，第 81、146 小節開始十六分音符，第 126 小節使用切分音，第 136 小節使用附點節奏；接近結尾的一段，第 166–185 小節，還把記譜拍號改為複拍子。這是巴洛克固定低音曲及當時其他變奏性作品的常見手法。這些改變通常，但並非總是，與新一輪固定低音的開始同時發生。
en: Finally, note how Purcell continually varies the rhythmic values (metrical levels) involved, using a wide range of options. This includes introducing continuous eighth notes (m. 36), sixteenth notes (m. 81 and m. 146), syncopation (m. 126), dotted rhythms (m. 136), and for one passage near the end, changing the notated meter to compound time (mm. 166–185). This is a common device in Baroque ground bass (and other variations-style works of the time); again, these changes usually (but not always) coincide with the start of a new iteration of the ground.

en: Take a template and try to compose your own ground bass composition, following these steps:

title: 固定低音
text: 先用簡單的柱式和弦，為固定低音配置以自然音為主的和聲，並確保聲部進行良好，把它當作初步版本。再寫一組不同的和聲配置，包含其他調的主音化；尤其嘗試替第一個音重新配和聲，以改變聽起來的樂句長度，如上文速查表所述。寫出與低音相配、能形成更有趣織度的旋律聲部。尋找上方聲部可在另一聲部以模仿方式再現的寫法，也可回顧前面的 Purcell 分析尋找靈感。最後，選出最好的構想，整合成一首兼顧織度與和聲趣味、並有整體發展方向的作品。不妨試寫六輪固定低音，讓第一輪與最後一輪簡單而相似。
en: A simple, predominantly diatonic harmonization of the ground, with simple block chords, making sure to follow good voice-leading practice. Use this as a prototype. A set of alternative harmonizations including tonicizations of other keys and re-harmonizations of the first note in particular to vary the apparent phrase length (as discussed above in reference to the "cheat sheet"). Melodic parts that fit with the bass and create more interesting textures. Seek out ways of writing upper parts that can recur in another voice in imitation (and refer back to the Purcell analysis above for ideas!). Finally, combine the best of your ideas into an overall piece that balances textural and harmonic interest and charts an overall trajectory. Why not try a piece with six iterations of the ground, of which the first and last are simple and alike?

title: 嘉蘭特圖式
text: 重點整理圖式是基本的音樂型態。十八世紀的作曲家與即興演奏者會學習並運用它們，作為創作新音樂的簡單基礎。這些型態種類很多，通常與音樂中的特定位置或功能有關，例如用於開頭。
en: Key Takeaways Schemas are basic musical patterns that composers and improvisers of the 18th century would learn and use as a simple basis for creating new music. There are many types of patterns, and they are typically associated with a particular place or function within the music, for instance as a way of beginning.

title: 嘉蘭特圖式
text: 圖式是「慣用的音樂樂句」（Gjerdingen 2007，6），提供旋律、和聲及節奏／拍節的骨架，供人創作嘉蘭特風格的新音樂。「圖式」可以有三種具體含義。第一，它是原型，也就是某種常見型態的理想化版本；第二，它可以是實例，也就是與原型相似的某個具體型態；第三，它可以是理論，用來解釋經常出現的音樂現象。理解圖式時，這三種觀念會一起運作：我們把某個具體型態，也就是實例，看成一般理想型態，也就是原型的一個版本；這種關係又幫助我們理解它在特定樂段中如何發揮作用，也就是理論層面。
en: Schemas are “stock musical phrases” (Gjerdingen 2007, 6) that act as melodic, harmonic, and rhythmic/metric skeletons for creating new music in the Galant style. We can apply the term "schema" in three specific ways. First, a schema is a prototype—an idealized version of a common pattern. Second, a schema can be an exemplar—a single pattern that resembles the prototype. Third, a schema can be a theory—an explanation of a commonly occurring musical event. All of these ideas go into how we understand schemas. We understand an individual pattern (exemplar) as a version of an ideal general pattern (prototype), and that relationship helps us understand how that pattern is functioning within a particular passage of music (theory).

title: 嘉蘭特圖式
text: 圖式常有名稱。有些根據早期理論家的描述命名，例如 Joseph Riepel 描述過 Monte、Fonte 與 Ponte；有些則以理論家的姓名命名，例如 Meyer 圖式取名自 Leonard Meyer。
en: Schemas are often given names, sometimes based on descriptions from earlier theorists (the Monte, Fonte, and Ponte were described by Joseph Riepel, for example) or, at other times, named after theorists themselves (the Meyer is named after Leonard Meyer).

title: 嘉蘭特圖式
text: 定義圖式時，既要看其中發生什麼，也要看它通常出現在作品的哪個位置。「發生什麼」涉及兩個以上的「階段」，大致就是相繼發生的音樂事件，包含：
en: Schemas are defined both by what happens in the schema and by where it typically appears in a piece. The "what" part involves two or more "stages" (basically, events) and includes:

title: 嘉蘭特圖式
text: 旋律特徵：以音階級數表示，通常同時列出最高的旋律聲部與最低的低音聲部。和聲特徵：以數字低音記號表示。拍節特徵：標示各階段位於小節強拍（S）或弱拍（W）。
en: melodic features, shown by scale degrees, usually for both the top (melodic) and bottom (bass) voices; harmonic features, shown with figured bass notation metric features, showing whether a stage occurs on a strong ("S") or weak ("W") beat of the bar

title: 嘉蘭特圖式
text: 「出現位置」大致區分為通常用於樂曲開頭的起始圖式、用於延續的圖式，以及作為結尾的終止圖式。本章各介紹一種類型；〈嘉蘭特圖式摘要〉則列出更多例子。
en: The "when" part basically distinguishes between schemas that are typically used to start a piece ("opening gambits"), as a "continuation," or as a concluding "cadence." This section introduces one of each type, and the Galant Schemas – Summary chapter sets out many more examples.

title: 嘉蘭特圖式
text: 起始圖式：以 Meyer 為例
en: Opening Gambits Such as the Meyer

title: 嘉蘭特圖式
text: Meyer 是起始圖式的一例，共有四個階段。第一與最後階段是主和弦，中間兩個階段則不是。以下彙整它的旋律、和聲與拍節：
en: The Meyer is an example of an opening schema. It is four stages long: the first and last are tonic chords, and the two in the middle are not-tonics. Here's a summary of what the melody, harmony, and meter do during this schema:

title: 嘉蘭特圖式
text: 階段 1 2 3 4 拍節 W S W S 旋律 do [latex]\hat1[/latex] ti [latex]\hat7[/latex] fa [latex]\hat4[/latex] mi [latex]\hat3[/latex] 低音 do [latex]\hat1[/latex] re [latex]\hat2[/latex] ti [latex]\hat7[/latex] do [latex]\hat1[/latex] 數字低音 [latex]^5_3[/latex] [latex]^4_3[/latex] [latex]^6_5[/latex] [latex]^5_3[/latex] 羅馬數字 I V V I
en: Stage 1 2 3 4 Meter W S W S Melody do [latex]\hat1[/latex] ti [latex]\hat7[/latex] fa [latex]\hat4[/latex] mi [latex]\hat3[/latex] Bass do [latex]\hat1[/latex] re [latex]\hat2[/latex] ti [latex]\hat7[/latex] do [latex]\hat1[/latex] Figures [latex]^5_3[/latex] [latex]^4_3[/latex] [latex]^6_5[/latex] [latex]^5_3[/latex] Roman numerals I V V I

title: 嘉蘭特圖式
text: 這個圖式可以分成兩部分：先是從 I 走向 V 的開頭部分：
en: We can break this schema down into two parts, a first, opening one that moves from I to V:

title: 嘉蘭特圖式
text: 階段 1 2 拍節 W S 旋律 do [latex]\hat1[/latex] ti [latex]\hat7[/latex] 低音 do [latex]\hat1[/latex] re [latex]\hat2[/latex] 數字低音 [latex]^5_3[/latex] [latex]^4_3[/latex] 羅馬數字 I V
en: Stage 1 2 Meter W S Melody do [latex]\hat1[/latex] ti [latex]\hat7[/latex] Bass do [latex]\hat1[/latex] re [latex]\hat2[/latex] Figures [latex]^5_3[/latex] [latex]^4_3[/latex] Roman numerals I V

title: 嘉蘭特圖式
text: 接著是從 V 回到 I 的收束部分：
en: ... and a closing part moving back from V to I:

title: 嘉蘭特圖式
text: 階段 1 2 拍節 W S 旋律 fa [latex]\hat4[/latex] mi [latex]\hat3[/latex] 低音 ti [latex]\hat7[/latex] do [latex]\hat1[/latex] 數字低音 [latex]^6_5[/latex] [latex]^5_3[/latex] 羅馬數字 V I
en: Stage 1 2 Meter W S Melody fa [latex]\hat4[/latex] mi [latex]\hat3[/latex] Bass ti [latex]\hat7[/latex] do [latex]\hat1[/latex] Figures [latex]^6_5[/latex] [latex]^5_3[/latex] Roman numerals V I

title: 嘉蘭特圖式
text: 如〈嘉蘭特圖式摘要〉所示，還有許多型態與 Meyer 相似的圖式，例如 Pastorella、Jupiter、Aprile。它們都從主和弦開始，中間兩階段離開主和弦，最後再返回。與 Meyer 一樣，它們是起始主題第一個樂句的原型，而且低音與和聲結構不像旋律那麼固定。這三種圖式的中間兩階段都可能表現屬和聲；第二階段也常搭配屬前和聲。
en: As the Galant Schemas – Summary chapter shows, there are many other schemas with a similar pattern to the Meyer, such as the Pastorella, the Jupiter, and the Aprile. In each of these cases, the schema starts with a tonic chord, moves away for two stages, and then returns to the tonic at the end. Like the Meyer, they are prototypes for the first phrase of an opening theme. As with the Meyer, the bass and harmonic structure are less fixed than the melody. The two central stages may articulate dominant harmony in all three schemas, and the second stage is also commonly accompanied by predominant harmony.

title: 嘉蘭特圖式
text: 若 Meyer 的每個階段各占一小節，它常出現在起始主題的呈示部或前句中。若每小節包含兩個階段，Meyer 可能只構成一個基本樂思，後面再接收束音型，例如下文的 Prinner。
en: When each stage of a Meyer schema is given one measure of music, it is commonly found in the presentation or antecedent part of an opening theme. If those stages occur at the rate of two per measure, the Meyer may form a basic idea that would be followed by a closing gesture, such as the Prinner described below.

title: 嘉蘭特圖式
text: 收束音型：以 Prinner 為例
en: Closing Gestures Such as the Prinner

title: 嘉蘭特圖式
text: Prinner 是起始圖式之後的典型回應。它有四個階段，對應四個低音：fa–mi/me–re–do [latex](\hat4–\hat3–\hat2–\hat1)[/latex]。旋律通常以平行十度搭配低音，形成 la/le–sol–fa–mi/me [latex](\hat6–\hat5–\hat4–\hat3)[/latex]。和聲方面，低音 fa（[latex]\hat4[/latex]）與 do（[latex]\hat1[/latex]）通常搭配 [latex]^5_3[/latex] 和弦；中間的 mi/me（[latex]\hat3[/latex]）與 re（[latex]\hat2[/latex]）則搭配 [latex]^6_3[/latex] 和弦。第三階段常有 7–6 掛留：
en: The Prinner is a typical response to an opening schema. It has four stages corresponding to four bass notes: fa – mi/me – re – do [latex](\hat4–\hat3–\hat2–\hat1)[/latex]. The Prinner’s melody typically accompanies the bass in parallel tenths: la/le – sol – fa – mi/me [latex](\hat6–\hat5–\hat4–\hat3)[/latex]. Harmonically, the fa ([latex]\hat4[/latex]) and do ([latex]\hat1[/latex]) bass notes tend to take [latex]^5_3[/latex] chords while the two middle bass notes, mi/me ([latex]\hat3[/latex]) and re ([latex]\hat2[/latex]), take [latex]^6_3[/latex] chords. There is often a 7–6 suspension on the third stage:

title: 嘉蘭特圖式
text: 階段 1 2 3 4 拍節 S W S W 旋律 la/le [latex]\hat6[/latex] sol [latex]\hat5[/latex] fa [latex]\hat4[/latex] mi/me [latex]\hat3[/latex] 低音 fa [latex]\hat4[/latex] mi/me [latex]\hat3[/latex] re [latex]\hat2[/latex] do [latex]\hat1[/latex] 數字低音 5 6 7-6 I 羅馬數字 IV I vii I
en: Stage 1 2 3 4 Meter S W S W Melody la/le [latex]\hat6[/latex] sol [latex]\hat5[/latex] fa [latex]\hat4[/latex] mi/me [latex]\hat3[/latex] Bass fa [latex]\hat4[/latex] mi/me [latex]\hat3[/latex] re [latex]\hat2[/latex] do [latex]\hat1[/latex] Figures 5 6 7-6 I Roman numerals IV I vii I

title: 嘉蘭特圖式
text: Prinner 有幾種變體，其中一種將 Prinner 移高五度，用來轉向屬調。在這個版本中，第一階段仍是 [latex]^5_3[/latex] 和弦，也仍可視為下屬和弦 IV，但此時是相對於屬調而言。
en: There are a few variants on the Prinner, including one that modulates to the dominant by using a version of the Prinner transposed up a fifth. In this version, the first stage of the Prinner is still a [latex]^5_3[/latex] chord and can also still be viewed as a subdominant (IV) chord, but now relative to the dominant key.

title: 嘉蘭特圖式
text: Prinner 也可以用來從主調轉到屬調，這種變體稱為「轉調 Prinner」：
en: The Prinner can also be used to modulate from the tonic to the dominant. This variant is called the Modulating Prinner:

title: 嘉蘭特圖式
text: 階段 1 2 3 4 拍節 S W S W 旋律 mi [latex]\hat3[/latex] re [latex]\hat2[/latex] do [latex]\hat1[/latex] ti [latex]\hat7[/latex] 低音 do [latex]\hat8[/latex] ti [latex]\hat7[/latex] la [latex]\hat6[/latex] sol [latex]\hat5[/latex] 數字低音 [latex]^5_3[/latex] 6 7-♯6 [latex]^5_3[/latex] 主調中的羅馬數字 I V vii/V V 屬調中的羅馬數字 IV I vii I
en: Stage 1 2 3 4 Meter S W S W Melody mi [latex]\hat3[/latex] re [latex]\hat2[/latex] do [latex]\hat1[/latex] ti [latex]\hat7[/latex] Bass do [latex]\hat8[/latex] ti [latex]\hat7[/latex] la [latex]\hat6[/latex] sol [latex]\hat5[/latex] Figures [latex]^5_3[/latex] 6 7-♯6 [latex]^5_3[/latex] RNs in the tonic key I V vii/V V RNs in the dominant key IV I vii I

title: 嘉蘭特圖式
text: 其他類型
en: Other

title: 嘉蘭特圖式
text: 除了起始與收束圖式，還有通常用於延續、終止的圖式，甚至有一種常見的終止後圖式。〈嘉蘭特圖式摘要〉提供主要類型的例子，以及其他變體與細節。上面的抽象表格很適合說明圖式是什麼，但看看實際記譜也很有幫助。以下提供簡單的和聲實現，讓你探索這幾章所談的圖式：
en: Apart from schemas for opening and closing, others are typically used for "continuation" and "cadences," and we even have one common "post-cadential" type. The Galant Schemas – Summary chapter provides examples of the main types, along with information about further variants and details. Additionally, while abstract layouts like the tables above are best for setting out what these schemas are, it's obviously also useful to check them out in musical notation. Here is a simple realization for exploring the schemas discussed in these chapters:

title: 嘉蘭特圖式
text: 附和弦的 Partimenti 圖式原型譜例以下為原作者提供的兩頁靜態譜面，對應線上譜例的20種圖式。Mark Gotham 與 FourScoreAndMore.org 採 CC0 公眾領域貢獻宣告。 原作者 PDF至原來源查看譜例／圖片 ↗第1頁：起始圖式，以及回應、延續、過渡圖式。至原來源查看譜例／圖片 ↗第2頁：終止前與終止圖式。圖中文字：Partimenti Prototypes＝Partimenti 原型；Opening＝起始；Answer/Process/Transition＝回應／延續／過渡；Pre-Cadential＝終止前；Cadential＝終止。Modulating Prinner＝轉調 Prinner；Deceptive Cadence＝假終止；Evaded Cadence＝迴避終止；Converging Cadence＝匯合終止。其他專名與本章及摘要中的圖式名稱對照。頁尾表示 Mark Gotham 與 FourScoreAndMore.org 以 CC0 放棄本文件的著作權利。

title: 嘉蘭特圖式
text: 學習圖式，確實需要親手練習。
en: Learning schemas really calls for hands-on practice.

title: 嘉蘭特圖式
text: 演奏：先把提供檔案中的範例演奏一遍，最好在幾個不同調上練習。原文說明：MuseScore 可從 Notes／Transpose 功能表移調。記憶：試著記住一些型態，可用以下方式自我測試：寫在紙上，先從空白音階開始。不看譜，憑記憶演奏。裝飾：圖式幫助音樂形成結構，但本身還不算完整樂曲；從骨架到真正的音樂，需要補上許多細節。因此，試著在這些基本型態上即興加裝飾，從簡單的迴音、經過音等開始，再嘗試更大的改變。完整樂曲：熟悉個別圖式後，試著依它們通常出現的位置與次序組合成曲。可以先使用以下範本：範本 1：PDF。範本 2：.mscz、.mxl、PDF。
en: Playing: Begin by playing through these examples from the files provided, preferably in a range of different keys. (Note: you can transpose scores in MuseScore with the Notes menu: Notes/Transpose). Memorization: See if you can memorize some of these patterns. Test yourself by: writing them out on paper (start with a blank scale) playing them from memory Embellishment: Schemas help to structure music, but they are not really musical pieces in themselves: it takes a lot of fleshing out to get from these skeletons to real music. That being the case, try improvising embellishments of these basic patterns. Start with simple turns, passing notes and the like, then move on to more ambitious changes. Full pieces: When you're confident with individual cases, try piecing them together, according to their usual position and ordering. Start by using templates like these: Template 1: .pdf Template 2: .mscz, .mxl, .pdf

title: 嘉蘭特圖式
text: 每份範本都結合了幾種圖式，可以視為樂曲的原型；既示範圖式如何運作，也為風格仿作練習提供框架。使用這些範本時，要在骨架上加入豐富的音樂性格與裝飾。以下是幾個入門建議：
en: These templates each provide a combination of schemas which can be thought of as prototype pieces, both to illustrate how they work and as a template for scaffolding exercises in pastiche composition. Use these templates, but bury them beneath layers of musical character and embellishment. Here are some tips for getting started:

title: 嘉蘭特圖式
text: 節奏：選一個有特色的節奏，作為全曲基礎並經常使用，但不要每次完全相同，看看能變出多少種樣貌。旋律：加入裝飾，例如在某些級進中加入迴音，或填入大跳之間的音。伴奏：以一種以上有特色的型態配置和弦伴奏，例如阿爾貝提低音。織度：尤其在較長的作品中，改變同時出現的聲部數，以及它們之間的關係。
en: Rhythm: Try picking a single characteristic rhythm to serve as the basis for your piece and use it often (but not exactly: see how many different ways you can adapt it). Melody: Introduce embellishments, decorating some stepwise motions with turns, for instance, and filling in some large leaps. Accompaniment: Use one or more characteristic patterns for chordal accompaniments, like the Alberti Bass. Texture: Particularly for longer pieces, vary the number of voices present and the way they relate.

en: Key Takeaways There are many different schemas. This chapter provides an introductory overview of the main ones along with some (brief) discussion of variants and details.

title: 嘉蘭特圖式摘要
text: 這些檔案收錄一組圖式，盡可能以接近原型的方式記譜：列出旋律與數字低音，第一組檔案另外在中間聲部加上和弦，實現那些數字。樂譜當然有用，但圖式其實是獨立於任何具體實現的原型，因此表格等較抽象的表示方式，在某些方面更合適。這也是本章及其他相關文獻以這種方式呈現圖式的原因。
en: These files provide a set of schemas, with the constituent parts set out as prototypically as is possible in musical notation: that is, with melody and figured bass lines, along with (in the first file's case) chords in a middle part realizing those figures. Musical notation is obviously useful, though really, schemas are prototypes that exist apart from any specific realization, so the more abstract representations in tables and the like are better in some ways. That's why you'll see them set out in this fashion here and in other literature on this topic.

title: 嘉蘭特圖式摘要
text: Fonte 與 Meyer、乃至五度循環都有密切關係。它先將原文所稱的 A 小調主音化，例如上主音的小調，再將低一個全音的大調主音化，也就是全曲的主調。可獨立取用的基本部分，就是其中一次主音化：
en: The Fonte has a strong relation to the Meyer and indeed to the cycle of fifths. This effectively tonicizes the A minor key (e.g., the supertonic minor) and then a major key a tone below (the overall tonic). The modular part is just one of those tonicizations:

title: 嘉蘭特圖式：八度法則與音階的模進配和聲
text: 八度法則
en: The Rule of the Octave

title: 嘉蘭特圖式：八度法則與音階的模進配和聲
text: 「八度法則」是圖式與 partimento 傳統的重要部分。可以把它想成低音配和聲的速查表：每個音階級數各有對應和弦，只要把低音與相應和弦配起來，就能完成不少工作。
en: The "Rule of the Octave" is an important part of the schema/partimento tradition. You might like to think of it as a kind of cheat sheet for harmonizing bass lines: there's one chord for each scale degree, and you can go a long way by just matching up those bass notes with their corresponding chord.

title: 嘉蘭特圖式：八度法則與音階的模進配和聲
text: 八度法則的和聲配置有許多略有差異的版本。這裡主要依據 Fedele Fenaroli 的版本（拿坡里，1775），只作少數調整，使全程聲部數一致，含低音共四部，並避免任何暗示平行禁則的進行。
en: There are many, subtly different versions of the Rule of the Octave harmonization. The version used here is closely based on that of Fedele Fenaroli (Naples, 1775), with just a couple of modifications to preserve a consistent number of voices throughout (four voices, including the bass) and to avoid any suggestion of parallels.

title: 嘉蘭特圖式：八度法則與音階的模進配和聲

title: 嘉蘭特圖式：八度法則與音階的模進配和聲
text: 檔案下載：.mscz、.mxl、PDF。我們從簡單原則開始，以平行 [latex]^6_3[/latex]，也就是第一轉位和弦，逐步建立這個版本的八度法則。可以把它理解成從缺少層次的和聲，走向層次豐富的和聲；也可以當作一份「建立法則的配方」，用四個簡單步驟掌握它。
en: File downloads: .mscz, .mxl, .pdf Let's begin by building up our version of the Rule of the Octave from simple principles, starting with parallel [latex]^6_3[/latex] (first inversion) chords. You could also think of this as a matter of moving from a flat to a rich harmonic hierarchy, or else as a "Regolo recipe" : how to make or understand the rule in four easy steps.

title: 嘉蘭特圖式：八度法則與音階的模進配和聲
text: 先只用平行 [latex]^6_3[/latex] 和弦，為低音音階作簡單的和聲配置。這在音樂語法上沒有錯，但層次感與變化都不多，因此不太有趣。接著在第一個與最後一個和弦改用 [latex]^5_3[/latex]，讓主音具有收束感。再把上行與下行版本中的屬和弦改為 [latex]^5_3[/latex]，進一步建立和聲層次，因為它們也是重要和弦。最後，在每個主和弦與屬和弦之前，包括它們的轉位形式，都加上七和弦。其中一處還需要半音變化，以更明確地將屬音主音化。你認為為什麼只在這一處改變，而不在進行中的其他位置也這樣做？
en: We begin with a simple harmonization of the bass scale using parallel [latex]^6_3[/latex] chords only. There's nothing grammatically incorrect about this, but neither does it have much of a sense of hierarchy or variety. In short, it's not very interesting. Next we put in strategic [latex]^5_3[/latex]s on the first and last chords to give a sense of closure on the tonic. Then we also add a [latex]^5_3[/latex] on the dominant chords of both ascending and descending forms to further nuance the hierarchy (these are important chords too). Finally, we precede each of the tonic and dominant chords (including those in inversion) with seventh chords. In one case, this also involves a chromatic alteration for a stronger sense of tonicizing the dominant. Why do you think we might only make that change this one time, and not anywhere else in the progression?

title: 嘉蘭特圖式：八度法則與音階的模進配和聲
text: 如前所見，八度法則可以從以平行 [latex]^6_3[/latex] 和弦為低音音階作模進配和聲的角度理解。本節介紹其他音階配和聲的模進形式，基本上是由一個以上和弦構成的型態，沿音階方向反覆移動。有些型態上行、下行都能用相同方式處理；另一些則須作調整。
en: As we've seen above, the Rule of the Octave can be thought of as in terms of a sequential harmonization of bass scales (parallel [latex]^6_3[/latex] chords). This section looks at some other sequential harmonizations of the bass scale here. Basically, this involves patterns of one or more harmonies which repeat sequentially in the direction of the scale. Some of these work in the same way for both ascending and descending forms; others require some modification.

title: 嘉蘭特圖式：八度法則與音階的模進配和聲
text: 與前面一樣，我們先只用平行 [latex]^6_3[/latex] 和弦，為音階作簡單配置。後續譜表系統則依序採用以下型態：

title: 嘉蘭特圖式：八度法則與音階的模進配和聲

title: 嘉蘭特圖式：八度法則與音階的模進配和聲
text: 上行：在低音音階的每個音上方，交替使用五度與六度。下行：可以和上行一樣，在每個低音上交替五度與六度；也可以在不同低音上交替配置五度、六度，本檔案採後者。
en: Ascending: In the ascending form, we alternate between the fifth and sixth above each note of the bass line scale. Descending: In the descending form, we could do the same note-by-note alternation as the ascending form, or else alternate between the fifth and sixth on separate notes (as in this file).

title: 嘉蘭特圖式：八度法則與音階的模進配和聲
text: 7–6 型態：連續掛留
en: 7–6 patterns: chains of suspensions

title: 嘉蘭特圖式：八度法則與音階的模進配和聲
text: 上行：7–6 掛留的上聲部向下解決，因此配合上行音階時，需要加上向上八度的跳進，重新開始型態；反覆的型態因此較接近 7–6–8。下行：下降的模進與下行音階方向相同，因此不必修改。基本上就是回到一開始的平行 [latex]^6_3[/latex] 和弦，只把最高聲部延後或錯開。
en: Ascending: 7–6 suspensions involve a descending upper part, so in the ascending form of this pattern, we need to add in a leap up the octave to restart the pattern, so the repeating pattern is more like 7–6–8. Descending: Here the descending sequence matches the descending scale, so no modification is necessary. We essentially go back to the parallel [latex]^6_3[/latex] chords we started with, and just delay or offset the top line.

title: 嘉蘭特圖式：八度法則與音階的模進配和聲
text: 五度循環
en: Cycles of fifths

title: 嘉蘭特圖式：八度法則與音階的模進配和聲
text: 五度循環以根音向下五度的進行為基礎。在這個型態中，每隔一個低音取一個音，就能找出另一條通常向下的音階進行。這是因為我們通常不會真的連續下行兩次五度，而是下行五度、再上行四度；和聲進行等價，音域卻能維持在同一範圍或八度內。完成一次「下行五度、上行四度」後，會比起點低一級，因此形成級進；若維持自然音、不轉調，就能構成音階。以下列出幾種主要形式：
en: The cycle of fifths is a based on a progression of root motion descending by fifths. Hiding in this pattern is another (usually descending) scalic progression between alternate bass notes. This arises because instead of literally going down two fifths, we usually go down a fifth and up a fourth, which is the equivalent progression, just keeping it in the same register / octave. At the end of one such "down a fifth, up a fourth," we end up a step lower than where we started, and so we also have a stepwise progression that can be scalic (if it is diatonic—i.e., not modulating). We set this out in some of the main forms:

en: So far, we've used 7–6 and 4–3 suspensions, so that leaves us one more important type: the 2–3 suspension (which is the inversion of 7–6).

title: 嘉蘭特圖式：八度法則與音階的模進配和聲
text: 上行：和前面的 7–6 掛留一樣，配合上行音階時，每次都須重新開始型態，因此相對於上聲部形成 2–3–1，相對於低音則形成 9–8–10。下行：同樣地，下行版本不必重新起頭。2–3 型態構成一連串 [latex]^4_2[/latex] 到 6 的進行，類似重要的 V[latex]^4_2[/latex]–I6，只是這裡保持自然音，不逐一將各調主音化。
en: Ascending: Just like the 7–6 suspensions above, for the ascending scale, we need to restart each pattern, so it ends up being 2–3–1 with the upper part, or 9–8–10 with the bass. Descending: Again, no restart is needed for the descending form. The 2–3 pattern sets up a series of [latex]^4_2[/latex] to 6 progressions like the important V[latex]^4_2[/latex]–I6 progression, except that we've kept it diatonic here (i.e., without tonicizing each key).

en: This section introduces students to how Western classical composers use harmony to create a sense of trajectory in a phrase of music. It begins with basic diatonic harmony and ends with tonicization and modulation to closely related keys.

text: 本部分假設你已熟悉〈基礎樂理〉所涵蓋的主題。學過一些對位法也會有幫助，尤其是該部分的入門章，但不是必要條件。
en: This section assumes a familiarity with the topics covered in Fundamentals. It's helpful, but not necessary, for students to have studied some counterpoint as well, particularly the introductory chapter of that section.

title: III. 西方古典音樂的自然音和聲、主音化與轉調
text: 章節安排
en: Organization

title: III. 西方古典音樂的自然音和聲、主音化與轉調
text: 章節依兩項原則安排：一是樂句模型，二是低音旋律型態。由於樂句結尾的公式性較高，本部分先研究結尾，再談開頭，最後處理中段。
en: The chapters are organized around two principles: (1) the phrase model and (2) bass-line patterns. The section starts by examining phrase endings since these are relatively formulaic, then moves to beginnings, and finally takes on middles.

title: III. 西方古典音樂的自然音和聲、主音化與轉調
text: 第一章介紹樂句模型、定義樂句，並討論作曲家如何透過終止式形成樂句結尾。這一章只使用 I 與 V 和弦。
en: The first chapter introduces the phrase model, defines phrase, and discusses how composers create phrase endings via cadences. It only uses I and V chords.

title: III. 西方古典音樂的自然音和聲、主音化與轉調
text: 接下來四章，會學習如何用原位 V7 加強終止，以及運用強屬前和弦 IV、ii(6)與終止 [latex]^6_4[/latex] 和弦。閱讀終止 [latex]^6_4[/latex] 一章之前，須先學習裝飾性和弦外音。
en: In the next four chapters, students learn to strengthen cadences using V7 (root position only) and strong predominants (IV and ii(6)), and the cadential [latex]^6_4[/latex]. It's important that students learn about embellishing tones before reading the cadential [latex]^6_4[/latex] chapter.

title: III. 西方古典音樂的自然音和聲、主音化與轉調
text: 再接下來六章完成自然音和聲的學習：先說明如何在樂句開頭擴展主和聲，再談如何延長樂句中段。
en: The next six chapters complete the study of diatonic harmony, focusing first on how to expand the tonic at the beginning of the phrase, then on how to create length in the middle of a phrase.

title: III. 西方古典音樂的自然音和聲、主音化與轉調
text: 本部分最後介紹主音化與轉調。主音化一章可以分兩階段學習：先只處理 V 的主音化，再處理 V 以外和弦的主音化。
en: The section ends with tonicization and modulation. The tonicization chapter can be done in two parts: (1) tonicizations of V only; (2) tonicizations of chords other than V.

title: 和聲、終止式與樂句結尾入門
text: 重點整理本章先介紹《Open Music Theory》的和聲部分，再開始討論如何讓樂句產生結束感。目前只使用 I 與 V。本書以兩個較大的概念安排和聲教學：和聲功能與樂句模型。樂句結尾常由終止式標示，主要有正格終止與半終止兩類。正格終止包含 V–I 進行。若兩個和弦都是原位，而且主和弦上的最高聲部為 do [latex](\hat{1})[/latex]，便是完全正格終止；其中任何一項不符合，則是不完全正格終止。半終止包含 x–V 進行，x 可以是多種和弦。
en: Key Takeaways This chapter provides an introduction to the harmony section of Open Music Theory, then begins a discussion of how to create a sense of ending in a phrase. We focus exclusively on using I and V for now. Two larger concepts inform the way we present harmony here: harmonic function and the phrase model. Endings are often marked by cadences, of which there are two primary types: authentic cadences and half cadences. Authentic cadences involve the progression V–I. They are perfect when both harmonies are in root position and do [latex](\hat{1})[/latex] is in the soprano over tonic. If either of these conditions is not met, the authentic cadence is imperfect. Half cadences involve the progression x–V, where x is any of a variety of harmonies.

text: 和聲入門
en: Introduction to Harmony

title: 和聲、終止式與樂句結尾入門
text: 本部分著重西方古典音樂共同慣例時期的作曲家，如何在樂句中使用和聲。和聲是讓樂句朝向目標推進的重要因素之一。學習時，要同時記住兩個相關的大概念：和聲功能與樂句模型。
en: In this section, we'll focus on how composers of common-practice Western classical music use harmony in a phrase. Harmony is one important component (among others) of creating a phrase's sense of forward motion toward a goal. As we study harmony, it's important to keep two larger related concepts in mind: harmonic function and the phrase model.

title: 和聲、終止式與樂句結尾入門
text: 和聲功能將和弦分為三類：
en: Harmonic function refers to three categories of chords:

title: 和聲、終止式與樂句結尾入門
text: 主功能（T）：聽起來安定，帶來歸屬或中心感的和弦。在西方古典音樂中，屬於這類的只有 I，小調中為 i。屬前功能（PD）：使音樂離開主功能、走向屬功能的和弦，可再分兩組：強屬前和弦，預示屬功能和弦即將到來：IV 與 ii；小調中為 iv 與 iio。弱屬前和弦，使音樂離開主功能，通常走向作用較強的屬前和弦：iii 與 vi；小調中為 VII、III、VI。屬功能（D）：帶來急切解決到主和弦之感的和弦：V 與 viio，小調中也相同。
en: Tonic (T): Chords that sound stable, providing a sense of home or center. In Western classical music, the only chord that belongs to this category is I (in minor: i). Predominant (PD): Chords that transition away from tonic function toward dominant function. This category can be split into two groups: Strong predominants signal that a dominant function chord is imminent: IV and ii (in minor: iv and iio). Weak predominants transition away from tonic, typically moving to a stronger predominant: iii and vi (in minor: VII, III, and VI). Dominant (D): Chords that provide a sense of urgency to resolve toward the tonic chord: V and viio (the same in minor).

title: 和聲、終止式與樂句結尾入門
text: 樂句模型說明樂句中和聲功能的典型次序與流向。其原則是：樂句至少需要主功能與屬功能和聲，才會有發展方向。更常見的情況是再加入屬前和聲，加強朝向收束的感覺。樂句幾乎總是依模型由左向右進行，少有由右向左的情況；稍後會討論一些例外。範例 1彙整了這個模型。
en: The phrase model refers to the typical order and flow of harmonic functions in a phrase. The principle of the phrase model is that a phrase needs at least tonic function and dominant function harmonies in order to exhibit a sense of trajectory. More often, phrases also include a predominant harmony to heighten the sense of trajectory toward closure. Phrases almost always progress from left to right in the phrase model, not from right to left, although we'll discuss some exceptions later. This is summarized in Example 1.

title: 和聲、終止式與樂句結尾入門
text: 範例 1。樂句模型：（a）形成向前推進感所需的最少功能；（b）較常見的樂句功能配置，最後的主功能可有可無；（c）和聲功能不由右向左進行。
en: Example 1. The phrase model: (a) the minimum functions needed to create forward motion, (b) more common functional layout for a phrase (the final tonic is optional), (c) harmonic functions do not progress right to left.

title: 和聲、終止式與樂句結尾入門
text: 終止式入門
en: Introduction to Cadences

title: 和聲、終止式與樂句結尾入門
text: 讓樂句結尾產生收束感的一種方式，是使用終止式。它是形成目標的旋律與和聲型態，有些像文章句子裡的標點。終止式不只幫助我們判斷樂句何時結束，也有助於確立調性，因此分析時，通常可以先聽出可能的終止位置。
en: One way to create a sense of closure at the end of a phrase is through cadences—melodic and harmonic patterns that create goals, kind of like punctuation marks in literary sentences. They're important not only because they can help you determine phrase endings, but also because they help establish a key. As a result, listening for potential cadence points is typically a good first step in analysis.

title: 和聲、終止式與樂句結尾入門
text: 範例 2 呈現兩個樂句，以及兩種主要的終止感：（1）未完全結束；（2）已收束。第一個樂句在第 4 小節以半終止（HC）結束，聽來意猶未盡。第二個樂句從第 5 小節開始，在第 8 小節以聽來已收束的正格終止結束。PAC 標籤表示這是其中一種特定類型，稱為完全正格終止，下文會介紹。
en: Example 2 shows two phrases and the two main categories of cadence: (1) inconclusive and (2) conclusive. The first phrase ends in m. 4 with a half cadence (HC) that sounds inconclusive. The second phrase begins in m. 5 and ends in m. 8 with an authentic cadence that sounds conclusive. The label PAC marks this as a particular kind of authentic cadence called a perfect authentic cadence, discussed below.

text: 正格終止：聽起來已經收束
en: Authentic Cadences (they sound conclusive!)

title: 和聲、終止式與樂句結尾入門
text: 當 V–I 進行在樂句末尾形成結束，小調中為 V–i，就構成正格終止。正格終止有兩種：
en: An authentic cadence occurs when the harmonic progression V–I (or V–i in minor) marks the end of a phrase. There are two kinds of authentic cadence:

title: 和聲、終止式與樂句結尾入門
text: 完全正格終止（PAC）必須同時符合以下兩項條件，見範例 2 第 8 小節：主和弦上的最高聲部為 do [latex](\hat{1})[/latex]。V 與 I 都是原位。若仍有 V–I，但以上任何一項條件不符合，就是不完全正格終止（IAC），如範例 3。例如：主和弦上的最高聲部是 mi，小調中為 me [latex](\hat{3})[/latex]，如範例 3；或V、I，或兩者採用轉位。
en: A perfect authentic cadence (PAC) occurs when both of the following conditions are met (Example 2, m. 8): Do [latex](\hat{1})[/latex] is in the soprano over the tonic chord Both V and I are in root position An imperfect authentic cadence (IAC) occurs if either of the above two conditions isn't met, but V–I is still involved (Example 3). For instance, an IAC can occur when: Mi (me in minor) [latex](\hat{3})[/latex] is in the soprano over the tonic chord (as in Example 3), or V, I, or both harmonies are inverted

en: Example 3. An imperfect authentic cadence (IAC) in Fanny Hensel, "Ferne" Op. 9, No. 2 (0:00–0:14).

title: 和聲、終止式與樂句結尾入門
text: 半終止：聽起來意猶未盡
en: Half Cadences (they sound inconclusive!)

title: 和聲、終止式與樂句結尾入門
text: 樂句在 V 上結束時，便構成半終止（HC），如範例 2 第 4 小節。V 前面可以接多種和弦，因此我們常把半終止的和聲進行寫成「x–V」。
en: A half cadence (HC) occurs when a phrase ends on V (Example 2, m. 4). A variety of chords can precede V, so we often refer to the harmonic progression that marks HCs as "x–V."

title: 和聲、終止式與樂句結尾入門
text: 目前先把可用和弦限於 I 與 V，小調中為 i 與 V，以便學習聲部進行的基本技巧。
en: For now, we'll restrict our vocabulary to only I and V chords (or i and V in minor) so we can learn some basic techniques of voice-leading.

title: 和聲、終止式與樂句結尾入門
text: 終止強度與不完全正格終止
en: Cadential Strength and the IAC

title: 和聲、終止式與樂句結尾入門
text: PAC 能帶來明確的最終結束感，因此是作曲家可用的最強終止類型；HC 聽起來尚未結束，因而最弱。IAC 的特別之處，在於它的終止強度位於 HC 與 PAC 之間（範例 4）。
en: PACs are the strongest kind of cadence available to a composer because of the sense of finality they can create, and HCs are the weakest kind of cadence because of their unfinished sound. IACs are special because they occupy the space between HCs and PACs in terms of cadential strength (Example 4).

title: 和聲、終止式與樂句結尾入門
text: 範例 4。終止強度的連續範圍。
en: Example 4. Spectrum of cadential strength.

title: 和聲、終止式與樂句結尾入門
text: IAC 有許多寫法：理論上，作曲家可以搭配不同的和弦轉位與旋律音階級數，因此也能選擇讓 IAC 的結束感較強或較弱。
en: Since there are many ways to compose an IAC (a composer can theoretically use various combinations of inverted chords and scale degrees in the melody), a composer can choose to make an IAC more or less strong.

title: 和聲、終止式與樂句結尾入門
text: 前面的範例 3 終止感較強：它使用原位 V–i，最高聲部為 me [latex](\hat{3})[/latex]；位置在一句歌詞的結尾，使用二分音符，後面有休止符，而且接下來的音樂聽起來像新樂句。
en: The cadence in Example 3 above is relatively strong: it uses root position V–i with me [latex](\hat{3})[/latex] in the soprano, it comes at the end of a sentence in the lyrics, it uses a half note, it's followed by a rest, and the music that follows sounds like a new phrase.

title: 和聲、終止式與樂句結尾入門
text: 範例 5 中可能的 IAC 相對較弱：它使用 V6–I，該瞬間很快就過去了。後面的材料既可能被理解為延續尚未結束的樂句，也可能呼應剛結束樂句的開頭；後一種聽法會加強把第 5 小節視為 IAC 的理由。演出者對範例 5 是否真的有 IAC，可能看法不同，並據此調整演奏。
en: The potential IAC in Example 5 is comparably weaker: it uses V6–I, the moment goes by relatively quickly, and it's followed by material that could easily be understood as continuing a phrase that's under way or as referencing the beginning of a phrase that has just concluded, something that would strengthen reading m. 5 as an IAC. Performers may disagree on whether Example 5 contains an IAC or not, and they may adjust their playing accordingly.

title: 和聲、終止式與樂句結尾入門
text: Schubert D. 845 第三樂章可能的不完全正格終止靜態樂譜尚待補齊；原始資源含有本章必要的音樂範例。
en: Musical example (requires internet)Static score pending; the original resource contains a musical example.

title: 和聲、終止式與樂句結尾入門
text: 範例 5。Schubert 鋼琴奏鳴曲 D. 845，第三樂章中可能的不完全正格終止。
en: Example 5. A potential IAC in Schubert's Piano Sonata D. 845, III.

title: 和聲、終止式與樂句結尾入門
text: 情況還可能更複雜：作曲家常用符合 IAC 描述、卻沒有真正結束樂句的進行，來避開 PAC。在範例 6 中，第 8 小節有一個可能的 IAC；但第 9 小節開始重複第 5 小節的材料，比較第 9 小節低音與第 5 小節最高聲部，就會聽到這段音樂像是在重新準備終止，試圖得到比第 8 小節更強的收束。因此，譜上將第 8 小節的終止標籤畫掉，表示這個終止已被化解（subverted），沒有真正成立。
en: An additional complication is that composers often avoid creating a PAC using progressions that fit the description of an IAC, but that don't mark the end of a phrase. In Example 6, m. 8 contains a potential IAC, but when m. 9 begins to repeat the material from m. 5 (compare the bass voice in m. 9 with the soprano in m. 5) it sounds like the passage is trying the run-up to the cadence again to achieve something stronger than the potential IAC at m. 8. We indicate that the cadence in m. 8 is subverted by crossing the label out on the score.
