title: 和聲、終止式與樂句結尾入門
text: 可能性這麼多，如何判定一處是否真的是 IAC？下一節「聽辨終止式」提供一些幫助。
en: With so many possibilities, how can we determine what counts as a true IAC? The next section ("Hearing Cadences") offers some help.

title: 和聲、終止式與樂句結尾入門
text: 聽辨終止式
en: Hearing Cadences

title: 和聲、終止式與樂句結尾入門
text: 聽出終止式固然有直覺成分，但也是可以逐漸磨練的能力。建議依以下步驟練習：
en: While there is certainly a degree of intuition involved with hearing cadences, it's also a skill that can be honed over time. We recommend listening for cadences following this process:

title: 和聲、終止式與樂句結尾入門
text: 聽辨終止式的步驟標出可能的終止位置。分析相關和聲。聽聽每個可能的終止位置之後，是否有重新開始的感覺。
en: Summary: steps for hearing cadences Mark potential cadence points Analyze the harmonies involved Listen for a sense of beginning after each potential cadence point

title: 和聲、終止式與樂句結尾入門
text: 先聆聽，標出可能的停頓、目標或收束位置。初學者一開始常把太多位置標成終止。有個簡單原則：除非片段速度相當慢，兩小節長的樂句並不常見。接著，檢查這些可能終止位置的和聲：x–V：可能的半終止。V–I：可能的正格終止。若 I 上方的最高聲部是 do [latex](\hat{1})[/latex]，而且兩個和弦都是原位，便可能是 PAC。若 I 上方的最高聲部是其他音，例如 mi [latex](\hat{3})[/latex] 或 sol [latex](\hat{5})[/latex]，便可能是 IAC。若 V、I，或兩者採轉位，便可能是 IAC。若不包含以上兩種進行，就不是可能的終止式。這不表示它沒有任何結束感，只是說它不構成終止式。[1]最後，聽聽每個可能的終止位置之後發生什麼。真正的終止標示樂句的結尾，所以後面很常有開始的感覺。這個「開始」可能重複剛結束樂句的開頭，也可能用新材料展開新樂句。若在候選終止位置之後聽到開始感，就能有力地支持那裡確實是終止。若聽到的是前一樂句中段材料的重複，候選位置可能並非真正的終止，而是原本可能出現的終止被化解了。
en: At first, listen and mark potential points of rest, goal, or closure. It's common for students to initially mark too many cadences. One rule of thumb is that unless an excerpt's tempo is quite slow, it's not common for phrases to be two measures long. Next, check the harmonies involved in these potential cadence points: x–V = potential HC V–I = potential AC If do [latex](\hat{1})[/latex] is in the soprano over I and both harmonies are in root position, it's a potential PAC. If something else like mi [latex](\hat{3})[/latex] or sol [latex](\hat{5})[/latex] is in the soprano over I, it's a potential IAC. If V, I, or both harmonies are inverted, it's a potential IAC. If it doesn't involve one of the above two progressions, then it's not a potential cadence. (Note that this doesn't mean it doesn't represent some kind of ending. It just means it's not a cadence.[1]) Finally, listen for what happens after each potential cadence point. Since true cadences mark the end of a phrase, it's very common for cadences to be followed by a sense of beginning. This "beginning" may be a repetition of the beginning of the phrase that just ended, or it may be new material that starts a new phrase. Hearing a sense of beginning following a cadence point is a great way to help verify that what you've marked as a potential cadence is indeed a true cadence point. If, instead, you hear repetition of material from the middle of the previous phrase, your potential cadence may not be a true cadence. Instead, it likely represents a potential cadence point that has been subverted.

title: 和聲、終止式與樂句結尾入門
text: 寫作正格終止：只用三和弦
en: Writing Authentic Cadences (with triads only)

title: 和聲、終止式與樂句結尾入門
text: 下方方框彙整 PAC 與 IAC 的寫作步驟，範例 7–10 加以示範。
en: The steps for writing a PAC or IAC are summarized in the box below and illustrated in Examples 7–10.

title: 和聲、終止式與樂句結尾入門
text: 寫作 PAC 或 IAC確定調性。先寫完整的低音：sol–do [latex](\hat5-\hat1)[/latex]。再寫完整的最高聲部：PAC：re–do 或 ti–do [latex](\hat2-\hat1[/latex] 或 [latex]\hat7-\hat1)[/latex]。IAC：re–mi 或 sol–sol [latex](\hat2-\hat3[/latex] 或 [latex]\hat5-\hat5)[/latex]。補入內聲部，逐一思考：低音與最高聲部已經有哪些音？還需要哪些音，才能補齊和弦？要重複哪個音？原位和弦通常重複低音。若是小調，記得在 V 中使用導音 ti [latex](\uparrow\hat7)[/latex]，使它成為大三和弦，而非小三和弦，藉此產生走向主和弦的動力。
en: Writing a PAC or IAC Determine the key Write the entire bass: sol–do [latex](\hat5-\hat1)[/latex] Write the entire soprano: PAC: re–do or ti–do [latex](\hat2-\hat1[/latex] or [latex]\hat7-\hat1)[/latex] IAC: re–mi or sol–sol [latex](\hat2-\hat3[/latex] or [latex]\hat5-\hat5)[/latex] Fill in the inner voices by asking: What notes do I already have in the bass and soprano? What notes do I need to complete the chord? What note will I double? (Remember, in root position chords, it's common to double the bass.) If you're writing in minor, remember that you need to use the leading-tone, ti [latex](\uparrow\hat7)[/latex], in your V chord (making it a major triad, not minor) to give it momentum toward the tonic.

title: 和聲、終止式與樂句結尾入門
text: 寫作大調完全正格終止：譜例靜態樂譜尚待補齊；原始資源含有本章必要的音樂範例。範例 7。寫作大調完全正格終止。

en: The steps for writing a HC are summarized in the box below and illustrated in Examples 11 and 12.

title: 和聲、終止式與樂句結尾入門
text: 寫作半終止確定調性。先寫完整的低音：do–sol [latex](\hat1-\hat5)[/latex]。目前只用 I 與 V；稍後會看到，V 前面更常使用其他和弦。再寫完整的最高聲部：do–ti 或 mi–re [latex](\hat1-\hat7[/latex] 或 [latex]\hat3-\hat2)[/latex]。sol–sol [ [latex]\hat5-\hat5[/latex] ] 也可能，但不常見。補入內聲部，逐一思考：已經有哪些音？還需要哪些音，才能補齊和弦？要重複哪個音？原位和弦通常重複低音。若是小調，記得在 V 中使用導音 ti [latex](\uparrow\hat{7})[/latex]，使它成為大三和弦，而非小三和弦。
en: Writing a HC: Determine the key Write the entire bass: do–sol [latex](\hat1-\hat5)[/latex] (note: for now, we'll use only I and V chords, although we'll see later that other chords more commonly precede V) Write the entire soprano: do–ti or mi–re [latex](\hat1-\hat7[/latex] or [latex]\hat3-\hat2)[/latex] (note: sol–sol [ [latex]\hat5-\hat5[/latex] ] is possible, but not common) Fill in the inner voices by asking: What notes do I already have? What notes do I need to complete the chord? What note will I double? (Remember, in root position chords, it's common to double the bass.) If you're writing in minor, remember to use the leading-tone, ti [latex](\uparrow\hat{7})[/latex], in your V chord, making it a major triad, not minor.

title: 和聲、終止式與樂句結尾入門
text: 例如，有時旋律暗示結尾，和聲卻沒有配合；有時和聲暗示結束，旋律卻不願收束。終止式是特別的目標位置，因為旋律與和聲都在這裡同意樂句應當結束。↵
en: Sometimes, for example, the melody suggests an ending, but the harmony doesn't participate. Or, sometimes the harmony suggests an end, but the melody refuses to close. Cadences are special goal points because they represent places where both the melody and harmony agree on a phrase ending. ↵

title: 以 V⁷ 加強結尾
text: 重點整理本章介紹作曲家如何在屬和弦上加七音，加強它走向主和弦的吸引力。V7 可用三種方式解決到主和弦：基本解決：所有傾向音都依其傾向解決。不完整的 V7：省略 V7 的五音，改為重複根音，使它能解決到完整主和弦。導音下跳：完整 V7 中的導音向下跳到 sol（[latex]\hat{5}[/latex]），形成完整主和弦。
en: Key Takeaways This chapter introduces how composers add a seventh to the dominant to strengthen its pull toward the tonic. There are three ways a V7 can resolve to tonic: The default resolution: where all active notes resolve according to their tendencies. Incomplete V7: where the fifth is omitted from the V7 and the V7's root is doubled instead to create a complete tonic. Leading-tone drop: where the leading tone in a complete V7 leaps down to sol ([latex]\hat{5}[/latex]) to create a complete tonic.

title: 以 V⁷ 加強結尾
text: 範例 1 的樂句以完全正格終止（PAC）結束，與〈和聲、終止式與樂句結尾入門〉中看過、寫過的例子相似。不過，這裡的 V 多了一個 fa（[latex]\hat{4}[/latex]），使它從大三和弦變成屬七和弦。七音增加和弦的不協和，因而增加不安定感，也就強化 V 走向 I 的吸引力。請比較範例 2 中兩個片段的音響。
en: The phrase in Example 1 ends with a perfect authentic cadence (PAC) similar to those we saw and wrote in the Introduction to Harmony, Cadences, and Endings chapter. Here, however, the V chord contains an extra note, fa ([latex]\hat{4}[/latex]), that transforms it from a major triad into a dominant seventh chord. Since the seventh adds dissonance (and therefore instability) to the chord, it strengthens the pull of the V chord toward I. Compare the sound of the excerpts in Example 2.

en: Example 2. A PAC involving: (a) only triads and (b) a V7 chord.

title: 以 V⁷ 加強結尾
text: V7 到 I 的基本解決
en: The Default Resolution of V7 to I

title: 以 V⁷ 加強結尾
text: 完整 V7 的各音依典型傾向解決後，會得到含三個根音、一個三音，沒有五音的主三和弦（範例 3a 與範例 3b）。這是完全正常、符合預期且常見的 V7–I 解決方式。這裡可以省略五音，因為它不提供判定和弦所必需的資訊；根音與三音則不可少，根音決定和弦名稱，三音決定和弦性質。
en: When the notes of a complete V7 chord resolve according to their typical tendencies, we end up with a tonic triad that has three roots and one third—no fifth (Examples 3a and 3b). This is a completely normal, expected, and common resolution of V7 to I. It's okay to leave out the fifth here since it doesn't provide essential information about the chord. By contrast, the root and third are essential: the root determines the chord’s name, and the third determines its quality.

title: 以 V⁷ 加強結尾
text: 範例 3c 讓 re（[latex]\hat{2}[/latex]）上行到 mi（[latex]\hat{3}[/latex]），這種解決非常少見。主和弦因而出現兩個根音、兩個三音的特殊重複配置，通常會引發聲部進行問題，因此建議避免。
en: The resolution in Example 3c, where re ([latex]\hat{2}[/latex]) goes up to mi ([latex]\hat{3}[/latex]), is very uncommon, and such an unusual doubling in the tonic chord (two roots, two thirds) usually leads to voice-leading problems. We suggest avoiding this kind of resolution.

en: Musical example (requires internet)Static score pending; the original resource contains a musical example.

title: 以 V⁷ 加強結尾
text: 範例 3。V7 的基本解決。
en: Example 3. Default resolution of V7.

title: 以 V⁷ 加強結尾
text: 以基本方式將 V7 解決到 I，可依以下步驟：
en: To resolve V7 to I using a default resolution:

title: 以 V⁷ 加強結尾
text: 先寫完整的低音：sol 到 do（[latex]\hat{5}[/latex]–[latex]\hat{1}[/latex]）。再寫完整的最高聲部：從 V7 的傾向音中選一個，放在最高聲部，再依其傾向解決。範例 4 列出 V7 各傾向音的走向。小調中要使用 ti（[latex]\uparrow\hat{7}[/latex]），不要用 te（[latex]\downarrow\hat{7}[/latex]），使 V7 的三和弦部分維持大三和弦性質。補入內聲部，思考：「已經有哪些音？還需要哪些音？這些音各有什麼解決傾向？」
en: Write the entire bass: sol to do ([latex]\hat{5}[/latex]–[latex]\hat{1}[/latex]) Write the entire soprano by choosing an active note to place in the soprano over V7, then resolving that note according to its tendency. Example 4 shows the tendencies for active notes in V7. If you are writing in minor, remember to use ti ([latex]\uparrow\hat{7}[/latex]), not te ([latex]\downarrow\hat{7}[/latex]) in V7 to make the chord major! Fill in the inner voices by asking “what do I have, what do I need, and what is the tendency of those notes?”

title: 以 V⁷ 加強結尾
text: V7 中的音 在 I 或 i 中的解決音 fa ([latex]\hat{4}[/latex]) mi/me ([latex]\hat{3}[/latex]) re ([latex]\hat{2}[/latex]) do ([latex]\hat{1}[/latex]) ti ([latex]\hat{7}[/latex]) do ([latex]\hat{1}[/latex])
en: Note in V7 Resolution in I (or i) fa ([latex]\hat{4}[/latex]) mi/me ([latex]\hat{3}[/latex]) re ([latex]\hat{2}[/latex]) do ([latex]\hat{1}[/latex]) ti ([latex]\hat{7}[/latex]) do ([latex]\hat{1}[/latex])

title: 以 V⁷ 加強結尾
text: 範例 4。V7 中傾向音的解決方向。
en: Example 4. Tendencies of active notes in V7.

title: 以 V⁷ 加強結尾
text: V7 到 I 的其他解決方式
en: Alternative Resolutions of V7 to I

title: 以 V⁷ 加強結尾
text: 有時作曲家希望主和弦是完整的，而不是基本解決所得的不完整和弦。V7 的兩種替代解決方式可以得到完整 I。寫作步驟仍相同：先寫完整低音，再為 V7 選一個最高聲部的傾向音並寫出其解決，最後把兩個內聲部當作一組，一起思考：「已經有哪些音？還需要哪些音？它們要走到哪裡？」
en: Sometimes a composer may want the tonic chord to be complete rather than the incomplete chord that occurs in the default resolution. Two alternative resolutions of V7 make it possible to create a complete I. Note that the steps for writing remain the same as for the default resolution: write the entire bass, write the entire soprano choosing an active note over V7, then fill in the inner voices together as a pair by asking “what do I have, what do I need, and where do those notes go?”

title: 以 V⁷ 加強結尾
text: 不完整的 V7
en: Incomplete V7

title: 以 V⁷ 加強結尾
text: 範例 5a 與範例 5b 省略了 V7 的五音，使它能解決到完整 I。省略五音後，為了維持四聲部，必須選一個音重複。只能重複根音；若重複 ti（[latex]\uparrow\hat{7}[/latex]）或 fa（[latex]\hat{4}[/latex]），當兩個聲部都依傾向解決時，便會產生平行八度，如範例 5c 與範例 5d。
en: Examples 5a and 5b show a resolution where the fifth has been omitted from the V7, allowing that chord to resolve to a complete I. When we omit the fifth, we need to select a note to double in order to retain our four-voice texture. The only note we can double is the root, since doubling ti ([latex]\uparrow\hat{7}[/latex]) or fa ([latex]\hat{4}[/latex]) would create parallel octaves when both voices resolve according to their tendencies (Examples 5c and 5d).

title: 以 V⁷ 加強結尾
text: 導音下跳
en: Leading-Tone Drop

title: 以 V⁷ 加強結尾
text: 完整 V7 也可以解決到完整 I，但必須容許一個傾向音走向不同於預期的位置。範例 6 示範「導音下跳」如何做到這一點。[1] 這裡，內聲部的 ti（[latex]\uparrow\hat{7}[/latex]）向下跳到 sol（[latex]\hat{5}[/latex]）。這樣可行，是因為：（1）ti（[latex]\uparrow\hat{7}[/latex]）不是不協和音；（2）ti（[latex]\uparrow\hat{7}[/latex]）位於內聲部，不那麼顯眼；（3）在能移動到主和弦 sol（[latex]\hat{5}[/latex]）、又不產生平行的音之中，ti（[latex]\uparrow\hat{7}[/latex]）距離最近。
en: It's also possible to create a complete I from a complete V7, but in order to do so, we have to allow a tendency tone to move somewhere other than its expected resolution. Example 6 shows how this is possible using a leading-tone drop. [1] Here, ti ([latex]\uparrow\hat{7}[/latex]) drops down to sol ([latex]\hat{5}[/latex]) in an inner voice. This works because: (1) ti ([latex]\uparrow\hat{7}[/latex]) is not a dissonant note; (2) ti ([latex]\uparrow\hat{7}[/latex]) is in an inner voice, so it's not too noticeable; and (3) ti ([latex]\uparrow\hat{7}[/latex]) is the closest note that can move to sol ([latex]\hat{5}[/latex]) in the tonic without causing parallels.

title: 以 V⁷ 加強結尾
text: 範例 6。使用導音下跳的 V7 替代解決方式。
en: Example 6. Alternative resolution of V7 involving a leading-tone drop.

title: 以 V⁷ 加強結尾
text: 這裡要特別強調兩點：
en: Two things are worth emphasizing here:

title: 以 V⁷ 加強結尾
text: 導音下跳只用於女低音或男高音聲部，讓它沒有按預期解決這件事較不明顯。導音一律向下跳到 sol（[latex]\hat{5}[/latex]），不跳到距離更遠的 mi（[latex]\hat{3}[/latex]）；sol（[latex]\hat{5}[/latex]）較近。
en: Use the leading-tone drop only in the alto or tenor voice to hide the fact that it's not resolving as expected. The leading tone always leaps down to sol ([latex]\hat{5}[/latex]), never to mi ([latex]\hat{3}[/latex]), which is further away than sol ([latex]\hat{5}[/latex]).

title: 以 V⁷ 加強結尾
text: 整理
en: Summary

title: 以 V⁷ 加強結尾
text: 範例 7 彙整 V7–I 的三種解決方式。你可能注意到，本章還沒談 V7 在半終止（HC）中的用法。半終止原本就不安定，加上七音會更不安定，因此 V7 在半終止中少見得多。這類終止較常出現在浪漫時期音樂，所以 Janet Schmalfeldt（2011，202）把使用 V7 的半終止稱為「十九世紀半終止」。
en: Example 7 summarizes the three possible ways to resolve V7–I. You may notice that we have not discussed how V7 works in half cadences (HCs). V7 is much less common in a HC since the HC is already unstable, and adding a seventh makes it that much more unstable. Since such a cadence more often appears in Romantic music, Janet Schmalfeldt (2011, 202) has termed HCs involving V7 the "19th-century HC."

title: 以強屬前和弦加強結尾
text: 重點整理本章介紹兩個強屬前和弦：IV 與 ii6。兩者都可為低音的 fa [latex](\hat{4})[/latex] 配和聲。它們通常位於屬和弦之前，預示屬和弦即將到來。使用強屬前和弦時，聲部寫作最常見的錯誤是平行八度或平行五度。
en: Key Takeaways This chapter introduces two strong predominants: IV and ii6. Both harmonize fa [latex](\hat{4})[/latex] in the bass. They typically precede a dominant chord and predict that a dominant chord is on its way. The most common part-writing error when using strong predominants is parallel octaves or fifths.

title: 以強屬前和弦加強結尾
text: 如〈和聲、終止式與樂句結尾入門〉所述，大多數樂句結尾會在 V 之前加入強烈的屬前功能（PD），使收束更有力，如範例 1。換句話說，樂句常以低音 fa–sol [latex](\hat4 - \hat5)[/latex] 形成半終止（HC），或以 fa–sol–do [latex](\hat4 - \hat5 - \hat1)[/latex] 形成正格終止（AC）。終止之前的低音 fa [latex](\hat{4})[/latex]，通常搭配強屬前和弦，如範例 2；可選和弦是較常見的 ii6，以及 IV。
en: As we noted in the Introduction to Harmony, Cadences, and Phrase Endings chapter, most phrase endings are strengthened using a strong predominant (PD) that comes before the V chord (Example 1). Another way to say this is that it’s common for a phrase to end with the bass pattern fa–sol [latex](\hat4 - \hat5)[/latex] in a half cadence (HC) or fa–sol–do [latex](\hat4 - \hat5 - \hat1)[/latex] in an authentic cadence (AC). The fa [latex](\hat{4})[/latex] in the bass just before a cadence is the note that typically gets harmonized with a strong predominant (Example 2)—these chords are ii6 (the more common option) and IV.

title: 以強屬前和弦加強結尾
text: 使用 ii6 寫作
en: Writing with ii6

title: 以強屬前和弦加強結尾
text: 強屬前區域讓寫作多了一層挑戰，因為這裡容易出現平行八度、五度，如範例 3。應仔細檢查此處的聲部進行。有效的方法之一，是讓上方聲部盡可能與低音反向。低音會由 fa 上行到 sol [latex](\hat{4}-\hat5)[/latex]，所以上方聲部最好向下進行。以下列出正格終止的寫作步驟；若要寫半終止，只須省略末尾的 I。
en: The strong predominant area adds a degree of challenge to writing because it's where parallel octaves and fifths tend to show up (Example 3). You'll want to carefully check your writing around strong predominants for parallels. One thing that can help is to make as many upper voices as possible in contrary motion with the bass. Since the bass will move up from fa to sol [latex](\hat{4}-\hat5)[/latex], that means it's best to move your upper voices down. Below are the steps for writing an authentic cadence. Note that if you want to write a half cadence, you just leave off the I chord at the end.

title: 以強屬前和弦加強結尾
text: 強屬前區域容易出現的平行五度與八度靜態樂譜尚待補齊；原始資源含有本章必要的音樂範例。

title: 以強屬前和弦加強結尾
text: 範例 3。強屬前區域的平行進行。
en: Example 3. Parallels in the strong predominant area.

title: 以強屬前和弦加強結尾
text: 使用 ii6 的寫作步驟
en: Steps for writing with ii6

title: 以強屬前和弦加強結尾
text: 先寫完整的低音：fa–sol–do [latex](\hat4 - \hat5 - \hat1)[/latex]。再寫完整的最高聲部：先處理 V，在最高聲部放入一個傾向音。讓它在 I 上適當解決。從上方接近這個傾向音，以便與低音反向；或以共同音連接。補入內聲部，思考：「已經有哪些音？還需要哪些音？它們要如何移動，才能保持平順並避免平行？」ii6 是第一轉位和弦，因此可選擇重複任何能讓聲部進行最平順、又能避免平行的音。
en: Write the entire bass: fa–sol–do [latex](\hat4 - \hat5 - \hat1)[/latex]. Write the entire soprano: Start with the V chord, and place an active note in the soprano. Resolve the active note appropriately over I. Approach the active note from above to make contrary motion with the bass, or by common tone. Fill in the inner voices by asking “What do I have? What do I need? How should these voices move to create smooth motion and avoid parallels?” In ii6, since it's a first inversion chord, remember that you may double any note that gives you the smoothest voice leading and that avoids parallels.

title: 以強屬前和弦加強結尾
text: 範例 4 示範這個過程。

title: 以強屬前和弦加強結尾
text: 使用 IV 寫作
en: Writing with IV

title: 以強屬前和弦加強結尾
text: IV 接 V 時，因為根音級進，產生平行的風險比 ii6 更高。應避免像範例 5 那樣，所有聲部一起向上平行進行。與 ii6 相同，盡可能讓上方聲部與低音反向，也就是向下，便有助於避免這個問題。
en: The danger of writing parallels is even greater with IV than with ii6 because of the root motion by step. Avoid doing something like Example 5, where all voices move upward in parallel motion. Just as with ii6, if you make your upper voices move in contrary motion to the bass (down) where possible, you'll avoid the problem.

title: 以強屬前和弦加強結尾
text: 所有聲部同向造成的平行進行靜態樂譜尚待補齊；原始資源含有本章必要的音樂範例。

title: 以強屬前和弦加強結尾
text: 範例 5。所有聲部朝同一方向移動，造成平行進行。
en: Example 5. Parallels created by moving all voices in the same direction.

title: 以強屬前和弦加強結尾
text: 使用 IV 的步驟與 ii6 相同：先寫完整低音，再從 V 出發、向前後安排最高聲部，最後補入內聲部，如範例 6。重複音方面有一個重要差異：ii6 是第一轉位，重複音的選擇較有彈性；IV 是原位，因此幾乎總是重複低音。
en: The steps for writing with IV are the same as those for ii6: write the entire bass, write the entire soprano starting with V and working outward, then fill in the inner voices (Example 6). There's one important difference with respect to doubling: whereas the ii6 chord’s doubling is quite flexible since it's a first-inversion chord, the IV chord almost always sees its bass doubled since it's a root-position chord.

title: 以強屬前和弦加強結尾
text: 原位 ii
en: Root position ii

title: 以強屬前和弦加強結尾
text: 原位 ii 比 ii6 或 IV 少見得多，但在大調中仍可作為強屬前和弦。小調的 iio 和其他減三和弦一樣，通常不採原位。
en: The ii chord in root position is much less common than ii6 or IV, but it can be used as a strong predominant in major keys. (In minor keys, the iio chord, like any diminished triad, doesn’t normally show up in root position.)

title: 以強屬前和弦加強結尾
text: 使用原位 ii 仍可能寫出平行，但比使用 IV 或 ii6 時較不容易發生。範例 7 提供幾種常見選擇。請注意，ii 上方的最高聲部最常用 re 或 fa [latex](\hat2[/latex] 或 [latex]\hat4)[/latex]，而不是 la [latex](\hat6)[/latex]。
en: While it's possible to write parallels with ii, it's less likely than with IV or ii6. Example 7 shows some common options. Note that it's most common to place re or fa [latex](\hat2[/latex] or [latex]\hat4)[/latex], not la [latex](\hat6)[/latex], in the soprano over ii.

title: 以強屬前和弦加強結尾
text: 範例 7。使用 ii 寫作。
en: Example 7. Writing with ii.

title: 以強屬前和弦加強結尾
text: 結合使用 IV 與 ii(6)
en: Using IV and ii(6) in combination

title: 以強屬前和弦加強結尾
text: 有時作曲家會在樂句結尾、屬和弦之前，同時使用 IV 與 ii(6)。這時 ii 一律在 IV 之後。雖然兩者都是強屬前和弦，ii(6) 與後續 V 卻有特別的關係：ii 的根音與 V 的根音相隔五度，就像 V 與 I 的根音相隔五度一樣，見範例 8。這種根音關係，使 ii 的屬前作用比 IV 更強，因此在樂句結尾同時使用兩者時，ii 總是在 IV 之後，不在 IV 之前。
en: Sometimes a composer will choose to use both IV and ii(6) before the dominant at a phrase ending. In such cases, ii always comes after IV. Although both IV and ii(6) are strong pre-dominants, ii(6) shares a special relationship with the V chord that follows: the root of ii is a fifth away from the root of V, similar to how the root of V is a fifth away from the root of I (Example 8). This root relationship makes ii a stronger predominant than IV, which is why ii always comes after IV, never before IV, when both are used at a phrase ending.

title: 裝飾性和弦外音
text: 重點整理裝飾性和弦外音可分三類，彙整於範例 13：只涉及級進：經過音、鄰音。涉及跳進：倚音、逸音。涉及同音停留：掛留音、上行掛留音、持續音、先現音。
en: Key Takeaways Embellishing tones can be grouped into three categories (summarized in Example 13): Involving only stepwise motion: passing tone, neighbor tone Involving a leap: appoggiatura, escape tone Involving static notes: suspension, retardation, pedal, anticipation

title: 裝飾性和弦外音
text: 範例 1 再次呈現 Maria Szymanowska 的第6號進行曲，前面討論強屬前和弦時也看過這首作品。你可能注意到，第 8–10 小節低音中的某些音，不符合我們的和聲分析。範例 1 把這些音塗成藍色並圈出；它們統稱為「裝飾性和弦外音（embellishing tones）」，因為它們裝飾了屬於和弦的音。下文將它們分成三類介紹。
en: Example 1 reproduces Maria Szymanowska's March no. 6, which we also saw in our discussion of strong predominants. You might have noticed that some of the notes in the bass in mm. 8–10 don't fit our harmonic analysis. These notes, which are blue and circled in Example 1, are collectively called “embellishing tones” because they embellish notes that belong to the chord. Embellishing tones can be grouped into three categories, which we describe below.

title: 裝飾性和弦外音
text: 範例 2。多數裝飾音常見的三音結構。
en: Example 2. Common three-note layout of most embellishing tones.

title: 裝飾性和弦外音
text: 幾乎所有情況下，裝飾音都位於三音音型的中間，第一個與最後一個音則和低音協和，如範例 2。中間的裝飾音本身，可能與低音協和，也可能不協和；不過，它幾乎總是不屬於當下和弦的音。
en: In nearly all cases, an embellishing tone is the middle note of a three-note gesture in which the first and last notes are consonant with the bass (Example 2). The actual embellishing tone itself may be either consonant or dissonant with the bass. In almost all cases, however, the embellishing tone is a note that doesn't belong to the underlying chord.

title: 裝飾性和弦外音
text: 經過音與鄰音：以級進移動
en: Passing tones, neighbor tones: Embellishing tones that move by step

title: 裝飾性和弦外音
text: 範例 1 示範兩種以級進移動的裝飾性和弦外音：經過音（PT）與鄰音（NT）。經過音以級進進入，再沿相同方向級進離開，可以上行也可以下行，見範例 3。鄰音以級進進入，再沿相反方向級進返回，形成上鄰音或下鄰音，見範例 4。
en: Example 1 showed the two kinds of embellishing tones that move by step: passing tones (PTs) and neighbor tones (NTs). Passing tones are approached by step and left by step in the same direction, either ascending or descending (Example 3). Neighbor tones are approached by step and left by step in the opposite direction, producing either an upper neighbor or a lower neighbor (Example 4).

title: 裝飾性和弦外音
text: 倚音與逸音：涉及跳進
en: Appoggiaturas and escape tones: Embellishing tones that involve a leap

title: 裝飾性和弦外音
text: 範例 5 與範例 6 示範兩種涉及跳進的裝飾性和弦外音：倚音（appoggiatura，APP）與逸音（escape tone，ET）。倚音以跳進進入，再反方向級進離開，如範例 7；它的拍位通常比前後音更強。逸音則以級進進入，再反方向跳進離開，如範例 8；它的拍位通常比前後音更弱。兩者都以下行離開較常見，如範例 7a 與範例 8a；上行離開較少見，如範例 7b 與範例 8b。
en: Examples 5 and 6 show the two kinds of embellishing tones that involve a leap: appoggiaturas (APPs) and escape tones (ETs). Appoggiaturas are approached by leap and left by step in the opposite direction (Example 7). The appoggiatura typically occurs on a stronger part of the beat than its surrounding notes. Escape tones are approached by step and left by leap in the opposite direction (Example 8). The escape tone typically occurs on a weaker part of the beat than its surrounding notes. It is more common for appoggiaturas and escape tones to be left by motion downward (Examples 7a and 8a) than upward (7b and 8b).

title: 裝飾性和弦外音
text: 掛留、先現與持續音：涉及同音停留
en: Suspensions, anticipations, and pedal tones: Embellishing tones involving static notes

title: 裝飾性和弦外音
text: 範例 9–11 示範四種同音停留型態中的三種：掛留音（SUS）、上行掛留音（retardation，RET）與持續音（PED）。第四種先現音，會在下文另外說明。
en: Examples 9–11 show three of the four kinds of embellishing tones that involve static notes (i.e., notes that don't move): suspensions (SUS), retardations (RET), and pedal tones (PED). A fourth kind of embellishing tone, the anticipation, deserves special comment below.

title: 裝飾性和弦外音
text: 掛留音從前一個同音延續而來，再向下級進離開；上行掛留音同樣從前一個同音延續，之後向上級進離開，見範例 9 與範例 10。兩者都位於比前後音更強的拍位。〈第四類對位法〉對掛留有更詳細的討論。
en: Suspensions are approached by a static note and left by step down, while retardations are approached by a static note and left by step up (Examples 9 and 10). Both suspensions and retardations are always on a stronger part of the beat than the surrounding notes. (Suspensions are discussed in greater detail in the chapter on fourth species counterpoint.)

title: 裝飾性和弦外音
text: 持續音常出現在低音聲部。它是一連串保持同音的音，上方和弦不斷更換，而這個低音並不屬於其中某些和弦。通常以持續音的音階級數標記，見範例 11。
en: Pedal tones are often found in the bass. They consist of a series of static notes below chord changes that do not include the bass. We typically label them using the scale degree number of the pedal note, as in Example 11.

But anticipations are a two-note (rather than three-note) gesture, in which a chord tone is heard early as a non-chord tone (Example 12). title: 以終止四六和弦加強結尾
text: 重點整理本章介紹終止四六和弦 [latex]\mathrm{cadential}^6_4[/latex]，簡寫為 [latex](\mathrm{cad.}^6_4)[/latex]。它是屬和聲的裝飾，由低音 sol（[latex]\hat{5}[/latex]）上方的六度與四度兩個裝飾音結合而成。我們把 [latex]\mathrm{cad.\ }^6_4[/latex] 與它解決到 V(7) 的過程合併標記為 [latex]\mathrm{V}\begin{smallmatrix}(8-7)\\6-5\\4-3\end{smallmatrix}[/latex]。通常能接到 V 的和弦，也都能接到 [latex]\mathrm{cad. }^6_4[/latex]；最常見的是強屬前和弦。解決 [latex]\mathrm{cad.}^6_4[/latex] 時，須依數字指示，讓低音上方的六度下行為五度，四度下行為三度。
en: Key Takeaways This chapter introduces the [latex]\mathrm{cadential}^6_4[/latex] [latex](\mathrm{cad.}^6_4)[/latex], an embellishment of the dominant that results from the combination of two embellishing tones a sixth and a fourth above the bass note sol ([latex]\hat{5}[/latex]). We label the [latex]\mathrm{cad.\ }^6_4[/latex] and its resolution to V(7) as one unit: [latex]\mathrm{V}\begin{smallmatrix}(8-7)\\6-5\\4-3\end{smallmatrix}[/latex]. Any chord that normally approaches V can approach [latex]\mathrm{cad. }^6_4[/latex]. Most commonly, this is one of the strong predominants. When resolving [latex]\mathrm{cad.}^6_4[/latex], be sure to follow the figures such that the sixth above the bass falls to a fifth above the bass and the fourth above the bass falls to a third above the bass.

title: 以終止四六和弦加強結尾
text: 前面已看到，屬和弦可以加上七音來強化，尤其常用於正格終止；半終止與正格終止也常藉由強屬前和弦加強。本章介紹另一種強化屬和聲解決動力的方法：終止 [latex]^6_4[/latex]，簡寫為 [latex](\mathrm{cad.}^6_4)[/latex]。
en: So far, we've seen that the dominant can be strengthened, particularly at authentic cadences, by the addition of a seventh. We also saw that both half cadences and authentic cadences are commonly strengthened using a strong predominant. In this chapter, we look at another way to strengthen the the dominant’s drive toward resolution: the cadential [latex]^6_4[/latex] [latex](\mathrm{cad.}^6_4)[/latex].

title: 以終止四六和弦加強結尾
text: 範例 1 的正格終止，包含以 [latex]\mathrm{cad.}^6_4[/latex] 裝飾的 V7。這裡刻意使用「裝飾」一詞，因為 [latex]\mathrm{cad.}^6_4[/latex] 是低音 sol（[latex]\hat{5}[/latex]）上方兩個裝飾音的組合。範例 1 使用的是一個經過音與一個掛留音。它們總是位於低音上方的六度與四度，出現時常加強我們對終止的期待，因此稱為 [latex]\mathrm{cad.}^6_4[/latex]。雖然 [latex]\mathrm{cad.}^6_4[/latex] 常出現在終止位置，也可能在樂句其他位置出現，作為 V(7) 的裝飾。
en: The authentic cadence in Example 1 involves a V7 that has been embellished by [latex]\mathrm{cad.}^6_4[/latex]. We use the word “embellished” intentionally here because the [latex]\mathrm{cad.}^6_4[/latex] comprises two embellishing tones that appear over sol ([latex]\hat{5}[/latex]) in the bass. In Example 1, the embellishing tones are a passing tone and a suspension. These embellishing tones happen to always be a sixth and a fourth above the bass, and their appearance often intensifies the expectation to hear a cadence, hence the name “[latex]\mathrm{cad.}^6_4[/latex].” Although the [latex]\mathrm{cad.}^6_4[/latex] often shows up at cadence points, it may show up anywhere in a phrase as an embellishment of V(7).

title: 以終止四六和弦加強結尾
text: 關於 [latex]^6_4[/latex] 和弦[latex]^6_4[/latex] 和弦的特別之處，在於它包含與低音不協和的四度。因此，作曲家會以特殊方式處理 [latex]^6_4[/latex] 和弦，可分為四類。為了反映這些特定用法，每一類 [latex]^6_4[/latex] 都有與其功能相關的標籤。後續章節會介紹其餘 [latex]^6_4[/latex] 類型。
en: A note on [latex]^6_4[/latex] chords. [latex]^6_4[/latex] chords are special because they involve a dissonance (the fourth) with the bass. Composers therefore treat [latex]^6_4[/latex] chords in distinct ways, which fall into four categories. To acknowledge their special usage, each variety of [latex]^6_4[/latex] chord has its own label that relates to how the chord functions. Future chapters will introduce the remaining [latex]^6_4[/latex] chord types.

title: 以終止四六和弦加強結尾
text: 終止四六和弦的標記
en: Labeling cadential 6/4

title: 以終止四六和弦加強結尾
text: 你可能注意到，範例 1 的 [latex]\mathrm{cad.}^6_4[/latex] 包含 B[latex]\flat[/latex]、G、E[latex]\flat[/latex]，在片段的調性中，正好拼成主三和弦的第二轉位。為什麼卻標成 [latex]\mathrm{V}^6_4[/latex]？除了 [latex]\mathrm{cad.}^6_4[/latex] 是兩個裝飾音結合、並非獨立三和弦之外，還有兩個理由支持使用 [latex]\mathrm{V}^6_4[/latex]，而非 I[latex]^6_4[/latex]：
en: You might have noticed that the [latex]\mathrm{cad.}^6_4[/latex] in Example 1 involves the notes B[latex]\flat[/latex], G, and E[latex]\flat[/latex], which spells a tonic triad in second inversion in the excerpt’s key. Why are we labeling this chord [latex]\mathrm{V}^6_4[/latex], then? Besides the fact that [latex]\mathrm{cad.}^6_4[/latex] arises from the combination of two embellishing tones (and therefore isn't a standalone triad), here are two additional reasons to use the label [latex]\mathrm{V}^6_4[/latex] over I[latex]^6_4[/latex]:

title: 以終止四六和弦加強結尾
text: 這個和弦出現在強屬前和弦之後。若標為 [latex]\mathrm{I}^6_4[/latex]，就暗示屬前功能走向主功能；但低音為 sol（[latex]\hat{5}[/latex]）時，我們並不會聽到這種進行。[latex]\mathrm{V}^6_4[/latex] 反映它聽起來是 V 的延伸裝飾；I[latex]^6_4[/latex] 則只反映音符的拼寫。[1]
en: The chord appears after a strong predominant. If we label it [latex]\mathrm{I}^6_4[/latex], we'd be implying that a predominant goes to tonic, which is not the sound we hear, given that sol ([latex]\hat{5}[/latex]) is in the bass. [latex]\mathrm{V}^6_4[/latex] reflects the chord’s sound as an elaboration of V, whereas I[latex]^6_4[/latex] reflects the chord’s spelling only.[1]

title: 以終止四六和弦加強結尾
text: 終止 [latex]^6_4[/latex] 可以解決到 V 三和弦，見範例 3a、3c；也可以解決到 V7，見範例 3b、3d。標記 [latex]^{6-5}_{4-3}[/latex] 中的連線，說明 [latex]\mathrm{cad.}^6_4[/latex] 如何解決，也就是「這個進行必須保留在同一聲部中」。低音上方六度所在的聲部，應向下走到五度；四度所在的聲部，應向下走到三度。
en: Cadential [latex]^6_4[/latex] can resolve either to a V triad (Examples 3a, 3c) or a V7 chord (Examples 3b, 3d). The lines in the label [latex]^{6-5}_{4-3}[/latex] tell you how the [latex]\mathrm{cad.}^6_4[/latex] resolves, indicating “keep this motion in the same voice.” That is, whichever voice has a sixth above the bass should fall to a fifth above the bass, and whichever voice has the fourth above the bass should fall to a third above the bass.

title: 以終止四六和弦加強結尾
text: 加入七音同樣簡單：原本重複低音的聲部，向下級進成為和弦七音。數字 8–7 表示這項移動，即低音上方八度降到七度。
en: Adding a seventh is just as straightforward: whatever voice is doubling the bass moves down a step to take the seventh of the chord. This motion is reflected by the figures 8-7 (the octave above the bass moves down to a seventh above the bass).

title: 以終止四六和弦加強結尾
text: [latex]\mathrm{cad.}^6_4[/latex] 是屬和聲的裝飾，因此任何能接到 V 的和聲，也能接到 [latex]\mathrm{cad.}^6_4[/latex]。最常見的仍是強屬前和弦 IV 與 ii6，如範例 4。
en: Since the [latex]\mathrm{cad.}^6_4[/latex] embellishes the dominant, any harmony that approaches V can also approach [latex]\mathrm{cad.}^6_4[/latex]. Most commonly, though, these are the strong predominants IV and ii6 (Example 4).

title: 以終止四六和弦加強結尾
text: 這裡有兩項原則：
en: Two guidelines apply here:

title: 以終止四六和弦加強結尾
text: 和處理其他屬前區域時一樣，要留意屬前和弦與 [latex]\mathrm{cad.}^6_4[/latex] 之間的平行八度。進入與離開 [latex]\mathrm{cad.}^6_4[/latex] 通常都很平順，應避免跳進到 [latex]\mathrm{cad.}^6_4[/latex] 的和弦成員。作曲家偶爾會跳進到低音上方的六度，但跳到四度的情況少得多，因為四度不協和，因此尤其應避免。
en: As always when dealing with the predominant area, watch out for parallel octaves between the predominant and [latex]\mathrm{cad.}^6_4[/latex]. Motion into (and out of) the [latex]\mathrm{cad.}^6_4[/latex] is usually very smooth. Avoid leaping to a member of the [latex]\mathrm{cad.}^6_4[/latex]. While composers do occasionally leap to the sixth above the bass, it's comparatively much rarer to leap to the fourth above the bass because it’s a dissonance, so that in particular should be avoided.

text: 若你還不認同從音響判斷的說法，可以演奏範例 1，但停在 [latex]\mathrm{cad.}^6_4[/latex] 上。它聽起來安定嗎？大概不會。主和弦帶來安定與「回家」的感覺；屬和聲則讓人期待解決。[latex]\mathrm{cad.}^6_4[/latex] 顯然更偏向不安定。↵
en: If you're not convinced by the sound of the chord argument, try playing the passage in Example 1, but stop on the [latex]\mathrm{cad.}^6_4[/latex]. Does it sound stable? Probably not. Tonic chords are associated with stability and a sense of “home,” while dominants are associated with a desire to resolve. The [latex]\mathrm{cad.}^6_4[/latex] surely sounds more unstable than stable. ↵

text: 重點整理和聲延長是西方古典音樂樂句開頭的常見特徵。延長主和聲最常見的方式，是讓主和弦與 V6 或轉位 V7 交替。
en: Key Takeaways Prolongation is a common feature of phrase beginnings in Western classical music. The most common way to prolong the tonic is by alternating tonic with V6 or inverted V7 chords.

title: 以 V⁶ 與轉位 V⁷ 在樂句開頭延長主和聲
text: 西方古典音樂的樂句開頭，通常會延長主和聲，以確立主調。「延長」就是讓某個和聲的影響，超過單一和弦發聲的時間。假設你買了一份冰淇淋，希望享用久一點。一種方法是每次只吃一小口，拉長吃的時間；這樣雖然可行，最後卻可能變成在喝冰淇淋湯。另一種方法是先吃一些，放回冷凍庫，去做別的事，之後再回來吃。你可以說「我整天都在吃冰淇淋」，儘管你並沒有真的每一秒都在吃，哪怕你很想如此。
en: Phrase beginnings in Western classical music typically feature a prolongation of tonic harmony to establish the home key. “Prolongation” just means that the harmony’s influence lasts longer than a single chord. Say, for example, that you bought a serving of ice cream that you wanted to enjoy over an extended period. One way to do it would be to take small bites to extend the length of time you're eating. While this method would work, you might be eating ice cream soup by the end. Another way to do it would be to eat some, put it in the freezer, do some other activity, then come back and eat some more. You might say, “I've been eating ice cream all day,” even though you haven't literally been eating ice cream every second of the day (as much as you might want to).

title: 以 V⁶ 與轉位 V⁷ 在樂句開頭延長主和聲
text: 音樂中也有類似情況。樂句開頭可以持續或重複主和弦，延長它的重要性，如範例 1，就像小口小口吃冰淇淋；但在幾次主和弦之間插入其他和弦，通常更有趣、也更有收穫，就像先把冰淇淋放回冷凍庫，過一會再回來吃。
en: Something analogous happens in music. We could prolong the tonic’s importance at the beginning of a phrase by holding or repeating the chord (like taking small bites of the ice cream), as in Example 1, but more interesting and rewarding is to use other chords between instances of the tonic (like putting the ice cream in the freezer and coming back to it later).

en: Example 1. Prolongation by sustaining or repeating a chord.

title: 以 V⁶ 與轉位 V⁷ 在樂句開頭延長主和聲
text: 範例 2 示範樂句開頭最常見的主和聲延長方式：在主三和弦之間使用轉位 V7。主和聲的影響仍較強，因為：（1）它位於比 V7 更強的拍位或超小節拍位；（2）它至少出現一次原位，而 V7 則使用較弱的轉位形式。
en: Example 2 shows one instance of the most common way to prolong tonic at the beginning of a phrase: using inverted V7s between tonic triads. The tonic’s influence is felt more strongly because (1) it’s on stronger beats or hyperbeats than the V7, and (2) it appears at least once in root position, whereas the V7 is in a weaker inversion.

en: The tonic prolongations covered in this chapter are the ones most commonly seen in Western classical music, and they all share several traits:

title: 以 V⁶ 與轉位 V⁷ 在樂句開頭延長主和聲
text: 由三個和弦構成。第一與最後和弦是 I 或 I6。中間和弦是 V6 或轉位 V7。V6 或轉位 V7 的解決，沿用〈以終止 [latex]^6_4[/latex] 加強結尾〉學過的原則。
en: They are three chords long The first and last chords are I or I6 The middle chord is V6 or an inverted V7 The V6 or inverted V7 resolves using the same principles we learned in Strengthening Endings with Cadential [latex]^6_4[/latex]

This is because ti ([latex]\hat{7}[/latex]) is in the bass, and we know that ti ([latex]\hat{7}[/latex]) must resolve to do ([latex]\hat{1}[/latex]). As always, follow the typical writing procedure.

text: [latex]\mathrm{V}^4_2[/latex] 通常透過 [latex]\mathrm{I-V^4_2-I^6}[/latex]，使原位 I 走向第一轉位 I，見範例 5。原因是 [latex]\mathrm{V}^4_2[/latex] 的低音 fa（[latex]\hat{4}[/latex]）必須解決到 mi（[latex]\hat{3}[/latex]），因為 fa（[latex]\hat{4}[/latex]）是和弦七音。仍請依一般寫作步驟進行。

title: 運用樂句模型進行和聲分析
text: 重點整理本章介紹一種和聲分析策略：藉由低音線索，有根據地推測樂句中使用的和聲進行。聆聽並辨認樂句的結尾。分析各樂句結尾終止式的和聲。辨認導向終止式的強屬前和弦。回到樂句開頭，朝終止式的方向逐步分析。
en: Key Takeaways This chapter provides a strategy for harmonic analysis, in which we use the bass line to make an educated guess about what harmonic progression is active in a phrase: Identify phrase endings by listening. Provide a harmonic analysis of each phrase ending's cadence. Identify the strong predominant that leads to the cadence. Back up the the beginning of the phrase and analyze toward the cadence.

title: 運用樂句模型進行和聲分析
text: 概述
en: Overview

title: 運用樂句模型進行和聲分析
text: 到目前為止，我們大多以短小的音樂片段為例，著重觀察作曲家如何營造樂句開始與結束的感覺。本章將探討一個較長的樂句，其中運用了我們已學過的部分和聲；目標是學會如何快速進行和聲分析，以及如何從分析中辨識樂句模型的運作方式。下方的教學影片（例 1）示範整個過程，影片後則列出步驟概要與相關指引。
en: So far, we’ve mostly been looking at short segments of music, focusing on how composers create a sense of beginning and ending in a phrase. In this chapter, we consider a longer phrase of music that employs some of the harmony we’ve learned so far, with the goal of learning how to perform a harmonic analysis quickly and how to identify the phrase model at work in our analysis. The video lesson below (Example 1) walks through the process and is followed by an outline of the steps (along with some guidance).

title: 運用樂句模型進行和聲分析
text: OMT 和聲分析教學影片
en: OMT Performing Harmonic Analysis (requires internet)

title: 運用樂句模型進行和聲分析
text: 例 1。和聲分析教學影片。
en: Example 1. Video lesson on harmonic analysis.

title: 運用樂句模型進行和聲分析
text: 進行和聲分析
en: Performing a Harmonic Analysis

title: 運用樂句模型進行和聲分析
text: 辨認樂句結尾。聆聽時，下列線索往往很有幫助：新樂句開始，或先前樂句的開頭再次出現。這表示「舊」樂句應該剛剛結束。抵達目標的感覺，通常以終止式為標誌。分析樂句結尾。聆聽並標示終止式；樂句結尾通常會有終止式，但也可能沒有。分析結尾的和聲：我們知道，若是半終止，樂句就結束在 V；若是正格終止，樂句就以 V(7)–I 結束。在半終止（HC）的低音中找出 sol [latex](\hat{5})[/latex]，在正格終止（AC）的低音中找出 sol–do [latex](\hat5-\hat1)[/latex]。也要留意終止四六和弦 [latex](\mathrm{cad.^6_4})[/latex]；它常會出現在終止式中。尋找強屬前和弦。從終止式往前回溯，尋找強屬前和弦。記得，強屬前和弦的低音通常是 fa [latex](\hat{4})[/latex]，但也可能是 re [latex](\hat{2})[/latex]。從開頭開始分析。運用你對主和聲延長的了解，觀察低音線條，有根據地推測此處如何延長主和聲。接著，檢視每個低音上方和弦所含的各音，確認推測是否正確。
en: Identify phrase endings. It's often helpful to listen for: A new phrase beginning or a repetition of a previous phrase beginning. This tells you an “old” phrase must have just ended. A sense of goal, often marked by a cadence. Analyze the phrase ending. Listen, and label the cadence if present (it often is). Provide a harmonic analysis of the ending: You know that if there's a half cadence, the phrase ends on V, and if there's an authentic cadence, the phrase ends with V(7)-I. Look for sol [latex](\hat{5})[/latex] in the bass at a HC or sol–do [latex](\hat5-\hat1)[/latex] in the bass at an AC. Be careful to look for [latex](\mathrm{cad.^6_4})[/latex], which is often present at a cadence. Look for a strong predominant. Back up from the cadence to look for a strong predominant. Remember that usually fa [latex](\hat{4})[/latex] is in the bass for the strong predominant, though re [latex](\hat{2})[/latex] is also possible. Analyze from the beginning. Use your knowledge of tonic prolongations and take a look at the bass line to make an educated guess about what you think is happening to prolong tonic. Verify your guess to make sure it's accurate by taking stock of the notes in the chord above each bass note.

title: 運用樂句模型進行和聲分析
text: 在和聲分析中辨認樂句模型
en: Identifying the Phrase Model in Harmonic Analysis

title: 運用樂句模型進行和聲分析
text: 若要辨認樂句模型如何在特定樂句中運作，可以使用〈和聲、終止式與樂句結尾入門〉所學的和聲功能標籤。每個樂句都只有一組（僅此一組！）Tb–PD–D–Te 標籤：開頭的主和聲（Tonic beginning）、屬前和聲（Predominant）、屬和聲（Dominant），以及結尾的主和聲（Tonic ending）。標示方式如下：
en: To identify how the phrase model operates in a given phrase, we can apply the harmonic function labels we learned in Introduction to Harmony, Cadences, and Phrase Endings. For each phrase, we get one (and only one!) set of the labels Tb–PD–D–Te: Tonic beginning, Predominant, Dominant, and Tonic ending. To apply them, do the following:

title: 運用樂句模型進行和聲分析
text: 找到樂句結尾。在終止式的屬和弦上標示 D。若樂句以正格終止結束，在終止式的主和弦上標示 Te；若以半終止結束，則可省略這個標籤。找到強屬前和弦。在緊接終止式屬和弦之前的強屬前和弦中，由左至右找到第一個，標示 PD。標示開頭的主和聲。在樂句開頭的主和弦上標示 Tb。少數情況下，樂句可能延後這個主和弦的出現，甚至完全省略它。這種延後或省略的情形，在浪漫時期的音樂中較常見。
en: Locate the phrase ending. Apply the D label to the cadential dominant. If the phrase ends with an authentic cadence, apply the Te label to the tonic of the cadence. If it ends with a half cadence, you can omit this label. Locate the strong predominant. The PD label goes on the first strong predominant (reading left to right) that comes immediately before the cadential dominant. Label the opening tonic. The Tb label goes on the tonic that starts the phrase. Rarely, a phrase may delay this tonic or may omit it altogether. This kind of delay or omission is more common in Romantic music.

title: 以導音和弦在樂句開頭延長主和聲
text: 重點整理作曲家有時會以 [latex]\mathrm{vii^{o7}}[/latex] 或其轉位，代替轉位的 [latex]\mathrm{V^7}[/latex] 和弦來延長主和聲。[latex]\mathrm{vii^{o7}}[/latex] 的各種轉位，可採用與 [latex]\mathrm{V^7}[/latex] 某一特定轉位相同的用法。[latex]\mathrm{V^7}[/latex] 與 [latex]\mathrm{vii^{o7}}[/latex] 如何配對，取決於各和弦所配置的低音。凡是可用 [latex]\mathrm{V^6_5}[/latex] 或 [latex]\mathrm{V^6}[/latex] 的位置，都可使用 [latex]\mathrm{vii^{o7}}[/latex]。[latex]\mathrm{vii^{o}\begin{smallmatrix}6\\5\end{smallmatrix}}[/latex] 或 [latex]\mathrm{vii^{o6}}[/latex] 可代替 [latex]\mathrm{V^4_3}[/latex]。[latex]\mathrm{vii^{o}\begin{smallmatrix}4\\3\end{smallmatrix}}[/latex] 可代替 [latex]\mathrm{V^4_2}[/latex]。
en: Key Takeaways Instead of using an inverted [latex]\mathrm{V^7}[/latex] chord to prolong tonic, composers sometimes use [latex]\mathrm{vii^{o7}}[/latex] or its inversions. Each inversion of [latex]\mathrm{vii^{o7}}[/latex] can be used in the same way as a particular inversion of [latex]\mathrm{V^7}[/latex]. The pairings of [latex]\mathrm{V^7}[/latex] and [latex]\mathrm{vii^{o7}}[/latex] are based on the bass note each chord harmonizes. [latex]\mathrm{vii^{o7}}[/latex] can be used anywhere that [latex]\mathrm{V^6_5}[/latex] or [latex]\mathrm{V^6}[/latex] can be used. [latex]\mathrm{vii^{o}\begin{smallmatrix}6\\5\end{smallmatrix}}[/latex] or [latex]\mathrm{vii^{o6}}[/latex] can be used in place of [latex]\mathrm{V^4_3}[/latex]. [latex]\mathrm{vii^{o}\begin{smallmatrix}4\\3\end{smallmatrix}}[/latex] can be used in place of [latex]\mathrm{V^4_2}[/latex].

title: 以導音和弦在樂句開頭延長主和聲
text: 前面介紹過，基本上可以使用四種進行來延長主和聲，並依低音線將它們分類（可回顧該章的彙整小節）。本章將介紹另一種替這些相同低音線配置和聲的方法：使用能代替 V7 的導音和弦。例 1 摘自莫札特的〈羔羊經〉（Agnus Dei），以 viio7 及其轉位延長主和聲。原作下方的改寫版本，顯示原作的低音線也可以搭配 V7 及其轉位。聆聽時，請留意兩個版本在色彩上的差異。你或許會聽出，原作充滿一種美妙的張力，而改寫版本的這種張力較少。
en: Earlier, we saw how the tonic can be prolonged using essentially four kinds of progressions, which we categorized according to their basslines (see the summary section of that chapter for a reminder). In this chapter, we consider an alternative way to harmonize those same tonic-prolongation bass lines using a harmony that can substitute for V7: the leading-tone chord. Example 1 shows a passage from Mozart's "Agnus Dei" that uses viio7 and its inversions to prolong tonic. Below the actual version, a recomposition shows that the bass line from the actual version can also be harmonized with V7 and its inversions. As you listen, notice the differences in color between the two versions. You may hear that the actual version is full of a wonderful tension that is less present in the recomposed version.

text: 在說明如何替代之前，有三點需要強調：
en: Before we address how this substitution works, here are three points we need to emphasize:

title: 以導音和弦在樂句開頭延長主和聲
text: 導音三和弦一律使用第一轉位 viio6，因為其他位置會形成與低音不協和的音程，作曲家通常會避免。在小調中，建立導音和弦時，要記得使用 ti [latex](\uparrow\hat{7})[/latex]，而非 te [latex](\downarrow\hat{7})[/latex]。換句話說，要記得升高第七級，使它成為導音。在大調中，若不作變音處理，導音七和弦的性質是半減七和弦（例如 C 大調中的 B–D–F–A）。不過，作曲家往往偏好全減七和弦的音響，因此在大調中，我們幾乎總會發現，作曲家將和弦七音降低，使它成為全減七和弦（例如 C 大調中的 B–D–F–A♭；見例 2）。兩種都可以使用，但 viio7 遠比 vii∅7 常見；下文會說明原因。
en: The leading-tone chord as a triad is always used in first inversion viio6. This is because any other inversion creates a dissonance with the bass that composers tend to avoid. In minor, we need to remember to use ti [latex](\uparrow\hat{7})[/latex], not te [latex](\downarrow\hat{7})[/latex], to build the leading-tone chord. In other words, remember to raise the leading tone. In major, the leading-tone seventh chord’s quality is half diminished if we don't alter it (e.g. in C major: B-D-F-A). Composers tend to prefer the sound of a fully diminished 7th chord, though, so we nearly always find that in major keys, composers lower the chordal seventh to make the chord fully diminished (e.g., in C major: B-D-F-A♭) (Example 2). You can use both, but viio7 is much more common than vii∅7, and we’ll see why below.

text: 依低音是哪個音而定，[latex]\mathrm{vii^{o7}}[/latex] 幾乎所有的轉位（以及 [latex]\mathrm{vii^{o6}})[/latex]，都可代替 [latex]\mathrm{V^7}[/latex] 的某種轉位（也包括 [latex]\mathrm{V^6})[/latex]；見例 3。例如，凡是可用 [latex]\mathrm{V^6_5}[/latex] 或 [latex]\mathrm{V^6}[/latex] 的位置，都可以使用 [latex]\mathrm{vii^{o7}}[/latex]。同樣地，[latex]\mathrm{vii^{o}\begin{smallmatrix}6\\5\end{smallmatrix}}[/latex] 或 [latex]\mathrm{vii^{o6}}[/latex] 可以代替 [latex]\mathrm{V^4_3}[/latex]；[latex]\mathrm{vii^{o}\begin{smallmatrix}4\\3\end{smallmatrix}}[/latex] 則可以代替 [latex]\mathrm{V^4_2}[/latex]。
en: Almost all inversions of [latex]\mathrm{vii^{o7}}[/latex] (plus [latex]\mathrm{vii^{o6}})[/latex] can substitute for an inversion of [latex]\mathrm{V^7}[/latex] (and [latex]\mathrm{V^6})[/latex] according to which note is in the bass (Example 3). What this means is that, for example, [latex]\mathrm{vii^{o7}}[/latex] can be used anywhere that [latex]\mathrm{V^6_5}[/latex] or [latex]\mathrm{V^6}[/latex] can be used. Similarly, [latex]\mathrm{vii^{o}\begin{smallmatrix}6\\5\end{smallmatrix}}[/latex] or [latex]\mathrm{vii^{o6}}[/latex] can be used in place of [latex]\mathrm{V^4_3}[/latex], and [latex]\mathrm{vii^{o}\begin{smallmatrix}4\\3\end{smallmatrix}}[/latex] can be used in place of [latex]\mathrm{V^4_2}[/latex].

title: 以導音和弦在樂句開頭延長主和聲
text: 好在聲部寫作方面，需要另外學習的內容並不多。繼續遵循一般的聲部寫作程序，並依上方聲部各傾向音的傾向加以解決即可。例 4 複習這些傾向，並加入一個我們先前尚未在屬功能和弦中見過的音：le/la [latex](\downarrow\hat{6}[/latex]/[latex]\hat{6})[/latex]。例 5 展示以 viio7 及其轉位延長主和聲的方式，並將每種方式與使用 [latex]\mathrm{V^7}[/latex] 及其轉位的對應進行相比較。
en: Luckily, there isn't too much else to learn with respect to part writing. Continue to follow typical part-writing procedures and to resolve active notes in the upper voices according to their tendencies. Example 4 reviews these tendencies and adds the one new note we haven't seen yet in a dominant-function chord: le/la [latex](\downarrow\hat{6}[/latex]/[latex]\hat{6})[/latex]. Example 5 shows tonic prolongations involving viio7 and its inversions, and it compares each to a corresponding prolongation involving [latex]\mathrm{V^7}[/latex] and its inversions.

title: 以導音和弦在樂句開頭延長主和聲
text: 你可能注意到，[latex]\mathrm{vii^{o}\begin{smallmatrix}4\\2\end{smallmatrix}}[/latex] 並沒有對應的 [latex]\mathrm{V^7}[/latex] 轉位。這是因為它的低音是 le [latex](\downarrow\hat{6})[/latex]，而這個音不屬於 [latex]\mathrm{V^7}[/latex]。[latex]\mathrm{vii^{o}\begin{smallmatrix}4\\2\end{smallmatrix}}[/latex] 是很少見的和聲，因為預期中 le 下行至 sol 的解決 [latex](\downarrow\hat6-\hat5)[/latex]（見例 4）發生在低音。目前我們已看到，低音的 sol [latex](\hat{5})[/latex] 通常承載 V 或 [latex]\mathrm{V^7}[/latex]，這裡也一樣：[latex]\mathrm{vii^{o}\begin{smallmatrix}4\\2\end{smallmatrix}}[/latex] 接到 [latex]\mathrm{cad.^6_4}[/latex]（例 6）。不過，還是要再次強調，[latex]\mathrm{vii^{o}\begin{smallmatrix}4\\2\end{smallmatrix}}[/latex] 並不是常見的和弦。
en: You might have noticed that [latex]\mathrm{vii^{o}\begin{smallmatrix}4\\2\end{smallmatrix}}[/latex] doesn't correspond to an inversion of [latex]\mathrm{V^7}[/latex]. That's because it's built on le [latex](\downarrow\hat{6})[/latex], which isn't in [latex]\mathrm{V^7}[/latex]. [latex]\mathrm{vii^{o}\begin{smallmatrix}4\\2\end{smallmatrix}}[/latex] is a very rare harmony because the expected resolution from le down to sol [latex](\downarrow\hat6-\hat5)[/latex] (see Example 4) occurs in the bass. So far, we've seen that sol [latex](\hat{5})[/latex] in the bass typically supports V or [latex]\mathrm{V^7}[/latex], and that's also the case here: [latex]\mathrm{vii^{o}\begin{smallmatrix}4\\2\end{smallmatrix}}[/latex] goes to [latex]\mathrm{cad.^6_4}[/latex] (Example 6). Again, though, [latex]\mathrm{vii^{o}\begin{smallmatrix}4\\2\end{smallmatrix}}[/latex] is not a very common chord.

title: 以導音和弦在樂句開頭延長主和聲
text: vii∅7 會帶來 viio7 沒有的聲部進行問題，因為它的 re [latex](\hat{2})[/latex] 與 la [latex](\hat{6})[/latex] 之間有完全五度。這或許也是作曲家偏好 viio7 而非 vii∅7 的另一個原因：使用 ∅7 時，必須留意平行五度，如例 7 所示。一個簡單的避免方法是：使用 vii∅7 或其轉位時，務必讓 re [latex](\hat{2})[/latex] 位於 la [latex](\hat{6})[/latex] 上方。唯一無法遵循這項建議的情形，是 [latex]\mathrm{vii^{∅}\begin{smallmatrix}6\\5\end{smallmatrix}}[/latex]，因為此時 re [latex](\hat{2})[/latex] 就在低音。雖然使用 [latex]\mathrm{vii^{∅}\begin{smallmatrix}6\\5\end{smallmatrix}}[/latex] 仍有辦法避免平行，我們建議直接改用 [latex]\mathrm{vii^{o}\begin{smallmatrix}6\\5\end{smallmatrix}}[/latex]，或延長 I6（如下例所示）。
en: vii∅7 presents voice-leading challenges that are not present with viio7 because it contains a perfect fifth between re [latex](\hat{2})[/latex] and la [latex](\hat{6})[/latex]. This is perhaps another reason that composers favor viio7 over vii∅7: with ∅7, we need to watch out for parallel fifths, as in Example 7. An easy way to avoid them is to always make sure that re [latex](\hat{2})[/latex] is above la [latex](\hat{6})[/latex] when you use vii∅7 or its inversions. The one time where this advice is impossible is with [latex]\mathrm{vii^{∅}\begin{smallmatrix}6\\5\end{smallmatrix}}[/latex], where re [latex](\hat{2})[/latex] is in the bass. Although it's possible to avoid parallels with [latex]\mathrm{vii^{∅}\begin{smallmatrix}6\\5\end{smallmatrix}}[/latex], we'd recommend just using [latex]\mathrm{vii^{o}\begin{smallmatrix}6\\5\end{smallmatrix}}[/latex] or expanding I6 (as shown below) instead.

title: 以四六和弦延長和聲
text: 重點整理本章介紹終止 [latex]^6_4[/latex] 以外的另外三種 [latex]^6_4[/latex] 和弦。經過（passing，簡寫 pass.）[latex]^6_4[/latex]：以 [latex]^6_4[/latex] 和弦為低音中的經過音配置和聲。通常用於延長主和聲或屬前和聲，且總是位於兩個功能相同的和弦之間。鄰音（neighbor，簡寫 n.）[latex]^6_4[/latex]：低音保持不動，上方兩個聲部作上鄰音進行。通常用於延長主和聲或屬和聲，前後兩個和弦一定都是原位。琶音（arpeggiating，簡寫 arp.）[latex]^6_4[/latex]：低音以琶音進行經過和弦五音，上方聲部則以某種方式維持該和弦。它可以延長任何和聲，分析時通常不必特別標示。下方例 6 的表格，彙整我們建議在分析中標示的三種 [latex]^6_4[/latex] 的特徵。
en: Key Takeaways This chapter introduces three additional [latex]^6_4[/latex] chords beyond cadential [latex]^6_4[/latex]. Passing (pass.) [latex]^6_4[/latex] involves a passing tone in the bass that has been harmonized by a [latex]^6_4[/latex] chord. It typically prolongs tonic or predominant harmonies, and it always occurs between two chords of the same function. Neighbor (n.) [latex]^6_4[/latex] involves a static bass above which two of the upper voices perform upper neighbor motion. It typically prolongs tonic or dominant harmonies, and the chords on both sides of it are always in root position. Arpeggiating (arp.) [latex]^6_4[/latex] involves a bass that arpeggiates through the fifth of the chord while the upper voices sustain the chord in some way. It may prolong any harmony, and we don't typically bother recognizing it in analysis. The table in Example 6 below summarizes the characteristics of each of the three types of [latex]^6_4[/latex] that we advocate labeling in analysis.

title: 以四六和弦延長和聲
text: 目前我們已看到，主和聲（T）區域最常以屬功能和弦延長，尤其常用轉位的 [latex]\mathrm{V^7}[/latex]。本章將介紹另外幾種較少見的方法，不只可以延長主和弦，也能延長屬和弦與屬前和弦。前面說過，[latex]^6_4[/latex] 和弦含有與低音不協和的四度，因此需要特殊處理。我們已學過終止四六 [latex]\mathrm{cad.^6_4}[/latex]；這裡轉而討論 [latex]^6_4[/latex] 和弦的另外三種用法：經過 [latex]^6_4[/latex]、鄰音 [latex]^6_4[/latex] 與琶音 [latex]^6_4[/latex]。分析時，每遇到 [latex]^6_4[/latex] 和弦，都應先停下來辨認它的類型（終止、經過、鄰音或琶音），因為 [latex]^6_4[/latex] 的類型決定了它的標記。對於 [latex]^6_4[/latex] 和弦，只標羅馬數字並不足夠，還必須標明類型。
en: So far, we've seen that the tonic (T) area is most commonly prolonged using dominant-function chords, especially inverted [latex]\mathrm{V^7}[/latex]s. In this chapter, we look at some additional, less common ways to prolong not only tonic chords, but also dominant and predominant chords. Earlier, we saw how [latex]^6_4[/latex] chords are treated in special ways because they contain a dissonance with the bass (the fourth). We've already learned about [latex]\mathrm{cad.^6_4}[/latex]; here, we turn to the three other ways [latex]^6_4[/latex] chords can be used: passing [latex]^6_4[/latex], neighboring [latex]^6_4[/latex], and arpeggiating [latex]^6_4[/latex]. Note that in analysis, whenever you encounter a [latex]^6_4[/latex] chord, you should stop and identify which kind it is (cadential, passing, neighboring, or arpeggiating) because the kind of [latex]^6_4[/latex] determines the label. For [latex]^6_4[/latex] chords, the Roman numeral by itself isn’t a sufficient label—the type also needs to be included.

title: 以四六和弦延長和聲
text: 經過（pass.）[latex]^6_4[/latex] 是建立在低音經過音上的 [latex]^6_4[/latex] 和弦（例 1），最常用於延長主和聲或屬前和聲。請留意，[latex]\mathrm{pass.^6_4}[/latex] 前後的和弦，功能一定相同（例如 [latex]\mathrm{IV^6-pass.^6_4-ii^6}[/latex]），不能是不同功能（例如 [latex]\mathrm{IV^6-pass.^6_4-I}[/latex]）。
en: The passing (pass.) [latex]^6_4[/latex] is a [latex]^6_4[/latex] chord built on a passing tone in the bass (Example 1). It's most commonly found prolonging tonic or predominant harmonies. Importantly, the chords on both sides of the [latex]\mathrm{pass.^6_4}[/latex] are always the same function (e.g., [latex]\mathrm{IV^6-pass.^6_4-ii^6}[/latex]), not of different function (e.g., [latex]\mathrm{IV^6-pass.^6_4-I}[/latex]).

title: 以四六和弦延長和聲
text: 寫出完整低音。低音應為三個級進的音，第一個與最後一個音屬於相同的功能區域（T 或 PD）；中間的音就是經過音。拼出 pass.[latex]\mathbf{^6_4}[/latex]。和 [latex]\mathrm{cad.^6_4}[/latex] 一樣，拼出 [latex]\mathrm{pass.^6_4}[/latex] 時，要找出低音上方四度與六度的音。另外要有一個聲部重複低音，也和 [latex]\mathrm{cad.^6_4}[/latex] 一樣。寫出完整女高音。女高音應採用級進的旋律線，不要採用保持不動的聲部線。填入內聲部，讓它們盡量少移動。
en: Write the entire bass. You should have three notes in stepwise motion where the first and last notes belong to the same functional area (T or PD). The middle note will be your passing tone. Spell the pass.[latex]\mathbf{^6_4}[/latex]. Just like with [latex]\mathrm{cad.^6_4}[/latex], to spell [latex]\mathrm{pass.^6_4}[/latex], determine what notes are a fourth and sixth above the bass. One voice will double the bass, just like in [latex]\mathrm{cad.^6_4}[/latex]. Write the entire soprano. The soprano should be a line that moves by step, not the static line. Fill in inner voices, making them move as little as possible.

title: 以四六和弦延長和聲
text: 寫出完整低音。低音為三個相同的音，通常是 do–do–do 或 sol–sol–sol（[latex]\hat1-\hat1-\hat1[/latex] 或 [latex]\hat5-\hat5-\hat5[/latex]）。拼出 n.[latex]\mathbf{^6_4}[/latex]。[latex]\mathrm{n.^6_4}[/latex] 配置在中間那個低音上。和 [latex]\mathrm{cad.}[/latex] 與 [latex]\mathrm{pass.^6_4}[/latex] 一樣，找出中間低音上方六度與四度的音，並以一個聲部重複低音。寫出完整女高音。女高音可選擇作上鄰音進行，也可保持不動。與 [latex]\mathrm{cad.}[/latex] 或 [latex]\mathrm{pass.^6_4}[/latex] 相較，[latex]\mathrm{n.^6_4}[/latex] 更常採用保持不動的女高音。填入內聲部，讓它們盡量少移動。
en: Write the entire bass. The bass will be three of the same note, typically do–do–do or sol–sol–sol ([latex]\hat1-\hat1-\hat1[/latex] or [latex]\hat5-\hat5-\hat5[/latex]) Spell n.[latex]\mathbf{^6_4}[/latex]. The [latex]\mathrm{n.^6_4}[/latex] will be over the middle bass note. As with [latex]\mathrm{cad.}[/latex] and [latex]\mathrm{pass.^6_4}[/latex], determine a sixth and fourth above the middle bass note. One voice will double the bass. Write the entire soprano. For the soprano, choose either an upper-neighbor line or the static line. Unlike with [latex]\mathrm{cad.}[/latex] or [latex]\mathrm{pass.^6_4}[/latex], [latex]\mathrm{n.^6_4}[/latex] will more frequently have a static line in the soprano. Fill in the inner voices, making them move as little as possible.

text: 琶音（arp.）[latex]^6_4[/latex] 通常由低音跳進到和弦五音、上方聲部繼續維持該和弦而形成。常見於結尾的低音琶音進行（例 3），或圓舞曲風格的伴奏（例 5）。與其他類型不同，[latex]\mathrm{arp.^6_4}[/latex] 在分析時通常不必另外標示。例 5 雖然用數字標出了它，但並非一定要這麼做；每個小節都可以直接標為 I。
en: Arpeggiating (arp.) [latex]^6_4[/latex] is typically created when the bass leaps to the fifth of a chord while the upper voices sustain the chord. It's commonly found in, for example, ending bass arpeggiations (Example 3) or waltz-style accompaniments (Example 5). Unlike the other types, [latex]\mathrm{arp.^6_4}[/latex] typically doesn’t need to be labeled in analysis. Example 5 identifies it using figures, but it’s not necessary to do so—each measure could simply be labeled as I.

title: 以變格進行延長和聲
text: 重點整理由 IV 到 I 的變格進行，可在正格終止（AC）之後，或樂句開頭延長主和聲。分析時，將變格用法的 (IV) 加上括號，以區別於 IV 更常見的屬前功能。在十八、十九世紀音樂中，(IV) 的這種用法較常出現在和聲延長中，而非終止式中，因此本書這一部分使用「變格進行」一詞，而非「變格終止」。兩個和弦都是原位時，變格進行的寫作並不困難；但只要其中一個和弦使用轉位，就要留意平行音程。
en: Key Takeaways Plagal motion from IV to I serves to prolong tonic either after an authentic cadence (AC) or at the beginning of a phrase. We place plagal (IV) in parentheses in analysis to differentiate it from the more common use of IV as a predominant. In 18th- and 19th-century music, this use of (IV) more commonly occurs as part of a prolongation rather than as part of a cadence, so this part of the book will use the term “plagal motion” rather than “plagal cadence.” Writing with plagal motion is not difficult when both harmonies are in root position, but watch for parallels when either harmony is inverted.

title: 以變格進行延長和聲
text: 本章播放清單
en: Chapter Playlist

title: 以變格進行延長和聲
text: 前面提過，ii 與 IV 等具有屬前功能的和弦，通常用於加強樂句朝向屬和弦的動力，常出現在樂句結尾。本章探討一種特殊情況：IV 在此不具屬前功能，而是延長 I，形成變格進行（plagal motion）。分析時，將變格用法的 (IV) 加上括號，以區別於 IV 更常見的屬前功能。變格進行最常在兩個位置延長主和聲：一是正格終止之後（如例 1），二是樂句開頭，代替更常見、使用屬功能和弦的主和聲延長。
en: Earlier we saw that chords that function as predominants, such as ii and IV, are typically used to strengthen a phrase’s motion toward the dominant, often at the end of a phrase. In this chapter, we look at a special situation in which IV functions not as a predominant but rather to prolong I, which produces plagal motion. In analysis, we place plagal (IV) in parentheses to differentiate it from the more common use of IV as a predominant. Plagal motion most commonly serves to prolong tonic in two places: after an authentic cadence (as in Example 1) or at the beginning of a phrase in place of the more common tonic prolongations involving dominant-function chords.

en: Example 1. Plagal motion after a PAC in Handel, "Hallelujah Chorus," from Messiah (3:02-3:29).

title: 以變格進行延長和聲
text: 變格進行與變格終止你有時會看到所有 (IV)–I 進行都被稱為「變格終止」，但本書這一部分改用較廣義的「變格進行」，以維持我們對終止式的定義：標誌樂句的結尾。真正以 (IV)–I 結束的樂句確實存在；不過，在十八世紀古典音樂中，(IV)–I 更常在完全正格終止之後，或樂句開頭延長主和聲。若所有情況都稱為「變格終止」，便會錯誤地暗示 (IV)–I 一定會結束樂句。「變格進行」則能描述 (IV)–I 更常見的延長功能，同時也不否認它確實能夠結束樂句的情況。
en: Plagal motion versus plagal cadence You may sometimes see all (IV)–I motions described as “plagal cadences,” but this part of the book uses the broader term “plagal motion” instead, preserving our definition of cadences as marking the ends of phrases. While true phrase endings involving the progression (IV)–I do exist, in 18th-century classical music, it's more common to see a (IV)–I tonic prolongation either after a PAC or at the beginning of a phrase. Using “plagal cadence” in all scenarios would inaccurately imply that (IV)–I always ends a phrase, whereas “plagal motion” allows us to describe the more common usage of (IV)–I as prolongational without rejecting the situations in which (IV)–I really does end a phrase.

title: 以變格進行延長和聲
text: 作曲家在正格終止之後使用變格進行時，最常讓 I 與 (IV) 都採用原位。只要遵循以下三項建議，這種進行的平行風險便很低，因此不難寫作（例 2）：
en: It's most common to see both I and (IV) in root position when composers use plagal motion after an authentic cadence. The progression isn't difficult to write, since the danger of parallels is low, provided you follow three pieces of advice (Example 2):

title: 以變格進行延長和聲
text: I 與 (IV) 都使用完整和弦，不省略五音。重複低音，這也是原位和弦的常見做法。所有上方聲部都採用級進，或保留共同音。
en: Make both I and (IV) complete (don't omit the fifth). Double the bass (as is common in root position chords). Move all upper voices by step or common tone.

title: 以變格進行延長和聲
text: 女高音最常使用 do（[latex]\hat{1}[/latex]）。這很合理，因為變格進行出現在完全正格終止之後，而旋律在該終止式中，已經完成走向 do（[latex]\hat{1}[/latex]）的歷程。一如往常，請遵循一般的聲部寫作程序。
en: It's most common to have do ([latex]\hat{1}[/latex]) in the soprano, which makes sense given that plagal motion comes after a PAC where the melody has already completed its journey toward do ([latex]\hat{1}[/latex]). As always, follow typical writing procedures.

title: 以變格進行延長和聲
text: 原位和弦的變格進行（如例 2）有時也會出現在樂句開頭，但例 3 顯示，(IV) 也能接到 I6。這時要留意 (IV) 與 I6 之間的平行音程：如果例 3 的女低音走到 G（以括號標示），而非 B♭，就會與低音形成平行八度。請記得，在樂句開頭，以轉位 V7 延長主和聲的情形，遠比使用 (IV) 常見。因此，在樂句開頭看到 fa–mi（[latex]\hat4-\hat3[/latex]）時，仍應先想到 [latex]\mathrm{V^4_2-I^6}[/latex]，而非 [latex]\mathrm{(IV)-I^6}[/latex]。
en: While the root-position version of plagal motion (as in Example 2) also occurs at phrase beginnings sometimes, Example 3 shows that (IV) can also go to I6. Here, watch for parallels between (IV) and I6: if the alto in Example 3 went to G (shown in parentheses) instead of B♭, it would create parallel octaves with the bass. Remember that it's more common by far for tonic to be prolonged by an inverted V7 than by (IV) at a phrase beginning. When you see fa–mi ([latex]\hat4-\hat3[/latex]) at the beginning of a phrase, your instinct should still be to use [latex]\mathrm{V^4_2-I^6}[/latex] rather than [latex]\mathrm{(IV)-I^6}[/latex].

title: 低音 la（第六級）在樂句開頭、中段與結尾的用法
text: 重點整理本章討論作曲家如何依低音 la [latex](\hat6)[/latex] 在樂句中的位置——開頭、中段或結尾——採用不同的和聲配置。在樂句開頭，低音 la [latex](\hat6)[/latex] 常以兩種方式延長主和聲：以 IV6 配置和聲，形成 [latex]\mathrm{I-IV^6-V^6_5-I}[/latex] 進行（例 1 與例 3）。以變格用法的 (IV6) 配置和聲，形成 [latex]\mathrm{I-IV^6-I^6}[/latex] 進行（例 2 與例 4）。在樂句中段，低音 la [latex](\hat6)[/latex] 常用於：阻礙進行 V(7)–vi（例 5 與例 7）。以 vi 配置和聲，連接主和聲（T）與強屬前和聲（PD）區域（例 6 與例 8）。在樂句結尾，低音 la [latex](\hat6)[/latex] 常用於：形成弗里吉安半終止，即小調中的 iv6–V（例 7 與例 9）。代替預期中屬於強屬前和聲的低音 fa [latex](\hat4)[/latex]（例 10）。
en: Key Takeaways This chapter discusses the various ways in which composers harmonize la [latex](\hat6)[/latex] in the bass depending on where it's found within a phrase: beginning, middle, or ending. At phrase beginnings, la [latex](\hat6)[/latex] is often used to prolong tonic in two ways: harmonized with IV6 in the progression [latex]\mathrm{I-IV^6-V^6_5-I}[/latex] (Examples 1 and 3) harmonized with plagal (IV6) in the progression [latex]\mathrm{I-IV^6-I^6}[/latex] (Examples 2 and 4) At phrase middles, la [latex](\hat6)[/latex] is often used: in a deceptive motion (V(7)–vi) (Examples 5 and 7) to connect the tonic (T) and strong predominant (PD) areas, harmonized with vi (Examples 6 and 8) At phrase endings, la [latex](\hat6)[/latex] is often used: to create a phrygian half cadence (iv6–V in minor) (Examples 7 and 9) as a "stand-in" for the expected strong PD note fa [latex](\hat4)[/latex] (Example 10)

title: 低音 la（第六級）在樂句開頭、中段與結尾的用法
text: [latex]\mathrm{I-IV^6-V^6_5-I}[/latex] 的寫作可能不太容易，尤其是 [latex]\mathrm{IV^6}[/latex] 接到 [latex]\mathrm{V^6}[/latex] 時，既有平行音程的風險，也可能重複導音。沒有任何單一建議能保證避開所有問題。寫作 [latex]\mathrm{I-IV^6-V^6_5-I}[/latex] 時，女高音採用 do–do–re–do [latex](\hat1-\hat1-\hat2-\hat1)[/latex] 或 mi–mi–fa–mi [latex](\hat3-\hat3-\hat4-\hat3)[/latex] 會有幫助，但仍須仔細檢查平行。以 [latex]\mathrm{V^6_5}[/latex] 代替 [latex]\mathrm{V^6}[/latex]，也能降低部分平行風險（例 3）。請注意，這個進行在小調中不太適用，因為低音從 le 到 ti [latex](\downarrow\hat6-\uparrow\hat7)[/latex] 會形成增二度。小調中少數使用此進行的情況，會將 le 升為 la，由 [latex](\downarrow\hat6[/latex] 改成 [latex]\uparrow\hat6)[/latex]，以避免增二度（例 3c 與例 3d）。
en: Writing [latex]\mathrm{I-IV^6-V^6_5-I}[/latex] can be tricky, particularly when [latex]\mathrm{IV^6}[/latex] goes to [latex]\mathrm{V^6}[/latex], since there is a danger both of parallels and of a doubled leading tone. No single piece of advice can guarantee that you’ll avoid problems. When you write [latex]\mathrm{I-IV^6-V^6_5-I}[/latex], the soprano lines do–do–re–do [latex](\hat1-\hat1-\hat2-\hat1)[/latex] and mi–mi–fa–mi [latex](\hat3-\hat3-\hat4-\hat3)[/latex] will help, but you'll need to check carefully for parallels. Using [latex]\mathrm{V^6_5}[/latex] instead of [latex]\mathrm{V^6}[/latex] will also mitigate some of the danger of parallels (Example 3). Note that this progression doesn't work well in minor, where the bass would create an augmented second from le to ti [latex](\downarrow\hat6-\uparrow\hat7)[/latex]. The rare occurrences of this progression in minor raise le to la [latex](\downarrow\hat6[/latex] to [latex]\uparrow\hat6)[/latex] to avoid the augmented second (Examples 3c and 3d).

text: 阻礙進行
en: Deceptive motion

title: 低音 la（第六級）在樂句開頭、中段與結尾的用法
text: 當 V 和弦讓人期待終止式，卻轉向出乎預期的非主和聲時，就稱為阻礙進行（deceptive motion）。最常見的情況是 V(7) 接到 vi 而非 I，低音由 sol 走到 la [latex](\hat5-\hat6)[/latex]。較少見的情況，則是在阻礙進行中，為 la [latex](\hat6)[/latex] 配置 IV6 而非 vi。V(7)–vi 的阻礙進行本身就有平行風險；以下兩點可以避免這些問題（例 7）：（1）照常將 ti 解決到 do [latex](\hat7-\hat1)[/latex]；（2）讓所有上方聲部都與低音反向進行，也就是向下行。
en: When a V chord sets up the expectation for a cadence, but moves instead to an unexpected, non-tonic harmony, this is called deceptive motion. Deceptive motion most commonly occurs when V(7) moves to vi rather than I, with the bass moving sol–la [latex](\hat5-\hat6)[/latex]. Less commonly, la [latex](\hat6)[/latex] may be harmonized with IV6 rather than vi in a deceptive motion. Writing deceptive motion with V(7)–vi carries an inherent danger of parallels that can be avoided by doing the following two things (Example 7): (1) resolve ti–do [latex](\hat7-\hat1)[/latex] as you would do normally, and (2) move all upper voices in contrary motion to the bass (downward).

text: 阻礙進行與阻礙終止有些人用「阻礙終止」一詞，描述我們所稱的「阻礙進行」。由於 V(7)–vi 是避開終止式，而非形成終止式，我們認為「阻礙終止」無法準確描述這個進行的作用，因此偏好較中性的「阻礙進行」。
en: Deceptive motion vs. Deceptive cadence Some people use the term “deceptive cadence” to describe what we refer to as “deceptive motion.” Since the progression V(7)–vi avoids a cadence rather than creating one, we find that the term “deceptive cadence” inaccurately describes the progression’s purpose, so we prefer the more neutral description “deceptive motion.”

title: 低音 la（第六級）在樂句開頭、中段與結尾的用法
text: 弗里吉安半終止（PHC）是一種特殊的樂句終止方式，只出現在小調，使用 iv6–V 進行。之所以稱為「弗里吉安」，是因為低音 le 走到 sol [latex](\downarrow\hat6-\hat5)[/latex] 時形成半音，其音響類似弗里吉安調式中的 ra 走到 do [latex](\downarrow\hat2-\hat1)[/latex]。這個進行有平行音程的風險，也可能在 le 與 ti [latex](\downarrow\hat6-\uparrow\hat7)[/latex] 之間寫出增二度。選擇在 iv6 中重複 do [latex](\hat1)[/latex]，便能避免這些問題（例 10）。弗里吉安半終止很常從 i 接入，女高音則採用 me–fa–sol [latex](\hat3-\hat4-\hat5)[/latex]，如例 10 所示。
en: The phrygian half cadence (PHC) is a special kind of cadential phrase ending that occurs only in minor and involves the progression iv6–V. It's called “phrygian” because of the half step that occurs when le moves to sol [latex](\downarrow\hat6-\hat5)[/latex] in the bass, a sound that’s similar to when ra moves to do [latex](\downarrow\hat2-\hat1)[/latex] in the phrygian mode. The progression carries a danger of parallels and of writing an augmented second between le and ti [latex](\downarrow\hat6-\uparrow\hat7)[/latex]. These can be avoided if you choose to double do [latex](\hat1)[/latex] in the iv6 chord (Example 10). Very often, PHCs are approached from i, and are accompanied by the soprano me–fa–sol [latex](\hat3-\hat4-\hat5)[/latex], as in Example 10.

text: 重點整理iii 和弦（小調中為 III）是弱屬前和弦，通常先經過強屬前和弦，再走向 V。在大調中，iii 通常為下行的 ti [latex](\hat7)[/latex] 配置和聲；同樣地，在小調中，III 通常為下行的 te [latex](\downarrow\hat7)[/latex] 配置和聲。iii/III 通常採用原位。iii 不能當成 I6 的替代和弦（見例 1 下方的說明）。iii 並不是很常見的和弦。
en: Key Takeaways The iii chord (III in minor) is a weak predominant that typically moves through a strong predominant on the way to a V chord. In major, iii usually harmonizes a descending ti [latex](\hat7)[/latex]; similarly, in minor, III usually harmonizes a descending te [latex](\downarrow\hat7)[/latex]. iii/III is usually found in root position. iii is not used as a substitute for I6 (see the explanation below Example 1). iii is not a very common chord.

title: 以中音和弦為低音 mi（第三級）配置和聲
text: 低音 mi（[latex]\hat{3}[/latex]）最常搭配 I6 和弦，不過作曲家偶爾會選擇 iii 而非 I6（例 1）。iii 的用法相當特定：接在 I 和弦之後，為上方聲部中下行的 ti/te [latex](\hat7/\downarrow\hat7)[/latex] 配置和聲。它通常接到強屬前和弦，但也可以直接接到 V，形成 I–iii–V，低音作 do–mi–sol [latex](\hat1-\hat3-\hat5)[/latex] 的琶音進行。iii 通常採用原位。
en: It’s most common for mi ([latex]\hat{3}[/latex]) in the bass to be harmonized with a I6 chord. Occasionally, however, composers choose to use iii rather than I6 (Example 1). The iii chord is used in one relatively specific situation: after a I chord, harmonizing a descending ti/te [latex](\hat7/\downarrow\hat7)[/latex] in an upper voice. It commonly moves to to a strong predominant, though it can move directly to V in a bass arpeggiation do–mi–sol [latex](\hat1-\hat3-\hat5)[/latex] harmonized I–iii–V, and is usually in root position.

title: 以中音和弦為低音 mi（第三級）配置和聲
text: 必須強調，在西方古典音樂中，iii 不能直接當成 I6 的替代和弦。例如，先前介紹主和聲延長的章節提過，低音 do–re–mi [latex](\hat1-\hat2-\hat3)[/latex] 通常配置為 [latex]\mathrm{I-V^4_3-I^6}[/latex]。作曲家不會改用 [latex]\mathrm{I-V^4_3-iii}[/latex] 作為替代。這是因為 iii 的功能類似 vi，屬於弱屬前和弦，最常先經過強屬前和弦，再到 V；[latex]\mathrm{I-V^4_3-iii}[/latex] 卻反過來，由 V 走到 iii，不符合這個風格的常規。最後請記住，iii 在共通寫作時期的調性音樂中並不常見，因此應節制使用。
en: It's important to emphasize that iii isn't simply a substitute for I6 in Western classical music. For instance, in an earlier chapter on tonic prolongations, we saw that the bass line do–re–mi [latex](\hat1-\hat2-\hat3)[/latex] is commonly harmonized with [latex]\mathrm{I-V^4_3-I^6}[/latex]. Composers don't use [latex]\mathrm{I-V^4_3-iii}[/latex] as an alternative. That's because iii functions like vi, as a weak predominant that most often travels through a strong predominant to get to V. The progression [latex]\mathrm{I-V^4_3-iii}[/latex] shows the opposite: V getting to iii, which isn't stylistically normative. Finally, keep in mind that iii does not appear very often in common-practice tonality, so it should be used sparingly.

en: In the minor-mode progressions (Examples 2c and 2d), te [latex](\downarrow\hat{7})[/latex] descends to le [latex](\downarrow\hat{6})[/latex] when III moves to a predominant. Notice that III involves te [latex](\downarrow\hat{7})[/latex], not ti [latex](\uparrow\hat{7})[/latex]. That is, III is major, not augmented, which is what would happen if we used ti [latex](\uparrow\hat{7})[/latex].

title: 屬前七和弦
text: 重點整理本章討論屬前七和弦 ii7、IV7、vi7 與 iii7。ii7 及其轉位是最常見的屬前七和弦；例 2 比較 ii7 各種位置與轉位的常見程度。使用屬前七和弦寫作時，和弦七音的處理有兩項一般原則：以級進或共同音接近七音。七音向下級進解決。
en: Key Takeaways This chapter discusses the predominant seventh chords ii7, IV7, vi7, and iii7. ii7 and its inversions are the most common predominant seventh chord, and Example 2 shows which inversions of ii7 are more common than others. When writing with predominant seventh chords, two general principles apply with respect to the treatment of the chordal seventh: Approach the chordal seventh by step or common tone. Resolve the chordal seventh down by step.

title: 屬前七和弦
text: 前面說過，在屬和弦加入七音，可以加強它走向主和弦的動力。本章將看到，在屬前和弦加入和弦七音，也能產生類似效果：加強它們走向屬和弦的動力（例 1）。在 ii 加入七音很常見；其他屬前和弦也會加入七音，尤其是 IV 與 vi，只是較少出現。所有屬前七和弦都遵循兩項處理和弦七音的一般原則：
en: Earlier, we saw how adding a chordal seventh to the dominant strengthened its drive toward the tonic. In this chapter, we see that something similar can be accomplished by adding a chordal seventh to predominant chords: it can intensify their motion to the dominant (Example 1). Adding a seventh to ii chords is common; it also occurs with the other predominant chords (particularly IV and vi), but less frequently. All predominant seventh chords share two general guidelines for the treatment of a chordal seventh:

title: 屬前七和弦
text: 通常以級進或共同音接近和弦七音。和弦七音向下級進解決。
en: The chordal seventh is usually approached by step or common tone. The chordal seventh resolves down by step.

text: 其他屬前七和弦 IV7、vi7 與 iii7，遠不如 ii7 及其轉位常見。其中 IV7 與 vi7 又比 iii7 常見；考慮到 [latex]\mathrm{iii}[/latex] 三和弦本來就不常見，這很合理。IV7 與 vi7 通常都採用原位；vi7 只用於連接主和聲與強屬前和聲區域，不用於阻礙進行（換句話說，V7 接到 vi7 並不常見）。例 7 展示這些和弦的聲部進行範例，遵循一般的聲部寫作程序與和弦七音的處理。

Among them, IV7 and vi7 are more common than iii7, which makes sense given that [latex]\mathrm{iii}[/latex] as a triad isn't very common in the first place. text: 重點整理模進是將一個音樂型態移至不同音高後重複。模進可分為上行與下行兩類。下行模進包括：下行五度模進（五度循環）與下行三度模進（帕海貝爾）。上行模進包括：上行 5–6 模進（上行級進）。寫作模進時：先寫出完整原型。寫出第一次移位重複的完整第一個和弦。依各聲部的音程型態，完成其餘的移位重複。

title: 樂句中段的自然音模進
text: 模進（sequence）是將一個音樂型態移至不同音高後重複（例 1）。「原型」（model）指這個型態最初的呈現；「移位重複」（copy）則指其後的各次重複。模進的原型通常由兩個和弦及一條旋律構成；在後續的移位重複中，和弦與旋律都一起移至新的音高。也可能只有旋律，或只有和聲作模進；這時通常會明確稱為「旋律模進」或「和聲模進」。若只說「模進」，通常表示旋律與和聲都參與其中。
en: A sequence is a pattern that has been repeated and transposed (Example 1). The term “model” refers to the initial statement of the pattern, and the term “copy” refers to subsequent repetitions of the pattern. Sequence models are typically comprised of a two-chord pattern and a melody, and both the chords and melody get transposed in subsequent copies of the pattern. It’s possible for only the melody or only the harmony to be sequential. In such cases we usually specify “melodic sequence” or “harmonic sequence.” When we just say “sequence” it usually means both melody and harmony participate.

title: 樂句中段的自然音模進
text: 分析模進時，最具挑戰的工作之一，可能就是辨認原型及各次移位重複的範圍。初學者常把過短的片段認作原型，而這些片段其實不足以構成可辨認的型態。記住原型通常不只包含一個和弦，而且很常是兩個和弦，會很有幫助。例 2 說明原因：例 2a 的型態只有圓形，例 2b 則交替出現圓形與方形。在例 2b 中，很容易辨認重複的型態是「圓形—方形」；但例 2a 就不明確了：每次重複的是兩個圓形？三個？兩種都可以？究竟哪一組才是原型？
en: Perhaps one of the most challenging tasks in analyzing sequences is determining where the model and its copies are. Beginning analysts often identify things that are too short to qualify as a model for a pattern. It can be helpful to remember that the model should usually contain more than one chord, very often two chords. Example 2 shows why. Example 2a shows a pattern comprised only of circles, whereas Example 2b shows a pattern that alternates circles and squares. In 2b, it’s easy to identify what the pattern is that’s being repeated (circle–square). In 2a it’s unclear: are two circles being repeated every time? Three? Both? What is the model?

title: 樂句中段的自然音模進
text: 模進可分為下行與上行兩大類。其中某些模進十分常見，因此有了專門的名稱；下文介紹最常見的幾種。不過，有兩點要強調：（1）模進不只有這幾種，只是這幾種特別常見；沒有特定名稱的模進，直接標為「上行模進」或「下行模進」即可。（2）可惜樂理對下列常見模進有許多不同命名方式。本章為每種列出兩個常見名稱，但其他命名方式也存在。
en: We can divide sequences into two main categories: those that descend and those that ascend. Within each of those categories, certain sequences are so common that we have given them special names. The most common ones are covered below. It’s important to emphasize two things here, though: (1) these are not the only kinds of sequences. It’s just that these ones are quite common. Unnamed sequences can simply be labeled “ascending sequence” or “descending sequence”; (2) unfortunately, music theory has all kinds of different naming conventions for the common sequences below. We have chosen to give two common names for each one, but other naming conventions exist.

title: 樂句中段的自然音模進
text: 下行模進
en: Descending sequences

title: 樂句中段的自然音模進
text: 下行五度模進（又稱五度循環模進）
en: Descending fifths (a.k.a. circle-of-fifths)

title: 樂句中段的自然音模進
text: 下行五度模進是將兩個和弦構成的原型，逐次向下移動一級（例 3 與例 6）。之所以稱為「下行五度」，是因為相鄰和弦的根音依次下行五度，或上行四度；四度是五度的轉位音程。作曲家這麼做，是為了避免持續下行五度所造成的不合理大音域。例 3 的片段恰好全部使用自然音七和弦，但這種模進也可以只用三和弦，或每隔一個和弦才加入七音。有時作曲家不會像例 3 那樣全部使用原位，而會交替使用原位與第一轉位和弦（例 6d）。
en: Descending fifths sequences involve a two-chord model being transposed down by step (Examples 3 and 6). The sequence is called “descending fifths” because each successive chord root descends by fifth (or ascends by fourth—the inversion of a fifth. Composers do this to avoid writing an unreasonably large range which would happen if they kept descending by fifth). The excerpt in Example 3 happens to use all diatonic seventh chords, but the sequence can also happen with triads alone or with every other chord having a 7th. Sometimes, instead of using all root position chords, as in Example 3, composers choose to alternate root position and first inversion chords (Example 6d).

title: 樂句中段的自然音模進
text: 下行三度模進是將兩個和弦構成的原型，逐次向下移動三度，因此稱為「下行三度」（例 4 與例 7）。有些人則以帕海貝爾命名，因為他的〈D 大調卡農〉使用了這種模進的一個版本。這種模進常全部採用原位和弦（如例 7d），或交替使用原位與第一轉位和弦（如例 4）。
en: Descending thirds sequences involve a two-chord model being transposed down by third (hence the name “descending thirds”) (Examples 4 and 7). Some people choose instead to call this sequence “Pachelbel” after his Canon in D, which features a version of the sequence. It’s common to see the sequence involve all root position chords (as in Example 7d) or alternating root position and first inversion chords (as in Example 4).

title: 樂句中段的自然音模進
text: 上行 5–6 模進在上方聲部使用所謂的「5–6 技法」延長單一和弦，藉此模擬兩個和弦的型態。這裡的 5–6 來自數字低音，意思很簡單：原本位於低音上方五度的聲部，移到低音上方六度。例 5 展示一個上行 5–6 模進，例 8c 則是該模進的和聲縮減譜，突顯女高音的 5–6 進行。請留意例 5：當五度移到六度時，我們可以選擇標上新的和弦。雖然我們偏好少用一些羅馬數字，仍另外提供一種分析，將每個可能的垂直音組合都標出來。
en: Ascending 5–6 sequences mimic a two-chord pattern by prolonging a single chord using something called “5–6 technique” in an upper voice. The 5–6 here comes from figured bass. It simply means a voice that is a fifth above the bass moves to a sixth above the bass. Example 5 shows an ascending 5–6 sequence and Example 8c shows a harmonic reduction of the sequence that highlights the 5-6 motion in the soprano voice. Notice in Example 5 that when the 5th moves to the 6th, we could decide to label a new chord. Although we prefer to use fewer Roman numerals, we’ve also shown an alternative analysis that labels every possible verticality.

text: 模進的寫作
en: Writing sequences

title: 樂句中段的自然音模進
text: 寫作模進最容易的方法，是先完成原型，再將聲部進行「複製貼上」到後續各次移位重複。請注意，移位重複必須呈現與原型相同的聲部進行，只是移至另一個音高位置；否則就不是模進。因此，必須再次檢查原型的寫作：原型裡的任何錯誤，都會在後續每次移位重複中再次出現。步驟如下：
en: Writing sequences is easiest if you establish the model first and then “copy-and-paste” the voice leading for each subsequent copy. Note that your copy should exhibit the same voice leading as your model, but transposed to a different pitch level, otherwise it’s not a sequence. For that reason, it’s important that you double check the writing in the model. Any error that you make in the model will get repeated to all subsequent copies. The steps are:

title: 樂句中段的自然音模進
text: 寫出原型。遵循一般的聲部寫作程序；女高音宜平順，避免過多跳進。寫出第一次移位重複中，完整的第一個和弦。照原型第一個和弦的聲部排列配置。例如，若原型第一個和弦的三音在女高音，每次移位重複的第一個和弦，也必須讓三音位於女高音。辨認每個聲部（女高音、女低音、男高音、男低音）的音程型態，將這個型態一路複製到模進結束。檢查最後一個和弦的聲部排列，是否與原型中相對應的和弦一致，就能快速確認是否寫對。若在小調，記得只有當屬功能和弦解決到主和弦時，才升高第七級形成導音。
en: Write the model Follow the typical writing procedure here, and prefer a soprano that is smoother rather than leapy. Write the entire first chord of your first copy. Copy the exact same spacing from the first chord of your model. For instance, if the third of the chord is in the soprano in the model’s chord 1, then the third of the chord must also be in the soprano for every copy’s chord 1. Determine the pattern of intervals you’ve written for each voice (soprano, also, tenor, bass) and copy that pattern to the end of the sequence. You can check if you’ve done it right quickly by seeing if the spacing of the final chord matches its analogous partner in the model. If you’re in minor, remember to raise the leading tone only if a dominant-function chord is resolving to tonic.

title: 主音化
text: 重點整理主音化是讓非主和弦暫時聽起來像主和弦的過程。這是藉由從暫時調性借用的半音變化和弦來達成，稱為副和弦（applied chords），包括副屬和弦 V(7) 與副導音和弦 viio(7)。副和弦以斜線標記。斜線前表示副和弦在暫時調性（secondary key）中的身分，斜線後則表示被主音化的和弦。英文由左往右讀，將斜線讀成「of」；例如 V/ii 讀作「five of two」，意思是「ii 的屬和弦」。副和弦幾乎都會使用臨時記號，尤其是使音高上升的記號。另一種理解副和弦的方法，是把它視為同根音自然音和弦經過變音的版本。例如，ii 變成 II♯，也就是 V/V。
en: Key Takeaways Tonicization is the process of making a non-tonic chord sound like a temporary tonic. This is done with chromatic chords called applied chords, or secondary dominant chords (V(7)) and secondary leading-tone chords (viio(7)) borrowed from the temporary key. Applied chords are notated with a slash. The chord before the slash is the identity of the applied chord within the secondary key, and the chord after the slash is the chord being tonicized. It's read aloud from left to right with the word "of" replacing the slash: V/ii becomes "five of two." Applied chords nearly always involve accidentals, and especially accidentals that raise the pitch. Another way of thinking about applied chords is to imagine them as altered versions of the diatonic chord with which it shares a root (for example, ii becomes II♯, which is V/V).

title: 主音化
text: 本章播放清單
