en: This section begins with Rhythm and Meter, one of the musical domains that defines pop music as a genre most clearly. The following chapter on Drumbeats discusses in detail how rhythms are manifested in the drum kit, and introduces students to the drum kit and staff notation for drum parts.

title: 流行音樂
text: 接下來幾章由小到大討論流行音樂曲式：先談〈旋律與樂句〉，再進入〈流行音樂曲式入門〉、〈AABA曲式與分節歌形式〉及〈主歌—副歌曲式〉。這幾章適合依序學習。
en: The next few chapters discuss form in pop music, from a small scale (Melody and Phrasing) to a larger scale (Introduction to Form in Popular Music, AABA Form and Strophic Form, Verse-Chorus Form). These chapters are best taught sequentially.

title: 流行音樂
text: 之後以圖式觀點理解流行音樂和聲，從〈流行音樂和聲圖式入門〉開始。教師可以依需求選擇介紹多少種圖式。
en: The next several chapters take a schematic approach to understanding harmonies in popular music, beginning with an Introduction to Harmonic Schemas in Pop Music. Instructors can cover as many or as few of these schemas as they like.

title: 流行音樂
text: 最後一章透過〈脆弱、缺席與逐漸浮現的主音〉，從更大的範圍觀察流行音樂的調性。
en: The final chapter zooms out and provides a broader view of tonality in popular music through the phenomena of Fragile, Absent, and Emergent Tonics.

title: 流行音樂的節奏與拍子
text: 重點整理等值移位切分（straight syncopation），可以理解為把原本規整的節奏中，某些音的起點提早半個時值。另一些切分，則來自把一個節奏單位分成接近等長的幾組。特別常見的是3+3+2的tresillo（三三二節奏）。鼓聲部的節奏細節，請參閱〈鼓點〉章。
en: Key Takeaways Straight syncopation can be understood as taking a square rhythm and shifting some of the notes early by half the duration. Other syncopations are derived from dividing a unit into nearly even parts. A particularly common nearly even syncopation is the tresillo pattern of 3+3+2. The Drumbeats chapter contains more details on rhythm within drum parts.

title: 流行音樂的節奏與拍子
text: 本章播放清單
en: Chapter Playlist

title: 流行音樂的節奏與拍子
text: 等值移位切分
en: Straight Syncopation

title: 流行音樂的節奏與拍子
text: 當代流行／搖滾音樂中的一種典型切分做法，是取一串等時值音符，把第一個音的時值縮成一半，再將其餘音的起點都提早這半個時值。
en: In contemporary pop/rock music, syncopation typically involves taking a series of notes of equal durations, cutting the duration of the first note in half, and shifting the remaining notes early by that half duration.

title: 流行音樂的節奏與拍子
text: 例如，四個原本都落在拍點上的四分音符，可以把第一個改成八分音符，其後每個四分音符都提早一個八分音符開始，於是後面的音都落在拍間的非拍點位置。
en: For example, a series of four quarter notes, all sounding on the beat, can be transformed in this way by making the first note into an eighth note and sounding each successive quarter note one eighth note early—all on the offbeats.

title: 流行音樂的節奏與拍子
text: 這個做法可用在不同拍節層次。切分的移位單位，也就是縮短後第一個音的時值，以及後面各音提早的幅度，總是原本等時值音符的一半。下列切分都相當常見：
en: This process can occur on any metrical level. The unit of syncopation (the duration of the first note, and the amount of shift applied to the following notes) is always half the duration of the straight notes. All of the following syncopations are relatively common in contemporary pop/rock music:

title: 流行音樂的節奏與拍子
text: 如果原本每個音長兩拍，先把第一個縮成一拍，其餘各音的起點提早一拍。如果原本每個音長一拍，就提早一個分割單位；在單拍子中，這等於半拍。如果原本每個音就是一個拍的分割單位，就再提早一個細分單位。
en: If the duration of the series of “straight” notes is two beats, they will be syncopated by changing the first note to a single beat and shifting each of the other notes early by a beat. If the duration of the straight notes is one beat, they will be syncopated by a division (one half beat in simple meter). If the straight notes are each divisions, they will be syncopated by shifting each note by a subdivision.

title: 流行音樂的節奏與拍子
text: 本章約定：把每音一拍的一串音，提早半拍，稱為拍層次切分（例1）；把每音一個分割單位的一串音，提早一個細分單位，稱為分割層次切分。
en: As a convention, when we take a series of notes that each have a duration of one beat and shift them early by half a beat, we will call that beat-level syncopation (Example 1). When we take a series of notes that each have a duration of one division and shift them early by a subdivision, we will call that division-level syncopation.

title: 流行音樂的節奏與拍子
text: 音樂譜例靜態樂譜待補；原始資源包含音樂譜例。
en: Musical example (requires internet)Static score pending; the original resource contains a musical example.

title: 流行音樂的節奏與拍子
text: 例1。等值移位切分，把音的起點提早該拍節層次單位的一半。
en: Example 1. Straight syncopation moves the attacks forward by half the value of the metric level.

title: 流行音樂的節奏與拍子
text: 聽寫等值移位切分
en: Transcribing straight syncopations

title: 流行音樂的節奏與拍子
text: 等值移位切分經常出現連續的非拍點節奏，因此不難辨認。聽歌時，一邊打拍或輕敲計拍脈動，若發現連續幾個音都從拍點之間開始，拍點本身卻沒有新音起奏，就是切分的線索。
en: Straight syncopated rhythms are easily identified by the frequently occurring off-beat rhythms. For example, if you listen to a song and conduct or tap the counting pulse, you may notice several notes in a row that are articulated between these pulses, with no notes articulated right on a pulse—this indicates syncopation.

title: 流行音樂的節奏與拍子
text: 辨認出切分片段後，即使只有兩、三個音，也要判斷它位於哪個拍節層次。例如在單拍子中，如果音不從計拍脈動上開始，每兩拍點之間卻各有一個音起奏，就是拍層次切分。若每兩拍點之間有兩個音起奏，則再聽一次，改敲每拍的分割單位；如果分割點本身沒有新音，而每兩個分割點之間各有一個音，就屬於分割層次切分。
en: Once you identify a syncopated passage—which may only involve two or three notes—figure out the metrical level on which the syncopation occurs. For example, in simple meter, if no notes are articulated directly on the counting pulse beats and one note is articulated in between each beat, the syncopation is occurring at the beat level. If no notes are articulated directly on the counting pulse beats and two notes are articulated in between each beat, listen to the passage again while tapping the division. If no notes are articulated directly on the division taps and one note is articulated in between each tap, the syncopation is occuring at the division level.

title: 流行音樂的節奏與拍子
text: 知道切分的層次後，就能判斷移位的時值。拍層次切分，每兩個計拍點之間有一個音，移位幅度是一個分割單位：原本長一拍的每個音，都提早一個分割單位。分割層次切分則提早一個細分單位：原本長一個分割單位的音，提早一個細分單位開始。
en: Determining the metrical level allows you to identify the durational value of the shift. If the syncopation occurs on the beat level (one note sounding between each counting pulse beat), the value of syncopation is a division: each beat-length note has been shifted one division early. If the syncopation occurs on the division level, the value of syncopation is a subdivision: each division-length note has been shifted one subdivision early.

title: 流行音樂的節奏與拍子
text: 最後，判斷這個切分模式如何開始：它是否直接從非拍點起奏？還是像例1，先連續出現兩個較靠近的起音——拍點上一個短音，接著是第一個較長的切分音？
en: Lastly, determine how the syncopated pattern begins. Does the offbeat pattern simply begin offbeat? Or does the pattern begin with two quick notes back-to-back as in Example 1—one short note on the beat followed by the first of the longer syncopated notes?

title: 流行音樂的節奏與拍子
text: 確認切分層次、移位幅度，以及開頭是否保留縮短的正拍音之後，應該就較容易記譜。如果仍有困難，可以利用歌詞音節與重音，追蹤每個音，以及哪些音落在拍點、哪些在拍間。先記下歌詞，再寫節奏，往往很有幫助。
en: Once you have determined the level of syncopation, the duration of the shift, and whether or not the pattern begins with a truncated onbeat note, the rhythmic pattern should be easy to notate. If, however, you are still having difficulty, try using the lyric syllables and the stress patterns of the lyrics to help you keep track of the individual notes and which ones are on or off the beat. Writing lyrics down before notating the rhythm can be a big help.

title: 流行音樂的節奏與拍子
text: Tresillo（三三二節奏）
en: Tresillo

title: 流行音樂的節奏與拍子
text: 另一種常見的流行／搖滾節奏，根植於非洲與古巴音樂傳統：把一拍或兩拍分成三組接近等長的單位。例如，把一個二分音符分成兩個附點八分音符與一個八分音符，就是3+3+2。它近似三連音，卻仍保留每拍二分、四分、八分等細分方式，產生有點像「假三連音」的感覺，稱為tresillo（例2）。Luis Fonsi與Daddy Yankee的〈Despacito〉（2017），在開頭cuatro獨奏之後，貝斯與大鼓便能聽到tresillo。這種節奏非常普遍，即使其他方面不太帶有非洲—古巴音樂特色的流行歌曲，也常使用。
en: Drawing on its roots in African and Cuban musical traditions, another common rhythmic pattern in pop/rock is to divide a beat (or two beats) into three almost-equal groups: for example, dividing a half note into two dotted eighth notes and an eighth note (3+3+2). This pattern approximates a triplet while still maintaining the simple division of beats by 2, 4, 8, etc., creating an experience of something like a “fake triplet.” The term for this rhythmic pattern is tresillo (Example 2). A tresillo pattern can be heard after the opening cuatro solo of “Despacito” by Luis Fonsi and Daddy Yankee (2016) in the bass and bass drum. The tresillo pattern is extremely common, even in pop music that otherwise doesn’t seem to draw on Afro-Cuban music.

title: 流行音樂的節奏與拍子
text: 音樂譜例靜態樂譜待補；原始資源包含音樂譜例。

title: 流行音樂的節奏與拍子
text: 例2。Tresillo節奏。
en: Example 2. Tresillo rhythms.

title: 流行音樂的節奏與拍子
text: 在多數流行／搖滾曲風中，tresillo甚至比真正三連音更常見；不過，真正三連音也會出現，必須分清楚。Jump, Little Children的〈Cathedrals〉（1998）把兩者並置，很適合練習演奏與辨認。例3中，小提琴奏四分音符三連音，吉他奏均分八分音符；三連音停止後，吉他才改用tresillo重音分組。
en: The tresillo is actually more common than “real” triplets in most pop/rock genres, but true triplets do occur, so take care to distinguish between the two. “Cathedrals” by Jump, Little Children (1998) juxtaposes both, and it’s an excellent example for practicing performing and identifying tresillo patterns and real triplets. In Example 3, notice that the violins play quarter-note triplets against simple eighth notes in the guitar, but the guitar begins a tresillo accent pattern after the triplets stop.

title: 流行音樂的節奏與拍子
text: 音樂譜例靜態樂譜待補；原始資源包含音樂譜例。
en: Musical example (requires internet)Static score pending; the original resource contains a musical example.

title: 流行音樂的節奏與拍子
text: 例3。Jump, Little Children的〈Cathedrals〉（1:01）。
en: Example 3. “Cathedrals” by Jump, Little Children (1:01).

title: 流行音樂的節奏與拍子
text: Tresillo最常採3+3+2分組，也可以是3+2+3或2+3+3。
en: While tresillo patterns occur most often in 3+3+2 groupings, 3+2+3 and 2+3+3 are also possible.

title: 流行音樂的節奏與拍子
text: Tresillo也能擴展：例4把3+3+2的分組擴大為3+3+3+3+2+2。Nicole Biamonte（2014）稱它為double tresillo（雙倍tresillo）。U2的〈Electric Co.〉（1980）開頭，吉他把十六分音符細分拍組成3+3+3+3+2+2；大鼓維持均勻四分音符拍點，上方踩鈸則演奏均勻的細分拍。
en: The tresillo pattern can be expanded: in Example 4, the 3+3+2 pattern is doubled, resulting in 3+3+3+3+2+2. Nicole Biamonte (2014) refers to this pattern as the double tresillo. In the opening of “Electric Co.” by U2 (1980), the guitar plays subdivisions (sixteenths) grouped 3+3+3+3+2+2, while the kick drum plays straight beats (quarters) under the hi-hat playing straight subdivisions.

en: Transcribing rhythms worksheet (.pdf, .mscz). Asks students to transcribe and identify straight syncopations as well as tresillo rhythms in “Sorry” by Beyoncé (2016). Worksheet Playlist

title: 鼓點
text: 重點整理多數流行音樂鼓點都有反拍重音（backbeat），也就是四拍子中第2、4拍的重音，通常由小鼓演奏。大鼓常使用切分節奏。踩鈸、Ride鈸與Crash鈸，常在拍、拍的分割或細分層次，演奏規律脈動。除了基本搖滾鼓點，常見鼓型還包括倍速律動、半速律動、每拍大鼓（four on the floor）與dembow。流行音樂以四拍子最普遍，其次常見單三拍子。單三拍子的流行鼓型，常把小鼓放在第3拍。
en: Key Takeaways The backbeat is common to most pop drumbeats. The backbeat is an accented articulation on beats two and four in quadruple meters, usually played by the snare drum. The kick drum is often syncopated. Cymbals—hi-hats, ride, and crash—often play regular pulses at the beat, beat division, or beat subdivison level. Common drumbeats other than the basic rock beat include double-time, half-time, four-on-the-floor, and dembow. Quadruple meters are by far the most common meter in pop music; simple triple is the next most common. A simple triple drumbeat in pop music will often have a snare hit on beat three.

title: 鼓點
text: 本章播放清單
en: Chapter Playlist

title: 鼓點
text: 鼓點是饒舌、搖滾、爵士等許多流行音樂曲風的節奏基礎。它可以由鼓組實際演奏，也可以取樣既有錄音，或在音序器、數位音訊工作站（DAW）中編寫。本章會介紹鼓組本身、鼓譜記法，以及多種曲風共有的鼓點特徵，也會說明幾種特定鼓型與曲風之間的關係。
en: Drumbeats are the rhythmic cornerstone of many genres of popular music, including rap, rock, and jazz. Sometimes a drumbeat is performed on a drum kit, sometimes it’s sampled from an existing recording or programmed into a sequencer or DAW (digital audio workstation). In this primer, we’ll learn about the instrument itself, notating drum set parts, and the features of drumbeats that are common to many styles of music. We’ll also learn how a few particular drumbeats are associated with specific genres.

title: 鼓點
text: 原聲鼓組
en: The Acoustic Drum Kit

title: 鼓點
text: 例1標出鼓組六類常見部件，下方逐一介紹。
en: Example 1 illustrates six common components of a drum kit, each of which is described further below.

title: 鼓點
text: 例1。標準原聲鼓組。
en: Example 1. A standard acoustic drum kit.

title: 鼓點
text: 樂器聲音示範說明 1.小鼓（snare drum）小鼓聲音示範底部繃有金屬響弦，敲擊時會振動，產生沙沙的雜音成分，涵蓋很廣的可聽頻率範圍。用力敲擊可像木頭爆裂或雷響，輕奏則能呈現喀聲、點擊與帶響弦聲的滾奏等效果。 2.大鼓（kick drum），也稱bass drum大鼓聲音示範鼓組中音高最低的鼓，以腳踏板操作。原本由音樂會大鼓改製，有些仍保留轟鳴聲，另一些則呈現低沉短促的撞擊，或極低頻效果；透過合適的揚聲器，身體也能感受到這些振動。 3.通鼓（toms／tom-toms）通鼓聲音示範基頻比小鼓更集中、音高比大鼓高。鼓組通常有兩、三個不同音高的通鼓；明確音高在其整體音色中，可以較突出，也可以較不明顯。 4.Ride鈸（叮叮鈸）Ride鈸聲音示範大型懸掛鈸。較薄的Ride鈸常見於爵士，可以發出溫暖、綿延的一片聲響；金屬樂常用的厚鈸，則可能產生尖銳、高頻而帶顆粒感的聲音。敲擊中央隆起的鈸鐘（bell），可得到高而清亮的鈴聲。 5.踩鈸（hi-hat）踩鈸聲音示範由一對同尺寸鈸組成，下片反向放置，使兩片只有邊緣接觸。未踩踏板時張開，踩下後閉合。敲擊音色取決於開合程度：閉合時常發出明亮的「滴、滴、滴」，張開時則更猛烈、帶碰撞或沙響，也能呈現兩者之間的多種音色。單用腳踏板，也能做出飛濺般的聲響效果。 6.Crash鈸（碎音鈸）與重音效果鈸Crash鈸聲音示範依尺寸、外形與演奏方式，可發出撞擊、飛濺、持續沙響，或短促強烈的聲音。直徑常見6至18英吋，厚度也不同；有些外形與其他鈸不同，有些加上鉚釘或較大的開孔。
en: Instrument Audio Description 1. Snare drum Audio, video, or interactive resource (requires internet) A drum with metal wires stretched underneath that buzz when the drum is struck. This results in a noisy sound (that is, one that fills out much of the audible frequency spectrum). Played with force, it sounds like wood cracking or like a thunderclap. Played softly, it offers a range of effects from clicks and taps to buzzing rolls. 2. Kick drum (or bass drum) Audio, video, or interactive resource (requires internet) The lowest-pitched drum in the kit, played with a foot pedal. It is originally based on a modified concert bass drum, and some still sound with the same booming quality. Other kick-drum sounds have a dull thud, or a sub-bass effect that (over the right speakers) is felt in the body as much as it is heard. 3. Toms (or tom-toms) Audio, video, or interactive resource (requires internet) Drums with a more focused pitch fundamental than the snare and are higher-pitched than the kick. There are often two or three toms on a drum kit, each with a distinct pitch. The pitch can be a more or less prominent feature of the toms’ sound. 4. Ride cymbal Audio, video, or interactive resource (requires internet) A large suspended cymbal. Depending on the thickness of the cymbal, the ride may sound like a warm wash of sound (thinner rides, common in jazz) or a sharp, high-pitched crunch (thicker rides, common in metal music). High, pure ringing sounds can be produced by playing the “bell” of the ride, located in the middle of the cymbal. 5. Hi-hat cymbals Audio, video, or interactive resource (requires internet) A pair of cymbals of the same size; the bottom cymbal is upside-down so only their edges touch. The cymbals are open by default and close when a foot pedal is pressed. When struck, the hi-hats’ timbre depends on how open or closed the two cymbals are. The hi-hat is most often struck while closed, producing a characteristic, bright “tick tick tick”; the open sound has a more aggressive crashing or rattling quality; and a wide range of intermediate timbres are also available. When played with the foot pedal only, the cymbals make a splashing effect. 6. Crash and accent cymbals Audio, video, or interactive resource (requires internet) Depending on size, contour, and playing technique, these can produce a variety of crashing, splashing, sizzling, and barking sounds. They range in size (6–18” diameters are common) and thickness. Some have shapes and contours unlike other cymbals, or are augmented with rivets or large holes.

title: 鼓點
text: 鼓組的組合非常有彈性：多數部件，有人甚至認為全部部件，都可以自由增減。有些鼓手會加裝牛鈴、鈴鼓、木塊，以及能觸發預設聲音的電子打擊墊。部件種類與配置方式，幾乎沒有固定上限。
en: The drum kit is uniquely modular—that is, most (some might say all) of its constituent parts are optional. Other auxiliary percussion add-ons found on some drum kits include cowbells, tambourines, wood blocks, and electronic pads that can trigger programmed sounds. The sheer variety of drum kit elements and their various configurations is near-limitless.

title: 鼓點
text: 並非所有流行音樂都使用原聲鼓組。鼓機、電子鼓，以及數位音訊工作站外掛，讓作曲與製作有更多自訂可能。電子打擊樂常使用原聲樂器的取樣，或模擬其音色。
en: Not all pop music uses an acoustic drum kit for its percussion. Drum machines, electronic drum sets, and plug-ins for digital audio workstations allow further customization for music composition and production. Most of the sounds used in electronic percussion are samples or imitations of acoustic instruments.

title: 鼓點
text: 鼓組的五線譜記法
en: Five-Line Staff Notation for Drum Kit

title: 鼓點
text: 很多鼓點從創作、演奏到錄音，都沒有寫成樂譜。不過，鼓手、編曲者與其他音樂工作者，也經常用五線譜溝通細節。鼓組配置與演奏具有即興性，因此記法尚未完全標準化；下列慣例是本書採用、也相當常見的一套方法。只要可能產生歧義，就應加上說明或鼓譜圖例。
en: Many drumbeats are created, performed, and recorded without ever being written down. But drummers, arrangers, and other music-industry professionals often use a five-line staff to communicate the details of a drumbeat. Drum kit notation is not fully standardized due to the improvisatory and modular nature of its performance practice, but the conventions given below and used throughout this textbook represent a particularly common method. Best practice is always to include explanatory notes and/or a drum key whenever the notation could be at all ambiguous.

title: 鼓點
text: 例2說明如何用譜上的線與間，表示鼓組不同部件：
en: Example 2 shows how each line and space of the staff denotes a different part of the drum kit:

title: 鼓點
text: 譜號：鼓屬打擊樂器，使用打擊樂譜號。符頭：小鼓、大鼓、通鼓等使用一般橢圓符頭；鈸類使用叉形（x）符頭。位置：大鼓寫在譜內最下面一間。小鼓寫在由下往上第三間。通鼓使用譜內其他線與間。踩鈸寫在五線譜上方一間。Ride鈸寫在最上面一線。其他Crash鈸與重音效果鈸，使用譜上方加線區域。用腳踏板演奏踩鈸時，寫在五線譜下方一間。特殊樂器：其他部件或效果可能沒有標準記法，應加註名稱，避免混淆。
en: Clef: as a percussion instrument, the drums take a percussion clef. Notehead type: standard oval noteheads are used for drums (snare, kick, tom, etc.), while cross (x) noteheads are used for cymbals. Placement: The kick drum uses the bottom-most space on the staff. The snare takes the third space from the bottom. The toms are shown on the other lines and spaces in the staff. Hi-hats occupy the space above the staff. The ride takes the uppermost line. Other crash and accent cymbals use ledger lines above the staff. When the hi-hat is played with the foot pedal, rather than with drumsticks, this is notated in the space just below the staff. Unusual instruments: Other elements and effects may not have a standard representation, and should be labeled to avoid confusion.

title: 鼓點
text: 例2。鼓組各部件的常見記法。採用這些符桿方向與符頭形式，有助於清楚閱讀。
en: Example 2. Common notation for various parts of the drum kit. Using these particular stem directions and notehead types are important for clarity.

title: 鼓點
text: 記寫鼓聲部時，可分成兩個聲部，如例3：
en: When notating a drum part, separate things into two voices, as in Example 3:

title: 鼓點
text: 鈸類通常維持規律脈動，符桿朝上。大鼓與小鼓常一起構成鼓型的主要特徵，符桿朝下。
en: The cymbals, which usually keep a steady pulse; notated with upstems. The kick and snare drum, which often cooperate to articulate the characteristic features of a drumbeat; notated with downstems.

title: 鼓點
text: 音樂譜例靜態樂譜待補；原始資源包含音樂譜例。
en: Musical example (requires internet)Static score pending; the original resource contains a musical example.

title: 鼓點
text: 例3。標準搖滾鼓點：大鼓在第1、3拍，小鼓反拍重音在第2、4拍，踩鈸維持均勻八分音符。
en: Example 3. The standard rock beat with kick on beats one and three, a snare backbeat on two and four, and regular eighth notes in the hi-hat.

title: 鼓點
text: 這些原則也有合理例外。例如，腳踩踩鈸的符桿可朝上，表示它與其他鈸類配合，也可朝下，表示它與大鼓一起由雙腳協調。鼓花（fill）也常不遵循兩聲部原則，因為規律鈸聲可能暫停，讓鼓手用雙手演奏小鼓、通鼓等。
en: Exceptions to these rules can often be justified. For example, when the hi-hat is played with the foot pedal, it may be stemmed either direction: up to show coordination with other cymbal articulations, or down to show coordination between the feet (that is, with the kick drum). Notated drum fills are another place where this two-voice rule may be broken, because a regular cymbal pulse will often stop so that the drummer can use both hands to play snare, toms, etc.

title: 鼓點
text: 小鼓與反拍重音
en: The Snare Drum and the Backbeat

title: 鼓點
text: 多數流行歌曲採單四拍子，採譜時通常記為[latex]\mathbf{^4_4}[/latex]；多數這類鼓型都有反拍重音，也就是通常由小鼓演奏的第2、4拍。上方例3中，小鼓反拍是基本搖滾鼓點的一層：它與第1、3拍的大鼓交替，上方踩鈸維持八分音符。嘻哈黃金年代常見的boom-bap鼓型，也以這種大鼓、小鼓交替為基礎。
en: Most popular songs are in a simple quadruple meter (usually notated by transcribers as [latex]\mathbf{^4_4}[/latex]), and most popular music drumbeats in this meter have a backbeat. The backbeat refers to beats two and four, usually played by the snare drum. Example 3 above shows how a snare-drum backbeat is one layer of the basic rock beat: kick-drum hits on beats one and three alternate with the snare backbeat, complemented by a regular eighth-note pulse in the hi-hat. The same alternation of kick and snare hits underpins the “boom-bap” beat found in much golden-age hip hop.

title: 鼓點
text: 在許多曲風中，小鼓反拍是三層節奏裡最穩定的一層。下文會說明如何改變大鼓與鈸類節奏，保留熟悉的反拍，同時改變律動性格。作曲者與製作人也常用兩種方式改造反拍：
en: In many genres the snare backbeat is the most stable of the three layers. Below, we’ll see how the kick and cymbal layers can be manipulated to change the character of a groove, without sacrificing the familiarity of the backbeat. Two common ways that songwriters and producers modify the backbeat are:

title: 鼓點
text: 把反拍節奏交給小鼓以外的聲音。加快或放慢反拍節奏，使它與整體律動速度的關係改變。
en: Giving the backbeat rhythm to instruments other than the snare drum Speeding up or slowing down the backbeat rhythm enough to alter its relationship to the tempo of a groove.

title: 鼓點
text: 以下分別說明。
en: Each technique is discussed further below.

title: 鼓點
text: 不由小鼓演奏的反拍重音
en: Non-Snare Backbeats

title: 鼓點
text: 反拍不一定要用小鼓。皇后合唱團〈We Will Rock You〉（例4）用跺腳與拍手，代替鼓組，構成基本搖滾鼓點。嘻哈與電子音樂，也常以拍手或彈指取代小鼓。多種反拍聲音還能疊在一起，創造不同音色，例如下方例8與例9。
en: The snare isn’t the only instrument that can play the backbeat. In Queen’s “We Will Rock You” (Example 4), the basic rock beat is made with stomping feet and clapping hands instead of drums. In hip hop and electronic music, it’s common to replace snare hits with hand claps or finger snaps. Multiple backbeat sounds can also be layered together to create a variety of backbeat timbres (as in Examples 8 and 9 below).

title: 鼓點
text: 皇后合唱團〈We Will Rock You〉官方影片
en: Queen - We Will Rock You (Official Video) (requires internet)

title: 鼓點
text: 例4。皇后合唱團〈We Will Rock You〉（1977）中，不用鼓組演奏的反拍。
en: Example 4. A backbeat without drums in Queen’s “We Will Rock You” (1977).

title: 鼓點
text: 在搖擺、咆勃等爵士曲風中，鼓手可能踩踏板讓踩鈸閉合，演奏反拍；詳見〈搖擺節奏〉。這通常會產生短促、清脆的打擊聲，音色與小鼓有不少相似之處。踩鈸反拍是小鼓反拍的先驅。Ella Fitzgerald〈Fascinating Rhythm〉的例5，在第2、4拍使用踩鈸反拍，另有一次提早八分音符的起奏。注意，這裡小鼓採切分節奏，踩鈸卻更規律。
en: In many jazz subgenres, including swing and bop, the drummer might play a backbeat on the hi-hats by closing the two cymbals together with a foot pedal (see Swing Rhythms for more information). The result is usually a short, sharp, percussive sound, similar in many ways to the timbre of the snare drum. This hi-hat backbeat was the precursor to the snare backbeat. Example 5, from Ella Fitzgerald’s rendition of “Fascinating Rhythm,” shows a hi-hat backbeat on beats two and four (and one eighth-note anticipation). Notice how the snare in this example plays a syncopated rhythm, whereas the hi-hat is much more regular.

title: 鼓點
text: 音樂譜例靜態樂譜待補；原始資源包含音樂譜例。
en: Musical example (requires internet)Static score pending; the original resource contains a musical example.

title: 鼓點
text: 例5。Ella Fitzgerald〈Fascinating Rhythm〉錄音（1959）中，典型的踩鈸爵士反拍。
en: Example 5. A typical jazz backbeat on the hi-hats in Ella Fitzgerald’s recording of “Fascinating Rhythm” (1959).

title: 鼓點
text: 半速與倍速律動
en: Half- and Double-Time Feels

title: 鼓點
text: 當速度介於80至160bpm時，基本搖滾鼓點中大鼓與小鼓交替的節奏，通常容易被感知為拍，或基本拍感（tactus）。這稱為常規律動（normal feel）：鼓型與速度一起建立清楚、容易隨之舞動的律動。有時，相同的大鼓、小鼓交替，會暗示超過160或低於80 bpm的速度；如果整體音樂也明顯很快或很慢，鼓型仍可支撐那個速度。但有時，即使反拍異常快或慢，其他聲部仍讓人感到80至160 bpm的基本拍；這時便用倍速與半速，描述鼓型與其他聲部之間的關係（例6）。
en: When the tempo is 80–160 bpm, the rhythm of the kick and snare in a basic rock beat will likely be understood as the beat or tactus. Such drumbeats can be said to have a normal feel, in which the drums and tempo work together to establish a clear groove that would be easy to dance to. Sometimes grooves use the same alternation of kick and snare to suggest a tempo above 160 bpm or slower than 80 bpm. These fast and slow drumbeats might still support the tempo for a groove, if that tempo is also felt as notably fast or slow. Other times, however, the rest of the groove still suggests a tactus of 80–160 bpm despite the unusually fast or slow backbeat. In such cases, we use the terms double-time and half-time to describe the misalignment of the drums with the rest of the groove (Example 6).

title: 鼓點
text: 例6。格線記譜比較（a）倍速、（b）常規、（c）半速律動。黃色陰影表示三種版本相同的基本拍感；深藍色是大鼓，淺藍色是小鼓。
en: Example 6. Box notation illustrating (a) double-time, (b) normal, and (c) half-time feels. The yellow shading indicates the tactus, which would be the same for all three feels. Dark blue is used for kick drum, and light blue for snare.

title: 鼓點
text: Metallica〈Trapped Under Ice〉的主要律動採倍速鼓型（例7）。若把小鼓反拍按一般鼓型理解，會對應約320 bpm；這樣數「1、2、3、4」已不舒服，更別說跟著動身體。甩頭的聽眾更可能抓住一半速度、約160 bpm的基本拍感。異常快速的鼓型，與較慢但仍很快的基本拍之間，產生急促、強烈的推進力。到了2:00，鼓型改成常規律動。
en: The main groove of Metallica’s “Trapped Under Ice” has a double-time feel (see Example 7). The snare suggests a backbeat alternating at a tempo of about 320 bpm—a pace at which it’s uncomfortable to count “1 2 3 4,” let alone move your body. Headbanging fans are more likely to lock into a tactus half the speed of the backbeat (160 bpm). The disagreement between the unusually fast drums and the slower (but still fast!) tactus gives this song a frantic, driving energy. Later in the song (2:00), the drums shift to a normal feel.

title: 鼓點
text: 音樂譜例靜態樂譜待補；原始資源包含音樂譜例。
en: Musical example (requires internet)Static score pending; the original resource contains a musical example.

title: 鼓點
text: 例7。Metallica〈Trapped Under Ice〉（1984）中的倍速反拍。
en: Example 7. A double-time backbeat in Metallica’s “Trapped Under Ice” (1984).

title: 鼓點
text: Phil Collins〈Take Me Home〉的速度為119 bpm，位於容易感知為基本拍的範圍中。慢速反拍若按常規鼓型理解，卻只暗示約60 bpm，對多數聽者而言太慢（例8）。若仍以119 bpm打拍，就會聽成半速鼓型。取代小鼓的拍手聲，步調緩慢；十六分音符踩鈸、切分通鼓與木塊，加上同樣快速的合成器固定音型，彼此形成張力，使律動帶有斷裂感，同時放鬆又焦躁。
en: Phil Collins’s “Take Me Home” has a tempo of 119 bpm, right in the middle of the preferred tempo range for a tactus. The song’s slow backbeat would suggest a tempo of only 60 bpm—too slow for most listeners (see Example 8). If we instead keep time at the 119-bpm pulse, we hear a half-time drumbeat. The tension between the slow pacing of the backbeat (with a clap substituting for snare), the skittering sixteenth-note hi-hats, and the syncopated toms and woodblock, supported by a similarly fast synth ostinato, gives this groove a fractured feeling, at once relaxed and anxious.

title: 鼓點
text: 音樂譜例靜態樂譜待補；原始資源包含音樂譜例。
en: Musical example (requires internet)Static score pending; the original resource contains a musical example.

title: 鼓點
text: 例8。Phil Collins〈Take Me Home〉（1985）中的半速反拍。
en: Example 8. A half-time backbeat in Phil Collins's "Take Me Home" (1985).

title: 鼓點
text: Dembow
en: Dembow

title: 鼓點
text: 小鼓不一定演奏反拍，其中一種特別常見的其他節奏是dembow。這個詞既指曲風，也指常見於該曲風、雷鬼動（reggaeton）、舞廳雷鬼（dancehall）等音樂的節奏型。最簡單的dembow，每一拍都打大鼓，小鼓則演奏tresillo（3+3+2）的後兩組起點。Bad Bunny〈LA CANCIÓN〉副歌就是一例（例9，0:52）。
en: The snare drum doesn’t always play the backbeat, and one non-backbeat snare pattern is particularly noteworthy. Dembow refers to both a genre of music and a rhythmic pattern common in that genre and in others (e.g., reggaeton, dancehall). In its simplest form, the dembow drumbeat has a kick drum on all four beats and snare drum playing the last two parts of a tresillo (3+3+2) rhythm. The chorus of Bad Bunny's "LA CANCIÓN" is one example (see Example 9, 0:52).

text: 音樂譜例靜態樂譜待補；原始資源包含音樂譜例。
en: Musical example (requires internet)Static score pending; the original resource contains a musical example.

title: 鼓點
text: 例9。Bad Bunny〈LA CANCIÓN〉（2019）中的dembow鼓型。
en: Example 9. A dembow pattern in Bad Bunny's "LA CANCIÓN" (2019).

title: 鼓點
text: 大鼓
en: The Kick Drum

title: 鼓點
text: 小鼓反拍是四拍子律動中最常見的特徵，大鼓型態則更自由。前文提到，第1、3拍打大鼓，是基本搖滾鼓點的一部分。另一種常見方式稱為four on the floor（每拍大鼓）：每個四分音符都打大鼓，通常搭配小鼓反拍，如Blondie〈Heart of Glass〉（例10），也可以完全不用小鼓。
en: Whereas the snare-drum backbeat is the most common feature of a quadruple meter groove, the kick drum pattern is more flexible. As we’ve seen, kick drum played on beats one and three is a common option, forming part of the basic rock beat. Another common pattern is called four on the floor: the kick drum plays every quarter note, usually alongside a snare-drum backbeat, as in Blondie’s “Heart of Glass” (Example 10), or with no snare at all.

title: 鼓點
text: 音樂譜例靜態樂譜待補；原始資源包含音樂譜例。
en: Musical example (requires internet)Static score pending; the original resource contains a musical example.

title: 鼓點
text: 例10。Blondie〈Heart of Glass〉（1978）中的每拍大鼓加反拍鼓型。
en: Example 10. A four-to-the-floor + backbeat pattern in Blondie’s “Heart of Glass” (1978).

title: 鼓點
text: 流行鼓型中，大鼓比小鼓更常使用切分。Kendrick Lamar〈HUMBLE.〉的例11，以拍手聲維持穩定反拍，大鼓則有大量等值移位切分。不過，即使其他位置切分，大鼓仍固定在每小節第一拍出現。
en: Syncopation is more common in the bass drum than in the snare of pop drumbeats. Example 11 shows the drumbeat of Kendrick Lamar’s “HUMBLE.”, which has a consistent backbeat provided by the hand claps, but plenty of straight syncopation in the kick drum. Note that the kick still enters reliably on the downbeat of each measure, despite syncopation elsewhere.

title: 鼓點
text: 音樂譜例靜態樂譜待補；原始資源包含音樂譜例。
en: Musical example (requires internet)Static score pending; the original resource contains a musical example.

title: 鼓點
text: 例11。Kendrick Lamar〈HUMBLE.〉（2017）中的大鼓切分。部分踩鈸上方的o，表示用踏板稍微打開踩鈸；小鼓位置的x，表示拍手聲。
en: Example 11. Kick drum syncopation in Kendrick Lamar’s “HUMBLE.” (2017). The “o” over some hi-hats indicates the cymbals are opened slightly with the foot pedal. The “x” in the snare space indicates claps.

title: 鼓點
text: 鈸類
en: Cymbals

title: 鼓點
text: 相對小鼓反拍，鈸類也可以採不同節奏。最常見的是均勻八分音符或十六分音符，規律四分音符也不罕見。還有其他方式，例如〈Heart of Glass〉中的踩鈸，主要只在非拍點出現（上方例10）。很多曲風最常用踩鈸維持脈動，Ride鈸也常見；Crash鈸則較常用於密度較疏的脈動，或聲響更猛烈的律動與曲風。
en: The cymbals also can have varying rhythms in relation to the snare backbeat. The most common rhythmic options are consistent eighth notes or sixteenth notes, though steady quarter notes are by no means rare. Other patterns are also possible, like in “Heart of Glass” where the hi-hats mostly play only the off-beats (see Example 10 above). The hi-hats are the most common cymbal used to keep this pulse in many genres; the ride cymbal is also common; the crash cymbal is an option used most often for slower-paced pulses and/or in more aggressive sounding grooves and genres.

title: 鼓點
text: 接下來兩例呈現鈸類節奏的不同選擇。肖戰〈光點（Made to Love）〉[1]使用均勻的十六分音符踩鈸（例12）；還能聽到短促、俐落的非小鼓取樣演奏反拍，以及約0:10開始的切分大鼓。另一例是Dream Theater〈As I Am〉（例13）：0:55的第一種鼓型採半速反拍，中國鈸（china cymbal）奏四分音符，Crash鈸標出小節第一拍。1:14的下一種律動稍微加快，改成常規律動，Crash鈸奏八分音符。
en: The next two examples show the range of options for cymbals in drumbeats. The first is from Xiao Zhan’s “Made to Love,”[1] with a consistent sixteenth-note pulse in the hi-hats (Example 12; you can also hear a snappy non-snare sample for the backbeat and, starting around 0:10, a syncopated kick drum). The second example is from Dream Theater’s “As I Am” (see Example 13). The song’s first drumbeat (at 0:55) is a half-time backbeat with quarter notes on the china cymbal and downbeats marked by the crash cymbal. The next groove (1:14) speeds up a little and shifts to a normal feel with the crash playing eighth notes.

text: 音樂譜例靜態樂譜待補；原始資源包含音樂譜例。
en: Musical example (requires internet)Static score pending; the original resource contains a musical example.

title: 鼓點
text: 例12。肖戰〈光點（Made to Love）〉（2020）中的十六分音符踩鈸。

title: 鼓點
text: 複四拍子與單三拍子的鼓型
en: Compound Quadruple and Simple Triple Drumbeats

title: 鼓點
text: 多數流行音樂採單四拍子；在不少曲風中，接著常見的是複四拍子與單三拍子。
en: Most pop music is in simple quadruple meter, but the next most common meters in most popular music genres are compound quadruple and simple triple.

title: 鼓點
text: 複四拍子的基本搖滾鼓點，只需配合每拍三分的方式調整：大鼓仍在第1、3拍，小鼓仍在第2、4拍演奏反拍，鈸或其他樂器則奏拍的分割單位。Harold Melvin & the Blue Notes〈If You Don’t Know Me by Now〉的鼓型，就是由這三層組成（例14）。[2]
en: In compound quadruple time, the basic rock beat is simply adjusted for the new three-part beat division: the kick drum still plays on one and three, the snare still plays the backbeat on two and four, and cymbals (or some other instrument) still articulates the beat division. These three elements make up the drumbeat in “If You Don’t Know Me by Now,” by Harold Melvin & the Blue Notes (see Example 14).[2]

title: 鼓點

title: 鼓點
text: 例14。Harold Melvin & the Blue Notes〈If You Don’t Know Me by Now〉（1972）中，慢速複四拍子的鼓型。
en: Example 14. A slow compound quadruple drumbeat in Harold Melvin & the Blue Notes’s “If You Don’t Know me By Now” (1972).

title: 鼓點
text: 在單三拍子中，無法於每小節內，以等長間隔反覆交替大鼓與小鼓。常見做法是把小鼓「反拍」延到每小節第3拍；Paramore〈That’s What You Get〉就是如此（例15）。前奏的小鼓先在「3 e + a」做熱鬧的鼓花，之後進入下方採譜的律動。大鼓的tresillo，讓延後小鼓擊點的節奏仍富變化。歌曲第二段主歌（原文標0:27）也值得注意：鼓改用像四拍子的基本搖滾鼓點，其他樂器卻仍維持原來的三拍子。
en: In simple triple time, it isn’t possible to alternate kick and snare hits of equal length in each measure. The most common approach is to delay the snare “backbeat” until the third beat of every measure; this is what happens in Paramore’s “That’s What You Get” (see Example 15). After an intro with exuberant “3 e + a” fills on the snare, the drums settle into the groove transcribed below. The tresillo kick-drum rhythm keeps things interesting while delaying the snare hit. The second verse of this song (0:27) is also notable: the drums shift to a basic rock beat (as if in quadruple meter) while the rest of the band keeps playing in the triple meter established up to this point.

title: 旋律與樂句
text: 重點整理流行／搖滾歌曲的段落，通常包含兩、三或四個樂句，常見組織方式如下：兩部分：aa′。三部分：aa′b，常見於十二小節藍調。四部分：srdc，即陳述、重述／回應、轉離、結束。
en: Key Takeaways Sections in pop/rock music typically consist of two, three, or four phrases. These phrases are usually organized as follows: Two-part: aa′ Three-part: aa′b (often a 12-bar blues) Four-part: srdc (statement, restatement/response, departure, conclusion)

title: 旋律與樂句
text: 本章播放清單
en: Chapter Playlist

title: 旋律與樂句
text: 本章討論主歌、副歌、橋段等歌曲段落的內部結構。每個段落至少包含兩個樂句；在流行／搖滾音樂中，一個樂句通常約四小節，對應一行歌詞。分析這些結構時，以小寫字母標示樂句。
en: This chapter discusses the structure of song sections such as a verse, chorus, or bridge. Each section consists of at least two phrases—in pop/rock music, a phrase is a musical unit that typically lasts for four bars and corresponds to one line of the lyrics. In labeling these structures, phrases are designated by lowercase letters.

title: 旋律與樂句
text: 兩部分的樂句組織
en: Two-Part

title: 旋律與樂句
text: 若段落中的樂句能分成前、後兩半，就是兩部分結構。後半通常以與前半相同的音樂為基礎，因此標作aa′。兩半常以相同材料開始，卻有不同結尾，形成前句—後句的關係，也就是由較弱的收束走向較強的收束。
en: A section is two-part when the phrases that make up the section can be grouped into a first half and a second half. In two-part sections, the second half is usually based on the same music as the first half, and thus it is labeled aa′. Often these two halves begin the same but have different endings, participating in an antecedent–consequent (weak → strong) relationship.

title: 旋律與樂句
text: 〈Livin’ on a Prayer〉副歌（1:33）採aa′結構（例1）。第一個四小節樂句從「喔，我們已走了一半……」開始，第二個從「握住我的手……」開始。兩句旋律與和聲相同，所以都用a；歌詞不同，因此第二句加上撇號，標成a′，讀作「a prime」。很多歌曲未必如此界線分明，但只要兩個樂句開頭使用相似材料，就可用相同字母；新歌詞、不同結尾或音樂變化，則以撇號表示。
en: The chorus to “Livin’ on a Prayer” (1'33") has an aa′ structure (Example 1). The first four-bar phrase (“Oh, we’re half-way there…”) and the second four-bar phrase (“Take my hand…”) have identical melody and harmony (so they both get the letter a), but different lyrics (so the second a is marked as "a prime": a′). Note that in many songs, this relationship is not as clear cut. However, if the two phrases begin with similar musical material, give them the same letter. New lyrics, new musical endings, or musical variations simply warrant a “prime.”

title: 旋律與樂句
text: 很少數段落的前、後兩半，會使用明顯不同的音樂；這時標作ab。
en: Very rarely, a section's phrases can be grouped into two clear halves based on different music. Such a section is labeled ab.

title: 旋律與樂句
text: 歌詞樂句喔，我們已走了一半喔，靠著祈禱過日子a握住我的手，我發誓我們一定撐得過去喔，靠著祈禱過日子a′
en: Lyrics Phrase Whoa, we're halfway there Whoa, livin' on a prayer a Take my hand, we'll make it I swear Whoa, livin' on a prayer. a′

title: 旋律與樂句
text: 例1。〈Livin’ on a Prayer〉。
en: Example 1. "Livin' on a Prayer."

title: 旋律與樂句
text: 三部分的樂句組織
en: Three-Part

title: 旋律與樂句
text: 包含三個樂句的段落，構成三部分結構。如果前兩句以相同音樂為基礎，第三句不同，就標作aa′b。
en: A section containing three phrases is a three-part section. If the first two phrases are based on the same music and the third is different, the section is labeled aa′b.

title: 旋律與樂句
text: 十二小節藍調進行是aa′b三部分段落最常見的例子。〈Hound Dog〉的歌節，就是aa′b（例2）。
en: 12-bar blues progressions are the most common example of a three-part aa′b section. “Hound Dog” contains aa′b strophes (Example 2).

title: 旋律與樂句
text: 歌詞樂句你不過是條獵犬整天哀叫a你不過是條獵犬整天哀叫a′你從沒抓到兔子，也不是我的朋友。b
en: Lyrics Phrase You ain't nothin' but a hound dog Cryin' all the time a You ain't nothin' but a hound dog Cryin' all the time a′ Well, you ain't never caught a rabbit and you ain't no friend of mine. b

title: 旋律與樂句
text: 例2。〈Hound Dog〉。
en: Example 2. "Hound Dog."

title: 旋律與樂句
text: 四部分的樂句組織
en: Four-Part

title: 旋律與樂句
text: 四個樂句組成的段落，常有類似樂句型（sentence）的功能進程：呈示→延續→終止／結束。在流行／搖滾中，第一句提出基本樂思，第二句重複或回應，第三句使用對比材料，常伴隨片段化、和聲節奏加快及離開主和聲；第四句則作結。結尾可以返回基本樂思與主和聲，也可以使用新材料，在旋律、節奏與和聲上形成有力收束。Walter Everett（2001，132頁）把這種四樂句的組織稱為srdc：陳述（statement）、重述／回應（restatement/response）、轉離（departure）、結束（conclusion）。
en: A section composed of four phrases often contains a sentential structure (presentation → continuation → cadential/conclusion). In pop/rock music, this often appears as a basic musical idea in the first phrase, a repetition or “response” to it in the second, contrasting material in the third phrase (often employing fragmentation, acceleration of harmonic rhythm, and movement away from tonic harmony), and a conclusion in the fourth phrase―either with a return to the basic idea and tonic harmony or with still newer material that forms a strong melodic, rhythmic, and harmonic conclusion. Walter Everett (2001, 132) has called such a four-phrase sentential structure in pop/rock music srdc (statement, restatement/response, departure, conclusion).

title: 旋律與樂句
text: 若按一般材料字母標記，srdc可能是aaba：陳述材料在重述與結尾再現；也可能是aabc，表示結尾使用新材料。偶爾也能是abcd或abca，但前提是b明確回應a，不能只是毫無關聯的新材料。
en: In conventional lettering, an srdc section could employ an aaba structure (with statement material returning as a restatement and again as the conclusion), or an aabc structure (where the conclusion material is new). Occasionally abcd or abca are possible, but only if b is a clear response to a, not simply new material.

title: 旋律與樂句
text: srdc通常能清楚分成兩半：sr與dc。
en: An srdc structure tends to tend to divide neatly into halves: sr and dc.

title: 旋律與樂句
text: Bobby Darin的〈Dream Lover〉（例3），就是四部分srdc樂句組織的典型例子。
en: Bobby Darin's "Dream Lover" (Example 3) provides a classic example of a four-part srdc phrase structure.

title: 旋律與樂句
text: 歌詞樂句每晚我都盼望、祈禱夢中情人會走入我的生命s（陳述）一個能擁在懷裡的女孩讓我體會她魅力的魔法r（重複）因為我想要（耶—耶，耶）一個女孩（耶—耶，耶）能稱作（耶—耶，耶）屬於我（耶—耶）d（轉離）我想要一個夢中情人好讓我不必獨自做夢c（結束）
en: Lyrics Phrase Every night I hope and pray A dream lover will come my way s (statement) A girl to hold in my arms And know the magic of her charms r (repetition) 'Cause I want (yeah-yeah, yeah) A girl (yeah-yeah, yeah) To call (yeah-yeah, yeah) My own (yeah-yeah) d (departure) I want a dream lover So I don't have to dream alone c (conclusion)

title: 旋律與樂句
text: 例3。〈Dream Lover〉。
en: Example 3. "Dream Lover."

title: 流行音樂曲式入門
text: 重點整理本章介紹音樂曲式的基本概念。具體曲式請參閱接下來的〈AABA與分節歌形式〉及〈主歌—副歌曲式〉。透過核心與輔助段落的概念，可以比較不同流行曲式。段落可依曲式與和聲上的功能來定義。
en: Key Takeaways This chapter addresses foundational concepts of form in music. (For discussions of specific forms, see the following two chapters: AABA and strophic form and verse-chorus form.) Pop forms can be related to one another through the concepts of core and auxiliary sections. Sections can be defined through their formal and harmonic functions.

title: 流行音樂曲式入門
text: 若想了解流行曲式與古典曲式之間的關係，可對照〈曲式段落通論〉。
en: Those interested in the connections between pop and classical forms may wish to cross-reference Formal Sections in General.

title: 流行音樂曲式入門
text: 流行曲式中的段落
en: Sections within Pop Forms

title: 流行音樂曲式入門
text: 流行／搖滾音樂中的一個段落，通常長8至24小節，包含2至4個樂句；某些輔助段落可能只有一個樂句。段落呈現單一曲式功能，如歌節、橋段、前副歌等，內部構成完整的兩、三或四部分樂句組織。一個段落通常配一節歌詞。
en: In pop/rock music, a section typically spans between 8 and 24 bars and includes 2–4 phrases. (Some auxiliary sections may contain a single phrase.) A section presents a single formal function (such as strophe, bridge, prechorus, etc.) and presents a complete two-, three-, or four-part pattern. A section typically sets a stanza of lyrics.

title: 流行音樂曲式入門
text: 段落分界常由歌詞詩體結構，例如兩行詩或一節歌詞的結束，以及下列可直接聽到的特徵顯示：
en: Section boundaries are usually made apparent by poetic structure (the end of a couplet or stanza) or by surface features of the song such as:

title: 流行音樂曲式入門
text: 節奏、和聲與旋律出現清楚的抵達點。配器或音量改變。回到之前聽過的段落開頭。
en: a clear rhythmic, harmonic, and melodic arrival a change in instrumentation or volume a return to the beginning of a previously heard section

title: 流行音樂曲式入門
text: 例如U2〈Pride (In the Name of Love)〉在2:42，由主歌轉入副歌，好幾項特徵同時標出分界：
en: For instance, take the transition from a verse section to a chorus section at 2:42 in U2’s “Pride (In the Name of Love).” The section boundary is delineated by a number of features simultaneously:

title: 流行音樂曲式入門
text: 主歌的四行詩節，以近似押韻的sky與pride收尾，再開始新詩節。鼓花標出主歌結束；這是常見的樂句或段落結尾手勢。整體音量迅速增大。吉他演奏更活躍，另一個吉他聲部也加入重複它。主唱音域升高。加入伴唱，配合主唱。
en: The text closes out the verse’s quatrain with a (more-or-less) rhyming lyric (“sky”–”pride”) before beginning a new stanza. The end of the verse is signaled by a drum fill, a common end-of-phrase or end-of-section gesture. The general dynamic gets louder very quickly. The guitar becomes more active and is doubled by a second guitar part. The lead vocals rise in register. Background vocals are added to the lead vocal part.

title: 流行音樂曲式入門
text: 這些特徵共同劃分段落，其中大部分也讓新段落，也就是副歌，比前面的主歌更有能量。
en: All of these features help delineate the boundary between sections, and most of them also give the new section (the chorus) a higher energy level than the previous section (the verse).

title: 流行音樂曲式入門
text: Spotify：〈Pride (In the Name of Love)〉，2009重製版
en: Spotify Embed: Pride (In The Name Of Love) - Remastered 2009 (requires internet)

title: 流行音樂曲式入門
text: 術語與基本概念
en: Terminology and Basic Concepts

title: 流行音樂曲式入門
text: 以下定義以Jay Summach（2012）的研究為基礎。
en: The definitions used here are based on the research of Jay Summach (2012).

title: 流行音樂曲式入門
text: 核心段落：構成歌曲主要音樂與詩詞內容的段落，例如主歌、副歌、歌節與橋段。
en: core section: Core sections form the main musical and poetic content of a song. Examples of core sections in pop forms include verse, chorus, strophe, or bridge sections.

title: 流行音樂曲式入門
text: 輔助段落：為核心段落提供框架，負責引入、暫時讓位，或逐漸收尾。例如前奏、收尾段（outro）與尾聲（coda）。
en: auxiliary section: Auxiliary modules help to frame the core modules, introducing them, providing temporary relief from them, or winding down from them. They can include introduction, outro, or coda sections.

title: 流行音樂曲式入門
text: 歌詞變動型（lyric-variant）：段落或樂句每次出現時，大部分歌詞都不同。
en: lyric-variant: A section or phrase is lyric-variant if each time it appears it brings (mostly) different lyrics.

title: 流行音樂曲式入門
text: 歌詞固定型（lyric-invariant）：段落或樂句每次出現時，大部分歌詞相同。歌詞固定常見於曲式收束處，例如歌節末尾的尾端疊句，或主歌—副歌循環末尾的副歌。
en: lyric-invariant: A section or phrase is lyric-invariant if each time it appears it brings (mostly) the same lyrics. Lyric invariance tends to come at points of formal closure (tail refrains at the ends of strophes, choruses at the end of a verse-chorus song’s formal cycle).

title: 流行音樂曲式入門
text: 音樂變動型（music-variant）：段落或樂句每次出現時，大部分音樂材料不同。
en: music-variant: A section or phrase is music-variant if each time it appears it brings (mostly) different music.

title: 流行音樂曲式入門
text: 音樂固定型（music-invariant）：段落或樂句每次出現時，大部分音樂材料相同。
en: music-invariant: A section or phrase is music-invariant if each time it appears it brings (mostly) the same music.

title: 流行音樂曲式入門
text: 以主和聲起始（on-tonic）：樂句或段落由主和聲，也就是原位I和弦開始。
en: on-tonic: A phrase or section is on-tonic when it begins with tonic harmony (I in root position).

title: 流行音樂曲式入門
text: 以非主和聲起始（off-tonic）：樂句或段落由主和聲以外的和弦開始。
en: off-tonic: A phrase or section is off-tonic when it begins on a harmony other than tonic.

title: 流行音樂曲式入門
text: 和聲封閉（harmonically closed）：樂句或段落結束於主和聲，也就是原位I和弦。
en: harmonically closed: A phrase or section is harmonically closed when it ends with tonic harmony (I in root position).

title: 流行音樂曲式入門
text: 和聲開放（harmonically open）：樂句或段落結束於主和聲以外的和弦。
en: harmonically open: A phrase or section is harmonically open when it ends on a harmony other than tonic.

title: 流行音樂曲式入門
text: 回轉進行（turnaround）：在和聲已收束的單位結尾，加入非主和弦，通常是屬和弦，銜接下一個以主和聲開始的單位。Sam the Sham and the Pharaohs的〈Woolly Bully〉，很多歌節末尾都有回轉；例如0:54，只用一個V7，準備下一歌節開頭返回I。[1]
en: turnaround: The use of a non-tonic chord (usually dominant) at the end of a harmonically closed unit to transition into the beginning of the following on-tonic unit. The song “Woolly Bully” by Sam the Sham and the Pharaohs contains a turnaround at the end of many of its strophes. One of these occurs at 0:54 ― a simple V7 chord to prepare the return of I as the next strophe begins.[1]

title: 流行音樂曲式入門
text: 收尾手法（closing rhetoric）：讓人預期歌曲即將結束的常見模式與技巧。例如立即重複核心段落或其中一部分，但最初核心段落的重複除外；讓織體變薄；在歌曲後段加強力度；淡出；或把之前和聲開放的段落帶向和聲封閉。這些手法常見於收尾段、尾聲，以及歌曲最後一個核心段落A或C。
en: closing rhetoric: Closing rhetoric involves common patterns and techniques that signal that the end of the song is likely coming soon. Typical patterns and techniques include immediate repetition of a core section (except for the first core section) or part of a core section, thinning out of the texture, late-song intensification, fadeout, and bringing a previously harmonically open section to a point of harmonic closure. Closing rhetoric is typically found in outros, codas, and the last core section of a song (A or C).

title: 流行音樂曲式入門
text: 分析記號
en: Analytical Notation

title: 流行音樂曲式入門
text: 以下是本書分析曲式時採用的記號慣例。
en: What follows are notational conventions for analyses of musical form in this text.

title: 流行音樂曲式入門
text: 大寫字母
en: Capital letters

title: 流行音樂曲式入門
text: 段落依功能使用大寫字母：
en: Sections are labeled with capital letters according to function:

title: 流行音樂曲式入門
text: 歌節用A。橋段用B。主歌用V。副歌用C。其他段落類型，會在後續章節介紹。
en: A section that functions as a strophe is labeled with an A A section that functions as a bridge is B A verse is labeled V A chorus is labeled C And so on—more sections are introduced in the following chapters.

title: 流行音樂曲式入門
text: 小寫字母
en: Lowercase letters

title: 流行音樂曲式入門
text: 樂句按音樂材料，以粗體小寫字母標記。如果兩句的和聲、旋律與節奏框架大致相同，就使用同一字母。命名方式類似詩歌韻式：第一句是a，後面使用相同音樂的句子也標a；換歌詞、改配器等小變化，加上撇號。下一個使用新音樂材料的樂句標b，依此類推。這些字母不表示功能。
en: Phrases are labeled with bolded lowercase letters according to their musical content. If two phrases use more or less the same musical framework (harmony, melody, and rhythm), they receive the same letter. Letters are assigned in the same manner as poetic rhymes: the first phrase is a, and any phrase that follows based on the same music is also a (primes are used for slight variations, such as new text or altered instrumentation); the next phrase with new musical material is b; and so on. These letters do not correspond to functions.

title: 流行音樂曲式入門
text: 唯一例外是段落內樂句呈現樂句型的功能進程，也就是srdc。此時，第一句陳述標s，重述／回應標r，轉離標d，結束標c。
en: The single exception to this convention is when phrases within a section demonstrate a sentential progression (srdc), in which case the first phrase (statement) is labeled s; restatement/response, r; departure, d; conclusion, c.

title: 流行音樂曲式入門
text: 延伸閱讀
en: Further Reading

title: 流行音樂曲式入門
text: Summach, Jason。2012。〈Form in Top-20 Rock Music, 1955–89〉（〈1955至1989年Top-20搖滾歌曲的曲式〉）。耶魯大學博士論文。
en: Summach, Jason. 2012. “Form in Top-20 Rock Music, 1955–89.” Ph.D. diss., Yale University.

title: 流行音樂曲式入門
text: 原作者指出，這首歌中吉他手並非每次都跟上回轉。0:28時，貝斯與上低音薩克斯風奏屬和弦，吉他仍留在主和弦。1:18時，歌手喊「注意囉！注意！注意！」，彷彿提醒吉他手別錯過下一小節的回轉；2:08也有同樣情形。吉他手與其他樂手一起奏出回轉時，歌手又喊「對了！對了！」，像是在稱讚他。↵
en: Interestingly in this song, the guitarist doesn’t always remember the turnarounds. Notice that at 0:28, the bass and baritone saxophone play the dominant, but the guitarist keeps tonic. At 1:18, the singer yells, “Watch it now! Watch it! Watch it!” as if warning the guitarist not to miss the turnaround in the next bar. He does the same in 2:08. When the guitarist gets the turnaround with the rest of the band, the singer yells, “You got it! You got it!” as if congratulating the guitarist. ↵

title: AABA與分節歌形式
text: 重點整理分節歌形式只由反覆出現的歌節構成，可簡記為AAA。AABA曲式又稱32小節歌曲形式：歌節先連續出現兩次（AA），接著是形成對比的橋段（B），最後再現起初的歌節（A）。AABA與分節歌形式，特別常見於較早期的流行音樂，也就是1960年代及更早的作品。這兩種曲式都以歌節為主要段落，呈現歌曲主要的歌詞與音樂內容。
en: Key Takeaways Strophic form consists only of repeated strophes. Its form would be abbreviated as AAA. AABA form, also known as 32-bar song form, consists of a twice-repeated strophe (AA), followed by a contrasting bridge (B), followed by another repetition of the initial strophe (A). AABA and strophic form were especially common in older pop music (1960s and earlier). AABA and strophic form both have strophe sections as the main section, which features the primary lyrical and musical content of the song.

title: AABA與分節歌形式
text: 本章Spotify播放清單
en: Chapter Spotify Playlist

title: AABA與分節歌形式
text: 分節歌形式
en: Strophic Form

title: AABA與分節歌形式
text: 全曲反覆使用同一個基本單位，而且這個單位包含多個樂句，就屬於分節歌形式。由於基本材料A不斷重複，有時簡記為AAA；這個反覆出現的基本單位稱為歌節。分節歌形式較常見於藍調、早期嘻哈與早期搖滾樂；約1970年以後，主歌—副歌曲式在許多流行音樂類型中成為主流。[1]
en: Songs that repeat the same basic multi-phrase unit throughout are in strophic form (sometimes abbreviated AAA because the same basic material, A, is repeated), and the basic unit that is repeated is called a strophe. Strophic form is more common in blues, early hip hop, and early rock-and-roll; verse-chorus form took over many pop genres after around 1970.[1]

title: AABA與分節歌形式
text: 例1以Chuck Berry的〈School Day (Ring Ring Goes the Bell)〉示範分節歌形式。歌曲有多個段落，都以相同的基本音樂為基礎，這些段落就是歌節。雖然歌詞改變，0:24開始的段落，其旋律、和聲與樂句結構，都與前後段落相同，或至少十分接近。即使0:41與1:21的器樂段，也保留相同的基本模式，只是以吉他獨奏換上不同旋律。整首歌都在反覆這個基本模式，或作些微變化；0:19至0:41可作為這個模式的示例。
en: Example 1 uses “School Day (Ring Ring Goes the Bell)” by Chuck Berry as an exemplar of strophic form. This song contains multiple sections, all of which have the same basic underlying music. These sections are the strophes. Though the lyrics change, the section beginning at 0:24 contains the same—or, at least, very similar—melody, harmony, and phrase structure as the prior and following sections. Even the instrumental sections at 0:41 and 1:21 have the same underlying pattern, just a different melody in the form of a guitar solo. The entire song is a repetition of this same basic pattern, or slight variations of it, modeled at 0:19–0:41.

title: AABA與分節歌形式
text: 〈School Day〉互動曲式圖與影音以下依原章公開互動圖的可見內容重繪，保留段落順序、相對寬度與層級，並附中文圖例，可離線閱讀。此圖不是原站匯出的圖片，也不表示已逐秒核對錄音。 原章互動曲式圖至原來源查看譜例／圖片 ↗例1，〈School Day (Ring Ring Goes the Bell)〉離線曲式圖。A＝歌節；instrumental＝器樂演奏。全圖七個A，第五個另有器樂標註。圖下英文說明：依原章BriFormer圖重繪為離線版本；不是校準過的時間軸。

title: AABA與分節歌形式
text: 例1。Chuck Berry〈School Day (Ring Ring Goes the Bell)〉（1957）。
en: Example 1. “School Day (Ring Ring Goes the Bell)” by Chuck Berry (1957).

title: AABA與分節歌形式
text: 〈School Day〉完全由歌節構成，但分節歌也可以包含所謂的輔助段落，例如前奏、收尾段與尾聲。Patsy Cline的〈Faded Love〉就是包含輔助段落的例子。聆聽時請對照例2的曲式圖，注意前奏、收尾段與間奏，並未大幅改變它基本的分節歌形式。
en: While “School Day” is composed entirely of strophes, it is important to note that strophic songs can also contain so-called auxiliary sections such as intros, outros, and codas. An example of a strophic song with auxiliary sections is “Faded Love” by Patsy Cline. Follow the form chart in Example 2 as you listen to this song, and notice that the intro, outro, and interlude do not change the fundamental strophic form significantly.

title: AABA與分節歌形式
text: 〈Faded Love〉互動曲式圖與影音以下依原章公開互動圖的可見內容重繪，保留段落順序、相對寬度與層級，並附中文圖例，可離線閱讀。此圖不是原站匯出的圖片，也不表示已逐秒核對錄音。 原章互動曲式圖至原來源查看譜例／圖片 ↗例2，〈Faded Love〉離線曲式圖。I＝前奏；A＝歌節；int.＝間奏；O＝收尾段；refrain＝疊句。四個A的末尾，各有一個虛線標出的疊句。圖下英文說明：依原章BriFormer圖重繪為離線版本；不是校準過的時間軸。

title: AABA與分節歌形式
text: 例2。Patsy Cline〈Faded Love〉（1963）。
en: Example 2. “Faded Love” by Patsy Cline (1963).

title: AABA與分節歌形式
text: 然而，如果歌曲除了歌節與輔助段落之外，還有另一個主要音樂想法，就不屬於分節歌形式。它可能採用下文討論的AABA曲式，或下一章介紹的主歌—副歌曲式。
en: However, if a song has more than one main musical idea other than strophes and auxiliary sections, it is not strophic. It could be AABA form, which is discussed below, or verse-chorus form, discussed in the next chapter.

title: AABA與分節歌形式
text: 〈Faded Love〉的歌節中也包含疊句；這是許多分節歌的重要成分。疊句是在歌節內，或其他歌詞會變動的較大段落內，反覆出現的歌詞與音樂動機。疊句常包含歌名，這首歌就是如此。
en: “Faded Love” also incorporates a refrain in its strophes, which is an important component of many strophic songs. A refrain is a recurring lyric and musical motive within a strophe (or any larger section that has varying lyric material). The refrain often contains the title lyric of a song, as it does here.

title: AABA與分節歌形式
text: 32小節歌曲形式（AABA）
en: 32-Bar Song Form (AABA)

title: AABA與分節歌形式
text: 另一種較常見於早期搖滾樂的結構是AABA曲式，也稱32小節歌曲形式；這是因為早期採用此結構的「黃金年代」歌曲，每段都長8小節。AABA與分節歌形式一樣，依靠歌節傳達歌曲主要的歌詞與音樂想法，但在中間加入形成對比的橋段。
en: Another formal structure that is more common in early rock-and-roll is AABA form, also called 32-bar song form because in earlier “Golden Age” songs that make use of this structure, each section is eight measures long. AABA form, like strophic form, relies on the strophe to communicate the main lyric and musical ideas of the song, but it adds a contrasting bridge section in the middle.

title: AABA與分節歌形式
text: 請聽披頭四的〈I Want to Hold Your Hand〉（例3）。簡短的前奏之後，歌曲先呈現兩個歌節。然而，〈Blue Suede Shoes〉在此之後接器樂歌節，披頭四卻在0:52轉入橋段。這個新段落藉由對比，並暫時不呈現主要歌節主題，累積張力，直到1:11歌節回歸。注意，歌曲在前奏之後以歌節開始，也以歌節結束；歌節還包含歌名。對許多人而言，它也是比較容易記住的部分。因此，歌節仍是主要段落，但現在多了一個增加趣味與張力的次要段落，也就是橋段；另外還有前奏這個輔助段落，幫助歌曲展開。
en: As an example, listen to “I Want to Hold Your Hand” by the Beatles (Example 3). After a brief introduction, the song begins with two strophes. However, where “Blue Suede Shoes” followed this with an instrumental strophe, the Beatles move to a bridge at 0:52. This new section builds tension by contrasting and withholding the main strophe theme before it returns at 1:11. Note that the song begins and ends with the strophe, and the strophe contains the title lyrics. For many people, it’s also the the more memorable part of the song. Thus, the strophe is still the primary section. But now it has a secondary section to add interest and tension: the bridge (and an auxiliary section, the intro, to help get the song off the ground).

title: AABA與分節歌形式
text: 〈I Want to Hold Your Hand〉互動曲式圖與影音以下依原章公開互動圖的可見內容重繪，保留段落順序、相對寬度與層級，並附中文圖例，可離線閱讀。此圖不是原站匯出的圖片，也不表示已逐秒核對錄音。 原章互動曲式圖至原來源查看譜例／圖片 ↗例3，〈I Want to Hold Your Hand〉離線曲式圖。I＝前奏；A＝歌節；B＝橋段；ref.＝疊句；extended＝延長。前奏之後是AABA，再接BA；最後一個A的尾端疊句有延長標註。圖下英文說明：依原章BriFormer圖重繪為離線版本；不是校準過的時間軸。

title: AABA與分節歌形式
text: 例3。披頭四〈I Want to Hold Your Hand〉（1963）。
en: Example 3. “I Want to Hold Your Hand” by The Beatles (1963).

title: AABA與分節歌形式
text: 第一輪AABA之後，〈I Want to Hold Your Hand〉又重複B與A。這是AABA歌曲的典型做法：幾乎都先有完整的一輪AABA，後面再接完整的一輪AABA，或不完整的一輪，通常是BA。第一輪AABA完成之後，通常不再出現新歌詞，而是重複主要循環的全部或結尾部分。
en: After the initial AABA cycle, “I Want to Hold Your Hand” repeats B and A again. This is typical for an AABA song—in almost all cases, they have a complete AABA cycle followed by either another complete cycle (AABA) or an incomplete one (typically BA). Once the first AABA cycle is complete, there tend not to be any new lyrics, only repetition of the whole or the end of the main cycle.

title: AABA與分節歌形式
text: AABA與分節歌形式的段落
en: Sections of AABA and Strophic Forms

title: AABA與分節歌形式
text: 本章及整部《開放音樂理論》所用的流行曲式術語，以Jay Summach（2012）的研究為基礎。
en: The pop form terminology used here and throughout OMT is based on the research of Jay Summach (2012).

title: AABA與分節歌形式
text: 歌節（A）
en: Strophe (A)

title: AABA與分節歌形式
text: 歌節作為主要段落，功能是呈現主要的歌詞與音樂內容，並提供一個讓歌曲可以圓滿結束的停駐點。
en: As a main section, the function of a strophe section is to present the primary lyric and musical content and to provide a point at which the song might satisfyingly end.

title: AABA與分節歌形式
text: 在分節歌形式（AAA）中，歌節是唯一的核心段落。每個歌節通常配上一節歌詞，音樂自成一體，而且和聲封閉。
en: In strophic form (AAA), strophes are the only core sections. Each strophe tends to set a stanza of text, with music that is self-contained and harmonically closed.

title: AABA與分節歌形式
text: 在32小節歌曲形式（AABA）中，歌節承載主要音樂與文字、提供和聲穩定性的功能，透過與橋段對比而更為突出。AABA歌曲的歌節功能，常涉及主和聲的延長。這類歌曲的歌節，通常比單純分節歌中的歌節短。
en: In 32-bar form (AABA), the strophe’s functions—holding primary music/text and providing harmonic stability—are elevated through contrast with the bridge section. In AABA songs, strophe function often involves the prolongation of tonic harmony. Strophes tend to be shorter in AABA songs than in strophic songs.

title: AABA與分節歌形式
text: 這兩種曲式中，歌節內部最常見的模式都是srdc。由三部分構成的歌節，最常見的模式則是12小節藍調進行。
en: In both forms, srdc is by far the most common internal pattern for strophes. For three-part strophes, the 12-bar blues progression is the most common pattern.

title: AABA與分節歌形式
text: 橋段（B）
en: Bridge (B)

title: AABA與分節歌形式
text: 橋段是對比段落，與古典曲式的延續功能有許多共同特徵。橋段在曲式循環中通常扮演過渡角色，既不是出發點，也不是抵達點。它與A形成對比，並暫時不讓A出現，因而提高聽者對A回歸的期待。Summach指出，橋段後面必須接回主要段落，才能完成它的功能（2012，79）。橋段通常強調非主和聲，並常以屬和聲結束。
en: Bridges are contrasting sections, and share many traits with the continuation function of classical form. Bridge sections tend to play a transitional role (neither the point from which to depart nor the point of arrival) in the formal cycle. This generates heightened expectation for the return of A by contrasting with A and temporarily withholding it. A bridge section “must be followed by [the primary section] in order for its function to be satisfied” (Summach 2012, 79). Bridge sections tend to emphasize non-tonic harmonies and commonly end on dominant harmony.

title: AABA與分節歌形式
text: 如下一章所述，主歌—副歌形式的歌曲，橋段比AABA中的橋段更自由；它可以與主歌和副歌形成對比，不一定要強烈建立對副歌回歸的期待。在AABA歌曲中，建立對歌節回歸的期待，並抵達屬和聲以準備回歸，則是橋段功能的要點。
en: As the next chapter discusses, in verse-chorus songs, bridge sections are more free than in AABA form to contrast verse and chorus sections without a strong need to build expectation for the return of the chorus. In an AABA song, building expectation for the return of the strophe and arriving on dominant harmony in preparation of that return are essential to bridge function.

title: AABA與分節歌形式
text: 前奏（I）
en: Introduction (I)

title: AABA與分節歌形式
text: 前奏把歌曲開始前沒有拍節的寂靜，帶入第一個核心段落的音樂活動。前奏通常較短，沒有歌詞、以器樂演奏，並常使用後面一個或多個核心段落的音樂材料。常見做法是逐步累積材料，例如讓樂器一件件加入、堆疊聲部，或以較一般的方式增加能量。
en: Introduction sections transition from the unmetered silence that precedes the song to the musical activity of the first core section. They tend to be short and untexted/instrumental, and they tend to present musical material from one or more core sections to come. This is often accomplished by the building up of musical material, perhaps through layering (e.g., one instrument at a time) or through a more generic building of energy.

title: AABA與分節歌形式
text: 前奏偶爾也使用核心段落以外的材料。這種前奏常與使用相同材料的收尾段呼應，兩者像一對書擋，形成首尾呼應的效果。也可能連續出現多個前奏段落，各自採用不同的音樂。[2]
en: Occasionally intros include non-core material. Such intros often correspond to an outro based on the same material, and together they create a “bookend” effect. It is also possible to have multiple intro sections in a row, with each based on different music.[2]

title: AABA與分節歌形式
text: 收尾段（O）與尾聲（X）
en: Outros (O) and Codas (X)

title: AABA與分節歌形式
text: 收尾段負責讓歌曲過渡回寂靜，因此會降低能量。錄音室中常以淡出達成這個效果。如果有獨立的收尾段，幾乎總是取材自緊接在它前面的最後一個核心段落；否則，通常會使用前奏材料，形成首尾呼應。收尾段會展現收尾手法。
en: Outros function as a transition from song back to silence, and thus decrease energy. Often this is accomplished in the recording studio by way of a fadeout. When an outro section is present, it is almost always based on material from the last core section that preceded it. Otherwise, outros tend to draw material from the intro, creating a “bookend” effect. Outros exhibit closing rhetoric.

title: AABA與分節歌形式
text: 尾聲是在歌曲結尾呈現新材料的段落；換句話說，它是沒有取材自先前音樂的結尾段落。和收尾段一樣，尾聲也展現收尾手法。
en: A coda is a song-ending section that presents new material—in other words, it is an outro not based on music previously heard. Like outros, codas exhibit closing rhetoric.

title: AABA與分節歌形式
text: Muse的〈Resistance〉同時有尾聲與收尾段，適合用來區分兩個術語。最後一次副歌之後，尾聲在4:05開始，帶來新的音樂與敘事材料。這個新段落讓敘事獲得某種結局，雖然仍帶有開放性；接著在4:54讓位給結束全曲的收尾段。除了4:54時內容與織體明顯改變，也能從前奏材料的回歸，辨認出這是收尾段而非尾聲：它產生了首尾呼應的效果。
en: Muse’s “Resistance” is useful for distinguishing between these two terms, since it has both a coda and an outro. The coda, which contains new musical and narrative material, begins at 4:05, following the final chorus. This new section, which brings something of a conclusion (if an open-ended one) to the narrative, gives way to a song-ending outro at 4:54. Aside from the clear change in content and texture at 4:54, the outro is recognizable as an outro (versus a coda) by the return of material from the introduction, creating the “bookend” effect.

title: AABA與分節歌形式
text: 間奏
en: Interludes

title: AABA與分節歌形式
text: 器樂間奏常見於流行曲式。它比完整段落短，明顯只是銜接兩個更重要的段落，並提供對比。不過，別過度使用這個名稱！直接把某段叫作「間奏」之前，先確認是否有更合適、更能描述功能的名稱，例如橋段或後副歌。
en: Instrumental interludes are common in pop forms. They are shorter than a full section and clearly serve to simply link and provide contrast between two more important sections. But be careful not to overuse this label! Before simply calling something an “interlude,” ensure there is no better, more descriptive label (such as bridge, postchorus, etc.).

title: AABA與分節歌形式
text: 疊句
en: Refrains

title: AABA與分節歌形式
text: 疊句是在其餘部分屬於歌詞變動型的段落內，一小段歌詞固定型材料。疊句太短，無法自成段落；通常只有一個樂句，甚至更短。
en: A refrain is a lyric-invariant passage within a section that is otherwise lyric-variant. A refrain is too short to form its own section—typically a single phrase or even less.

title: AABA與分節歌形式
text: 疊句最常出現在一個段落歌詞的最後一行左右，稱為尾端疊句；偶爾也在段落歌詞開頭出現，稱為開頭疊句。Jump, Little Children的〈Cathedrals〉（1998）就有開頭疊句，每個歌節都以同一句「在高樓的陰影之中……」開始。本章討論的〈Faded Love〉與〈I Want to Hold Your Hand〉，則都在歌節末尾使用尾端疊句，強調歌名歌詞。
en: A refrain is most often the last line or so of a section’s text (tail refrain); occasionally, it is the material at the beginning of a section’s text (head refrain). “Cathedrals” by Jump, Little Children (1998) contains a head refrain. Each strophe begins with the same line: “In the shadows of tall buildings.…” “Faded Love” and “I Want to Hold Your Hand,” each discussed in this chapter, both contain tail refrains at the ends of their strophes, emphasizing the title lyrics.

title: AABA與分節歌形式

text: 作業

text: AABA與分節歌形式（PDF、Word）：使用BriFormer網頁工具，為採用AABA或分節歌形式的流行歌曲製作曲式圖。
en: AABA and Strophic Form (.pdf, .docx). Uses BriFormer web app to create form diagrams of pop songs in AABA or strophic form.

title: AABA與分節歌形式
text: 嘻哈中的分節歌形式，可以聯繫到「cypher」現場表演傳統：不同饒舌歌手（MC）輪流在重複的節奏上即興演唱各自的段落（Duinker 2020）。↵Dexys Midnight Runners的〈Come On Eileen〉，有好幾個採用不同音樂內容的前奏段落。↵
en: Strophic form in hip-hop can be related to the "cypher," a live performance tradition in which various rappers (MCs) took turns improvising verses over a repeating beat (Duinker 2020). ↵Dexys Midnight Runners’s “Come On Eileen” contains several different intro sections with different musical content. ↵

title: 主歌—副歌曲式
text: 重點整理主歌—副歌曲式是靈活多變的歌曲形式，1960年代迅速成為搖滾樂的主流，此後持續占有主導地位。在主歌—副歌曲式中，歌名歌詞、最容易記住的音樂與主要敘事，分配在兩個核心段落：主歌與副歌。
en: Key Takeaways Verse-chorus form is a versatile song form that rapidly took over rock-and-roll in the 1960s and has dominated the genre ever since. In verse-chorus form, the title lyrics, the most memorable music, and the main narrative are split between two core sections: the verse and the chorus.

title: 主歌—副歌曲式
text: 主歌—副歌曲式之所以如此命名，是因為最重要的兩個段落是主歌與副歌。其他可能出現的段落還有前副歌、橋段與後副歌。
en: Verse-chorus form is so named because the two most important sections are the verse and the chorus. Other possible sections in verse-chorus form are prechorus, bridge, and postchorus.

title: 主歌—副歌曲式
text: 例1呈現一種典型的主歌—副歌曲式。
en: A prototypical verse-chorus form song is illustrated in Example 1.

title: 主歌—副歌曲式
text: 例1。主歌—副歌曲式的典型示意，並非某首特定歌曲。點圖可放大。
en: Example 1. A prototypical verse-chorus form, not referencing a specific song. Click to enlarge.

title: 主歌—副歌曲式
text: Bon Jovi的〈Livin’ on a Prayer〉採用典型的主歌—副歌曲式（例2）。原文也以它說明主歌—副歌曲式中五種核心段落的常見用法。
en: “Livin’ on a Prayer” by Bon Jovi follows a typical verse-chorus form (Example 2). It also illustrates common usage of five core sections in verse-chorus forms.

title: 主歌—副歌曲式
text: 〈Livin’ on a Prayer〉互動曲式圖與影音以下依原章公開互動圖的可見內容重繪，保留段落順序、相對寬度與層級，並附中文圖例，可離線閱讀。此圖不是原站匯出的圖片，也不表示已逐秒核對錄音。 原章互動曲式圖至原來源查看譜例／圖片 ↗例2，〈Livin’ on a Prayer〉離線曲式圖。I＝前奏；V＝主歌；P＝前副歌；C＝副歌；B＝橋段。第一個C後有一小段深色區塊，原圖未標字，正文稱為短間奏。全圖依序為I、VPC、未標字短區塊、VPC、BPC、C、C。原圖沒有後副歌Z。圖下英文說明：依原章BriFormer圖重繪為離線版本；不是校準過的時間軸。

title: 主歌—副歌曲式
text: 例2。Bon Jovi〈Livin’ on a Prayer〉（1986）。
en: Example 2. “Livin’ on a Prayer” by Bon Jovi (1986).

title: 主歌—副歌曲式
text: 循環
en: Cycles

title: 主歌—副歌曲式
text: 注意，〈Livin’ on a Prayer〉的段落會再現，而且似乎遵循某個模式。主歌—副歌曲式的段落，有一些典型的順序與分組。例如主歌、前副歌、副歌、後副歌，總是依這個順序推進，但不必全部出現。這些段落組合稱為循環。〈Livin’ on a Prayer〉的情形如下：
en: Notice that the sections used in “Livin’ on a Prayer” recur and seem to follow a pattern. Sections within a verse-chorus form have certain prototypical orderings and groupings. The verse, prechorus, chorus, and postchorus sections, for example, always progress in this order (though they don’t all need to be present). These groupings are referred to as cycles. In “Livin’ on a Prayer”:

title: 主歌—副歌曲式
text: 較長的前奏之後，第一輪循環開始：0:47進入主歌。1:18進入前副歌，增加能量與張力…………接入1:34的副歌。簡短間奏之後，1:54開始重複這個循環。最後一輪在3:00以吉他獨奏開始；它具有橋段功能，取代這一輪的主歌。這一輪之後，副歌持續重複，最後淡出結束歌曲。
en: After an extended intro, the first cycle begins: A verse at 0:47 At 1:18, a prechorus increases energy and tension… …into the chorus at 1:34. After a brief interlude, this cycle is repeated beginning at 1:54. A final cycle at 3:00 begins with a guitar solo (functioning as a bridge and replacing the verse in this cycle). The cycle is followed by repetitions of the chorus, and a fadeout ends the song.

title: 主歌—副歌曲式
text: 主歌—副歌曲式中的段落
en: Sections within Verse-Chorus Form

title: 主歌—副歌曲式
text: 以下術語、概念、定義與記號準則，綜合一般慣例與本章末尾〈延伸閱讀〉列出的資料。
en: Terms, concepts, definitions, and notational guidelines are taken from common convention and a combination of the resources listed below under Further Reading.

title: 主歌—副歌曲式
text: 主歌（V）
en: Verse (V)

title: 主歌—副歌曲式
text: 主歌屬於歌詞變動型，歌詞常用來推進敘事。1960年代以前，主歌通常和聲封閉。從1960年代開始，主歌越來越常呈現和聲開放（Summach 2012，114）。主歌和歌節一樣，通常以主和聲起始。
en: Verse sections are lyric-variant and often contain lyrics that advance the narrative. Until the 1960s, verse sections tended to be harmonically closed. Beginning in the 1960s, verse sections became more and more likely to be harmonically open (Summach 2012, 114). Verses (like strophes) tend to begin on-tonic.

title: 主歌—副歌曲式
text: 前副歌（P）
en: Prechorus (P)

title: 主歌—副歌曲式
text: 辨識前副歌最容易的線索，是能量增加。前副歌具有許多srdc中d句的功能特徵：片段化、和聲節奏加快、離開主和聲，以及和聲開放。[1]
en: Prechorus sections can be recognized most easily by energy gain. They bear many of the functional characteristics of the d phrase in srdc—fragmentation, acceleration of harmonic rhythm, movement away from tonic harmony, and harmonic openness.[1]

title: 主歌—副歌曲式
text: 副歌（C）
en: Chorus (C)

title: 主歌—副歌曲式
text: 副歌屬於歌詞固定型，包含歌曲主要的歌詞材料，例如歌名或容易記住的歌詞鉤句。副歌功能的另一項典型特徵，是相較主歌更強烈的音樂表現，例如更濃密或活躍的器樂織體、突出的伴唱，或音域更高的旋律（Summach 2012，106）。副歌最常以主和聲起始，但並非只能如此。日常談話有時把副歌與疊句混用，但討論音樂理論時，要注意區分。副歌本身構成完整段落；疊句則包含在某個段落之內，詳見下文。
en: Chorus sections are lyric-invariant and contain the primary lyrical material of the song (the title lyrics and/or lyrical hook). Chorus function is also typified by heightened musical intensity relative to the verse, including features like “a more dense or active instrumental texture; prominent background vocals; and/or a higher register melody” (Summach 2012, 106). Choruses most frequently (but not exclusively) begin on-tonic. Although the terms chorus and refrain are often used interchangeably when speaking colloquially, take care to keep them separate when discussing music theory. Chorus sections are distinct from refrains because choruses constitute an entire section by themselves, whereas refrains are contained within a section (as described below).

title: 主歌—副歌曲式
text: 後副歌（Z）
en: Postchorus (Z)

title: 主歌—副歌曲式
text: 後副歌是接在副歌之後的短段落，只負責結束這一輪循環，而不是引入或過渡到下一輪的開頭（Spicer 2011，第9段）。Destiny’s Child的〈Independent Women, Pt. 1〉在1:18有明確的後副歌，以「女孩，我不知道妳能那樣跳」這句歌詞開始。
en: A postchorus is a short section that follows a chorus and serves only to close the cycle (not to introduce or transition to the beginning of the next cycle) (Spicer 2011, para. 9). A clear postchorus can be heard in “Independent Women, Pt. 1” by Destiny’s Child at 1:18, beginning with the lyric “Girl, I didn’t know you could get down like that.”

title: 主歌—副歌曲式
text: 橋段（B）
en: Bridge (B)

title: 主歌—副歌曲式
text: 橋段在主歌—副歌曲式中，是使用方式相當靈活的段落類型。
en: Bridge sections are a flexible section type in verse-chorus form.

title: 主歌—副歌曲式
text: 主歌—副歌形式的歌曲，橋段通常只出現一次，後面接全曲最後的副歌，或最後的前副歌加副歌。在一輪循環內，橋段會取代主歌或前副歌，也可能兩者都取代，而不是額外增加一個元素。因此，同一輪循環通常不會同時出現五種核心段落。主歌—副歌形式的歌曲，也可能完全沒有橋段。
en: In verse-chorus form songs, the bridge tends to appear once, followed by the last chorus (or the last prechorus and chorus) of the song. Within a cycle, bridges will replace the verse and/or prechorus sections instead of being added in as an extra element. Thus, you will not usually see all five core section types in a single cycle. A verse-chorus song may not have a bridge at all.

title: 主歌—副歌曲式
text: 以上各點，都與AABA曲式使用橋段的方式不同。
en: Each of these points contrasts with the way bridges are used in AABA form.

title: 主歌—副歌曲式
text: 段落內突出的歌詞
en: Standout Lyrics within Sections

title: 主歌—副歌曲式
text: 疊句
en: Refrain

title: 主歌—副歌曲式
text: 疊句主要與AABA曲式和分節歌形式相關，但偶爾也會出現在主歌—副歌歌曲的段落內。要注意，疊句與副歌不同：疊句是段落內的歌詞，副歌則是完整、獨立的段落。
en: While refrains are primarily associated with AABA form and strophic form, they can occasionally be used within sections of a verse-chorus form song. However, take note that refrains are distinct from choruses—refrains are a lyric within a section, whereas a chorus is an entire standalone section.

title: 主歌—副歌曲式
text: 攀升句（climb）
en: Climb

title: 主歌—副歌曲式
text: 攀升句是具有前副歌功能的一個樂句。和疊句一樣，它只有一個樂句長，太短而無法自成段落。原文將攀升句的位置界定為歌節或主歌的最後一句。
en: A climb is a phrase with prechorus function. Like the refrain, because it is only one phrase long, a climb is too short to be its own section. The climb is always the last phrase of a strophe or verse.

title: 主歌—副歌曲式
text: Dexys Midnight Runners的〈Come On Eileen〉（1982）提供一個例子：留意主歌與橋段末尾，只有一句長的攀升句，也就是唱出「Tu-ra-lu-ra……」的部分；1:13可聽到。
en: An example of a climb is in “Come On Eileen” by Dexys Midnight Runners (1982): listen for the one-phrase climb at the end of its verses and bridge (“Tu-ra-lu-ra…”), as heard at 1:13.

title: 主歌—副歌曲式
text: 延伸閱讀
en: Further Reading
